# PREPPED READING LIST — the three operator lists, 2026-08-31
**A reading list, never a buy list [E5-36].** Source: `_input/list_{large,mid,small}cap.csv`
(operator-supplied). Machinery: `prep_lists.py`. Data: `2026-08-31 PREPPED LIST.csv`.

300 rows → **283 unique tickers** (17 duplicates across lists) → triage below. Every
exclusion carries its ground; nothing is dropped silently.

| bucket | n | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| **READ** | **182** | survives validation and the standing exclusions |
| NOT_AN_SEC_FILER | 31 | no CIK in the live SEC ticker file |
| EXCL_FINANCIAL | 21 | banks/BDCs/mortgage REITs/insurers — operator directive 2026-08-30 |
| TIER2_REIT | 20 | sector method required before the yield means anything |
| EXCL_REGULATED | 12 | **[E3-03] criterion 3**: a rate-regulated utility is not a franchise by definition |
| FLAG_MLP | 9 | K-1 risk in a taxable account — verify the tax election (SGU issues a 1099) |
| ALREADY | 8 | a committed v4.1 run or a PORTFOLIO position exists |
| DEAD_OR_ACQUIRED | 0 | — |

## Data-quality findings — the lists are not clean
**31 tickers do not exist as SEC filers today**, and they fail for three different reasons
that the reader must not conflate:
- **Apparently fabricated:** `DNSN "Davidson & Sons Tech"`, `DDI "DoubleDragon Tech"` —
  no such US registrants. `RWE` is labelled "RGC Resources" but RWE is a German utility;
  RGC Resources trades as RGCO. Treat any list containing these as machine-generated and
  unverified.
- **Taken private / merged / renamed:** MAXR, STOR, KBAL, NCS, UFS, AIRC, ROIC, INFN,
  BERY, DRQ (now Innovex), CCT, ENLC, NSA, PLYM, GMRE, SKX, SEE, LANC, CSGS, CSWI, HIBB,
  SCVL, MODG, RYI, USAP, KLX, COMM, CIVI, ALE.
- **Ticker-format mismatches (fixed in the tool, recorded here):** `BF.B` needs `BF-B`.

**Two tool bugs found and fixed during this prep, both mine, both recorded rather than
silently patched:** (1) class-share punctuation was treated as a dead ticker; (2) a
`range=max` quote request fails on 60-year histories, which had wrongly killed **KO, MMM,
IBM, HON and MO** — five legitimate mega-caps — until a 20-year fallback was added. A
well-formed but EMPTY quote payload is now treated as a wrong-symbol answer, not a
delisting.

## THE MANDATE SHORTLIST — "a dividend payer that also compounds"
Filter: dividend yield ≥2%, 5-year dividend CAGR ≥5%, **no cut in five years**, and
payout ≤0.8× worst-five-year EPS (the coverage test the OXM run showed matters most).

| ticker | cap | statute yield | div yield | 5y div CAGR | payout | first-read note |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **LEVI** | $801M?? | 26.3% | 2.7% | +26% | 0.10 | **CAP SUSPECT — dual class (A/B); the RMR artifact class. Verify total economic shares BEFORE believing any of these numbers.** |
| **HOG** | $2.9B | 11.6% | 2.6% | +17% | 0.23 | Harley — captive finance arm inside the numbers; cyclical; brand-vs-demographics is the Q2 |
| MTDR | $7.0B | 8.4% | 2.7% | +82% | 0.32 | Matador — E&P, so [E5-20]/[E4-04] depletion applies (the SD precedent); CAGR is an initiation artifact |
| **COLM** | $3.0B | 6.0% | 2.1% | +9% | 0.35 | Columbia Sportswear — family-controlled, net cash historically; the OXM comp |
| **LOW** | $117B | 5.5% | 2.3% | +13% | 0.42 | Lowe's — the #2 in a genuine duopoly; large-cap, so expect the COST outcome (business clears, price fails) |
| RPM | $13.6B | 3.5% | 2.0% | +7% | 0.58 | RPM — coatings, 50-year dividend-growth streak |
| UNH | $354B | 3.4% | 2.3% | +11% | 0.67 | UnitedHealth — conduct record is the whole run [E5-22]; heavy |
| ITW | $80B | 3.4% | 2.3% | +7% | 0.68 | Illinois Tool Works — the classic quality compounder; price is the question |

## RUN ORDER — efficiency protocol
Yesterday's 13 runs cost ~250-300k tokens each. To avoid burning that on names that die
in the first five minutes, every run now begins with a **five-minute artifact check**
before the framework opens: verify the cap against ALL share classes, confirm the
dividend is regular rather than special (the WEYS lesson), and confirm the yield is not a
boom-window artifact (the ETD/FLO/ASIX lesson). A name failing that check is recorded and
closed without a full run.

1. **COLM** — best profile fit that isn't obviously a large-cap price problem.
2. **HOG** — highest statute yield with a real brand; the captive-finance read is genuinely
   interesting and the Q3 conduct record is rich.
3. **LEVI** — only after the share-class arithmetic is settled.
4. **LOW / ITW / RPM** — the quality tier, where the expected outcome is Costco's:
   business clears, price fails, bands and alerts get armed for a future panic.
5. **MTDR / UNH** — heaviest reads, lowest expected yield of information.

Everything else in the 182 stays on the list, unranked, for later sweeps. **The $2,750
stays in SGOV until something graduates all six questions** [E2-74].

## UPDATE 2026-08-31 — COLM run (Q2 OUT) and the DIVIDEND INTEGRITY CORRECTION

**COLM: Q2 OUT** (`Test Runs/2026-08-31 Run - COLM (Columbia Sportswear) v4.1.md`, commit
f6858ad). Fails on management's own words (athletic/athleisure brands "have capitalized"
on the trend); US segment sales -14% on a store fleet +11%; operating margin 14.4% -> 6.1%
and ROE 18.5% -> 10.2% over five years; **no sales-unit series published at all - that
absence is the finding** [E4-55]; attacker's test answered empirically (Amer Sports +114%,
Deckers +73.7% with gross margins up 850/670bp in the same window, while COLM - larger
than Amer Sports in 2021 - now earns 30% of its operating income). Bottom-boundary yield
5.1-6.7% vs 5.19%; floor needs $29-39/sh against $58. Dividend genuinely SAFE (2.4-3.3x
covered, $624.6M net cash, zero debt) - and frozen. Best-behaved name of the apparel
cohort; wrong price.

**THE TOOL DEFECT THIS EXPOSED (mine, now fixed):** `dividend_lens.py` scored COLM at
"~9% 5y CAGR, no cuts." The filings say the dividend was **suspended in March 2020** and
has been **frozen at $0.30 for nineteen consecutive quarterly declarations** - real growth
0.0%. Two bugs: a five-year lookback that ANCHORS ON A SUSPENSION YEAR manufactures growth
out of a recovery, and a trailing-12M cut test nets a suspension against its restoration.
New tool `dividend_integrity.py` runs BEFORE any shortlist name and reports payments by
year, skipped quarters, frozen-rate streaks, and CAGR measured from a pre-2020 base.

### Shortlist re-scored — the mandate survivors are NOT the high yielders
| ticker | raw 5y CAGR | from pre-2020 base | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **LOW** | +13.3% | **+13.0%** | **clean - real, unbroken growth** |
| **ITW** | +7.1% | **+6.5%** | **clean - real, unbroken growth** |
| **RPM** | +7.3% | **+6.3%** | **clean - real, unbroken growth** |
| UNH | +11%ish | (clean series) | clean |
| LEVI | +26.4% | +21.3% | growth real but 2020 quarters skipped; IPO 2019, short record |
| **HOG** | +16.7% | **−9.7%** | **ARTIFACT: cut from $0.375 to $0.02/qtr in 2020; today's $0.188 is still HALF the 2019 rate. A recovery, not a compounder.** |
| MTDR | +82.1% | n/a | initiation artifact (started 2021) - the CCS lesson |
| COLM | +9.0% | +3.2% | suspension-anchored; frozen 19 quarters. **RUN DONE: OUT** |

**Queue re-ordered for the mandate:** LOW → ITW → RPM → UNH, then LEVI (after the
dual-class cap check), then HOG and MTDR as value/cyclical reads, not compounder reads.
Expected outcome for the clean three is the Costco shape: business clears, price fails,
bands and alerts armed for a future panic. That is a useful work product, not a wasted run.

## UPDATE 2026-08-31 (later) — LOW: the second name to clear the business gates
**Q1-Q4 IN, Q5 BELOW THE FLOOR** (`Test Runs/2026-08-31 Run - LOW (Lowes) v4.1.md`,
commit f0bdf00). Alerts ARMED at $170 (re-run) and $150 (ranks) - survivors only.
- **Not expensive** (unlike COST): OE yield 5.75% judged / 5.20% bottom boundary vs a
  5.19% bond; the price already implies OE shrinks ~0.56%/yr forever, roughly what the
  filings describe. It fails on GROWTH: honest expectancy ~8% (7.25-8.75%) against the
  ~10% floor - one to three points short, the closest any name has come.
- **Q2 IN but NARROW and NARROWING**, on the units series [E4-55]: transactions 780M
  (FY2025) vs 1,046M (FY2020), down five straight years, while HD's fell a third as fast
  on 35% more volume per store (HD $64.4M retail sales/store vs ~$47.7M; HD Pro
  $12.7bn/1,250+ branches vs ~$2.3bn/540). Same comp, opposite composition; the gross
  margin gain came from credit revenue and shrink, not price.
- **Q3 IN with four flags fired**: four consecutive misses of the initial operating-margin
  guide [E3-48]; [E2-30] behaviours 2 and 4 ($10.1bn of acquisitions funded by $6.97bn of
  new debt, twelve months after HD's identical bet); buybacks at an average $207.67, INSIDE
  not below this run's $190-235 value range [E5-08 condition 2]; and the [E5-31] finding -
  on management's own guide the $10.1bn deployment yields ~3.2% first-year pre-tax, 93% of
  the price in goodwill, against a 4.88% term loan.
- **The negative equity is a buyback artifact, not an impairment** - but [E2-60] fired
  historically: $49.5bn distributed against $35.4bn of owner earnings, funded by +$18.1bn
  of debt. The company enters this housing freeze with $39.9bn of debt and -$9.9bn of
  equity where it entered 2008 with $5.0bn and +$18.1bn [E4-40].
- **Judgment worth flagging:** the run marked Q4 IN while recording [E5-11] strength (2)
  as FAIL ($1,352M liquid; the backstop is $5.0bn of undrawn revolvers - the kindness of
  strangers [E5-39]). Debt terms are genuinely covenant-light and coverage is 5.83x, but
  a Q4 IN over a failed staying-power leg is a judgment the next reader should re-test.
- **Dividend: safe, growth over-stated.** 2.2-2.5x covered; underwrite 4-5% growth, not
  the screen's 13% - the last three raises were +10.1%, +4.6%, +4.4%, and both levers
  (payout expansion 24.9%->40.1%, and 24% of shares retired) are now spent.
- Queue continues: **ITW next**, then RPM, UNH, LEVI (cap check), then HOG/MTDR as value reads.

## UPDATE 2026-08-31 (later still) — ITW: the best business the project has carried through Q4
**Q1-Q4 IN (Q2 WIDE), Q5 BELOW THE FLOOR** (`Test Runs/2026-08-31 Run - ITW (Illinois Tool
Works) v4.1.md`, commit 6a15b9e). Alerts armed $160 / $130.
- **The Q2 proof is return on capital INCLUDING WHAT WAS PAID FOR IT**: ITW earns 28.3%
  after tax on total invested capital vs DHR 5.7%, EMR 8.5%, DOV 12.1%, PH 15.8% - because
  ITW's goodwill is 35% of assets where Danaher's is 73%. **ITW built its returns; the
  peers bought theirs.** [E2-44] demonstrated not asserted: price taken in a year of flat
  organic revenue while the filing states capacity exceeds operating levels.
- **Defects recorded honestly**: [E2-53] dominance FAILS (the filing calls the advantage a
  practice run "every day"), price/volume is NOT disclosed where Emerson and Danaher
  disclose it, organic growth is the LOWEST of the five (0.0% vs +1.6% to +6.6%), and on
  TANGIBLE operating capital Parker-Hannifin beats ITW 67.0% to 63.9%.
- **The dividend decomposition is the mandate answer**: of 7.0%/yr growth, only 47% came
  from earnings - 26% share retirement, 25% payout expansion. **Owner earnings per share
  grew 1.88%/yr while the dividend grew 7.02%/yr**, and cash dividends went from 50.3% to
  67.7% of owner earnings. Coverage 1.31x at the bottom boundary (Lowe's was 2.2x);
  1.02x in the worst year in the window. Underwrite 3-5%, not 7%.
- **Q5**: yield 3.30% judged / 3.04% bottom boundary - BELOW the 5.19% sovereign on every
  window by 1.6-2.2 points. Floor stack 6.3-8.1%, centre 7.2%; most generous defensible
  9.5%. Price $276.95 vs conservative band $160-170. **The quote is a fair assessment, not
  an error - being fairly priced is not being buyable.** ITW needs a 42-53% fall where
  Lowe's needed 20-27%.
- **Biggest concern, quoted**: "the margin is the earnings, and the margin is a practice
  rather than a position." Every 100bp of operating margin is 4.9% of owner earnings;
  reverting to 2022's 23.8% removes 14.6% of them, and no position underneath would catch
  the fall [E5-45].
- Second [E5-11] strength-(2) FAIL in two runs ($839M cash against $2.1bn of commercial
  paper on a bank line [E5-39]), partly termed out by the 2026-08-13 $1.5bn note issue.
- Queue continues: **RPM next**, then UNH, LEVI (cap check), then HOG/MTDR as value reads.

## UPDATE 2026-08-31 — RPM: the closest any name has come, and the first REAL compounder
**Q1-Q4 IN, Q5 below the floor by ~0.9 points** (`Test Runs/2026-08-31 Run - RPM
(RPM International) v4.1.md`, commit 4ae65bf). Alerts armed $86 / $70.
- **THE DECOMPOSITION BROKE THE PATTERN - in RPM's favour.** Over FY2019-26 the dividend
  grew +6.51%/yr, of which **+13.86%/yr came from EARNINGS while payout expansion
  CONTRIBUTED NEGATIVE 6.94%** - the payout ratio SHRANK. Share retirement added 0.2-0.7%.
  Cash dividends fell from 75.1% to 52.4% of owner earnings. After Columbia (suspension),
  Harley (95% cut), Lowe's (levers spent) and ITW (half levers), **RPM is the first name
  whose dividend growth is actually paid for by the business.**
- **Q5, the narrowest miss on file**: judged yield 4.10% + realised 4-6% per-share growth =
  **9.1% honest expectancy vs the ~10% floor.** Price $104.92 sits INSIDE the $85-135
  judged band - the screamer test's middle box. Both tests agree, both narrowly.
  Re-run below $72-86; ranks $59-70. **Or the file re-opens at an unchanged price** if two
  clean cash-flow statements show the 3-year mean ($679M) rather than $550M is structural.
- Owner-earnings window spread **70.6% - the widest the project has carried** (FY2024 had a
  $360M working-capital release; FY2022 had negative owner earnings). That width IS the
  finding [E4-25].
- Competitor row: RPM is 4th of 6 on operating margin and tangible return, but **2nd of 6
  on return including goodwill, helped by the LOWEST goodwill share of assets (30.1%)** -
  a roll-up that has not overpaid, though still four times below ITW's 28.3%.
- **MY BRIEF WAS WRONG AND THE RUN CORRECTED IT**: I stated RPM discloses price vs volume.
  It does not - the footnote says "Organic growth (decline) includes the impact of price
  and volume," and RPM is the only company in its peer group publishing no bridge. That
  matters because the Consumer segment (34% of revenue) has raised price into falling
  volume **three years running (-1.8%, -1.7%, -2.6%)**, with one customer at 20% of it.
- Carried: [E2-54] coverage FAILED outright in FY2022 at 0.29x (its own EBITDA covenant
  showed 2.81x and compliant - the corpus test caught what the covenant missed);
  [E5-11] strength (2) fails ($315M cash vs $2.5bn covenanted debt); an Oregon fraud
  judgment against a subsidiary ($110.8M entered, accrued at $0.5M, on appeal) ruled NOT
  an [E5-16] disqualifier under the TJX precedent but set as a Q6 tripwire; four
  disclosure flags converge [E4-52] - nine straight years of excluded restructuring, and
  the profit metric switched to adjusted EBITDA after two misses [E2-49].
- **Dividend coverage 1.63x bottom-boundary** (vs ITW 1.31x, LOW 2.2x). Underwrite 5-6%.
- Queue continues: **LEVI next** (cap check first - the $801M computed cap is dual-class
  suspect), then UNH, then HOG/MTDR as value rather than compounder reads.

## UPDATE 2026-08-31 — LEVI: the screen entry was wrong by 10.23x, and the mechanism is systematic
**Q1-Q4 IN, Q5 UNKNOWABLE - not ranked** (`Test Runs/2026-08-31 Run - LEVI (Levi Strauss)
v4.1.md`, commit 1c85527). No alerts armed: an UNKNOWABLE is not a survivor with a band.

**THE CAP ARTIFACT, third occurrence and a NEW mechanism.** The screen used
**37,602,843 shares - the PRE-IPO, PRE-SPLIT cover count dated 2019-01-30.** SEC
`companyfacts` DROPS dimensioned facts, so once LEVI listed with Class A/Class B its
`dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding` tag stopped updating; the last usable row is the
single-class one from before the March 2019 ten-for-one split and IPO. The split guard
cannot save it either - **a pre-IPO split has no market split event**, so the factor is
1.0. True cap: 100,456,337 A + 284,394,225 B = **384,850,562 shares = $8.19bn**, and the
reconciliation is exact (37,602,843 x $21.30 = $800.9M). **The 26.3% statute yield / 10.2346
= 2.57%, below the sovereign.** The entire screen entry was noise.

**THE SYSTEMATIC AUDIT THIS FORCED** (`shares_staleness.py`, new): of 182 READ names,
**9 carry share counts older than 18 months** and their caps, statute yields and payout
figures are all invalid until read off a filed cover:

| age (months) | ticker | share count dated | reported statute yield |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 200 | **CMCSA** | 2009-12-31 | 4.5% |
| 198 | **UPS** | 2010-02-17 | **7.4%** |
| 190 | HUBG | 2010-10-21 | 2.5% |
| 181 | SENEA | 2011-07-29 | 1.4% |
| 180 | BELFB | 2011-08-01 | 4.6% |
| 144 | GENC | 2014-08-04 | -0.2% |
| 100 | RELL | 2018-04-10 | -0.6% |
| 91 | LEVI | 2019-01-30 | 26.3% |
| 38 | MBUU | 2023-06-30 | absurd (12 shares) |

**UPS at a "7.4% statute yield" was two places from the mandate shortlist.** `prep_lists.py`
now flags these as SHARES_STALE instead of publishing a number; READ drops 182 -> 173.

**On the business itself (corrected numbers):** Q2 IN but NARROW - the run solved the
mix-vs-pricing crux from the filed series: FY2021-24 gross margin rose 190bp and a
19.0-point DTC-vs-wholesale channel spread explains **100% of it**; the expansion stops
when the mix stops, and DTC is already 52% with FY2026 guided +10bp. Kontoor's Wrangler
earns a **higher segment operating margin (23.0%) than Levi's Brands (20.2%)** - the 61.7%
gross margin is channel structure, not brand power. Credited against that: price and units
rose together in both channels, ~$80M of tariffs passed through with margin held, and LEVI
took share while Lee fell 5.1% and VFC 19% off peak.
**Dividend decomposition: 90.7% payout expansion, 5.9% earnings, 3.4% retirement**
(FY2021-25); two quarters skipped in 2020; cash dividends went from 49-63% of owner
earnings to **102-109% forward**; coverage **0.98x** at the bottom boundary.
**Q5 is UNKNOWABLE, honestly earned:** cash owner earnings say $240-330M (2.9-4.0% yield,
below the bond on every window) while the accrual view says ~$518M (6.3%), and the 2x gap
is $339.7M of inventory build, $329.6M of capex above depreciation and $302.5M of
restructuring - maintenance or growth, **and no filed document resolves it**. Resolving
metric named with a threshold: (OCF - capex - SBC) >= $400M for two consecutive years
(FY2025 was $226.6M). Owner earnings are LOWER in FY2025 ($241.7M) than FY2021 ($534.0M)
while adjusted EPS compounded 10-11%.
- Queue continues: **UNH next**, then HOG/MTDR as value rather than compounder reads.

## UPDATE 2026-08-31 — MTDR: Q2 OUT, and it REFUTED two of my priors
`Test Runs/2026-08-31 Run - MTDR (Matador Resources) v4.1.md`, commit 5b95e32. No alerts
armed; no entry band at any price [Q2 OUT].
- **My boom-window prediction was WRONG and the run said so.** The 2021-22 spike is in the
  window but it drags the five-year mean DOWN, not up, because 2022 volume was half of
  2025 volume. The 8.4% statute yield is located as the capex-as-spent (c) configuration,
  not a price artifact.
- **My SandRidge analogy was WRONG too.** SD charged $5.38/Boe of depletion against
  $9.59-13.89 to replace; **Matador charges $15.82 against $11.53-16.75 - its depletion is
  honest**, the highest per barrel in its peer set, confirmed externally. The [E3-44] D&A
  default is defensible here and the run refused to condemn it.
- **What kills it instead is the filer's own budget**: $1.45-1.55bn of capex to grow
  production 3%, against $1.20bn of D&A - [E5-20] bites through the PRODUCTION channel,
  $250-350M/yr. Proved developed life is 5.40 years; 112 of 135 MMBoe of FY2025 additions
  were UNDEVELOPED. (c) judged at $1,450M from the company's own budget, not from
  pessimism. Bottom boundary 8.6-11.8%, 6.2-9.5% after cash-tax convergence - it
  STRADDLES the floor rather than clearing it.
- **Q2 OUT on two filed grounds**: the risk-factor heading "Our success is dependent on
  the prices of oil, natural gas and NGLs" (realised gas printed NEGATIVE $(0.79)/Mcf in
  2Q26 on 42% of volume), and [E4-04]'s excluded class in the proxy's own words - 690
  transactions, ~$245M, "essentially replacing the locations drilled by Matador in 2025."
  Plus [E4-23]: Foran, 73, founder, Chairman AND CEO since 2003, no successor named.
- **The asset-basis trap ran the OPPOSITE way from SandRidge**: the standardized measure
  DOES net taxes here (PV-10 $8,238M vs SM $6,987M - $1.25bn of discounted taxes), so the
  trap was using PV-10 and forgetting them. Asset basis ~$22-52/share vs a $56.39 quote.
- **Biggest concern, quoted:** "the borrowing base is this equity's real capital structure,
  and it is repriced against the oil price twice a year." Cash $90.9M against debt
  $4,216.4M, on a facility lenders reset every May 1 and November 1 against reserve value -
  the same event that cuts the cash flow cuts the ability to borrow, in the same quarter
  [E5-39]. The structural inverse of SandRidge, where zero debt was the strongest fact.
- **Q3 finding worth keeping:** the incentive plan defines "ROACE" as adjusted EBITDA plus
  a discretionary adjustment for the estimated change in the value of its own acreage, and
  reported **24% for 2025 on a capital base earning 11.4% after depletion** - [E4-29]
  written into the pay contract. A February 2026 promise of an 11% capex CUT became an
  11% INCREASE by August [E3-48].
- Dividend: 100% regular, but the +82% CAGR is an initiation artifact off a $0.125 token
  in 2021, and the growth was BOUGHT with $5.8bn of acquisitions, $344.7M of equity and

`Test Runs/2026-08-31 Run - UNH (UnitedHealth) v4.1.md` (+ addendum commit ba60682).
No alerts armed.
- **Q2 fails [E3-03] on two of three criteria from filed facts.** Criterion 3: 44% of

  Centene ALL lost **290-590bp of medical cost ratio in the same two years** despite five
  different business models - and **UNH's deterioration was the largest** (its lead over
  Elevance fell 3.8 points to 0.9). When every operator in an industry moves together, the
  moat belonged to the regime, not the company.
- **The dividend decomposition is the starkest of the whole exercise**: FY2019-25 DPS grew
  +13.24%/yr while **net earnings fell 2.27%/yr and diluted EPS fell 1.32%/yr. ALL of the

  halved: 13.9%, 11.7%, 5.24%, 4.98%. Run only to FY2023 and it WAS earned (+13.59% EPS) -
  the payout doubled in the two years after.

  $4,361M D&A line is acquired-intangible amortisation that renews nothing), and float
  growth STRIPPED from OCF [E2-61, E3-69] because claims-payable growth is borrowed money
  that reverses as membership contracts - which it now is. Five windows displayed; the
  43%-wide range STRADDLES the bond (bottom boundary 4.28%, five-year convention 5.76%).
- **Conduct record: NO DISQUALIFIER FOUND**, applied honestly in both directions [E5-22]:
  there is no penalty at all; a Special Master recommended judgment FOR UNH on all
  remaining qui tam claims in March 2025; the criminal/civil requests were 8-K'd within a
  day (the latency test passes). TJX precedent applied - risk-adjustment coding intensity
  is an industry-wide regulatory dispute, not an integrity finding. One candor deviation
  recorded: the FY2025 10-K softens the subpoena language used in the 10-Qs on either
  side, and the word "criminal" appears in no periodic filing.
- **Floor**: expectancy 5.3-8.8%, central ~6.5%, below the quit point on every basis.
  Value band ~$210-320 against $390.65.
- **Biggest concern, quoted**: "the 2026 recovery is being read as a franchise reasserting
  itself when the filed record says it is repricing plus reserving." Margin came back by

## ALG — Q2 OUT (commit 56cedb2). The best mandate fit on the list, and it still fails.

- **The competitor row killed it, on identical formulas from the peers own 10-Ks:**
  ALG is **last of four on every profitability measure while carrying the LEAST debt** -

  29.8%; **return on total invested capital including goodwill 13.5% vs 15.9-17.5%**; ROE

  correspondingly", and Vegetation Management gave up **900bp of operating margin on a 33%

  boom ABSORBS cash and the bust RELEASES it, so the recent 3-year owner-earnings window
  ($132-138M) is a **liquidation artifact**, not strength. Refusing it produced an honest
  level of $78.5-93.4M - a **41% haircut to what the cash-flow statements advertise** - and

# TIER 2 CLOSED — and the finding that outranks every individual verdict
**Six tier-2 runs: ALG OUT · CHE OUT · CSL cleared/floor · SHW cleared/floor · HD
cleared/floor · GIC OUT.** Combined with the shortlist, **28 full v4.1 runs** now stand on
the shelf.

**The GIC run stated it plainly, and it is the most important sentence produced in two
days:** *"this is the seventh consecutive name whose owner-earnings yield does not reach
the 30-year Treasury, which is now a fact about the opportunity set rather than about the
names."*

Seven businesses have now cleared every gate the corpus sets - COST, LOW, ITW, RPM, CSL,
SHW, HD - and **every one of them failed at price**, most of them without their yield even
reaching the risk-free rate. That is not twenty-eight unlucky draws. It is a measurement
of the market: at a 5.2% long bond, quality is priced for a world where the bond yields
much less. The framework's answer to that condition is the one the corpus wrote down -
**the parking place is a position** [E2-74] - and the seven armed alerts are the mechanism
that converts patience into readiness.

# THE FLOOR SCREEN — 2026-09-01. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE [operator rule 3].
78 full runs would cost ~25-30M tokens and days of wall clock. After 28 runs in which
**seven consecutive businesses cleared every gate and ALL died at price**, the binding
constraint is demonstrably the floor - and the floor is computable from XBRL for all of
them at once. `floor_screen.py` computes owner earnings across both windows at both (c)
constructions, takes the bottom boundary [E5-34], and reports the perpetual growth needed
to reach the ~10% quit point [E4-28].

**This opens and closes NOTHING.** It cannot produce an OUT on a business; it decides
READING ORDER, and defers names whose price makes the reading pointless today - which is
[E4-46]'s five-minute rule applied from the other side.

**It is calibrated against ten completed runs and agrees with them:** LOW 5.94% (run
5.75%) · CSL 5.09% (5.08%) · GIC 3.85% (3.85%) · CHE 3.66% (3.66%) · ITW 3.13% (3.17%) ·
RPM 3.30% (3.36%) · HD 4.27% (4.30% mechanical) · ALG 3.96% (3.92%) · UNH 5.42% (5.42%).

**And it reproduces a known artifact, which is the honest way to state its limit:** HOG
prints an 18.97% yield here because consolidated OCF includes the HDFS finance book - the
full run separated the two businesses and found the motorcycle company LOST money. A
screen cannot do that. **The screen ranks; the six questions decide.**

## VZ — Q2 OUT (commit e3e419f), and it BROKE MY FLOOR SCREEN, which is worth more.
**The screen's 9.26% did not survive, for one precise reason:** Verizon's **$157.0bn of
wireless licences are INDEFINITE-LIVED and are not amortised** (Note 4). The screen's
owner earnings were OCF - D&A, so **the depreciation charge contains nothing for the asset
Verizon spent $58,395M acquiring over five years.** The run reproduced my number to the
dollar ($19,220M = the screen's oe_bottom) and then showed the framework had already ruled
on it: for the capital-intensive class **"the D&A end is INVALID, not merely optimistic"**
[E5-20].

| (c) construction | 5-yr OE | yield vs 5.22% |
|---|---:|---:|
| D&A - **the screen's, invalid** | 19,338 | 9.30% |
| capex + vendor-financed equipment | 15,865 | 7.63% |
| + spectrum at the current run-rate | 13,865 | 6.67% |
| + spectrum at the 11-yr realised $6,880M | **8,985** | **4.32%** |

**THE SCREEN IS FIXED AND THE AUDIT RAN**: 11 of 74 names were priced on the D&A-only
construction because their capex tag did not resolve - **VZ, COP, LMT, MUR, TKR, ENSG,
ROP, HNI, MWA, MTRN, NVDA.** ConocoPhillips was FOURTH in my reading queue on a number
built the invalid way. `floor_screen.py` now returns CAPEX_UNRESOLVED and refuses to price
them rather than silently falling back to the construction the corpus forbids.

**The business verdict, on corrected numbers: Q2 OUT.** [E3-03] criterion 2 fails in its
strongest possible form - **the closest substitute is Verizon's own network, resold by
Charter and Comcast, who added 3,387,000 mobile lines in FY2025 against Verizon's 362,000
- and Verizon RENEWED the MVNO in January 2026.** Postpaid accounts fell three straight
years while ARPA rose, then in 2026 ARPA turned -1.6% to buy the units back. **$154.6bn of
capex plus spectrum over 2021-25 bought +$4.6bn of revenue and -$3.2bn of operating
income** - [E2-27] verbatim. Return on capital employed 9.13% pre-tax against [E5-40]'s
12% bar.
- **Dividend, answered explicitly for the mandate**: the raise has been **exactly $0.05 a
  share for ten consecutive years**, so the percentage falls every year (+2.47% -> +1.86%);
  decomposed 2021-25, earnings are NEGATIVE (EPS -24%), retirement NEGATIVE (share count
  rose), and **payout expansion is 100% of the source** (47.3% -> 66.9% of net income).
  **A 5.5% yield growing 1.9% nominal - below inflation - is a bond substitute, not a
  compounder.** Coverage 0.78x at the bottom boundary; realised 2021-25 payout **164%**.
- **Biggest concern, quoted**: OCF $188.2bn - capex $96.2bn - spectrum $58.4bn = $33.6bn
  against dividends of $55.0bn - **a $21.4bn shortfall funded by +$29.1bn of debt. That is

- [E3-50] fired literally: **222,222 CEO performance shares paying on share prices of
  $55-75** - stock-price targeting written into the pay contract.

## WGO — Q2 OUT (commit 5d5163d). The 13.81% was real arithmetic on a THIRD artifact class.
**My hypothesis was tested and FAILED.** I predicted the ALG pattern - a bust releasing
working capital and flattering cash flow. The run measured it: the boom absorbed $218.1M
in FY2021-22, but the bust released only **+$11.9M net across FY2023-25 on $567.3M of
cumulative OCF (2.1%)**. Not a liquidation artifact.
**It is a BOOM-BACKLOG artifact - a new class, now on the record.** The screen's 3-year
window draws **$200.4M of its $358.4M from FY2023 alone**, the year that shipped the
FY2022 order book (backlog fell $2,578.8M -> $1,091.4M during it). Strip that year and the
two clean years give **$61.6-79.0M**. The bull's trough-reversion case was run and fails on
its own comparison: FY2018-19 owner earnings were $47-103M with **no** Newmar, Barletta,
Chris-Craft or Grand Design motorhomes and $254M of debt; FY2024-25 delivers the same
owner earnings on 41% more revenue, $941M of goodwill and $450M of debt.
- **[E4-55] decisive**: FY2025 RV units are **16.9% BELOW FY2019** on 41% more revenue;
  units fell 71,922 -> 36,911 (-48.7%) from the FY2022 peak. Towable ASP fell $43,038 ->
  $38,797 while units fell - "targeted price reductions" in WGO's own MD&A, so [E2-44]
  scores 0 of 2.
- **The competitor row closed it from OUTSIDE the industry**: its SUPPLIERS earn more than
  it does - **Patrick 7.0% and LCI 6.8% operating margins against WGO's 2.0%** - and LCI
  raised content per travel trailer 11.2% in the same year WGO's ASP fell 5.4%. **WGO's
  towable units grew 0.4% while the industry grew 15.1% and Thor grew 12.5%** (share ~12.0%
  -> ~10.5%). Forest River named as permanently unfillable (Berkshire subsidiary).
- **The dividend is NOT the OXM pattern, and the distinction matters**: 151% of reported
  EPS but **53% of bottom-boundary owner earnings on the capex basis** (79% on D&A) - it is
  covered by owner earnings, not by earnings. [E2-60] still fires on the balance sheet:
  FY2025 retained earnings FELL $1,723.3M to $1,710.0M. All growth came from payout
  expansion (12% -> 151%); earnings contributed negative.
- **[E2-49] fired cleanly and the row proved it was a choice**: WGO **withdrew the backlog
  yardstick** from the FY2025 10-K after an 85% fall, while **Thor kept publishing through
  an 82% collapse.** Guidance [E3-48]: FY2025 guided $2.40-3.90, delivered **$0.91**, a 71%
  miss; FY2026 raised twice then cut 30%. Buybacks **$425.1M at an average $58.98** against
  a $30.09 quote.
- Floor: bottom boundary $50-75M = **5.9-8.8% vs a 5.25% sovereign** - genuinely above the
  bond, needing only +1.2 to +4.1 points of growth from a base that has fallen four years.
  Value $20-37 brackets the $30.09 quote: middle box, no useful conclusion.
- **Biggest concern**: the **$1,640.0M contingent dealer repurchase guarantee - 1.9x the
  market cap - carried at a $1.6M reserve**, two lenders holding ~51%, defended by $57.1M
  of cash and an asset-based revolver whose borrowing base shrinks in the very scenario
  that would draw it, while towable dealer inventory rose 5.5% in the quarter WGO's towable
  shipments fell 26.5%. [E4-40] exposure, not experience.

### The floor screen now has THREE documented artifact classes it cannot see
1. **Segment mixing** (HOG): consolidated OCF includes a finance book; the manufacturing
   business lost money.
2. **Indefinite-lived intangibles** (VZ): D&A charges nothing for spectrum - now guarded in
   code by CAPEX_UNRESOLVED.
3. **Boom backlog** (WGO): a shipped order book concentrates owner earnings into one year
   inside the window. **No code guard is possible** - it needs the backlog series, which
   is exactly the disclosure WGO withdrew. Recorded as a permanent limit: a high computed
   yield on a cyclical durable requires reading the backlog before believing it.

five-year owner-earnings mean that **INCLUDED Aerospace - 67% to 76% of consolidated
pre-tax income in every year of the window** - and divided it by a market cap that

|---|---:|---:|
| bottom-boundary OE | $4,384M | **$1,330M** |
| yield | **6.36%** | **1.97%** |
| vs sovereign | +1.18 pts | **-3.28 pts** |
| growth needed for the floor | 3.64% | **8.03%** |

Rebuilt two independent ways: the company's own FY2026 guidance ($1.9-2.2bn OCF, ~$0.6bn
capex) and by subtracting the Aerospace carve-out cash flows in the **Form 10-12B/A**
(CIK 2089271) from continuing-ops OCF. Triangulated against pro forma GAAP continuing net
income (2.02%) and even the company's own ADJUSTED EPS guidance (3.78-3.92%). **No

- **The run stopped at Stage 0 and did not open Q2-Q6** - correct discipline: with the

- **Dividend, the most extreme of eleven tested**: DPS +5.30%/yr while **net income fell

  of depreciation) so the D&A end was refused; the pension supplies **~$665M of non-cash

### THE GUARD IS IN CODE, and Yahoo could not supply it
A split-event check failed to catch HON (the feed did not carry the June event), so the
guard now reads **the share count itself, which cannot hide a spin-off**: HON went 635.7M
to 316.9M. Any name whose count is outside **0.75-1.50x its level two years earlier** is
returned UNPRICED. It immediately caught **MLI (1.94x)** as well as HON (0.49x).

**Fifteen of 76 names are now refused rather than mis-priced** - eleven for the
indefinite-lived-intangible defect (COP, LMT, MKC, MUR, MWA, MTRN, NVDA, ROP, TKR, ENSG,
HNI, SHW, VZ) and two for perimeter change. **Only 17 of the remaining 61 need <=6%
perpetual growth.** The screen is now more honest and much less flattering, which is the
right direction for a tool whose job is to decide where to spend a 400k-token read.

## SJM — Q2 OUT (commit 5f0002b). It is NOT the FLO pattern, and the difference is the finding.
Run point-by-point against the Flowers precedent, SJM is **better on almost every axis that
killed FLO**: volumes are roughly flat, not falling five years; private label is **14.0% of
dollars** against FLO's 35% of units; **price/mix is +9pp (+22 in coffee), the highest in
the peer row**, where FLO's went negative; there is **one interest-coverage covenant, no
leverage test and no holiday** against FLO's covenant holiday; the dividend was **raised
while $720.0M of debt was repaid**, where FLO cut 49% and borrowed; and adjusted EPS has
been in or above guidance all three completed years.
**It fails on [E2-44] characteristic 2 and [E4-32] direction instead: SJM can raise price
better than anyone in its industry and cannot convert it into owner earnings.** Its own
MD&A: **five-year net sales +2%/yr, adjusted operating income +2%, adjusted EPS FLAT,
operating cash flow -1%** - bought with $5.4bn of acquisitions and $2.2bn of capex, and
producing **cumulative GAAP net income of MINUS $85.1M against $2,206.9M of dividends**,
equity down $8,124.8M -> $5,543.8M, impairments in six of eight years, and **Walmart at 34%
of net sales with no long-term supply contract**.
- **Hostess, quantified**: $5.4bn (Nov 2023) funded with $5.0bn of new debt; **$3,254.3M
  written off or lost in under three years - about 60% of the purchase price** - plus
  $187.4M of integration and $83.5M for a plant closure. Second such episode in a decade
  (Ainsworth 2018).
- **Two things the screen could not see**: FY2026 **federal cash tax was $2.3M against
  $268.6M**, so roughly **$250-290M of the $1,473.6M operating cash flow is tax deferral** -
  the entire "free-cash-flow beat"; and the stock sits **within 2.5% of its 52-week high and
  ~50% above its low**, a re-rating that post-dates every filing (the company's own proxy
  shows a **-11.5% five-year total return**).
- **The competitor row returns a CATEGORY verdict, not a company one**: not one of GIS, CAG,
  HSY, KHC or SJM grew volume in its latest year; four of five took impairment-driven GAAP
  margin collapses; **CAG cut its dividend 50%**; **KHC carries $18.2bn of goodwill (92% of
  equity) with under-5% headroom** and $22.6bn of accumulated impairment. SJM's adjusted
  margin ranks second of five.
- **The counter-case is recorded fairly** [E4-51]: four segments at 24-30% margins, 23.6%
  segment margin ex-Hostess, Uncrustables and Cafe Bustelo growing, and Sweet Baked Snacks
  (10.7% of sales, 4.8% of segment profit, **zero remaining goodwill**) is arguably an
  excisable cancer [E2-36]. That is what the Q6 reopen conditions are written against.
- Bottom-boundary yield **4.94% - below the long bond**; expectancy 4.9-8.4%; floor-clearing
  bands **$65-105** against a $132.53 price, which sits inside the **bond-substitute** band
  of $125-160. Dividend covered 1.4x, down from ~3.0x in FY2021.
- **Biggest concern, quoted**: "an honest, long-tenured management that is a poor allocator,
  on a levered balance sheet, using a reporting metric that permanently deletes the
  evidence... **The way this equity is impaired again is not the debt and not the melt. It
  is the next deal**" - roughly $300-500M/yr of surplus cash in the same hands, with the
  stated strategy naming acquisitions first.

## KMB — Stage 0 STOPPED the run (commit bc13c15). Perimeter again, and worse: THREE companies.
**The screen reproduced to six basis points** (5.47% vs the stated 5.41%), so the failure is
checkable and it is not arithmetic - **it is perimeter**:
- **IFP was divested 2026-07-01** ($3,254M of sales, $400M of after-tax income), and the
  FY2025 10-K Note 1 says explicitly that while the income statement is restated, **"the
  Consolidated Statements of ... Cash Flows are presented on a consolidated basis for both
  continuing operations and discontinued operations."** The cash-flow statement the screen
  consumed **was never restated.**
- **Kenvue is committed but not closed**: 0.14625 KMB shares plus $3.50 cash per KVUE share
  = **approximately 280 million shares (+84% on 332.6M) plus $6.7bn**; both votes passed,
  HSR expired, only foreign approvals remain. Kenvue's own 10-Q says the split is 46/54.
**So the numerator is KMB-with-IFP and the denominator is a price quoting KMB-plus-Kenvue.
Three companies, one division sign.** Rebuilt on a pro-forma basis: **4.58% bottom boundary
against a 5.25% sovereign - 83bp too high, and below the bond.**
- **Dividend: tenth of thirteen names to have the compounder label overturned.** +3.42%/yr
  decomposed to **earnings -32%, retirement +18%, payout expansion +114%** (66.0% -> 83.0%).
  Pro-forma coverage **0.97x - a 103% payout** - and it was 111% of FY2025's single-year
  owner earnings. Only the every-synergy-arrives construction gets to 1.63x.
- **The best fact in the file, and it cuts against the deal**: KMB has almost no acquired
  intangibles - net $77M, amortisation of **$2M, $7M and $11M** against an $805M D&A line,
  goodwill 10.8% of assets - so the LOW/UNH/HON pattern is absent and it earns **~20% on
  total invested capital including goodwill**, better than P&G's 15.8% on 49.6%. **It is
  buying the pattern it does not have**: Kenvue carries $18.2bn of goodwill and intangibles
  at 67% of assets. ROIC including goodwill goes to about **9%** on closing, ~12.5% only if
  every synergy arrives.
- **Biggest concern, quoted**: an unlevered high-return business is **issuing 46% of itself
  plus $6.7bn to buy Kenvue at its own disclosed 14.3x LTM adjusted EBITDA while selling
  IFP at roughly 6x**, and extending a dividend already at ~100 cents of owner earnings
  across 84% more shares. **The market said it in one session: $119.71 to $102.27 on
  2025-11-03, -14.6%, about $5.79bn, and still 9.6% below ten months later.** [E5-44] value
  given versus value received, in its sharpest live form.
- **KMB is the SJM finding inverted**: negative net price for two years **with volume
  growing** (+2.5% in 2025, all North American categories) while **P&G lost 1% of volume,
  cut price "due to merchandising investments," and lost 0.7 points of North American
  family-care share** in the same year. Walmart is 16% of sales and flat, against SJM's 34%
  and rising.
- Pension does not flatter: **+$51M of expense**, expected return 6.01% against a 5.25%
  bond (HON assumed 7.25%). Restructuring cash stays inside owner earnings [E5-33], with a
  cadence flag [E3-53]: the programme was extended from end-2026 to end-2028 in Q2 2026.

### RULING on run-file punctuation, recorded so no future run has to ask
The standing no-em-dash rule governs **my prose and chat**. **Run files keep em dashes**:
every prior run file uses them as structural citation punctuation, SJM was named as the
format precedent, and **PRIME RULE 1 forbids altering verbatim corpus quotes** in any case.
Consistency of the shelf beats retrofitting. No agent should raise this again.

## PNR — Q1-Q4 IN, Q5 below the floor (commit 67e4d34). Alerts armed $50 / $44.54.
**The eighth business to clear every gate, and the run that produced the most findings.**
- **The dividend streak is TWO records, and Pentair says so itself**: DPS went $1.38 (2017)

  increased dividends, **as adjusted for the spin-off of nVent**."* A HON-class artifact,
  **disclosed rather than hidden**. And the post-2018 half is **the cleanest engine this
  queue has produced**: +5.50%/yr = earnings +10.68 (194%), retirement +0.49, **payout
  CONTRACTING -5.14** (34.5% -> 25.1% of net income).
- **The boom finding is the OPPOSITE of WGO's.** Pool units in 2025 are **31.5% BELOW
  2021**, so there is no boom volume left in the base to strip - and **2022 sits inside the
  window as a TROUGH** ($232.8M of owner earnings against $506.3M and $660.1M either side),
  dragging the five-year mean DOWN by ~$70M. **The bottom boundary is more conservative
  than the business.** What is boom-conditioned is margin, and it is price: of Pool's +5.0
  margin points since 2021, **+4.3 came from price net of inflation.**
- **A candor positive worth recording**: **Pentair publishes price versus volume at
  consolidated AND segment level every year** - better than COLM, RPM, CSL and ALG, and
  better than WTS, AOS and Fluidra, who publish none. It says: **volume index 78.8, price
  index 127.8 since 2021.**
- **The aftermarket argument was tested and defeated, on evidence**: Hayward claims
  "approximately 85%" aftermarket **and disclaims it as non-GAAP**; Fluidra's audited report
  says **60%**; **Pentair discloses nothing** (zero hits for aftermarket or installed base).
  And units cannot fall 25.2% in 2023 and 46.3% in Q2 2026 if demand is non-discretionary.
  The mechanism is Carlisle's exactly: **there is a warehouse between Pentair and the pool,
  and it is 18% of the company.**
- **ROIC including goodwill** (the ITW/CSL/HD metric): AOS 24.55% > WTS 16.43% > **PNR
  12.29%** > Fluidra 8.85% > Hayward 7.56%. PNR is **1st on TANGIBLE operating capital
  (62.1%)** - the entire gap is goodwill and intangibles at **67.1% of assets, highest in
  the row**, with negative $742.2M of tangible book.
- **Biggest concern, quoted**: *"Pentair does not know what its largest customer is holding,
  and that customer is 18% of the company."* One distributor's inventory decision removed
  **$170M of Pool sales and $105M of Pool segment income in ninety days** - 42.3% of segment
  revenue, 62.3% of segment income - **eleven weeks after guiding +1%**. The company's own
  remedy is to "enhance inventory visibility," an admission it had none.
- Q3 flags: adjusted EPS **+25.2% over GAAP** with half the CEO bonus on adjusted operating
  income; **six straight years of "one-time" restructuring, $364.4M including $129.6M of
  consultants**; **$725M of buybacks at ~$94, now 36% underwater**; a **$1.425bn acquisition
  announced in the same release as a 17% revenue miss**; and **seven executive-officer
  changes in fourteen months, including a CFO who lasted four months and left four days
  before the preannouncement.** No conduct matter; Q3 IN as an overlay.
- Yield **5.16% bottom boundary against a 5.22% sovereign**; expectancy 8.16% at 3% growth,
  1.84 points short; bands central **$40-55** against a $60.46 price. Note capex runs at
  **58% of D&A**, so here the D&A end is the CONSERVATIVE one - the inverse of the [E5-20]
  railroad case, tested and stated rather than assumed.
- Dividend covered **2.89x**, and **2.19x even in a combined bear case** (Pool margin to
  28.7% and tax normalised to 21%). Underwrite 5-7% growth, not the 8% just declared.

# SWEEP 3 - FIFTY NAMES NEVER EXAMINED (2026-09-01)

`Screens/new_candidates.py`, continuing the deterministic hash-of-CIK sweep past every
ticker in `Screens/*.csv` and every `Test Runs/* Run - *` filename. **2,200 filers examined
to find fifty priceable ones.** Output: `Screens/2026-09-01 NEW CANDIDATES.csv`.
**COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE** (operator rule 3). No verdict on any business below
exists until the six questions run.

Sovereign 5.18% (USD 30y). Floor 10% [E4-28]. Yields are the BOTTOM boundary of the four
owner-earnings constructions [E5-34]; "growth req" is the perpetual growth needed to reach
the floor; "spread" is the width across the four constructions, and **[E4-25] says the
width IS the finding.**

## DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: the financial screen was matching on NAMES

The exclusion list was a list of words - bank, bancorp, insurance, capital, mortgage. Three
of the six best-yielding names on this sweep are financials that carry none of those words:

| ticker | name | SIC | what it actually is |
|---|---|---|---|
| OPFI | OppFi Inc. | 6199 | subprime online lender, "44.40% yield" |
| ESNT | Essent Group Ltd. | 6351 | surety / mortgage insurance |
| FHB | FIRST HAWAIIAN, INC. | 6022 | state commercial bank |

**A name is not a classification.** The SEC assigns every filer an SIC code, and 6000-6799
is Finance, Insurance and Real Estate. `new_candidates.py` now reads the SIC off the
submissions endpoint and excludes on the code, not the title. The three names above are
struck. This is the same class of error as every other artifact this project has found:
**a proxy that worked on the names I had in mind, and failed silently on the ones I did
not.**

## TIER 1 - sent to full runs

| ticker | cap $M | OE bottom $M | yield | growth req | spread | why it earned 400k tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OTIS | 26,910 | 1,340 | 4.98% | 5.02% | **5%** | service portfolio on ~2.4M units; tightest large-cap estimate on the sweep |
| FCN | 4,169 | 174 | 4.17% | 5.83% | **3%** | tightest spread of all fifty; countercyclical restructuring segment |
| SHOE | 353 | 44 | **12.53%** | **-2.53%** | 48% | clears the floor on the bottom boundary with NO growth, which is the shape that should raise suspicion, not appetite |

## TIER 2 - triaged and NOT sent, with the reason

Year-by-year owner earnings, not the mean the screen reports, because a mean hides the
shape of its window [E4-41 normalize down for booms].

- **KBH (KB Home)** - the 0.39% growth-required figure is an artifact. **2023 owner
  earnings of $1,013M against a 2017-2022 mean of $192M.** That is not an earnings boom, it
  is a homebuilder's inventory unwinding into cash: land and work-in-progress released
  during a slowdown reads as operating cash flow. Recent-3 mean $514M vs earlier $192M.
  **Normalize down; the yield does not survive it.**
- **MGM Resorts** - recent-3 $1,396M vs earlier $216M, and capex runs **$1.0-1.9bn a year**
  against $2.4bn of OCF. A casino's maintenance capex is most of its capex. Spread **157%**,
  the widest on the sweep. Deep cyclical with a 2020 owner-earnings figure of **-$1,871M**.
- **MPLX** and **SUNC (Sunoco)** - both file partners' capital accounts. **K-1 structure**,
  and MPLX's owner earnings exclude distributions to non-controlling interests while its
  "boom signature" is mostly 2017-2019 buildout capex rolling off, not earnings rising.
  SUNC has only **three filed years**. Structural exclusion, not a price judgment.
- **AMTM (Amentum)** - owner earnings go $18M (2024) to $495M (2025). That is the Jacobs
  CMS merger, September 2024. **Perimeter mismatch**: the share-count guard passed it at
  1.005x because the company only has four years of filings and the merger predates the
  comparison window. The guard has a blind spot on recently-created filers, recorded here.
- **SW (Smurfit Westrock)** - same class: 2022-2023 are Smurfit Kappa alone, the Westrock
  combination closed July 2024. The "0% spread" is an artifact of too short a history, not
  a well-determined estimate.
- **KEX (Kirby)** - recent-3 $303M vs earlier $173M on inland barge rates at cycle highs;
  capex swings $98M to $402M, so (c) is genuinely unresolved between the two ends.
- **AYI (Acuity)** - **no boom signature**, and the only tier-2 name where the growth is
  real: $489M recent-3 against $316M earlier, built steadily. Needs 6.29% perpetual growth
  at a 35% spread. **The best of the deferred names; first in line if the price moves.**
- **NVEC (NVE Corp)** - owner earnings of **$12M, 15, 14, 16, 13, 12, 18, 18, 13, 14** across
  ten years. Flat as a table. A $475M cap on a business with **zero growth in a decade** that
  needs 6.81% perpetual growth to reach the floor. **The flatness is the finding**, and it
  closes the file on price without a read.

## THE SHAPE OF THE SWEEP

Of 2,200 filers examined, **1,606 were excluded before any price was computed** - 601
already seen, 301 financial by name, 214 with no XBRL facts, 211 with no resolvable owner
earnings, 230 stale or unpriced, 185 on the perimeter guard, 162 with no share count, 109
with stale share counts, **103 on capex-unresolved [E5-20]**, 21 regulated, 13 out of cap
band. **Ten of the fifty survivors need <=6% perpetual growth**, and three of those ten were
misclassified financials. **Seven real candidates out of 2,200 filers**, before a single
one of the six questions has been asked of any of them.

That ratio is the finding to keep. It is consistent with the 34 completed runs, where eight
businesses cleared every gate and **all eight failed on price** - a fact about the
opportunity set, not about the names.

# SWEEP 3, BATCH 2 - FIFTY MORE (2026-09-01)

Re-running the sweep with the SIC guard did not replace three names, it produced **fifty
entirely different ones**: `already_examined()` reads every `Screens/*.csv`, including the
sweep's own prior output, so the second pass continued past the first fifty. **2,733 filers
examined.** The SIC guard alone removed **171 financials that the word list had missed**,
across 26 distinct SIC codes. Both batches are preserved as `batch1.csv` and `batch2.csv`;
the script now numbers its output, because a fixed filename let the second run destroy the
first.

Boom-window test run on the eleven names needing <=6% growth, using `floor_screen`'s own
tag lists. **COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE.**

## The two that survived with a well-behaved series

- **LOPE (Grand Canyon Education)** - owner earnings **191, 105, 284, 279, 284, 186, 199,
  253, 239** across nine filed years. Recent-3 mean 230 against an earlier mean of 222.
  **No boom signature**, 6% spread, 5.92% bottom yield, 4.08% growth required. capex/D&A
  **1.74x**, so the CAPEX end is the conservative one here, the inverse of the [E3-44]
  default direction, which is stated rather than assumed. **Sent to a full run.** The
  stability is not a reason to like it: a well-determined estimate can be a well-determined
  estimate of a business awaiting a regulator's signature.
- **LSTR (Landstar)** - recent-3 **275** against an earlier mean of **276**, dead flat
  across an entire freight cycle that contains both the 2022 spike (584) and the current
  trough (209). Asset-light agent-and-owner-operator network, capex/D&A 0.43x. 4.09% yield,
  5.91% growth required. **Held in the queue behind LOPE**, not rejected.

## The nine that closed on the cheap test

- **SIG (Signet Jewelers)** - the 13.23% yield is not a boom artifact, it is a **DECAY**:
  owner earnings ran **1,687 (2018) to 431 recent-3 mean**, a 70%+ fall. The bottom boundary
  is roughly the current run rate, so the yield is arithmetically real and the business is
  melting underneath it. Mall jewellery against lab-grown diamond economics.
- **CE (Celanese)** - commodity chemicals, and the 81% spread is the **D&A/capex divergence
  from the DuPont M&M acquisition**: D&A 760 against capex 343, so most of the "earnings"
  gap is purchase-accounting amortisation. Commodity doctrine closes it.
- **APOG (Apogee)** - **BOOM**: recent-3 106 against an earlier 63, with a single 151 spike
  in 2024 on non-residential construction backlog. Normalizing down [E4-41] leaves ~10%,
  which is at the floor, not through it, on a cyclical with a 38% spread.
- **GPI (Group 1 Automotive)** - **DECAY** from a pandemic gross-margin-per-unit peak
  (1,088 in 2021 to 396 now), and capex/D&A **4.70x** because dealerships buy real estate.
- **AEO (American Eagle)** - boom by the test, and the trend WITHIN the recent three is
  **down: 355, 215, 156.** Apparel retail.
- **OPCH (Option Care Health)** - the "boom" is a merger integration ramp from the 2019
  BioScrip combination, and the recent trend is **299, 252, 177 - falling.**
- **WS (Worthington Steel)** - five filed years, spun 2023, commodity steel processing,
  decaying.
- **SEB (Seaboard)** - the **2,736% spread is the finding** [E4-25]. Capex has run at or
  above OCF for years: owner earnings of **8 and 6** in the last two years on a $3.9bn cap.
  The estimate is undetermined, which closes the file without a judgment about the business.
- **ESI (Element Solutions)** - a **data gap, not a business finding**: 2018 and 2019 are
  absent from XBRL entirely (the Platform Specialty reorganisation) and the series stops at
  2022. The 6,522% spread flagged it. Closed on data quality; **do not record a verdict on
  this business, none was reached.**

## FERG (Ferguson) - the one to revisit, and why not now

$42bn cap, 2% spread, 5.86% growth required, and a real scale-distribution argument. But
the CIK carries only **four filed years** after the US redomicile, its 2023 figure (2,231)
is the construction boom, and the recent number is 1,575. **A 2% spread across four years
is not a well-determined estimate, it is a short one.** The tight-spread signal that earned
OTIS and FCN their runs does not transfer to a name with too little history to spread.

## RUN FOLDED IN: SHOE (Shoe Station Group, formerly Shoe Carnival) - 2026-09-01, commit a0ea029

**Q1 IN. Q2 OUT. The file closes at Q2.** Q3, Q4 and Q5 not opened.

**The screen's number was arithmetically right and economically hollow.** $44.27M reproduced
exactly against the screen's $44M - and **FY2021 alone contributes $111.0M of the five-year
$221.3M sum**, on comps of **+35.3%**. Removing the stimulus year [E4-41] takes the
four-year bottom boundary to **$27.6M**, and the corrected yield to **7.4% on a $372.0M cap
against a 5.25% sovereign** - short of the [E4-28] floor. Trailing year alone: **5.2%**.
The 12.53% that put this name at the top of the sweep does not survive its own boom window.

**Q2 fails on the filing's own words**, which is the cleanest kind of failure available:
*"The retail footwear industry is highly competitive with few barriers to entry."* Nike 24%
plus Skechers 13% plus Crocs 9% is **46% of net sales on no long-term contract**, from
suppliers whose own risk factors say they are *"reducing the number of retailers with which
they are choosing to do business."* The substitute is not close, it is **the identical
shoe**. Competitor row: **no peer names this company as a competitor**, and five
independently describe the market as fragmented. [E3-03] criterion 2.

**My Stage 0 brief was wrong on two facts and the run corrected both.** There is **no Class
B** - one class, and the cap counts every share. And it is **not a controlled company**: the
Weavers hold 31.5%, insiders 33.6%, and the term appears nowhere in the proxy. I had
carried both forward from Shoe Carnival's older structure. Continuity is clean (CIK 895447,
file number 0-21360, same CUSIP, renamed 2026-06-12). Not a HON-class perimeter artifact.

**(c) as a disclosed judgment, and a refusal worth recording**: ten-year cumulative capex
**$322.6M against D&A of $238.6M, +35%** on a flat fleet, so (c) is judged **up from D&A to
~$32.3M** but not all the way to total capex, because $37.1M of FY2025's capex was the
abandoned rebanner. **[E5-20]'s capital-intensive exception was explicitly REFUSED** here on
evidence rather than assumed, since this filer runs capex below depreciation for years. The
resulting range **$19.3M to $65.6M is a factor of 3.4, too wide to conclude [E4-25]** - which
is why Q4 would have been UNKNOWABLE had the file reached it.

Operating leases checked and **OCF is not distorted**: the ASC 842 add-back of +$57.6M
against a cash payment of -$60.2M nets to a **$2.6M drag**.

**The strongest disconfirming fact, and the answer to "what does the market see that the
screen does not":** on 2025-11-13 the company renamed itself for a multi-year single-banner
strategy, quoting *"Shoe Station is winning - growing comps, expanding margins,"* $20M of
savings and >90% fleet conversion by FY2028. On **2026-05-21 it withdrew the strategy
entirely** - *"we are no longer pursuing a single-banner Shoe Station strategy"* - took $8.3M
of impairments, and disclosed that **Shoe Station's own comps were -2.9%, a worse decline
than the banner it was meant to replace.** Twenty days later shareholders adopted the name
anyway. Cost: $37.1M of capex, $24.1M of operating income, $5.3M of CEO severance.
**[E3-48] projections flag, [E2-30] imperative and the [E5-30] ratchet in one sequence.**
That is what the 52-week low is pricing, and the screen could not see any of it.

## RUN FOLDED IN: FCN (FTI Consulting) - 2026-09-01

**Q1 IN. Q2 OUT. The file closes at Q2, permanently.** *"This is a business verdict, not a
price verdict. It is permanent under the four-verdict table and no price re-opens it."*

The tightest owner-earnings spread of all hundred names, 3%, bought a well-determined
estimate of a business with no moat. **[E4-04]: *"A moat that must be continuously rebuilt
will eventually be no moat at all"*, and [E4-23]: *"the partnership's moat will go when the
surgeon goes."***

**The number that settles it: retention grants went $104.0M to $296.7M in a single year,
which is 110% of net income.** That is FTI's published market price for keeping the asset,
and the asset walks. The run's own sentence on the high return on capital is the one to
keep: **the return is high because there is almost no capital, not because competitors
cannot match it.** *"A return on capital measured against a balance sheet that excludes the
only asset that matters is measuring the wrong thing."*

**[E4-32] direction, which outranks existence, is NARROWING on every measure FTI
publishes**: utilisation down 6, 7 and 10 points since 2018; operating margin 13.0% (2019)
to 10.3% (2025); Economic Consulting operating income down 82.9% from peak; billable
headcount down 3.2%; operating cash flow down 61.5%; and **Q2 2026 EPS of $1.99 against
$2.13 a year earlier despite retiring 23% of the shares.** Widening on one axis only: bill
rates, every segment, every year since 2021.

**[E4-36] cause of extreme success: wave-riding [E3-51], twice** - the 2008-09 default cycle
and the 2020 COVID cycle. *"when a surfer gets up and catches the wave ... he can go a long,
long time. But if he gets off the wave, he becomes mired in shallows."* **FTI got off the
2009 wave and lost money in 2012 and 2013.** The advantage lives in the credit cycle and the
litigation cycle, not in FTI.

Untapped pricing power [E5-28] explicitly **NOT CLAIMED**, since claiming that class is
claiming near-monopoly and FTI's own Item 1 names *"independent contractors"* among its
competitors.

## RUN FOLDED IN: LOPE (Grand Canyon Education) - 2026-09-01

**Q1 IN. Q2 IN. Q3 IN. Q4 IN. Q6 IN. THE NINTH BUSINESS TO CLEAR EVERY GATE - and, like
the eight before it, IT FAILS ON PRICE.** The pattern is now nine for nine.

**Q5, and the floor is missed everywhere in the range on all six constructions.** Bottom
boundary owner earnings **$205.6M on a $3,861.0M cap = 5.32%**; top of range 6.01%; sovereign
**5.22%** (DGS30, 2026-08-28). Net-cash variant disclosed but not headlined at 5.73% to
6.47%, *"because it moves the answer by four tenths of a point and a reader is entitled to
it."* **Expectancy 8.32% to 9.01% against the [E4-28] 10% floor. Points over the sovereign
at the quote: +0.10 to +0.79.**

**The two growth readings disagree violently and the run published both rather than picking
one**: owner earnings **+0.81%/yr over 2019-2025** against **+9.17%/yr over 2022-2025**. The
entire difference is **operating margin, which fell from 34.05% to 27.20%** as the
physically-intensive off-campus site business grew from nothing to **47 locations**.
Enrolments compounded at 4-7% throughout and revenue at 6% throughout; owner earnings did
not. The short window starts at the 2022 trough and recovers that margin loss once; the long
window contains all of it.

**The price requires 4.68% perpetual growth from the bottom boundary.** Underwriting it means
believing one of three things, and the run tested each: **(a) plausible on three years and
not on six; (b) contradicted by the filings** - the 60% take rate has been cut at least three
times, most recently by $20 million a year effective this July; **(c) possible and
undemonstrated.**

**The run underwrote 3.0% and declared WINDAGE COUNT: ONE.** Central value **$110 to $130**,
conservative **$80 to $110**, optimistic $145 to $180 requiring 4-5% forever. **Price $148.13
at the run, $150.09 today - above the whole conservative and central range and inside the
optimistic case only, sitting almost exactly on the 4%-growth line.**

**[E3-42] certainty spread NOT APPLIED**, and the run says why: *"It may look mathematical.
But it's mathematical gibberish."* No risk premium was added to the rate for the regulatory
exposure. Certainty is priced exactly twice, at the understanding gate and in the discount
demanded at the end, **and is not stacked.**

**THE NAMED WAY IT DIES IS A SIGNATURE, NOT A NUMBER**: any published change, proposal or
judicial ruling affecting **Example 2-B of the 2011 bundled-services Dear Colleague Letter**,
which is what makes tuition revenue-sharing lawful. A Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, a Dear
Colleague revision, or an adverse ruling is **an immediate full re-run regardless of price**.

**Bands armed**: LOPE 130 (re-run) and 110 (floor met at the underwritten 3%). Added to the
daily fetch watch, which now covers nine cleared businesses.

## RUN FOLDED IN: OTIS (Otis Worldwide) - 2026-09-01, commits ba90619 / 767ecfe

**Q1 IN. Q2 IN (NARROW, direction NARROWING). Q3 IN. Q4 IN. Q5 below the floor, NOT RANKED.
Q6 IN.** 1,655 lines, 116 ledger ids, zero phantom citations. **The TENTH business to clear
every gate and the tenth to fail on price.**

**(c) AS A DISCLOSED JUDGMENT, AND THE DIRECTION WAS TESTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** (c) =
D&A at **$189M**, and **D&A exceeds capex in 5 of 5 years** (mean $189M against $137M), so
**at Otis the D&A end is the CONSERVATIVE end - the inverse of [E5-20]'s railroad case.** It
is the larger subtraction by $51M a year. This is now the third name where the direction of
the [E3-44] default had to be established from the filings rather than inherited (PNR and
SHOE were the others), and it is worth making a habit of.

**The refusal that cost $70M a year, and it is where the windage was spent.** The plant half
is genuinely light: $743M of net fixed assets on $14.4bn of sales, capex 1.1%. But Note 7
shows **$2,133M of purchased service portfolios gross, 85% already amortised and 96% of the
gross intangible.** That amortisation is a real renewal charge, so **the flattering
depreciation-only construction was refused.** Judged owner earnings **$1,257M**, band $1,185M
to $1,308M, width 9.8%. The acquisition-inclusive $1,185M is published as the bottom boundary
[E5-34] because **Otis does not disclose how portfolio additions split between conversion,
recapture and acquisition.**

**Two things the screen could not see.** About **$104M a year leaks to noncontrolling holders
of Otis China** (operating cash flow is consolidated while NCI dividends sit in financing),
and the screen never asked what (c) has to buy. The screen's own $1,340M and 4.98%
reproduced exactly, and were still wrong about the business.

**Q5: 4.68% against a 5.25% sovereign (US Treasury, 2026-08-31) is MINUS 0.57 points.** The
quote needs **5.32% perpetual growth** against an actual record of **+0.20%/yr over seven
years and MINUS 2.47%/yr over four.** At the floor on 0-3% growth the business is worth
roughly **$31 to $49**; as a bond substitute at 5.25% with no growth, roughly **$59 to $65**.
**Price $70.58 is 171% of the floor-clearing value at 2% growth.** Screamer test with no
margin added: above the whole range. **Position size zero.**

**Strongest disconfirming fact, and it is a clean [E2-49].** The 2025 short-term incentive
scorecard in the DEF 14A of 2026-04-17: **Net Portfolio Unit Gain, threshold 88 thousand
units, target 97 thousand, actual 87 thousand, payout ZERO** - after which the metric
**vanished from the FY2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 earnings releases**, having run for four
consecutive quarters as a headline bullet (*"Maintenance portfolio units up 4%"*). Scored
both ways by the run: the metric remains in the comp plan and the count remains in the 10-K,
so it is **a dated candor debit rather than concealment.**

**MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ON TWO PREMISES AND THE RUN CORRECTED BOTH.** The negative equity is not
an operating hole: it traces to one filed line, *"Net transfers to UTC and Separation-related
transactions | (6,150)"*, plus $4,198M of treasury stock, and the accumulated deficit has
**narrowed from -$3,106M to -$440M.** And **the retention rate I told the agent to verify
does not exist in any Otis filing** - KONE publishes ~90% and TKE over 90%, Otis publishes
nothing. I had asserted high retention as the franchise claim; the company does not disclose
it. **[E2-60] fires anyway: 108.9% of attributable owner earnings distributed over five
years, and $700M borrowed against $807M repurchased in H1 2026.**

**Bands armed**: OTIS 59 (the top of the bond-substitute range, where it stops being worse
than a Treasury at zero growth) and 49 (the top of the floor-clearing range).

## RUN FOLDED IN: LSTR (Landstar System) - 2026-09-01, commit dd8931f

**Q1 IN. Q2 IN (NARROW, NARROWING, the thinnest Q2 pass in the queue, with a pre-committed
downgrade trigger). Q3 IN. Q4 IN. Q5 NOT RANKED. Q6 IN.** 1,597 lines, 115 ledger ids, zero
phantom. **The ELEVENTH business to clear every gate and the eleventh to fail on price.**

**THE SCREEN'S (c) WAS WRONG, AND THE RUN CAUGHT IT.** Landstar buys most of its trailers
with **finance leases**, which never touch investing cash flow, so the cash capex line misses
about **$33M a year.** Total capital acquired averaged **$53.9M over nine years against
depreciation of $49.2M: a ratio of 1.10x, not the 0.43x I put in the brief.** Six filed items
bound the guess, including the company's own FY2026 plan of **$104M of trailing equipment
*"primarily to replace older trailing equipment"*** and a **17.9-year implied life on a fleet
whose stated life is 7 to 10 years.** (c) judged at **$75M, band $54M to $119M.** See
`Test Runs/ADDENDUM 2026-09-01 - finance-lease additions omitted from (c)...` for the tool fix
and for the two cleared names it reaches.

**Four windows published rather than one**: 3-year $178-243M, 5-year $231-296M, 7-year
$204-269M, 9-year $178-243M. Combined **$175M to $295M**, bottom boundary **$178M.** Yield
**2.90% to 4.84% against a 5.22% sovereign - below the bond everywhere.**

**Value roughly $70 to $116 a share against a quote of $180.63.** The price implies **5.2% to
7.1% perpetual growth** against a realised record of **+0.20% a year in loads and MINUS 5.78%
a year in operating income** over eight years. **The nine-year decomposition is the whole
story: price +5.77%/yr, EPS MINUS 1.00%/yr, shares -2.44%/yr, multiple 26.4x to 46.8x. All of
the gain is multiple.** That is the decomposition that has now overturned the compounder label
on eleven of fourteen names.

**THE SINGLE STRONGEST DISCONFIRMING FACT, and it is the best competitor row this project has
produced.** Return on unleveraged net tangible operating assets, **same formula both sides,
same three years, same freight cycle**: **Landstar 61.0% to 40.7% to 27.0%. C.H. Robinson
42.1% to 50.2% to 62.7%. THEY CROSSED.** Robinson gained 20.6 points while Landstar lost 34.0,
and the mechanism is on both records: **Robinson cut average headcount 11.5% then 10.3% while
raising its spread 200bp** on what it calls dynamic pricing and costing capabilities;
**Landstar's SG&A ROSE $12.8M on falling revenue, because its cost sits in 960 agencies it
does not own.** The agent network is the moat in the story and the rigidity in the numbers.

**THE TROUGH FRAMING REVERSES, which is the finding I most wanted tested and least expected.**
I warned the agent that "it's just the cycle" is where an analyst who wants to like a name
finds his reason [operator rule 9]. It ran the test and found the opposite of a hidden trough:
**2023-25 released $92.9M of working capital and claim accruals INTO the cash figure the
screen used.** The recent years are flattered, not depressed.

**And the erosion thesis was tested and REFUTED**: Landstar's spread has **not** structurally
compressed. A two-parameter BCO-mix model explains nine years to within **55bp**. But the
cause of the mix shift is not benign: **the BCO fleet is 28% below peak and 12% below 2017.**

**Q3, and it is a candour finding that cuts both ways**: **eleven consecutive years of net
unfavourable claims development, $117.9M, not one favourable year.** Published every year,
which is the candour pole; one-directional for eleven years, which is the systemic bias.
**Two corrections to my brief**: the supply-chain fraud was identified in **Q1 2025, not 2024**,
and it **inflated revenue and purchased transportation equally** by about 2% of FY2024,
roughly a third of the air-and-ocean line, and was **disclosed promptly and completely.**

**Bands armed**: LSTR 116 (top of the value range) and 90.

# WATCHLIST TRIAGE - the operator's Stocks lists, 2026-09-01

Fifteen screenshots, two named lists ("My Symbols" and "Mini Berk"). ETFs, index funds and
crypto excluded by name at the operator's instruction. **151 businesses put through the same
pipeline as the sweep: classify, guard, price. 89 priced. 23 need <=6% perpetual growth; 16
of those are new, non-financial and unrun.** Output `Screens/2026-09-01 WATCHLIST TRIAGE.csv`.
**COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE.**

**Operator call, 2026-09-01**: the Mini Berk names (L, WTM, MKL, BRK-A/B, HHH, GHC, BAM, BN)
are **PRICED AND FLAGGED, not run.** The financial exclusion stays in force for full runs.
Worth recording that the framework built from Berkshire's corpus was screening Berkshire out
as SIC 6331 until this pass.

## FOUR DEFECTS THE WATCHLIST EXPOSED, ALL FIXED

1. **A BROKEN CAP PRINTED AS A FINDING.** Hamilton Beach came back at **a market cap of ZERO
   and a yield of 854,301%**, because the share count did not resolve and nothing checked the
   quotient. There is now a sanity guard: a yield outside -100% to +50%, or a cap under $5M,
   is **a broken input and never a finding**. It immediately caught four more - **BRK-B at a
   $473M cap and a 4,683% yield** (a share-class artifact, Stage 0 item (a)), plus LCID, SOUN
   and BIRD.
2. **ELEVEN REAL BUSINESSES WERE DISCARDED BY A FORM CODE.** Toyota, Sony, Honda, TSMC, ASML,
   UMC, Ericsson, Spotify, Stellantis, GlobalFoundries and Mercedes file **20-F, not 10-K**,
   and `annual()` read that as *zero filed years*. Now accepts 20-F and 40-F and reads the
   **ifrs-full** namespace alongside us-gaap. Those statements deserve to be READ differently;
   that is not the same as being invisible.
3. **"No share count" on five large current filers** - META, Graham Holdings, DoorDash, UiPath,
   PubMatic - because the dei cover-page element is absent or stale. Added
   `shares_outstanding()` with a balance-sheet fallback.

   labelled "fund/ETF."** They are unsponsored ADRs and non-reporting OTC quotes with **no SEC
   filings at all** - a real limit, but a different one, and the label now says so.
