## RUN FOLDED IN: BBWI (Bath & Body Works) - 2026-09-01, commit 485a2e6

**Q1 IN. Q2 OUT. The file closes at Q2.** 82 ledger ids, zero phantoms.

**THE PERIMETER WAS MIXED, AND THE RUN PROVED IT FROM THE FILED STATEMENT.** Bath & Body
Works **restated its income statement** for the Victoria's Secret separation **and did not
restate its cash-flow statement.** Its own FY2021 10-K (accession `0000701985-22-000009`)
prints the footnote directly under the statement: *"The cash flows related to discontinued
operations have not been segregated. Accordingly, the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows
include the results of continuing and discontinued operations."* **Victoria's Secret appears
by name inside the operating section** (*"Impairment of Victoria's Secret Goodwill 720"*).

The tag history proves it twice: revenue for FY2019 was restated **12,914 to 5,405** and
FY2020 **11,847 to 6,434**, while OCF of 1,236 and 2,039 is **identical in every accession
before and after**. **Five of the nine years are L Brands, not BBWI.**

**BOTH MY PERIMETER GUARDS WERE STRUCTURALLY BLIND, AND THE RUN DIAGNOSED WHY.**
`share_count_shift()` **can never detect a spin-off**: the parent distributes shares in the
SPUN entity and its own count is unchanged. `scale_shift()` was reading the series that had
**already been restated**, so it saw a smooth history and no step at all. The correct test is
**cross-accession comparison of the same period end**, which would have fired at 58%. Now
built as `restatement_shift()`; it fires on BBWI at 2.39x and on **nothing else across 28
tested names.**

**But note what the break did and did not do.** My 689 IS genuinely post-separation
(613+620+834 over three clean years). The "earlier mean of 942" I briefed was **not a BBWI
number at all.** So the contamination **did not inflate the yield - it fabricated a decline
and hid that the usable record is only four years long.**

**Q2 fails on the company's own Competition section** (*"highly competitive... numerous
competitors"*) and on the physical series [E4-55]: **sales per square foot $1,120, $1,074,
$1,041, $1,026 across four years while square footage grew every year.** Tariffs absorbed
rather than passed on with demand flat [E4-37, E2-44]. A store base its own 10-K calls
*"vulnerable"*, replaced at ~$140M a year, which **buys a replacement rather than defending
the same advantage** [E4-04]. Amazon launched the category in February 2026. And **e.l.f.
answers [E2-45]'s attacker test from inside the competitor row: +47.6%, +76.9%, +28.3%,
+24.6% on $22M of capex and no stores.** Victoria's Secret, the sibling, now grows faster.

**(c) as a disclosed judgment, at the total-capex end**: the $140M of *"new off-mall stores
and remodels"* is **maintenance** under [E2-23], because **62 mall stores were closed to open
94**, and the outcome test agrees - **$237M spent and revenue fell.** Owner earnings on the
clean perimeter only: **$659M to $712M.** ASC 842 checked, $7M net drag, same class as SHOE's
$2.6M.

**Strongest disconfirming fact.** Management's own FY2026 forecast of **$890M operating cash
flow contains $88M of interchange-litigation settlement and $85M of IEEPA tariff refunds** -
both cash, both non-recurring, both named by the company. Strip them [E4-41] and normalised
owner earnings are **about $438M, roughly half FY2025's $834M and 37% below the four-year mean
the yield was built on.** The best clean year also carries a **+$113M accounts-payable
release** the MD&A attributes to *"efforts to improve working capital"*, against **-$93M and
-$82M** in the two prior years.

**AND THE THING THAT BREAKS THE PATTERN: BBWI DID NOT FAIL ON PRICE.** It yields **11.28% even
normalised**, clearing the [E4-28] floor, and [E2-54] coverage passes at 2.9x to 4.3x with no
maturity wall and no springing covenant in force. **It failed on the business.** My leverage
hypothesis was confirmed arithmetically rather than assumed: **equity is 60% of enterprise
value, so the equity yield is geared 1.66x, and OE/EV including leases is 5.8% against a
5.27% sovereign.** The eleven-for-eleven price-failure record survives only because this file
closed at Q2 and never reached Q5.

## A THIRD SCREEN DEFECT, FOUND BY THE SAME RUN AND MEASURED ACROSS EVERYTHING

`DA_TAGS` omitted the bare **`Depreciation`** element, which is what BBWI tags
post-separation, so its D&A series stopped at the last contaminated year. Fixing that led to
a worse one: **`annual()` stops at the FIRST tag that resolves, and for McDonald's that is
`DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization` at $457M - a SUBCOMPONENT. The real charge is $2,199M.**

Total D&A is one add-back line; a subcomponent is by construction smaller. `da_annual()` now
takes the **largest** resolving element, which is both more correct and fails safe, since the
bottom boundary is a min() across constructions [E5-34] either way.

**What it was corrupting is the SPREAD, and the spread decides which names earn a 400k-token
read** [E4-25: the range width IS the finding]. **12 of 89 priced names had a materially wrong
width, and the error ran almost entirely one way - toward looking BETTER determined than they
are:**

| ticker | reported | actual |
|---|---|---|
| **MSFT** | 10% | **174%** |
| **WMT** | 5% | **127%** |
| **TXN** | 124% | **312%** |
| **CRM** | 44% | **152%** |
| **GOOGL** | 2% | **94%** |
| MCD | 46% | 20% *(the only one that narrowed)* |

**Checked and stated plainly: none of the seven names run today (SHOE, FCN, LOPE, OTIS, LSTR,
BBWI, GIS) appears in that list, so no full run was misdirected by it.** It was close. The
tight-spread signal that earned OTIS its 5% and FCN its 3% is the same signal that read
Walmart at 5%.

## SCREEN DEFECT: STAGE 0(a) WAS NEVER PERFORMED, AND IT CANNOT BE FIXED BY ARITHMETIC

The framework has always required the cap **across all share classes**. The screen never did
it. Ford is the second casualty after **BRK-B, which came back at a $473M cap and a 4,683%
yield** from the same defect.

**AND THE SEC DATA CANNOT FIX IT.** `companyfacts` **STRIPS DIMENSIONS**, so per-class counts
are simply absent: Ford's us-gaap share tags stop in **2009**, Berkshire's dei count stops in
**2011**, and Under Armour, Lennar and McCormick report **no dei count at all.** There is no
sum to take.

So `share_class_flag()` returns **a prompt to read, not a number** - operator rule 8: *every
flag is a prompt to read, never a score*. Across the 379 priced names it separates three
things:
- **Multiple COMMON classes, cap under-counted**: CUBB, BELFB, BRK-A, MSA, IA, SO, SENEA, DUK,
  GS, FCEL, NXH, GOOGL.
- **Senior claims listed ahead of common**, which the market cap does not see and which owner
  earnings accrue to first: **F** (F-PB, F-PC, F-PD), MNSB, MPLX.
- **Warrants**, dilution the share count does not carry: OXY, RGTI, SLDP and others.

**Its limit is stated rather than hidden: it catches only classes that are separately LISTED.
Ford's Class B is not publicly traded and would never appear in this test.** Only Stage 0,
performed by hand inside a run, will ever find that one. Which is exactly what happened.

## QUERY RESOLVED: the OXY SBC claim was a back-solve, and the screen was right

Recorded 2026-09-02, addendum commit `3a93421`. **Verdict: (a) - the agent's own intermediate
working, published as if it were a read figure. NO DEFECT IN THE SCREEN, no tool fix required.**

The agent had the nine-year series as an output but not its construction, so it **back-solved
on an assumed TWO-term deduction** (cash capex plus SBC) and labelled the residual "SBC":
`10,532 - 6,427 - 3,476 = 629`. But `floor_screen.py` builds owner earnings on **THREE** terms,
and `capital_acquired()` is cash capex **plus finance-lease additions**. The decomposition ties
exactly:

| FY | back-solved residual | filed SBC | finance-lease additions | sum |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 629 | 234 | 395 | **629, exact** |
| 2024 | 423 | 213 | 195 | 408 |
| 2023 | 443 | 203 | 226 | 429 |

The ~$15M residuals in 2023-24 are a capex-vintage difference from the **OxyChem discontinued-
operations restatement**, not SBC.

**THE PART WORTH KEEPING IS THE AGENT'S OWN DIAGNOSIS**: the finance-lease term is *exactly*
what this project added to `capital_acquired()` in the addendum of 2026-09-01 after COST and
HD. **So the reported "defect" was a correction this project had already published, mistaken
for a mislabelled input because the agent did not read the tool it was auditing.** Its rule,
which is worth adopting: **operator rule 8 says tools may not conclude, and it follows that a
back-solve against a tool is not a reading of the tool.** Rule 4's discipline, applied to our
own code.

**And one real finding survives: OXY is a substantial member of the class that addendum
identified.** Finance-lease additions ran **$226M, $195M, $395M** across 2023-25 - **6.1% of
cash capex in 2025 and rising**, above the 5% line used to size the population. It mildly
strengthens the direction (c) was already set in: $395M a year of capital acquired outside the
cash capex line is $395M the $5,700M volume-flat anchor did not contain.

**The SBC row of the OXY self-audit's corrections table is WITHDRAWN. That table now has three
valid rows, not four.** The capex/D&A (0.85x) and dividend ($0.79 to $0.01) corrections stand
and were separately verified.

### PLAB competitor row, second pass - four additions, one of which REVISES a published number

**1. THE ROE COMPARISON I RECORDED IS NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE, AND THE CORRECTION CUTS AGAINST
PHOTRONICS.** Noncontrolling interests are **USD 423.7M of USD 1,597.3M of total equity - 27%**
(DNP's 49.99% of PDMCX plus the Taiwan partners). **Photronics' ROE is struck on the PARENT

## THREE TOOL DEFECTS FIXED, ALL THREE FOUND BY RUNS RATHER THAN BY ME

**1. THE STALENESS GUARD WAS DEFEATED BY ITS OWN FALLBACK, AND IT REACHED 19 NAMES.**
`shares_outstanding()` has a 550-day guard; the master-queue script then wrote
`F.shares_outstanding(f) or M.shares_asof(f, TODAY)`, and **the `or` handed control to an
UNGUARDED path whenever the guard fired.** Measured across the 379 priced names: **19 used a
share count older than 550 days, several over 15 years old, and NOT ONE has a fresh
alternative.**

| ticker | as-of | age | reported yield |
|---|---|---|---|
| HUBG | 2010-10-21 | 15.9 yrs | 4.19% |
| MA | 2010-10-27 | 15.9 yrs | 1.61% |
| **DKS** | 2011-01-29 | 15.6 yrs | **4.27%** |
| **F** | 2011-04-28 | 15.4 yrs | **10.01%** |
| BRK-A | 2011-04-29 | 15.4 yrs | 3.13% |
| **NKE** | 2015-07-17 | 11.1 yrs | **4.66%** |
| **PINS** | 2019-03-31 | 7.4 yrs | **4.98%** |

**DKS and PINS are in the live tier-1 queue and their yields are unreliable.** F and NKE were
both caught independently by their own runs. The fallback is removed; a name whose share count
cannot be trusted is now returned **unpriced**, not priced on a fifteen-year-old number.

**2. THE BOOM DETECTOR IS BLIND TO A STEP CHANGE AT ITS WINDOW BOUNDARY** - Nike's diagnosis,
and it generalises. A recent-3-mean-versus-earlier-mean test catches a spike *inside* a window
and cannot see a level change *at its edge*. `level_shift()` added. **It correctly fires on
SIG (0.46, step down) and on the AEO/COST/QCOM step-ups.**

**3. AND IT DOES NOT CATCH NIKE, WHICH IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.** Nike reads 0.88, "no
step", because its problem is a third thing again: **ten constructions clustered inside a 17%
width ONLY BECAUSE EVERY WINDOW FROM THREE YEARS UP CONTAINED FY2024, the best of nine. The
first window excluding it drops 43%.** So `best_year_dependence()` was added - a leave-one-out
on the maximum. **It catches Nike at 16%** while confirming that OTIS (2%), LOPE (6%), Apple
(3%) and KLAC (3%) are genuinely well-determined, **so the tight-spread signal that earned OTIS
and FCN their runs survives the cross-check.**

**The general lesson, now written into the tool**: [E4-25] says the range width IS the finding.
The corollary is **check WHY a range is narrow before treating narrowness as knowledge.**

## RUN FOLDED IN: DG (Dollar General) - 2026-09-02, 1,403 lines plus two research files

**Q1 IN. Q2 OUT. FAIL, closed at Q2.** 97+5+21 ledger ids across three files, zero phantoms.
For the record: Q3 would have been IN narrowly; **Q4 would have been OUT, gruesome [E4-20].**
**PRICE (COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE): about $110-130 conservative, $145 judged, $165-170
generous, per share at zero growth, against a $131.09 quote.** Yield 4.55% to 6.86%, judged
5.89%. The screen reproduces exactly.

**THE 8x RANGE IS A WORKING-CAPITAL ROUNDTRIP, AND THE HEADLINE SERIES POINTS AT THE WRONG
YEAR.** Ex-working-capital the range is **2.41x, not 7.91x**. Fiscal 2022's $351M trough was a
**$1,920M inventory absorption on top of a still-peak year - ex-WC it was the BEST year in the
series at $2,271M.** The real collapse is **fiscal 2023-24 (ex-WC $941M and $1,003M, MINUS
58%)**, where the reported series gives no signal at all. And fiscal 2025's $2,302M is
flattered by **$614M of working-capital release plus $199M of tax timing, with the Q2 10-Q
already showing $318M reversing.** Working capital net-absorbed **$130M a year over eight
years**, which stays inside owner earnings per [E2-23]. **Determinable, so not UNKNOWABLE.**

**THE BEST PIECE OF TEST-CRAFT IN THE BATCH: THE PHYSICAL SERIES, DEFLATED.** The run applied
the BBWI sales-per-square-foot test, **reported the negative as the AEO run had cautioned** -
nominal $273 to $270 with a recovery to $273 TTM, no decline - **and then ran it in REAL terms
against CPI-U: $273 to $217, five straight declines, now 9-10% below 2017.** The nominal test
is the one that failed twice in this project. The deflated test is the one that works, and it
is now available to every retail run that follows.

**SHRINK, IN DOLLARS FROM THE SEGMENT NOTE**: $910.7M, $928.9M, **$634.3M** (2.35%, 2.29%,
**1.48%** of sales), with excess cost of **$336M and $326M of pretax profit** in 2023-24.
Self-inflicted in magnitude - self-checkout across ~9,000 stores, store-manager turnover, a
$1.7bn over-build - **structural in its 1.48% floor.**

**(c) = ABOUT 80% OF TOTAL CAPEX, and this is the OPPOSITE ruling to Kroger with the reason
stated.** New stores are only **16-24% of capex (16.4% last year)**, and **FY2026 guides capex
UP 13-21% while cutting openings 22%**, with about 11% of the budget on new stores; 20.6% of
the estate is remodelled annually. **Kroger's estate SHRANK, so its D&A end was invalid; DG's
GREW, so the split had to be measured rather than assumed - and DG publishes it.** Range
$1,316M to $1,985M, judged $1,703M. ASC 842 checked: **$20M drag, 0.55% of OCF, not
distorted** - but $11,138M of lease present value, **2.4x funded debt.**

**Q2 OUT ON NINE YEARS OF ARITHMETIC**: **+56.9% stores, +94.3% sales, $10.1bn of capex,
$11.1bn of leases - and pretax income UNCHANGED, $1,965.6M to $1,964.6M. The return on the
last $5.9bn of employed capital is NEGATIVE.** Same 5.2% operating margin as Walmart US at
**39% of its square-foot productivity**, while Walmart beat DG's comps three years running
from a **flat** store base.

**Strongest disconfirming fact, and it is substantial: the market is already pricing DG to
shrink.** The quote implies **MINUS 8.6% to MINUS 16.9% year-one owner-earnings growth**
against a business that just grew operating profit 28.6%, comped +3.0% **with positive traffic
and positive units**, cut shrink $294.6M, and beat then raised guidance. At 3% growth it pays
**2.0 to 4.4 points over the bond.** And genuinely in DG's favour: **Dollar Tree wrote off
$6.34bn on Family Dollar and sold it for about $434M net on 2025-07-05. [E2-45]'s attacker
test was run by the best possible attacker, and the attacker failed.**

**Q3 flags that converge**: a published **10%+ EPS / 6-7% margin** five-year framework, with
pay run on adjusted EBIT (70% of bonus) and adjusted EBITDA plus adjusted ROIC (PSUs),
**paying 182.4% and 200% of target in a year pretax income finished level with fiscal 2016.**
Public reporting is pure GAAP - zero occurrences of "EBITDA" in any 10-K - **credited before
the flag was used.** **OSHA appears in DG's filings ONLY inside an outside proponent's
shareholder proposal**: the $12M corporate-wide settlement and the Severe Violator designation
are absent from every 10-K and 10-Q. **[E5-22] passes on action; [E2-26] fails on disclosure.**
And **$7,764M of buybacks at about $215.7 average against $131 today**, with the 2023-25 pause
**contractually required** by the March 2025 Covenant Relief Period, not chosen.

## THE WATCHLIST STANDING COUNT AFTER TEN RUNS
**Ten businesses from the operator's lists have been run and ALL TEN FAIL, every one
reporting a price.** GM, F, OXY, PLAB, KR, AEO, NKE, DG, QCOM, ULTA.
**Ten of ten closed at Q2** - none reached a price failure at Q5, which is a different
result from the earlier 28 runs, where seven cleared every gate and died on price.

**Stated plainly because it cuts against the framework's own comfort:** the earlier finding
was *"the price is the binding constraint."* On the operator's watchlist it is not. These
ten are businesses selected by a person watching the market, and **the constraint that
binds them is [E3-03] - the franchise question - not the floor.** Two different populations,
two different failure modes, and the framework should not be allowed to claim it predicted
both. **[E4-26]: hunt disconfirming evidence hardest for your favourite hypothesis.**

# THE WATCHLIST STANDING COUNT AFTER THIRTEEN RUNS
**Thirteen businesses from the operator's lists are run. ALL THIRTEEN FAIL. ALL THIRTEEN
CLOSE AT Q2.** GM · F · OXY · PLAB · KR · AEO · NKE · DG · QCOM · ULTA · AATC · UAL · DKS.
Every one reported a price, as the output contract requires.

**Thirteen for thirteen at the same gate is now a strong enough result to be suspicious of,
and it is stated that way on purpose [E4-26].** Two readings compete and the evidence does
not yet separate them:

1. **The population.** These are names selected by a person watching a market, and what
   makes a business watchable — brand, scale, familiarity — is not what makes it a franchise.
   The earlier 28 runs drew from dividend screens and produced a different failure mode
   entirely: seven cleared every gate and died on price.
2. **The reader.** Ten consecutive Q2 OUTs create an expectation, and I write the briefs. The
   countermeasure is on the record rather than merely intended: **every brief since NKE has
   carried an explicit instruction to argue against me**, and the runs have used it — DKS
   states outright that a single 8-K sentence was the difference between OUT and NARROW→Q3,
   AATC put Econolite's seven renewals first, and UAL recorded that United beats its industry
   on nearly every measure it ran.

**The distinguishing test is available and cheap: the Mini Berk track is now unblocked and it
is a differently-selected population.** If float-bearing holding companies also close at Q2 at
this rate, reading 1 weakens. **AATC is the early evidence for reading 1** — the first name in
the whole queue whose yield clears the sovereign on *every* construction, which failed at Q2
anyway, and which nobody would call a watchlist favourite.

# THE MINI BERK TRACK AND ORLY — 2026-09-02. THE STREAK BROKE.

**Seventeen watchlist runs now stand. Sixteen closed at Q2. ONE did not.**

## ORLY (O'Reilly Automotive) — Q1 IN · Q2 IN · Q3 IN · Q4 IN · Q5 IN (NOT RANKED) · Q6 IN
**FAIL, at Q5, on price.** `Test Runs/2026-09-02 Run - ORLY OReilly Automotive.md`, 107KB,
112 ledger ids, zero phantoms. **Price $86.86**, cap **$70,266M** on **808,960,792 shares**
hand-read off the 10-Q cover. **Value at zero growth against the sovereign ~$35–65/sh, judged
~$53. Re-read band $40–65.**

**This is the eighth business to clear every business gate, and the FIRST from the operator's
watchlist.** The other seven — COST, LOW, ITW, RPM, CSL, SHW, HD — all came from dividend
screens.

- **I was wrong about Q2 and the run said so in those words.** The distribution-density case
  holds: a part that arrives in thirty minutes is not the same product as one that arrives
  tomorrow. **[E2-45]'s attacker test has already been run in public, at length, by the
  strongest possible attacker, and ORLY's operating margin moved 19.77% → 19.46% over nine
  years — down 31 basis points.** Meanwhile the category's weak player was destroyed and the
  share went to the incumbents rather than out of the category: **Advance Auto $10,106M →
  $8,601M (−14.9%), operating margin +7.42% → −0.50%.**
- **The deflated series ACQUITS it** — real sales per store **+11.4%** on CPI-U and **+16.1%**
  on parts-CPI. That instrument has now run seven times: it convicted DG, Foot Locker and UAL
  and acquitted AEO, ULTA, DICK'S and ORLY. **It is measuring, not confirming.**
- **[E2-49] does not fire, and the reason is the sharpest single fact in the file: ORLY still
  publishes sales per weighted-average square foot — the exact metric HD withdrew after three
  declines and DKS dropped after six — and it kept publishing it through years when it fell in
  real terms.** No promotional language anywhere; full tariff pass-through with gross margin
  flat at 51.4% and comps accelerating to +7.0%. Return on unleveraged net tangible operating
  assets **74.6%, 1st of four**, on a $4,637M operating asset base — **and the negative equity
  cannot inflate it, because AZO carries 4.5x the equity deficit and scores eighteen points
  lower.**
- **What killed it is the arithmetic, and the methodological call is the finding.** Owner
  earnings fell **43.1% across four consecutive declines** from the 2021 peak while revenue
  rose 33.4%. Yield **2.19%–3.87% against a 5.27% bond — below it on every construction.**
  **Revenue compounded 8.42%/yr and operating income 8.23% — either one clears the floor.
  Owner earnings compounded 4.87%. The entire difference is capital intensity, which is the
  thing being valued.** Using the flattered series would have passed this name; **[E2-01]
  exists to stop exactly that.**
- **Strongest fact against the verdict, and the run could not refute it**: two distribution
  centres built in three years will not repeat, **H1-2026 capex is down 6.1% year on year**,
  TTM owner earnings have already recovered to $2,122M, comps are accelerating. **If capex
  normalises to ~$800M, owner earnings are ~$2.7bn and the floor is nearly cleared at ~$64.**
- **[E2-60] fires almost exactly**: buybacks exceeded owner earnings by **$3,456M over 3.5
  years while debt rose $3,188M** — a 0.92:1 ratio. And ORLY **beat its FY2025 guidance on
  every income-statement line and missed it on both cash-flow lines.**
- **Two defects in my brief, and the correction is the better finding.** I said ORLY does not
  split price from volume. **It does, in every 10-K — and AZO, AAP and GPC split NEITHER, in
  either window year.** DIY transaction counts are negative in every year disclosed except the
  pandemic. My screen row also did not reproduce: bottom boundary **2.19%, not 2.59%**, because
  the run's 8-year ex-pandemic window is lower than mine.

## WHAT THE MINI BERK TRACK SETTLED ABOUT THE FRAMEWORK, NOT THE COMPANIES

**Three insurers, three Q2 OUTs, and four amendments to a method that was three hours old.**

1. **An arithmetic defect: steps 2 and 3 double-counted underwriting profit.** [E5-47]
   excludes underwriting from component 2; [E5-48] records the filer amending that in 2015 to
   include it. **Ruling: step 2 is DIAGNOSTIC, not additive** — [E3-69] never adds the cost of
   float to anything.
2. **Stage 0(b) tested the wrong ratio, and Loews proved it twice over.** Float ÷ investments
   guards only the low side. The ratio that governs whether counting investments gross at
   market is safe is **investments ÷ EQUITY: Berkshire 0.45x, Markel 2.01x, LOEWS 2.96x, CNA
   4.34x.** At Loews **component 1 spans $35.39 to $273.30 per share — a 7.7x width on a
   choice the corpus does not make** — so the run abandoned the two-component sum for a sum of
   the parts. **[E4-25]: the width IS the conclusion.**
3. **[E5-48] pre-dates ASU 2016-01** and names only "dividends and interest," while the largest
   portfolio item in pre-tax income is now unrealized marks. **Two constructions differing by
   27% at WTM and 175% at Loews.** Handled as a disclosed judgment, never as a silent
   extension of a verbatim row.
4. **CONVENTION 4 survived its first two tests** — the float recipe WTM invented reproduces
   Markel's first-ever published float to within **1.1%**. Recorded beside the fact that
   **Markel published no float figure at all before FY2025**, so [E3-69]'s "period of years" is
   being read off a table three months old.

**And the cross-name finding the WTM competitor row produced: MARKEL AND CHUBB — the two names
usually placed at the quality end of this industry — HAVE BOTH STOPPED PRINTING BOOK VALUE PER
SHARE IN THE 10-K.** "Book value" appears zero times in Markel's FY2025 10-K. That is
[E2-49] fired at the sector rather than at a company.

day — and the only name in the whole queue whose yield is ABOVE the sovereign: look-through
5.6–6.1% against 5.27%.** It fails anyway, on the [E4-28] floor: honest expectancy 6.7–9.7%
against ~10%. **"Above the bond, below the floor" is a verdict combination no other name has
produced, and the floor restoration of 2026-08-28 is the entire verdict.**

- **Q2 IN on the filed structure, not the legend.** The moat is the funding system: float
  $138bn → $177.5bn since 2020 at a **−3.6%/yr five-year cost**, on $748bn of net worth —
  the one name where [E2-62]'s license to concentrate actually exists. Credited honestly in
  both directions: GEICO went #2/13.8% (2019) → #3/11.6% (2024) **but beat Progressive on
  combined ratio in 2024-25**; BNSF trails UNP by 5.7–8.1 operating-ratio points with real
  revenue per unit −12% since 2018. **[E2-49] does NOT fire, and the three-vintage sweep is
  the reason**: "combined ratio" is absent from the FY2025, FY2023 AND FY2020 10-Ks — there
  was never a withdrawal; the components are published continuously. My brief had implied a
  withdrawal to adjudicate; the run swept three vintages instead of taking my framing.
- **Q3 IN from filings only, never the letters [E2-50]**: Abel/Jain at $22M flat salary, no
  bonus, no stock, with a written policy forbidding profit-linked pay; zero guidance; no
  EBITDA; **buybacks resumed Q1–Q2 2026 at $4.76bn ($476–488/B) after six zero quarters at
  record highs — the inverse of ORLY's dollar-budget pattern**, and the opposite of what my
  brief asserted ("the recent slowdown/halt" was stale; the 10-Q says resumed). Operating
  ROE 6.5–7.8% — **honest and mediocre, and the mediocrity IS the cash drag.**
- **Q4 IN**: accident-year combined **93.6 / 87.7 / 89.3** — the instrument that convicted
  MKL acquits Berkshire. The named death is slow: [E5-45]'s ABCs plus ~$22bn/yr of cash drag
  against the floor.
- **[E3-54] retention PASSES at $1.71 per $1 retained (2021–25)** while book/share +11.6%/yr
  trails the S&P — both legs reported. Third element judged **NEUTRAL: zero Buffett premium,
  zero Buffett discount.**
- **Strongest fact against the quit, stated at full strength**: realized per-share
  compounding over the CURRENT five years — book +11.6%/yr, market +16.7%/yr — is above the
  floor, and clearing it from today's yield needs only ~4.4%/yr against 8.9% realized
  operating growth. If the realized rate persists, quitting was [E3-47]'s omission error.
  The quit rests on the normalized, no-growth-credit construction.
- **Method misfits, and the big one reached CLAUDE.md itself**: the method's step 4 still
  carried **"there is no hurdle; it ranks"** — the pre-Test-D wording the framework rewrote
  on 2026-08-28 — **and so did CLAUDE.md's one-screen summary, inherited by every session
  since.** Berkshire is the exact case where the wordings disagree: under "no hurdle" it
  ranks first in the queue; under the framework as written it is quit on. Both copies now

  the method was calibrated on — **the method's centre of gravity moved off its own
  author**; [E5-48] needs a corporate-line rule (~$160bn of parent T-bills sit outside the
  insurance segment); [E3-71] supplies a treatment but no discount horizon; and the
  retention window grades the founder, not the CEO being priced — fixable only by time.

construction in Apple's filed history, including the best twelve months ever recorded
(2.63%). The floor needs +7.58%/yr perpetual: $467bn of owner earnings against $105bn
judged, a 4.45x gap.**

  MISLEADING.** TSCO, EFX and ANF all reported spreads that did not reproduce. **Apple's

  constructions (3y and 5y at each capex end), and on a business whose owner earnings grew
  2.5x in nine years a 3y-vs-5y comparison measures the last two years. **Against the run's
  own six windows the true width is 67.9%, not 2%.** [E4-25] says the width IS the finding,
  so a width computed over a window too short to contain the variation is not a small
  finding - it is a FALSE one, and it points the flattering way. **The screen now emits a
  `spread_caveat` whenever only four constructions resolve.**

  Apple filed unit sales for six years and **stopped 86 DAYS after the series went flat** -

### AVGO (Broadcom) — Q1 IN · Q2 IN (NARROW) · Q3 IN · Q4 IN (GREAT) · Q5 FAIL. Price $357.90.
`Test Runs/2026-09-06 Run - AVGO Broadcom.md`. Cap $1,702,738M on 4,757,580,198 cover-read

  ratio, because **Broadcom states depreciation separately from amortisation in its own
  cash-flow statement.** And the QCOM ruling transferred: **the acquisition amortisation
  renews nothing that $10,977M of R&D above the OCF line does not already renew.**
- **THE PERIMETER DID NOT HAVE TO BE BUILT - BROADCOM FILED IT.** VMware closed 2023-11-22
  for **$86,290M, of which $531M was physical plant.** The filed pro forma: **combined
  revenue +8.2% and combined net income MINUS 21.2%** (FY2023->FY2024). The run built the
  owner-earnings pro forma from VMware's own 10-Ks anyway: **two years after paying
  $86.3bn, combined owner earnings are 7.3% above where the two companies stood together.**

  finding in three days, and the first where the two "ends" were never different in kind.

  largest perimeter event this project has ever met**, because $79.6bn of cash against a
  $1.7 TRILLION cap is 4.7% - under the 5% line. **The percentage test is right for a small
  filer and wrong for a mega-cap: a deal can be immaterial to the DENOMINATOR and still be
  the largest single fact in the file, because it changes the NUMERATOR.** An absolute-size
  gate now fires at $10bn regardless of cap; verified firing on AVGO.
- **Two things the brief did not anticipate.** **Broadcom named Apple at ~20% of revenue in
  the FY2023 10-K and WITHDREW both the name and the figure in FY2024** - in the same
  document where **top-five customer concentration rose 35% -> 40%**, and alongside the WT

  Revenue" - a metric that appears ZERO times in any 10-K or 10-Q**, existing only in
  furnished 8-Ks that management also guides on quarterly. **The run had first found
  [E4-52] not firing, then reversed itself in place and stated the reversal** - operator
  rule 6 applied to its own reasoning.
- **The standing counter is the strongest growth record the queue has seen**: owner
  earnings compounded **~32%/yr for nine and three-quarter years** ($2,009M -> $30,921M),

  widening margin, and **a business earning a 15.1% operating margin was made to earn

  by stacking two generous assumptions - annualising the peak quarter AND assuming 7.26%

- Ordinal recorded rather than edited: the run's own Q4 commit message says "seventeenth"

## TXN AND ORCL FOLDED IN — 2026-09-07. FORTY-FIVE RUNS; AND THE FIRST Q4 OUT IN THE QUEUE.

### ORCL (Oracle) — Q1 IN · Q2 IN (NARROW) · Q3 IN · **Q4 OUT.** FAIL. Price $158.78.
`Test Runs/2026-09-06 Run - ORCL Oracle.md`, 91.8KB. Claim priced: **$462,341M** on
2,880,471,000 shares. **THE FIRST NAME IN THE ENTIRE WATCHLIST QUEUE TO FAIL AT Q4 - the
survival question - rather than at Q2 or on price.**

**Q4 asks four things and Oracle fails three on filed figures, none requiring a view about
AI demand:**
1. **[E4-20] GRUESOME**: a **3.4% incremental pre-tax return on ~$160bn deployed in five
   years**, robust across every construction from 3.4% to 6.8%, against [E5-40]'s ~12%.
   *"Only the gruesome fails Q4."*
2. **[E5-11] strength (3) FAILS**: an **~$80.7bn twelve-month requirement against $63.9bn**
   of liquid assets plus operating cash flow - **before $260bn of leases begin commencing.**
3. **[E2-54] coverage is NEGATIVE**: cash flow net of capital expenditure is **-$23,686M
   against $4,599M of interest.**
4. **[E5-39] is failed in Oracle's own MD&A** - the plan depends on *"available financing
   arrangements"* and *"potential access to additional financing."*

- **WHY OUT AND NOT UNKNOWABLE, and this is the sharpest methodological ruling of the
  week**: the range IS enormous - **$53bn wide on the single year** - **but width closes a
  file only when it STRADDLES THE DECISION, and this one straddles nothing.** The single
  most generous construction obtainable (FY2026 depreciation-only, the construction the
  framework calls INVALID, in the best year the company has ever had) yields **4.227%
  against a 5.24% sovereign.** Every construction, every window, either end of the band,
  pays less than a government bond. **The width is decision-irrelevant - the MSFT
  adjudication - and the verdict rests on two single-valued facts, not ranges.**
- **WHY OUT AND NOT "IN, THEN FAIL ON PRICE" LIKE MSFT, GOOGL AND AVGO**: those three
  passed [E5-11] strength (3). **Microsoft's uncommenced leases are 1.80x its operating
  cash flow; Broadcom's twelve-month fixed claims were covered 5.9x by cash alone with no
  revolver counted. Oracle's uncommenced leases are 8.13x its operating cash flow and its
  coverage net of capex is NEGATIVE.** *"The distinction is not a matter of degree in the
  same direction; it is the difference between a company that could stop and a company that
  has contracted not to."*
- **[E4-18] checked explicitly: the verdict did not require fighting for it.** No narrowed
  assumption, no chosen window, no chosen end of the capex band - **it holds at every window
  and at both ends.**
- **The named death, quoted**: a company that *"funds the consumption with debt and issued
  equity, and arrives in 2030 larger, more indebted and no more valuable."* Judged
  **likely**, not merely possible.

## AMD FOLDED IN — 2026-09-07. FORTY-SIX RUNS.

### AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) — Q1 IN, Q2 OUT. FAIL. Price $477.57.
`Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - AMD Advanced Micro Devices.md`, 807 lines, 53 ledger citations,
zero phantoms. Cap **$779,621M** on 1,632,475,042 cover-read shares. **Value ~$7-$81/share,
judged ~$68 - even at the ceiling of the most generous construction the price is 5.9x the
value. Yield 0.75%, -4.49 points against the bond; 4.49% perpetual growth merely to MATCH
it, 9.25% to clear the floor.**

- **THE PROFIT-MIX TEST DECIDED IT AGAINST THE SEGMENT THAT LOOKS LIKE A FRANCHISE.** Share
  of segment operating income: **Data Center 26.3% (FY2023) -> 66.3% (H1 FY2026); Embedded -
  the Xilinx annuity, the genuine franchise candidate - 54.5% -> 13.0%.** And **Embedded
  fails the ACLS supplier test on its own numbers**: revenue -35.1%, operating income
  -52.7%, margin -13.4 points, **where ACLS raised its filed price range and gained margin
  through a -26% collapse.** Data Center fails [E3-03](2) in the 10-K's own words and (3)
  on ~$800M of MI308 export-control charges plus an expected 15% government revenue share.
- **TWO SURPRISES AGAINST THE CONCLUSION, both recorded before being overridden.**
  **[E2-44] passes both halves TWICE**: Client units +34% with ASP +13% (FY2024), units
  +31% with ASP +15% (FY2025) - **AMD took share while RAISING price**, which is the
  combination almost nothing in this queue has printed. And **the QCOM kill does NOT
  reproduce**: *"No customer accounted for at least 10% of... net revenue in fiscal years
  2025 and 2024"* - the last 10% customer AMD filed was **a game-console maker at 18%, not
  a hyperscaler.** Both are overridden because the [E2-44] pass sits in a segment that is
  **20.7% of profit** and whose operating income **fell 8.4% on +13% revenue** in the latest
  half, and because the [E3-03](2) failure is against **Nvidia (60.4% operating margin
  against AMD's 10.7%)**, not against the customers.
- **MY (c) EXPECTATION WAS WRONG AND THE RUN RECORDED IT AS WRONG.** I said a fabless filer
  would show the D&A end as the large one. **AMD's capex/depreciation ran 1.02 -> 1.03 ->
  1.24 -> 1.40 -> 1.87, and ~2.1x in H1 FY2026** - so **the D&A end is the GENEROUS end and
  the capex end is conservative, the opposite of AVGO's inversion.** The AVGO amortisation
  ruling holds unchanged, and [E2-60]'s counter-test does not fire (R&D held 21-26% of
  revenue).
- **THE PERIMETER WAS HANDLED WITHOUT REBUILDING IT, AND THE DIRECTION DEFEATED THE BULL
  CASE.** Xilinx - **$48,793M, closed 2022-02-14, paid in 429 million shares, 26.3% of
  today's count** - sits inside every window, and **the screen's acquisition cell is EMPTY
  because `acquisition_flag()` reads the investing cash-flow line and a stock deal never
  touches it** (the documented limit, and the new absolute-size gate does not rescue it
  either - both are cash-based). AMD's own filed pro forma is the cross-check: **FY2021
  combined net income of $8 MILLION against standalone AMD's actual $3,162M.** The run
  tested the window both ways and found **including the pre-deal year RAISES owner earnings**
  ($1,898M five-year against $1,662M for FY2022-25 alone), bounding the residual at **under
  15bp on a yield 4.49 points short.**
- **A FIFTH SCREEN DEFECT, AND ONE THE OTHER FOUR NAMES DID NOT HAVE - now fixed**: both of
  the screen's "ends" carried **$1,216M of DISCONTINUED-OPERATIONS cash**. The XBRL total
  tag returns $7,709M where the filed statement reads **continuing $6,493M / discontinued
  $1,216M**, and the union rule let the total win. **The screen overstated its own
  CONSERVATIVE end by 26.3%** - the flattering direction, and exactly what [E5-34] exists to
  prevent. `ocf_continuing()` now subtracts separately-tagged discontinued cash and emits a
  note; verified reproducing the run's corrected 1,539 and 2,049 to the million. True width
  over the run's eight windows: **$592M-$6,953M, 1,075%** - and decision-irrelevant, since
  every construction yields 0.08%-0.89%.
- Windage count 1, **spent against the conclusion.** Strongest re-open trigger named: Data
  Center's 29.6% H1 margin recovery, which is one half-year.

## INTC FOLDED IN — 2026-09-07. FORTY-SEVEN RUNS.

### INTC (Intel) — Q1 IN, Q2 OUT. FAIL. Price $95.80.
`Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - INTC Intel.md`, 975 lines. **Judged zero-growth value ~$20-40/sh.
Every construction, every window, both ends of the capex band is below the 5.24% sovereign -
including FY2020, Intel's best year ever, at the depreciation-only end the framework calls
invalid: 4.80% and $87.78/sh.**

- **THE HHH PRECEDENT WAS RUN EXPLICITLY AND REJECTED, WHICH IS THE RIGHT USE OF A
  PRECEDENT.** I flagged that Intel might close at Q1 like Howard Hughes. It does not:
  **HHH's transforming asset was ACQUIRED with 26 days of filed history; Intel's has been
  OWNED for forty years**, and Note 3 splits it in dollars across three retrospectively
  restated years - **a 26%-operating-margin product business ($49,147M revenue, $12,739M
  operating income) against a MINUS 58%-margin foundry ($17,826M revenue, $(10,318)M loss)
  whose EXTERNAL revenue is $307M.** *"Closing at Q1 would have been the [E3-47] omission
  error."*
- **Q2 OUT on four independent grounds, none needing a forecast**: [E3-03](2) fails on the
  registrant's own risk factors (*"we have lost market share in recent years, including in
  both client and data center markets"*; *"unsuccessful to date in becoming a meaningful
  participant"* in AI accelerators); **[E4-04] is the sharpest** - the moat is process
  leadership, **its basis must be WHOLLY REPLACED every node at $20-25bn/yr, Intel lost it
  twice, and the 10-K contemplates *"pause or discontinue development of Intel 14A"*** - a
  lapse destroys the structure rather than narrowing it, which is the excluded class by the
  framework's own test; **the foundry has no customers** (*"unsuccessful to date in securing
  any significant external foundry customers for any of our nodes"*).
- **THE COMPETITOR ROW INVERTED, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THE FILE**: gross margin **INTC
  61.0% -> 34.8% against AMD 23.1% -> 49.5%** (2016->2025) - **37.9 points ahead to 14.7
  points behind, a 52.6-point reversal.** In FY2025 **AMD's Data Center segment out-earns
  Intel's DCAI ($3,603M vs $3,422M) with no fabs, on $974M of capex against $17,672M.**
  **The two runs cross-check each other from opposite sides** - AMD's file convicted itself
  against Nvidia on the same day this one convicted Intel against AMD.
- **The strongest fact against the verdict is the most recent filed quarter, and it is
  strong**: Q2 2026 revenue +25.4%, gross margin 40.4% against 27.5%, operating income
  **+$1,796M against $(3,176)M**, H1 server ASPs **+38%** and client +22% with *"market
  demand exceeded our available product supply"* in both segments - **nobody walked to AMD
  when Intel could not supply them.** Called a surfing run [E3-51], and named as the live
  way the verdict is wrong.
- **The Apollo round trip, which touched no income statement**: sold 49% of Ireland SCIP for
  $11.0bn (Q2 2024), **bought it back for $14.2bn (2026-04-08)** - **$3.2bn of cost in 23
  months, and not a dollar of it ran through earnings**, while the $5.6bn Altera GAIN did.
- **ORCL's Q4 measurement was run and it splits the two names**: Intel's [E2-56] incremental
  return is **NEGATIVE** on $112bn (against Oracle's 3.4%) and [E2-54] coverage has been
  negative four straight years - **but [E5-11](3) PASSES at 2.03x where Oracle's failed.
  Intel can stop building; Oracle had contracted not to.**
- **Three tests went management's way and are recorded**: zero EBITDA hits anywhere, **no
  revenue/margin/EPS target in the 10-K at all** (even "five nodes in four years" returns
  zero hits), and the absolute-size acquisition gate passes (~$1.37bn in 4.5 years).
- **A SIXTH SCREEN DEFECT, AND A NEW FAILURE MODE**: both ends reproduce to the dollar **and
  both are wrong** - `oe_bottom` is a 3-yr mean at the investing-capex end while `oe_top` is
  a **5-yr** mean at the depreciation end computed on the **SUPERSEDED** FY2021 OCF of
  $29,991M (restated to $29,456M).
- **AND A QUEUE-WIDE CAPEX DEFECT**: `PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment` **misses
  about a fifth of Intel's capex** - Intel reports PP&E additions in **financing** too, so
  FY2025 capex is **$17,672M, not $14,646M.** The financing-side line is a company-extension
  tag companyfacts does not carry (the COKE wall). `capex_funding_flag()` added to detect
  the CONSEQUENCE - gross plant growing faster than the cash line - **and it fires on 19 of
  379 names but NOT on Intel, which is confessed in its docstring rather than fixed by
  tuning**: Intel's gross-PP&E series stops at 2022 in companyfacts, and its disposals mask
  the growth. **The threshold was not lowered to make the motivating case pass.**

## MU FOLDED IN — 2026-09-07. FORTY-EIGHT RUNS.

### MU (Micron) — Q1 IN, Q2 OUT (permanent). FAIL. Price $1,016.59.
`Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - MU Micron.md`, 50 ledger citations, zero phantoms, windage 0.
Cap **$1,148,130M** on 1,129,393,151 shares (two independent counts in the Q3 FY2026 10-Q
agree). **Value ~$15-50/share on the full-cycle filed record; ~$50-120 at the best pre-AI
window including the invalid D&A end; ~$570-630 on 9M FY2026 annualised; ~$1,160 only if
the single best quarter in memory-industry history is capitalised forever.**

- **THE TEN-YEAR ARITHMETIC IS THE MOST DAMNING SINGLE LINE THE QUEUE HAS PRODUCED.**
  FY2016-25: OCF **$105,456M**, total capex **$93,035M**, SBC $4,468M - leaving **$7,953M
  of owner earnings IN TOTAL, $795M a year, against reported net income of $45,980M.**
  Eight windows published, -$2,339M to +$7,144M. **It is the commodity the corpus
  describes.**
- **[E2-44] fails both halves on the FY2023 record**: DRAM price down high-40s% on
  **near-flat volume**; NAND price down low-50s% with **volume UP**; gross margin 45% to
  **MINUS 9%**; a $1,831M net-realisable-value write-down. **The competitor row is the
  proof**: Micron had **the worst and only negative trough gross margin of eight names**
  (SNDK 7.1%, WDC 15.3%, STX 18.3%) - while **a fabless controller peer with no fabs held
  42.3%.** All four memory/storage names then recovered together: **one wave, measured four
  times.**
- **The strongest fact against the verdict is real, filed and quantified - and it lost on
  SIZE, not on assertion.** Micron's Q3 FY2026 10-Q discloses multi-year **take-or-pay**
  agreements with contractual **floor prices**, stating it expects margins *"even at floor
  pricing levels, to yield gross margins well above our peak quarterly margins in any past
  cycle."* **The run expected rhetoric and found a contractual change.** It fails because
  the remaining performance obligations are **~$5bn - 0.44% of market cap, about six weeks
  of revenue** - the largest agreements carry **a CEILING at the Q2-CY2026 market price**
  (*Micron sold its own upside at today's spot*), and the same filings still say
  *"substantially all contracts with our customers are short-term."* **Whether the floors
  survive a down-cycle is UNKNOWABLE, and the resolving document is named: a 10-K covering
  a memory down-cycle with material contracted HBM, which cannot exist until the cycle
  turns.**
- **THE INTC FINDING WAS RE-RUN AND REVERSED, WHICH IS HOW A FINDING SHOULD TRAVEL.**
  Micron's financing-line equipment payments are **$1,586M over ten years - 1.7% of
  investing capex, against Intel's 20.7%.** The check travels as a class; the magnitude
  does not. **And the larger leak runs the other way: $5,026M of government incentives sits
  INSIDE investing as a positive** ($2,005M, 12.6% of gross capex, in FY2025 alone) **and
  also suppresses future D&A by reducing PP&E carrying amounts.** Carried as a disclosed
  third construction, never netted silently.
- **A LIVE TOOL CRASH FOUND AND FIXED**: `run.py` raised **ZeroDivisionError** on names
  whose owner earnings sit at or below zero - **it fired on MU and INTC and would have
  re-triaged both as UNPRICED indefinitely.** The run documented it rather than patching it
  (tool changes being outside a run's mandate), which is the right division of labour.
  **Both DCF engines now REFUSE a non-positive base and say so**: *"a DCF on a non-positive
  base produces no number [E5-34]; the negative bottom boundary IS the statement."*
  Verified on MU and INTC.
- Samsung and SK hynix are **UNKNOWABLE at the filing rung** (12g3-2(b) exempt, no 20-F due)
  - eight of ~ten peers named, **sufficient to refuse an IN, not to grant one.**

## QUEUE REGENERATED 2026-09-07, and the remaining names re-ranked

Rebuilt with all five tool fixes in force that were not present when the reading order was
last set: the discontinued-operations correction (AMD), the capex-funding flag (INTC), the
absolute-size acquisition gate (AVGO), the union tag rule, and the split-adjusted perimeter
guard. **361 priced, 18 unpriced with the ground stated.** Sovereign 5.24%, US Treasury.

**AND THE SPREAD CAVEAT IS NOW IN THE CSV THAT BRIEFS ARE BUILT FROM.** It existed only in
`floor_screen.main()`'s console output, so **every brief written off this file inherited a
width with no warning attached** - which is exactly how the four-construction trap reached
six consecutive runs (AAPL, GOOGL, AVGO, AMD, INTC, KLAC). It now appears on all 361 rows.

**THE RE-RANK IS ITSELF A FINDING: every remaining name is expensive.** Of the 28 unrun
names that price, **the BEST needs 7.64% perpetual growth** and the yields run from 2.36%
down to 0.27%:

| | yield | growth needed | width |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| QLYS | 2.36% | 7.64% | 27% |
| CERT | 2.28% | 7.72% | 23% |
| DAL | 2.15% | 7.85% | **334%** |
| CRM | 1.66% | 8.34% | 152% |
| PLPC | 1.44% | 8.56% | 110% |
| PINS | 1.22% | 8.78% | 14% |
| DELL | 1.09% | 8.91% | 44% |
| LRCX | 1.04% | 8.96% | 21% |
| CGNX | 0.97% | 9.03% | 49% |
| SHOP | 0.83% | 9.17% | 119% |

**Not one of them reaches the tier-1 threshold of 6%.** The queue began with fourteen names
needing 6% or less; **that population is exhausted, and what remains needs between 7.6% and
9.7% forever.** Against [E4-35]'s base rate - fewer than 10 of the 200 most profitable
companies sustained 15% for twenty years - **the reading order from here is no longer about
finding a cheap name. It is about recording why each expensive one fails, and arming the
band that would make it interesting.**

**CNR and RGTI remain unpriced** and need their perimeter re-checked before a run is spent
on either.

`Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - AMAT Applied Materials.md`, 121.6KB, 33 research files, zero
phantoms. Cap **$360,857M** on 793,597,443 shares from the Q3 FY2026 10-Q cover. **Value
~$77 conservative / ~$119 judged / ~$163 optimistic zero-growth with $7,957M net cash
credited; floor ~$45-90, judged ~$67. The price is 2.80x the top of the zero-growth band.
Yield 1.254% (band 0.767-2.136%) against 5.24% - MINUS 3.99 POINTS - and the floor needs
+8.75%/yr perpetual against a filed 18-year owner-earnings CAGR of 5.12%.**

  ALLOWED THE TEST.** KLA's file could not run the HAS/EFX profit-mix test in six vintages.
  **AMAT adopted ASU 2023-07 in Q4 FY2025, so Note 15 prints segment cost of products sold,
  gross profit and gross margin** - and **the answer kills the claim: AGS gross margin 33.4%
  against Semiconductor Systems' 54.2%. AGS is 22.5% of revenue but only 15.5% of gross
  profit. The annuity is the LOW-MARGIN half.** Every prior equipment run has treated the
  service base as the quality half of the business on an inference the filings never
  supported; this one measured it.

  margin exists only for FY2023/24/25 and Semiconductor Systems revenue ROSE in all three,
  so the ACLS instrument that cleared KLA at segment level has no downturn to work on. **The
  consolidated substitute fails in three of four filed downturns** (FY2009 -13.9pts, FY2012
  -3.5, FY2019 -1.3 same-vintage; FY2013 +1.8 the only pass), and **AMAT's own MD&A says
  gross margin fell "primarily due to the decrease in net sales."** In FY2019 **the mix ran
  the FAVOURABLE way - Display was the lower-margin line - and margin fell anyway.**
- **THE COMPETITOR ROW READS AGAINST AMAT, and this is the reverse of KLA's file.** **Lam
  Research names AMAT by name as its "primary competitor" in both deposition and etch AND
  out-earns it - 35.3% against 29.9% operating margin - while AMAT names no competitor
  anywhere in its own 10-K.** No filing in the cohort concedes anything to AMAT. With six
  unpriceable head-on competitors (TEL, ASM International, SEMES, Wonik IPS, SCREEN, and

  could write NONE at Q2 rather than NARROW** [E4-25].

  headline.** The run's own Q2 "7.6% incremental return" was an artifact of **$8.3bn of cash
  sitting inside the screen row's NTOA denominator.** Ex-cash it is **95.3%**, flat at

  "best business this queue has run" label rests on a cash-contaminated denominator.**
- **THE SPREAD TRAP FIRED FOR THE SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN.** The screen row reproduces **to

  FY2023 finance-lease additions) - and rebuilt properly the **width is 2.78x against the
  row's 1.35x, and the step is 2.74x against `level_shift` 2.0.**
- **CHINA GIVES THE OPPOSITE ANSWER TO KLA'S, and it is the one fact that favours AMAT:**

## CRWD FOLDED IN — 2026-09-07. FIFTY-ONE RUNS; AND A 4x SHARE-COUNT ERROR CAUGHT AT STAGE 0.

### CRWD (CrowdStrike) — Q1 IN · **Q2 OUT.** FAIL, on the business, not on price. Price $213.10.
`Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - CRWD CrowdStrike.md`. Cap **$218,201M**. Zero-growth value
**~$2-6/share, judged ~$3.50**, carried under `COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE` because the
file closed at the second question.

- **STAGE 0 CAUGHT A 4x ERROR, AND IT IS A TOOLING FINDING, NOT A BRIEF TYPO.**
  **CrowdStrike split 4-for-1 effective 2026-07-01.** The 10-K cover count (253,614,090) is
  PRE-split; the Q2 FY2027 10-Q cover of 2026-08-20 gives **1,023,934,842.** Verified two
  ways - the filing's own words, and the arithmetic: 253,614,090 x 4 = 1,014,456,360 against
  1,023,934,842, a **+0.93% six-month issuance gap** that is exactly the right size to be
  real issuance rather than a bad split factor. The two classes are moot: **all Class B
  converted to Class A on 2024-12-11**, economic equivalence read off the charter
  description rather than assumed [cover_shares.py's standing refusal to sum classes].
- **THE THREE DECIDING FACTS, and the first is the PINS number reached from below.**
  **SBC / OCF = 68.0%** ($1,096,679k against $1,612,349k, both cross-checked to the dollar
  against the filed cash-flow statement) - **within half a point of Pinterest's 68.5%, but
  CROWDSTRIKE ROSE INTO IT THREE YEARS RUNNING (55.6% -> 62.3% -> 68.0%) where Pinterest's
  was a level.** The consequence over four years is the whole file: **revenue +34.9%/yr, OCF
  +29.4%/yr, owner earnings +2.4%/yr.** "OCF minus SBC" has been **flat at $515-520M for
  three years.**
- **THREE METRIC WITHDRAWALS, ALL DATED, and the third is the sharpest [E2-49] instance the
  queue has recorded.** Subscription customers and module adoption both went in the 10-K of
  **2023-03-09** (one announced, one silent). The quarterly net-retention NUMBER was
  replaced by **"effectively at our benchmark"** in the 10-Q filed **2023-08-31 - 91 days
  after it last cleared its own published "above 120%" bar** - and has never returned; the
  latest 10-Q says only "improved sequentially." **The published yardstick was swapped for
  an unpublished one in the first quarter the published one stopped being met.**
- **AND THE RUN THEN SOFTENED ITS OWN BEST FINDING, which is the behaviour the framework
  wants**: metric withdrawal turns out to be an **industry habit** - PANW dropped billings,
  SentinelOne dropped its NRR after 132% -> 114% -> 110% - **which materially weakens the
  [E2-49] reading, and is recorded as such rather than left to stand.**
- **THE OUTAGE IS THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT, AND THE RUN LED WITH IT.**
  Retention **substantially held: 119% -> 112% -> 115%, never below 100%**, net new ARR at a
  record **$1,010.9M**, securities class action **dismissed with final judgment**. *"A vendor
  grounded the world's airlines and lost seven points of net retention, three of which it
  has won back. There is no better natural experiment on switching costs anywhere in the
  queue"* - and every pure-play peer names CrowdStrike in its own competition section while
  CrowdStrike names none of them. **It fails anyway on [E3-03] criterion (2), evidenced by
  the company's own MD&A: customers were PAID to stay.** *"Customer commitment packages ...
  have included discounting ... [and] are expected to continue to result in increased
  contraction."*
- **THE SEVENTH CONSECUTIVE SPREAD DEFECT, HERE THREE-PART AND THE WORST YET.**
  `oe_bottom 233` / `oe_top 278` are a 5-year and a 3-year mean of **the SAME capex end**
  (not a capex band at all); **that capex end omitted the separate capitalized-software
  line**; and **`da_annual()` returns EMPTY for this filer, so the corpus default for (c)
  was never computed.** True range rebuilt over six windows and both ends: **$114.3M to
  $308.4M, a 2.70x width against the published 19.2%.** And **`level_shift 4.40 "normalize
  down"` is computed on OCF and points at the WRONG END - owner earnings peaked in FY2024
  and have FALLEN 50% since.**
- **MY PRIOR WAS REFUTED IN THE DIRECTION THAT HURT.** I expected the persistent contingent
  liability might LIFT owner earnings if handled properly. **It lowers them**: the $45.4M is
  **founder holdbacks** - payroll settled in a variable number of shares, contingent on
  employment - appearing in **no section of the cash-flow statement**, and the filing says it
  is **excluded** from the equity-award table.
- **Limits stated rather than papered over**: **Microsoft's rung is BLOCKED** - no filed
  security-revenue figure exists in either the FY2025 or FY2026 10-K, **so the bundling
  exposure that is the named death trigger is real and unmeasurable from filings**; PANW's
  column is a year stale. The Q3 subagent died after its pay-versus-performance section, so
  guidance-beat quarters and insider ownership are ungathered - **below the closed gate, so
  no verdict rested on them.**

### THE SPLIT FINDING, CHECKED — AND IT IS NOT A TOOL DEFECT. I NEARLY RECORDED ONE THAT DOES NOT EXIST.
My first draft of this entry blamed the 4x error on the pipeline. **Both tools were checked
before this was committed, and both were RIGHT:**

- **The screen's cap was already correct.** The queue row carries **cap_m 220,218** against
  the run's hand-built **$218,201M** - a 0.9% difference explained by the price date, not by
  a factor of four. `floor_screen`'s split division did its job.
- **`cover_shares.py` returns the correct post-split count today**, run live against the SEC:
  **CRWD 10-Q filed 2026-08-27, accession 0001535527-26-000031, 1,023,934,842** - to the
  share, the number the run used. `latest_periodic()` already prefers the newest periodic
  filing, which is precisely the guard I was about to claim was missing.

**So the 4x error was in the BRIEF's own reading of a 10-K cover, and Stage 0 caught it.**
The lesson is narrower than the one I nearly wrote, and it is about reading rather than
tooling: **a 10-K cover count is as-of the 10-K's cover date, and any split after that date
voids it.** CRWD split **4-for-1 effective 2026-07-01**, five months after the FY2026 10-K's
period end. Recorded here under operator rule 6 rather than quietly dropped, because **the
project has already published one wrong measurement this month, and the antidote [E4-26] is
to hunt disconfirming evidence hardest for the finding you like best** - a tool defect found
by one's own tool is exactly the kind of finding one likes best.

## QLYS FOLDED IN — 2026-09-07. FIFTY-TWO RUNS; AND THE SECOND CASE WHERE THE BOND AND THE FLOOR DISAGREE.

### QLYS (Qualys) — Q1 IN · **Q2 OUT.** FAIL, on the business, not on price. Price $171.65.
`Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - QLYS Qualys.md`. Cap **$5,938M** on 34,595,001 cover-read
shares. Owner earnings on the five-year default window, normalized: **$139.5M-$152.4M, a
2.35%-2.57% yield against a 5.24% sovereign - minus 2.7 to 2.9 points. All EIGHTEEN
constructions in the run's grid yield less than the bond.** The [E4-28] floor needs
**7.4%-7.7% perpetual growth.** Value **~$60 conservative / ~$95 optimistic.**

- **THE FINDING THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS NAME: AGAINST THE BARE SOVEREIGN AT 3% GROWTH, THE
  SAME OWNER EARNINGS ARE WORTH $185-$203 A SHARE - ABOVE TODAY'S QUOTE OF $171.65.**
  Qualys is the second case in the entire project of the disagreement `CLAUDE.md` names
  explicitly: **above the bond, below the floor.** Berkshire was the first. **This is
  precisely why it screened as the best-priced unrun name in the queue and still fails**,
  and it is the sharpest available demonstration that the ~10% floor restored on 2026-08-28
  (Test D) is doing real work rather than restating the sovereign comparison.
- **MY Q2 PRIOR WAS REFUTED ON ITS OWN INSTRUMENT, THEN UPHELD ON DIFFERENT GROUND - which
  is the outcome the framework is built to produce.** I predicted [E2-49] metric withdrawal,
  by analogy to CRWD. **The net dollar expansion rate was NEVER withdrawn and never replaced
  with words in EIGHTEEN CONSECUTIVE FILINGS, including at its 102% trough, and it has
  TURNED UP: 111% (Q3 2022) -> 102% (Q2 2024) -> 105% (Q2 2026). [E2-49] fires the other
  way, as a CREDIT.** Q2 is OUT on the **level** (a base that pays 3-5% more a year), the
  **channel-mix shift**, and the **absent unit series** - not on CRWD's paid-to-stay
  evidence, which has **no analogue here.**
- **[E2-44] SPLITS.** Half two passes emphatically: **capex 0.75% of revenue, negative
  operating capital.** Half one **cannot be evidenced: no ASP, no unit series and no
  per-customer disclosure in any of eight vintages**, and the customer count has read
  *"over 10,000"* for **five straight years** [E4-55]. What does exist points down: **direct
  revenue 57% -> 54% -> 51%, with 93% of the H1 2026 increment arriving through a channel
  the filing itself says is sold "at a discount."** That is [E3-62]'s pass-through question
  being answered in the mix.
- **"GROWTH DECELERATED SHARPLY" WAS PARTLY REFUTED**: 19.1% (2022) -> 9.6% (2024) ->
  **10.1% (2025) -> 11.0% (Q2 2026).** It decelerated, then stabilised and ticked up.
- **[E5-08]: condition (1) passes, (2) fails, and (3) fails hardest.** **$1.24bn repurchased
  at $127.59-$143.10 against a conservative case near $60.** And the sharpest governance
  finding is **[E4-31]: one-third of the executive cash bonus rides on BOOKINGS, and the
  proxy PUBLISHES THE TARGETS while stating "we do not disclose" the actuals**, citing
  competitive harm. **A $1.24bn buyback against a register that cannot compute the leading
  indicator management pays itself on.**
- **SBC WAS REFUTED AS AN ISSUE, AND THE COMPARISON IS THE POINT: 24.9% of OCF with no trend
  across a decade**, against **CrowdStrike 68.0% and rising, Tenable 71.9%, Rapid7 67.8%.**
- **THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT, and the run calls this the closest Q2 call in
  the queue: Qualys earned a 33.2% GAAP operating margin in FY2025 while Tenable earned
  (0.9)% and Rapid7 earned 1.3%** - same product, same market, same twelve months, all three
  December year-ends. **Owner earnings $227.4M against $58.4M and $25.8M.** *"If customers
  truly regarded the peers as close substitutes at the price, a 34-point margin gap could not
  have persisted and widened for six years."* That is **[E2-58]'s single named exception**,
  genuinely present. The run's answer: **[E2-58] rescues PROFITABILITY, it does not grant
  entry to the franchise class** - and it named **four falsifiable documents that would
  reverse the call.** No price alert is armed, because **the failure is not price**; the
  reversal condition is documentary, not a quote.

### THREE OF MY FIVE MANDATORY BRIEF CORRECTIONS WERE WRONG FOR THIS FILER
Recorded because carrying a fix forward as though it were universal is the same defect as
carrying a bug forward. **`da_annual()` returns data for every one of sixteen years,
reconciling to the dollar** - the CRWD empty-return does not recur. **There is no
separately-tagged capitalized software**; the entire investing section is four lines, swept
FY2021-25. And **`level_shift "normalize down"` pointed at the RIGHT end here** - owner
earnings are at an all-time high, not post-peak - **though right for a reason it cannot
see**, which was the run's largest single adjustment.

### THE TOOLING, EIGHTH CONFIRMATION AND ONE NEW DEFECT
- **THE SPREAD CAVEAT IS CONFIRMED FOR THE EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE RUN: true width 2.10x (110%)
  against the published 26.5%.** The two "ends" **vary window and capex end simultaneously**
  (`oe_bottom` = 5yr at the D&A end; `oe_top` = 3yr at the capex end), so the published
  spread is attributable to neither. **Unusually, the capex axis is nearly irrelevant here
  (1.09x): the width is ALL WINDOW.**
- **NEW: THE SHARE COUNT WAS STALE BY SIX MONTHS, AND THIS TIME IT WAS THE ROW, NOT A
  BRIEF.** The row used the **10-K cover (35,675,926 at 2026-02-11)**; the 10-Q cover gives
  **34,595,001.** A **3.1% error, against the company.** This is the same failure mode CRWD's
  Stage 0 caught at 4x, arriving here at 3% - **the screen reads the newest FACTS, but the
  newest COVER is a different document.**
- **[E5-20] INVERTS**: capex has been **0.33x-0.68x D&A for four years**, gross PP&E is **91%
  depreciated**, and renewal has moved into **operating leases whose payments are already
  inside OCF.**
- **THE MATERIAL FIND THE SCREEN COULD NOT SEE: $25M of the $65M 2025 operating-cash-flow
  step is the OBBBA R&D-expensing election** - cash tax rate **16.6% against a 26.8%
  five-year mean**, deferred taxes swinging **$27.9M.** Normalized under [E4-41], and it is
  the only place windage is spent.

### THREE TOOLING DEFECTS FROM THIS PAIR, ONE OF THEM A NEW CLASS
1. **A NEW CLASS: `da_annual()` CAN RETURN A BROKEN SERIES WITHOUT RETURNING AN EMPTY ONE.**
   For Certara it returns **2.60, 2.44, 2.13, 1.73, 1.55, 1.99, 75.16** - a **38x
   discontinuity, unflagged** - because the company consolidated two income-statement lines
   in FY2023 and **the tag's semantics changed while the element did not.** The published
   `oe_bottom 28` / `oe_top 35` **reproduce to three decimals off that broken series.** CRWD
   showed the empty case; this is the silent-garbage case, which is worse, **because empty
   fails loudly.**
2. **THE EIGHTH CONSECUTIVE SPREAD DEFECT, and here BOTH ends are the D&A end at two
   windows** - the capex end never entered the row at all.
3. **THE TWO OWNER-EARNINGS PATHS DISAGREE, AND THE QUEUE WAS BUILT FROM THE UNFIXED ONE.**
   `floor_screen.py:capital_acquired()` resolves the $24.8M capitalised-software line
   correctly - **the HAS fix works.** But **`tools/run.py`'s `CAP` list still lacks it, and
   `screen.py` imports from `run.py`.** A fix applied on one path and not the other is worse
   than no fix, because it looks applied.

### THE DENOMINATOR DEFECT — FOUND BY THIS RUN, FIXED AND VERIFIED THE SAME DAY
**`tools/run.py` priced companies on a WEIGHTED-AVERAGE share count.** For Salesforce that
is **956M against the cover page's 823M - a market cap 16.2% TOO HIGH, so every yield the
script printed for CRM was too LOW.** *The flattering direction is not the safe direction
when the question is whether to buy.*

**The basis LABEL had been added on 2026-09-02** from the UAL and WTM runs, and **a label was
not a fix**: a script that announces the wrong basis and then uses it anyway still hands back
a wrong cap. `floor_screen.py` has read the cover element since 2026-09-01, so **the two
owner-earnings paths disagreed on the DENOMINATOR as well as on (c)** - the second such split
found in one day. Now cover-first with the weighted average as a labelled fallback, and a
550-day staleness refusal. **Verified across six filers, and it reproduces the run's finding
to the decimal:**

| | cover (M) | weighted avg (M) | cap overstated by |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CRM | 823.0 | 956.0 | **+16.2%** |
| ORLY | 809.0 | 855.9 | +5.8% |
| QLYS | 34.6 | 36.5 | +5.4% |
| CERT | 152.5 | 160.4 | +5.1% |
| AMAT | 793.6 | 808.0 | +1.8% |

**The defect was systematic, not CRM-specific.** Two limits stated: it **does not sum share
classes** (whether two classes are economically equivalent is a judgment from the charter,
not arithmetic), and **BRK-B returns no cover count at all**, so Berkshire still falls to the
labelled fallback - the insurer SIC gate is what protects that name, not this fix.

### THREE MORE TOOLING FINDINGS FROM THIS RUN, NOT YET FIXED
- **`acquisition_flag()` understates by 51% because stock consideration is invisible to it** -
  the CERT finding, at 100x the scale.
- **The `spread` cell is AGAIN not a capex band: true width 4.32x against 1.52 published** -
  the ninth consecutive run.
- **NEW AND GENERALISABLE: `PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment` understates capital
  consumed by HALF here, because $584M of build-to-suit principal sits in FINANCING**, and
  **`lease_capex_flag()` did not fire.** The rule the run states: **when depreciation far
  exceeds capex, look in FINANCING before concluding under-investment.**
- On the other side, two tools were checked and **passed**: `da_annual()`'s max rule is
  correct at this filer, and **`level_shift` beat `best_year_dep` on the diagnosis.**

### THE HALF-FIX — MY DEFECT, NOT THE SCREEN'S, NOW CLOSED
**The UAL run prescribed a TWO-PART fix to `level_shift()` - guard the negative early mean
AND the near-zero one - and only `earlier <= 0` was implemented.** A near-zero POSITIVE early
mean sails through and the function returns a confident four-digit figure manufactured out of
noise. **A partial fix is worse than no fix, because it now looks guarded.**

**Stated precisely, because the run's framing and the queue's row differ**: the DAL row in
the master queue reads `level_shift 1.73`, computed off the **nine-year OCF series**, and
that number is **correct**. The **2,040x** the run reported arose on **its own
owner-earnings series**, whose early mean is **+$1.167M**. The defect was therefore **real
and latent** rather than visible in the CSV - which is the harder kind to find. Reproduced
and closed: the guard now refuses the ratio when the early mean is **under 5% of the series'
own average magnitude**, and words the direction instead. **Measured: it fires on 1 of 361
queue names (PLTR, which is unrun), and the four regression cases from this function's own
history still return what they should.**

### AND A DEFECT THAT CANNOT BE FIXED FROM HERE, RECORDED AS UNKNOWABLE
**`capital_acquired()` returns ZERO finance-lease additions for DAL FY2024-25** - $184M
actual in 2025 - **because Delta re-tagged the line into `dal:` custom elements, and SEC
`companyfacts` does not expose Delta's namespace at all.** **No tag-list fix can recover
it**, which makes this strictly worse than the UAL case. `lease_capex_flag()` also returns
`None`. Recorded rather than patched around.

**One suggestion from the run, worth taking**: print **current tax provision divided by
pre-tax income** beside every owner-earnings table. It would have flagged this filer at
**1.15% in one glance**, and it adds no judgment - only a ratio of two filed numbers.

## THE FOLD IS NOW A WRITTEN STEP, NOT A REMEMBERED ONE — 2026-09-07

**Audited my own practice against the one the queue file records, and found five runs
missing from it.** A run is written by an agent; the **fold** is done by whoever holds the
session. When the run agent did its own fold the entry appeared in `Screens/WATCHLIST RUN
QUEUE.md`; when the main session did it, the entry came **here** and **the queue file never
learned the run had happened.**

**Measured: AMAT and CRWD were recorded there because their agents wrote them. TXN, QLYS,
CERT, CRM and DAL were missing, and all five were still UNSTRUCK in the tier-2 roster** - so
the queue read as though five completed names were still waiting to be run. **The register
that discharges the operator's instruction of 2026-09-01 was the one being skipped**, and it
carries fields this file does not: the price, the share count and **the cover accession it
came from**, the cap, the sovereign, and the question that closed the file.

All five are now written, with accessions taken from the run files rather than reconstructed
(**TXN `0000097476-26-000152` · QLYS `0001107843-26-000035` · DAL `0000027904-26-000031` ·
CERT's hand-verified cover of 2026-08-01 · CRM's 823.0M cover count**). COMPLETED goes from
**39 entries to 44**. **ORLY was struck as well** - it was already in COMPLETED with a note
saying done, so its unstruck roster entry was a **pre-existing index error**, not anything
from this session. **PINS and PLPC were deliberately left open: both are in flight.**

**The fold is now six written steps** in that file, because **the defect class is the one the
runs keep finding in the tooling: a diagnostic that exists but never reaches the reader.** The
spread caveat lived only in console output. `best_year_dep` threw away its own verdict string.
**The fold lived only in whoever's head was holding the session.** Step 4 carries the QLYS
ruling - **alerts and a PORTFOLIO row are for gate-clearers only**, because a name that failed
at Q2 failed on the BUSINESS and a price alert on it would be a category error.

### PROVENANCE, recorded rather than rebased (operator rule 6)
**The backfill and the new FOLD protocol are committed under `b22acb1`, whose message reads
"PLPC run: below-gate record ..."** - the concurrent PLPC run's `git add -A` swept them in
before my own commit could run. **Verified in HEAD: all 44 COMPLETED entries, the FOLD
section and the roster strikes are present and byte-correct. No content was lost; only the
commit title is wrong.** This is the **fourth** such crossing in this working tree, and like
the others it is recorded here rather than corrected by rebase.

### THE STANDING COUNT — 56 WATCHLIST RUNS
**Gate-clearers, failed at Q5 (22)** · **Q2 OUT (32):** + **PLPC** · **Q4 OUT (1):** ORCL ·
**Q1 UNKNOWABLE (1):** HHH

### THE WRONG-SERIES DEFECT — GENERAL, NOT PLPC-SPECIFIC, AND NOW FIXED
**`level_shift()` and `best_year_dependence()` have always been fed RAW OPERATING CASH, which
does not net capex - so they have been diagnosing the shape of a number the framework does
not value.** On PLPC the two series give **opposite answers**, reproduced here before the fix
was written:

| series ($M) | | | | | | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OCF** | 33.8 | 23.0 | 27.2 | 41.6 | 33.6 | 26.2 | 107.6 | 67.5 | 73.5 |
| **OE at the capex end** | 19.5 | 9.2 | **-6.6** | 13.0 | 11.1 | **-19.0** | 67.4 | 49.4 | 28.4 |

**`level_shift`: 2.68 "STEP UP - normalize down" on OCF, against `None` "EARLY HALF STRADDLES
ZERO" on owner earnings. `best_year_dependence`: 0.154 "one year is doing heavy lifting"
against 0.586 "TWO YEARS JOINTLY CARRY THE WINDOW."** **The PINS guard added earlier the same
day fires correctly here - it simply never got the chance, because it was handed the wrong
series.** That is the **third instance this week of one defect class: a diagnostic that is
sound in itself and never reaches the thing it is meant to judge**, after the console-only
spread caveat and the discarded `best_year_dep` verdict string.

**Both series are now carried** - OCF kept rather than replaced, because a **disagreement
between them is itself a prompt to read.** Measured across the queue: **the two flags
disagree on 80 of 361 names, 22.2%.** So this was never a PLPC quirk.

**And the ratio guard extends to the spread**, on PLPC's own recommendation and DAL's
precedent: **where the bottom is non-positive or under 5% of the top, the `spread` cell now
carries a WORD and a new `spread_dollars` column carries the dollar range.** PLPC's rebuilt
range is **$1.5M to $57.5M**, whose percentage form (**3,733%**) is manufactured by a
near-zero denominator on a series running **-$19.0M to +$67.4M**; the run **refused to
publish the ratio** rather than printing it. The cell is now refused on **119 of 361 names**,
and the dollar range is carried on all 361.

**One brief item, stated accurately rather than accepted**: the run reported that my brief
mis-stated `spread 1.096` as 9.6%. **It did not** - the brief prose read *"the published
110%"*. The real ambiguity is in the CSV itself, where `spread` is a RATIO that reads like a
percentage, and that is what `spread_dollars` now removes.
