## DELL FOLDED IN — 2026-09-07. THE SEGMENT NOTE KILLED WHAT THE CONSOLIDATED NUMBERS SUPPORTED.

### DELL (Dell Technologies) — Q1 IN · **Q2 OUT.** FAIL, on the business. Price $524.14.
`Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - DELL Dell Technologies.md`, 56 ledger ids, all resolving,
`check_framework.py` PASS. Share count **648,107,991** off the cover of the 10-Q filed
2026-06-09, **accession 0001571996-26-000030**; cap **$339,699M**; sovereign **5.24%** (US
Treasury, 2026-09-04).

### THE ARITHMETIC THAT DECIDED IT, AND IT CAME OUT OF THE FILING'S OWN NEW DISAGGREGATION
Dell introduced a **new revenue disaggregation in Q4 FY2026**, splitting AI-optimized servers
out of servers-and-networking for the first time, and publishes ISG and CSG **cost of net
revenue, SG&A and R&D separately**. That makes segment gross margin computable, and the
identity closes to the dollar against filed segment operating income in all three years.

**ISG gross margin: 38.19% → 32.67% → 25.98%. Down 1,221 basis points in two years while ISG
revenue grew 79.5%.** The 10-K names the cause itself, unprompted: *"a shift in mix towards our
AI-optimized servers offerings."*

**Two equations, two unknowns, on the filed segment figures:**

    FY2025:   9,286·m_AI + 34,307·m_other = 14,241
    FY2026:  24,683·m_AI + 36,143·m_other = 15,804
    →  m_AI = 5.37%      m_other = 40.06%

**Back-tested on FY2024, the year not used to fit it: $12,923M predicted against $12,942M
filed — an error of 0.14%.** A two-parameter model that reproduces an out-of-sample year to
fourteen basis points is the structure, not a fitted curve.

**AI-optimized servers run at ~5% gross margin. The rest of ISG runs at 40%. On $22,810M of
incremental AI revenue over two years, ~$1,225M stayed home. Ninety-five cents of every
incremental AI dollar flowed through** — to Nvidia upstream and the hyperscaler downstream.
That is **[E3-62]**'s second step answered from a filed statement, and the textile-loom
sentence — *"Nothing was going to stick to our ribs as owners"* — is the fiscal-2026 ISG
income statement.

### THE COMPETITOR ROW RETURNED THE CLEANEST CORROBORATION THIS QUEUE HAS SEEN
**Super Micro's own filings reach the same number by a different route.** SMCI builds AI
servers and nothing else and carries **zero goodwill and zero intangibles**:
**gross margin 18.01% (FY2023) → 10.82% (FY2026) on revenue up 5.48×**, and **9.20¢ of gross
profit per incremental revenue dollar.** Two independent filers, two independent methods, one
answer: **AI-server assembly is a high-single-digit gross-margin business.** [E3-28] exists for
exactly this.

**And the supplier's side, in fiscal years ending five days apart:** NVDA gross margin
**71.07%** against DELL's **20.00%** — a **51.07-point gap**; NVDA gross profit **$153,463M =
6.76× DELL's entire gross profit** on revenue only 1.90× DELL's; NVDA operating income
**18.3× DELL's ISG segment operating income**; NVDA Data Center revenue alone **3.19× the whole
of ISG**. In FY2021 Dell's revenue was **5.2× Nvidia's**; in FY2026 Nvidia's is **1.90× Dell's**.

**The [E2-45] attacker's test, answered with a filed cost ratio:** DELL operating expenses
**12.82% of revenue** against **SMCI 3.73%** — the attacker runs at **one-third** Dell's cost
structure, is already at $39.1bn of revenue, grew **+77.8%** last year against Dell's +19%, and
compounded **+61.5%/yr over six years** against Dell's **+5.5%**. **[E2-58]'s one exception — a
cost advantage "both wide and sustainable" — is refused by the row.**

### FOUR PRIORS REFUTED, THREE OF THEM IN DELL'S FAVOUR
1. **THE ORCL PRIOR IS REFUTED AND THE DIRECTION IS THE OPPOSITE ONE.** The brief expected the
   financing book to flatter operating cash flow. **DFS financing-receivable growth is an
   OPERATING outflow** (−$2,740M in FY2026) **while the DFS debt that funds it is a FINANCING
   inflow.** Dell's OCF is **understated** by the finance book, not overstated; adding the
   growth back would raise FY2026 owner earnings from $7,829M to $10,569M. **ORCL failed on the
   capital it deployed; DELL fails on the margin it does not keep — opposite mechanisms, and
   assuming the same answer was the trap.**
2. **[E5-08] CONDITION (2) IS SATISFIED ON THE REALISED BUYBACK.** Dell retired **54 million
   shares for $6,031M in FY2026 — an average of $111.69**, with Q4 weighted averages of
   $133.22 / $132.34 / **$118.96** printed in the Item 5 table, against a value band of
   **$90–$230** at the bare bond. **Dell bought at or near the bottom of its own range.** Count
   down **778M → 652M, −16.2%** since the EMC deal. The live risk is prospective only: a further
   **$10bn authorised on 2026-02-26** with the shares at **4.7× the FY2026 average price**.
3. **THE EBITDA FLAG [E4-29] DOES NOT FIRE** — a recorded sweep finds **two** occurrences of
   "EBITDA" in the whole 10-K, neither a headline measure. **[E5-15] does not fire either**:
   $5M / $1M / $10M of stock issuance against $10.7bn of repurchases.
4. **THE CASH CONVERSION CYCLE DETERIORATED, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE PAYABLES LINE
   SUGGESTS.** DSO 38.6 → 56.5, DIO 19.6 → 41.9, DPO 104.2 → 135.1; **CCC −46.0 → −36.7 days.**
   The negative float per dollar of cost **shrank by 9.3 days** while the payables balance grew.

### THE PRIOR THAT HELD: NEGATIVE EQUITY, AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY MEANS
**$(2,470)M at 2026-01-30, WIDENED from $(1,482)M in a year the company earned $5,936M** — but
it is a **buyback artefact, not an accumulated-loss artefact**: treasury stock $(14,533)M
against retained earnings that turned **positive** (+$3,325M) for the first time since EMC.
For **[E5-11](3)** and **[E5-39]** the equity line therefore carries no information and must
not be used. The readable numbers are **core debt $17,018M against $11,528M of cash — net core
debt $5,490M on $8,149M of operating income**, which is not a stretched balance sheet.
**Saying otherwise from the deficit alone would have been the error**, and HPQ's balance sheet
has the identical shape ($(346)M).

### THE THREE FINDINGS FROM THE FLAGS, AND TWO ARE TOOLING DEFECTS
**1. `flags_disagree` was right and the negative year is one balance-sheet line.** The
capex-end negative is **FY2023 at −$369M**, and the cause is **accounts payable −$8,546M**;
every other working-capital line that year was a source of cash. The same line across the
series: **+5,742 → −8,546 → −498 → +1,703 → +12,665.** A **$21.2bn swing**, and it is the
entire distance between Dell's worst owner-earnings year and its best. **Dell's owner earnings
are a working-capital series wearing an earnings series' clothes** — and the two flags
disagree because a nearly constant $2.6–3.0bn capex subtraction from a volatile OCF series
raises the coefficient of variation and pushes the trough through zero. Both flags are correct;
the refusing one is the informative one.

**2. THE ACQUISITION FLAG IS WRONG THREE WAYS AND ONE OF THEM IS GENERAL.** It reported
*"NET CASH INFLOW ($4,237M) — cash acquired exceeded cash paid."* In fact: **(a)** $4,237M is
`sum(abs(v))`, not a net — the note mislabels its own arithmetic; **(b)** the −$3,957M is the
**Boomi divestiture**, which Dell netted into `PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired` in
the FY2022 10-K; **(c)** — **and this is the general defect** — **that value was RESTATED to
+$16.0M in the FY2024 10-K, and the screen is reading the withdrawn one.** `sources.annual()`
writes `if x["end"] not in out`, so it keeps whichever value the companyfacts array presents
**first**, not the one from the newest accession. **This is the INTC withdrawn-input defect,
reproduced on a different name, and it is not specific to either.** The same pattern is visible
on Dell at 2021-01-29 and 2019-02-01, and it also explains why FY2024 consolidated operating
income reads 5,211 in XBRL and **5,411** on the face of the FY2026 10-K.
**THE TRUE PERIMETER: $296M of cash paid for businesses over five years — 0.09% of cap. The
flag overstates it 14× and points the wrong way.**

**3. THE REAL PERIMETER PROBLEM IS DISPOSALS, AND THE HON PRECEDENT FIRES.** The FY2023 10-K,
verbatim: *"**Cash flows for both Fiscal 2022 and Fiscal 2021 are inclusive of cash flows
attributable to VMware, Inc.**"* — the income statement puts VMware in discontinued operations
but **the cash-flow statement is consolidated for all periods presented.** So FY2021's $11,407M
and FY2022's $10,307M of OCF include a business distributed to shareholders on 2021-11-01, with
**$1,004M / $1,523M of D&A, $263M / $329M of capex and $814M / $1,122M of SBC** riding inside
the owner-earnings inputs. **The honest history begins at FY2023 — four years, one short of the
[E2-42] default, and the shortfall is stated rather than repaired by reaching into a period
containing a different company.**

### THE SPREAD CAVEAT — ELEVENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN TO FIND IT LARGER, AND THE SCREEN MIXED WINDOWS
Across **six windows and both (c) ends**: **$3,005M to $7,829M, a 61.6% spread**, against the
published **44%**. And the screen's two figures are **two different windows at two different
capex ends** — `oe_bottom_m 3231` is the **5-year D&A end** (VMware-contaminated), `oe_top_m
4652` is the **3-year capex end**. **The INTC mixed-window defect, on a different name.**
A percentage IS definable here (every construction is positive, unlike DAL and PLPC), but the
honest headline is dollars and a word: **$3.0bn to $7.8bn, and the top of it is one year in
which suppliers extended terms by 33 days.**

### A STALE PRICE IN THE BRIEF'S SCREEN ROW — 13.0%, AND IT FLATTERED THE NAME
The row carried `cap_m 295522`, implying **$455.98/share** against a 2026-09-04 quote of
**$524.14** — **13.0% low**, so every derived field was optimistic. **The quote was corroborated
against a filed figure** rather than trusted: Dell's own Item 5 weighted-average repurchase
prices ($118.96–$133.22 in Nov 2025–Jan 2026, ~$147 in Feb–May 2026) track the feed's closes
($127.80, $119.16, $210.17) exactly. **The stock is 4.8× its 52-week low; it roughly quadrupled
between February and June 2026.** Three runs have now been bitten by quotes; cross-checking the
price against the buyback table is cheap and should be standard where an Item 5 table exists.

### MY OWN DEFECT, FOUND BY FINISHING THE ARITHMETIC AND CORRECTED IN AN ADDENDUM
I first normalised FY2026 by holding **DPO alone** at the prior year, giving −$346M of owner
earnings. **That is one-sided windage — the error [E4-11] names.** Receivables and inventory
moved against Dell in the same year; holding **all three** ratios gives a net **+$588M**, not
+$8,175M, and **ratio-neutral FY2026 owner earnings of $7,241M**. Corrected in an addendum, not
by editing history (operator rule 6). **The substantive finding survives unchanged**; the
magnitude of my own adjustment did not.

### WHAT DELL PASSED, RECORDED BECAUSE [E4-26] REQUIRES IT
**Dell has the highest operating margin of any assembler in the panel (7.18%) and has raised it
in six consecutive years** (4.25 → 4.60 → 5.64 → 6.12 → 6.53 → 7.18). **HPE, the direct ISG
analogue, posted an operating LOSS of $(437)M.** ROUNTA **29.36%** — **but Lenovo's is 29.52%**,
so the one Q2 test Dell passes it does not pass alone, and a metric matched by a direct
competitor is the industry's working-capital structure, not a moat. And the **[E2-26]
half-owner test passes on the segment note**: Dell disclosed, of its own motion, the
disaggregation that makes its own margin dilution visible. **That is the strongest thing in
management's favour in the file, and it is why the run was decidable.**

**The answer to the best bull point:** the rising operating margin is **harvesting**, not a
widening moat. Consolidated operating expenses **fell in absolute dollars** ($15,013M →
$14,558M) on 19% higher revenue; **SG&A fell $11,952M → $11,416M** and **R&D fell from 3.20% to
2.77% of revenue** — against IBM's 12.3% — in the year the product mix shifted hardest in the
company's history. **[E5-23]** requires defending the moat *all of the time*; **[E4-32]**'s
direction test fails while the headline passes.

### THE STANDING COUNT — 58 WATCHLIST RUNS
**Gate-clearers, failed at Q5 (22)** · **Q2 OUT (34):** + **DELL** · **Q4 OUT (1):** ORCL ·
**Q1 UNKNOWABLE (1):** HHH
**Twenty-nine businesses have cleared every gate across the whole project; all twenty-nine
failed on price.**

### NO ALERT ARMED, AND THE REVERSAL CONDITION IS IN WORDS
Per the QLYS ruling of 2026-09-07: DELL failed on the **business**, so a price alert would be a
category error. **The reversal condition: this verdict reverses if ISG gross margin stops
falling while AI-optimized-server revenue keeps rising** — i.e. if the incremental gross margin
on AI servers moves durably out of high single digits — **or if the services annuity resumes
growing with the hardware** (services revenue was $24,072M → $24,147M → $23,133M while product
revenue rose 40.5%). Both are readable from the same segment note in any future 10-K. **Nothing
about the price reverses it.**

## THE WITHDRAWN-VINTAGE DEFECT — found by the DELL run, 2026-09-07, and it moved 117 rows

**`annual()` kept the EARLIEST filing of a restated period, and SEC `companyfacts` carries
every vintage of a restatement under the same period end.** Dell's Boomi divestiture line was
**-$3,957M as originally filed and RESTATED to +$16.0M in the FY2024 10-K, and the screen was
reading the withdrawn one** - which is how `acquisition_flag()` reported a **$4,237M**
perimeter against a true **$296M**. Measured: **278 of 361 priced names carry at least one
restated annual value in the owner-earnings tags.**

**IT IS A PARAMETER, NOT A FIX, BECAUSE THE TWO USES WANT OPPOSITE ANSWERS** - and choosing
one silently is precisely how the look-ahead bug voided four backtests:
- **`earliest`** - what was knowable THEN. Correct for anything anchored in the past, and
  **left as the default so nothing historical changes by my hand.**
- **`newest`** - what is known NOW. Correct for a live screen pricing a company at today's
  quote, where **a restatement is public and reading the withdrawn figure IS the error.**

`regen_queue.py` opts in; `tools/pit.py` remains the real anchor guard, refusing facts by
`filed <= anchor` rather than trusting a caller's flag. **And the same defect existed in BOTH
`tools/sources.py` and `Screens/floor_screen.py`** - the third two-paths split found today,
after capitalised software and the share-count denominator.

**MEASURED ON THE QUEUE: 117 of 361 rows changed** - 32 bottoms, 34 tops, 39 growth-required,
51 `best_year_dep`, 74 `best_year_dep_oe`, 9 acquisition notes. Tier 2 went 154 to 152.

### AND IT EXPLAINS THE CERT "38x DISCONTINUITY" — the root cause was the vintage
Certara's D&A read **2.60, 2.44, 2.13, 1.73, 1.55, 1.99, 75.16** on the earliest vintage.
**On the newest it reads 2.60, 2.44, 2.13, 1.73, 56.07, 68.03, 75.16** - because **the 1.55
and 1.99 were WITHDRAWN pre-consolidation subcomponents and the true totals are $56.1M and
$68.0M.** The series was not merely broken; **it was two different definitions spliced
together, and the screen was reading the retired half.**

**Both fixes stand, and they are complementary**: the vintage recovers the true values, and
`da_discontinuity_flag` **still fires (32.4x, now at 1.73 → 56.07)** because the FY2023
consolidation of two income-statement lines is a **genuine** semantics change that a reader
must go and see. **It fires on the same 7 of 361 names under either vintage.** The CERT run's
diagnosis - *"the tag's semantics changed while the element did not"* - is confirmed, and the
series now shows it honestly instead of hiding it behind a withdrawn number.

**A consequence worth stating: CERT's `3y_da` goes from +$28.2M to MINUS $12.0M**, because
the real D&A exceeds OCF less SBC. That is the CVX/AVGO purchase-accounting finding again -
**the D&A end is unusable on a serial acquirer** - and it does not disturb the CERT verdict,
whose **capex end of $34.4M is unchanged** and is the number that run used.

## LRCX FOLDED IN — 2026-09-07. THE EQUIPMENT COHORT IS COMPLETE, AND ALL THREE FAILED THE SAME WAY.

### LRCX (Lam Research) — `Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - LRCX Lam Research.md`

**Q1 IN · Q2 IN NARROW · Q3 IN (overlay) · Q4 IN GREAT · Q5 FAIL ON PRICE · Q6 not opened.
The twenty-third gate-clearer.** Price **$307.65** (2026-09-04) × **1,251,321,000** shares
(FY2026 10-K cover, 2026-08-04, acc. `0000707549-26-000037`, cross-checked against the
balance-sheet count 1,251,278,000) = **$384,969M**. Sovereign **5.24%**.
Judged owner earnings **$3,457.7M = 0.898%, −4.34 points**. Value ~**$43 / $54 / $75**
zero-growth; ~**$23 / $29 / $40** at the floor. **The floor needs 9.10% perpetual growth.**

### THE COHORT IS THE FINDING, NOT THE NAME

**Three equipment makers, three files, three days. All three cleared every business gate.
All three failed at Q5 on price, by between 3.99 and 4.34 points, at the top of the same
wave.** They disagree about nearly everything else:

| | KLAC | **LRCX** | AMAT |
|---|---|---|---|
| best economics | 56.9% ex-cash return | **81.1% — 1st** | 73.9% |
| best evidence | **the ONLY mix-free [E2-44](1) pass in the cohort** | **no instrument exists at all** | instrument exists, unusable |
| China | flat ~$4.05bn — not de-risking | **all-time high $7.86bn, +26.7%** | **−$1,588M — real de-risking** |
| buyback direction [E5-24] | **reverse** | **FORWARD** | reverse |
| points over the bond | −4.17 | **−4.34 (dearest)** | −3.99 |

**The generalisable lesson: the best business in a cohort is not the one with the best
evidence, and neither is the cheapest.** Lam wins the capital measure by 7 points over AMAT
and 24 over KLA, and it is simultaneously the only one of the three that files **no
instrument capable of testing its own pricing power.** A screen that ranked the three on
return on capital would put Lam first; the framework puts it third on evidence and third on
price.

### WHAT LAM ADDS THAT THE FIRST TWO LEGS COULD NOT

**1. THE ABSENCE-AS-FINDING CASE IN ITS PUREST FORM [E4-25].** Both cohort tests were run and
**both are unrunnable**:
- **The segment gross-margin/ACLS instrument.** Lam files **one reportable segment**, and its
  segment gross margin exists for **three years, all with rising revenue.** That is *both* of
  AMAT's structural defects at once, and Lam is worse placed than AMAT, which has three
  segments with separately filed cost of products sold. **KLA passed this test mix-free
  (+0.57 points on −6.3% segment revenue). Lam cannot take it.**
- **The service/annuity profit-mix test.** **No gross profit, no cost of revenue and no margin
  is filed for the CSBG caption in any of seven vintages**, and the caption **mixes the
  annuity with new Reliant equipment sales** without sizing the split. So Lam's annuity claim
  is **less checkable than AMAT's**, and AMAT's — the only one testable in the cohort —
  **killed the claim** (AGS 33.4% against Semiconductor Systems' 54.2%). Applied to Lam **by
  analogy, labelled as an analogy**. Lam's CSBG is 35.9% of revenue, the largest in the
  cohort; if the analogy holds, Lam's mix is *more* weighted to the low-margin half.

**2. A CONTAMINATED PASS IS NOT A PASS [E4-18].** Lam's gross margin fell in **three of its
four filed revenue declines** — FY2009 (−11 pts and an operating loss), FY2012 (−5.5),
FY2019 (−1.5, on *"lower factory utilization"*, the price-taker signature). **The one pass,
FY2024's +2.7 points, is attributed by the registrant itself to *"a more favorable customer
mix"* in the year ex-China revenue fell 33.6% while China rose 41.0% to 42.2% of the
company.** The run refuses it rather than banking it. **This is the same year that
contaminates KLA's only downturn observation and AMAT's — the whole cohort's single recent
stress test is the China legacy-node pre-buy, in all three names.**

**3. THE FIRST FORWARD-RUNNING BUYBACK IN THE QUEUE, AND IT WAS FOUND AT A FINER RESOLUTION
THAN THE PRIOR RUNS USED.** The KLAC and AMAT runs both read the buyback annually and both
found [E5-24]'s first law *"run in reverse"*. **Lam files a QUARTERLY table with average price
paid per share, and it reverses the finding:**

| quarter | shares (000) | **avg price paid** |
|---|---|---|
| FY2025 Q4 (Jun 2025) | **15,763 ← largest in the record** | **$76.18 ← cheapest** |
| FY2026 Q1 | 9,686 | $105.67 |
| FY2026 Q2 | 9,387 | $153.62 |
| FY2026 Q3 | 3,516 | $210.57 |
| FY2026 Q4 (Jun 2026) | **811 ← smallest in the record** | **$325.14 ← dearest** |

**The price rose 4.3x and quarterly buying fell 95%.** On the ANNUAL series Lam looks like
KLA (largest outlay in the year of the highest average price). **The annual series is the
wrong resolution, and three runs have now used it.** Condition (2) still fails — on the
**level**, because every quarter was above the top of the value band — but the **direction
passes**, and that is a real distinction the queue had not previously drawn.
**Method note for future runs: read Item 5 / the repurchase note quarterly before concluding
on [E5-08] direction. The annual figure can invert the finding.**

### TOOLING — ONE NEW DEFECT AND ONE OLD ONE MADE WORSE

**1. `level_shift` — THE ROW'S CONFIDENCE IS A WINDOW ARTIFACT, AND THE FUNCTION'S OWN
REFUSAL BRANCH IS THE CORRECT ANSWER.** The brief's row read `level_shift 1.68 · level_shift_oe
1.64 · the two AGREE here`. **Both reproduce exactly** as `Screens/floor_screen.py:level_shift`
on a **nine-year** series — which makes the "earlier" half **FY2018–FY2023, already containing
three years of the wave being measured.** They agree because they share a contaminated base;
**agreement between two contaminated measures is not corroboration**, and the brief read it as
reassurance. **Given Lam's FULL eighteen-year filed series the same function REFUSES the
ratio:** *"EARLY HALF STRADDLES ZERO … a ratio against it is undefined in substance even where
it computes (**it gives 3.08x**). **The level HAS changed and the multi-year mean is averaging
TWO DIFFERENT BUSINESSES. READ THE FILING [E4-25].**"* **The refusal is right, it is more
informative than the number, and the reader of the row never sees it** — the defect class the
FOLD note itself names. **Hand-built step on owner earnings: 2.50x.**
**Cohort tally, all understating and all in the same direction: KLAC 1.73 → 3.86 · AMAT 2.0 →
2.74 · LRCX 1.68 → 2.50. Three for three.**

**2. THE SPREAD DEFECT — ELEVENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN, AND THE FIRST WHERE AN END COULD NOT BE
REPRODUCED AT ALL.** `oe_top 4,824` reproduces **to the dollar** as the 3-yr FY2024–26 mean at
the D&A end. **`oe_bottom 3,991` reproduces on NO window at either capex end.** Thirteen
windows run 2,580.5 → 4,512.7 (capex) and 2,636.8 → 4,824.3 (D&A); the nearest constructions
are the 5-yr FY2021–25 mean at the **D&A** end ($3,912.1M) and **FY2024 as a single year**
($3,999.5M) — neither is a bottom end and one is not a mean. **And `tools/screen.py` run live
returns a third answer again (1.16..1.24%).** Previous runs found "two different windows, two
different capex ends." **This one finds one end identified, one end unidentifiable, and a live
tool that agrees with neither.** True width **87.0%** against 20.9%.

**3. A CAPEX LEAK NO TOOL SEES.** The FY2026 cash-flow statement's non-cash schedule shows
**"Transfers of finished goods inventory to property and equipment $125,691"** ($90,873
FY2025; $71,267 FY2024) — **real capital additions that never cross the investing line**, 13.0%
above the filed capex figure. Same shape as UAL's operating-lease leak. Immaterial here;
it would not be on a thinner name.

### TWO DEFECTS IN THE PRECEDENT, RECORDED NOT EDITED (operator rule 6)

Both in `Test Runs/_research 2026-09-07 KLAC/competitor-row.md`. Neither changes that run's
verdict; both would mislead a future reader.
1. **§4.5/§4.6 call Lam's Item 1 "Competition" *"likewise generic"* and say *"Applied and Lam
   name nobody at all."*** **False.** Lam names **seven** companies — Applied Materials
   (twice), ASM International, Wonik IPS, Hitachi, Tokyo Electron (twice), Screen Holdings and
   Semes — in the sentences adjacent to the passage that file quotes. The correct narrow claim,
   which the same file also makes, is that *"the string 'KLA' does not appear anywhere in the
   filing."* **The AMAT run got this right and quoted the naming passage in full.**
2. **§5 records LRCX's China revenue as *"not stated in $"*.** **False.** Note 19 states it in
   thousands in every vintage back to FY2014 ($7,859,811 in FY2026). Only the MD&A summary
   table is in percentages.

### THE STANDING FINDING, UPDATED

**Twenty-three businesses have now cleared Q1 through Q4. Not one has cleared Q5.** The
equipment cohort adds the sharpest version of it yet: **the three names are the 1st, 2nd and
4th best returns on operating capital this queue has measured, and all three are priced
between 3.99 and 4.34 points below a government bond.** That is not three findings about three
companies. **It is one finding about a price level, measured three ways.**

## TWO TOOLING ITEMS FROM THE LRCX RUN, fixed after its own fold — 2026-09-07

### THE WINDOW IS ALSO A CHOICE — the fourth "wrong input" defect in two days
**`level_shift` reads a NINE-YEAR series, and for a long-cycle industry its "earlier half"
already contains part of the current wave** - so the flag agrees with itself **off a
contaminated base.** LRCX reads **1.68 "STEP UP" on nine years and REFUSES the ratio on its
full eighteen** (*"the level HAS changed... READ THE FILING"*).

**Measured: the nine-year and the full series give a different KIND of answer on 25 of 291
names with more than nine years filed (8.6%).** Not a Lam quirk.

**Carried, not chosen.** `level_shift_full`, `years_filed` and a `window_disagree` note now
sit beside the nine-year figures — **which window is relevant is a judgment for the reader,
and operator rule 8 forbids the tool making it.**

**This is the fourth defect in two days of ONE SHAPE: the diagnostic was sound and the INPUT
was wrong.** Wrong series (PLPC), wrong vintage (DELL), wrong aggregate (PINS), wrong window
(LRCX). Worth naming as a class, because the next one will look like the last four: **the
function is fine and it is being handed the wrong numbers.**

### THE .gitignore GAP DELL FOUND, CLOSED BY PATTERN RATHER THAN BLANKET
The research rules covered `.htm/.pdf/.xlsx` but **not `.txt`, so every agent that strips a
filing to text bypassed them silently.**

**Closed deliberately by NAME PATTERN, not by a blanket `*.txt`.** Of 400 tracked research
text files sampled, **190 are over 200KB and are plainly filing dumps — but 76 are under 20KB
and are analysis notes.** A blanket rule would **silently swallow a future run's working
notes, which is a worse failure than a large repository.** Verified both ways: `10K_FY2025.txt`
is ignored, `COMPETITOR_ROW.txt` is not. The **1,192 already-tracked files are untouched**,
because `.gitignore` does not untrack anything.

## UPDATE 2026-09-07 — CGNX (Cognex): Q2 OUT, and the FIRST "STEP DOWN" IN THE READING ORDER

`Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - CGNX Cognex.md`. **Q1 IN · Q2 OUT · Q3-Q6 recorded below the closed
gate.** Price **$62.25** (2026-09-04), 168,223,842 shares off the 10-Q cover (accession
`0000851205-26-000065`), cap **$10,472M**, sovereign **5.24% USD**. `check_framework.py` PASS,
60 ledger ids, 0 phantom citations.

### THE STEP DOWN, ADJUDICATED — the finding the run was commissioned for

Almost every name in this queue has read STEP UP. Cognex read **STEP DOWN on both nine-year
series (0.68 and 0.53) and NO STEP on its full eighteen (1.05).** `level_shift`'s own docstring
calls the low-ratio case the dangerous one. **The answer is that the flag has the direction
right and the object wrong, and the eighteen-year reading is the more nearly correct one.**

**The step is in the MARGIN, not the volume.** Decomposing the $152.5M fall in operating income
from 2021 to 2025: **41% gross margin, 38% operating-expense growth, 21% volume.** Revenue is
within 4% of its 2021 record. What did not come back is the margin.

**And the revenue is partly bought.** The FY2024 10-K discloses Moritex at *"approximately 8% of
total revenue in 2024 and 1% in 2023"* and organic growth of *"1%"*; the **FY2025 10-K withdraws
both**, so a reader of the newest filing alone cannot compute organic growth in the first full
year of a $296M acquisition. Rebuilt from the FY2024 disclosure: **organic 2025 revenue is
roughly $906-916M against a 2021 peak of $1,037M — down 11-13% over four years.**

**Verdict on the step: the owner-earnings step was CYCLICAL and has substantially reversed; the
gross-margin step is PARTLY PERMANENT and has not fully.** H1 2026 printed revenue +20%, GAAP
gross margin 70.9% and operating margin 26.0%. **And the peer row proves the cycle was
industry-wide:** Omron's Industrial Automation segment went 17.8% → **5.4%** → 10.4%; Basler's
EBIT went +13.2% → **−10.8%** → +7.9%. This was not a Cognex event.

### THE RUN CORRECTED ITS OWN ARITHMETIC IN AN ADDENDUM

I wrote Q2 with a **7.6-point** gross-margin step. Then the competitor agent named a document I
had not read — **the earnings releases furnished as 8-K Exhibit 99.1** — which carry an adjusted
gross-margin series the 10-Ks do not: **72.5% (2023) → 69.3% (2024) → 68.9% (2025) → 71.7%
(H1 2026).** **The durable step is about THREE points, not seven and a half.** Corrected in an
addendum rather than by editing the section (operator rule 6), and the verdict re-tested against
it and left unchanged, because the load-bearing findings are [E3-03](2) and [E4-04] and neither
is a claim about margin size.

### WHY Q2 CLOSED IT, AND THE PASS-THROUGH TEST IS THE CLEANEST DISCRIMINATOR THIS QUEUE HAS

**PLPC passed the pass-through test two entries ago and still failed Q2. Cognex fails it at four
consecutive attempts** — 2021, 2022, 2023-24 and 2025, four cost or mix shocks, four margin
losses, and exactly one filed mention of a price increase, which only *"partially offset"* the
cost. PLPC ended its shock **above** where it started.

**[E3-03] criterion (2) fails on the filer's own disclosure**, and this is the sharpest form of
it the queue has produced: **Cognex named Keyence, SICK, Datalogic and Omron in its FY2017,
FY2018 and FY2019 10-Ks and has named nobody since FY2020** — while **Zebra names Cognex,
Keyence and SICK in its FY2022 and FY2025 10-Ks.** Two SEC filers, from opposite sides, describe
the same substitute set. Add the customer's own engineering department, low-cost Chinese
entrants, and *"open-source tools available for free … including tools using AI"*: **seven
classes of substitute, all in Item 1.**

**[E2-44] SPLITS, and the split is the whole company.** Half one fails: 2023-24 was flat demand
with capacity not full, and the filed answer is *"Lower average selling prices due to pricing
pressures."* Half two passes emphatically: **capex is 0.9% of revenue** and net operating
tangible capital of ~$249M earns **~65% pre-tax**. This is a genuinely capital-light business
that cannot price.

**[E4-04] excludes it.** The company calls its own market *"characterized by rapidly changing
technology"* and describes its replacement schedule in its strategy section — rule-based tools,
then a decade of deep learning, then edge learning, then OneVision. **$139M a year buys the next
library; it does not defend the last one.** That is Rhodes Ridge, not Coca-Cola's advertising.

### THE COMPETITOR ROW — the most decisive one this queue has built

Six peers, filing-sourced, same window, every source URL in
`Test Runs/_research 2026-09-07 CGNX/competitor-row.md`.

**Over 2022-2025, Cognex is the ONLY company in its own peer row whose gross margin fell**:
Cognex **−4.9**, Keyence **+1.2**, Zebra **+2.7**, Datalogic **+0.9**, Omron **+0.7**, Basler
−1.0 after winning back 5.2 of a 6.2-point collapse.

**The Keyence comparison is not about the level. It is about what each margin did through the
same cycle.** Keyence's operating margin ran **50.3 / 51.4 / 55.4 / 54.1 / 51.2 / 51.9 / 51.0**
across 2019-2025 — a 5.1-point range — while Cognex's ran 19.7 to 30.4 to 12.6, a 17.8-point
range. **Keyence's worst year beats Cognex's best year by 20 points, and in the 2020 downturn
Keyence's sales fell and its margin went UP.** It does this on **2.8% of revenue in R&D against
Cognex's 14%**, while outspending Cognex in absolute R&D dollars by ~48%. **[E2-58]'s
wide-and-sustainable cost advantage exists in this industry and it is not Cognex's.**

**And National Instruments supplies the mechanism, which is the most transferable finding here.**
Pre-acquisition NI ran a **~70% gross margin, ~20% of sales on R&D, and a single-digit-to-low-
teens operating margin, because selling and marketing consumed 29-35% of sales.** **A 70% gross
margin does not by itself produce a Keyence operating margin.** Cognex's SG&A was **37% of
revenue in 2025** against Keyence's 29.3%. The 35-point gap is go-to-market cost, and it is
structural.

### [E4-55]: NO PHYSICAL SERIES EXISTS — the fourth name in a row

Seven vintages searched for units shipped, unit volume, units sold, installed base and average
selling price. **Zero hits**, except one qualitative FY2024 ASP sentence, never repeated. Cognex
joins **PLPC, KLAC and QLYS**: the honest series does not exist. *(The nearest substitutes that
DO exist: employees, which peaked at 2,992 in the trough year 2023 and are down 8% since; and
revenue per employee, still **21% below** its 2021 peak four years later.)*

### THE FINDING THE 10-K CANNOT SHOW YOU — [E4-29] READS CLEAN AND FIRES AT FULL STRENGTH

**This is the item worth carrying to other runs.** I scored the EBITDA-promotion flag **clean**
from the 10-K: the word EBITDA does not appear in Cognex's FY2025 Form 10-K. **It is the
headline of every earnings release the company furnishes, and the company's stated corporate
objective is an Adjusted EBITDA margin.** The CFO, FY2025 release:

> *"We surpassed our first execution milestone of 20% a full year ahead of plan … our next
> milestone is a **25% Adjusted EBITDA margin — targeted on a run-rate basis by the end of
> 2026**."*

FY2025 **GAAP operating margin 16.3%; Adjusted EBITDA margin 21.5%** — a 5.2-point headline gap
bought with $30.8M of D&A, which **[E5-41]** calls *"reverse float"*, the worst kind of expense
because it is already paid. **PROCESS LESSON: the fifth flag lives in the 8-K exhibit, not the
10-K, and a run that reads only the annual report will score it clean on a company that has
built its public narrative on it.** Worth adding to the standing Q3 checklist for every run:
**pull the latest 8-K EX-99.1 earnings release before scoring [E4-29] and [E4-22]'s third flag.**

*(The honest other half, per [E3-48]: Cognex's guidance has been **beaten** at or above the top
of the range in both periods checked — Q1 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin 16.8% against 12-15%
guided, Q1 2026 revenue $268.4M against $235-255M guided. That is the candid direction of the
projections flag. What survives is [E5-30]'s structural point: a guidance culture is a ratchet,
and this one is now anchored to a metric that deletes depreciation.)*

### DEFECTS FOUND

1. **`tools/run.py`'s D&A tag is DEPRECIATION ONLY and silently drops intangible amortization.**
   It returned $20.3M for CGNX FY2025; the filed statement carries *Depreciation $20,289* **and**
   *Amortization of intangible assets $10,504*. **True D&A is 52% higher.** Since D&A is the
   corpus default for (c) **[E3-44]**, the conservative end of every owner-earnings figure the
   tool printed for 2024-25 was too high by ~$10M/yr. **This will bite any filer with material
   acquired intangibles, which is most acquirers.** *(Same shape as the four defects the LRCX
   fold named: the function is fine and it is being handed the wrong numbers. This is the
   fifth — wrong LINE.)*
2. **The SBC tag returns $1.4M for CGNX FY2020 against a filed $42,661.** The union of
   `ShareBasedCompensation` with `AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense` picked a component.
   **Any window reaching 2020 overstates owner earnings by $41M in that year.**
3. **The queue's cap was 3.6% stale and LOW** (`cap_m 10107` implies $60.08; the strike was
   $62.25). Third consecutive run to find this; PINS was 3.9% and DELL 13.0%.
4. **The published spread of 49.3% is 77.2% on the rebuilt series** over eight windows and both
   (c) ends. **Twelfth consecutive run to find the true width larger.**
5. **A defect in the brief itself, and it is instructive.** The brief said *"Q3/Q4 should be
   short. Do not pad them."* **Q3 carried the single sharpest finding in the file.** Telling a
   run which gate will be boring is how a live [E4-29] flag gets scored clean.

## SHOP (Shopify) — Q1-Q4 IN, Q5 QUIT ON AT THE FLOOR. THE FIRST NAME TO CLEAR ALL FOUR BUSINESS GATES AND FAIL PURELY ON PRICE, AND THE LARGEST CAP DEFECT THE PROJECT HAS FOUND.
*Run: `Test Runs/2026-09-07 Run - SHOP Shopify.md`. Competitor row:
`Test Runs/_research 2026-09-07 SHOP/COMPETITOR_ROW.md`. 108 ledger ids, 0 phantom citations,
`check_framework.py` PASS. Price $145.09 (2026-09-04), cap $186,679M, sovereign 5.24% USD.*

### THE HEADLINE: THE SCREEN PRICED A $187 BILLION COMPANY AT $55 BILLION

`cap_m 54964` against a true **$186,679M — wrong by 3.40x, and the biggest absolute cap error
in the project's history.** Reproduced to the dollar. The mechanism is the LEVI/NKE/DKS/PINS
one in its sixth instance and its worst form: `dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding` has
**zero rows** for Shopify, so `floor_screen.shares_outstanding()` falls through to
`us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding` = **39,310,446 at 2014-12-31**, a count from **five
months before the May 2015 IPO** and **seven years before the June 2022 ten-for-one split**.
Split-adjusted that is 393,104,460, and 393,104,460 x $139.82 = **$54,963,867,000** exactly.

**Two things make this instance different from the five before it, and both are worth
recording:**

1. **The 550-day staleness guard inside `shares_outstanding()` should have caught it and did
   not.** The function ends `return (d, v) if (today - d).days <= 550 else None`, and
   2014-12-31 is **4,268 days** old. The row was nonetheless published with a confident
   four-significant-figure cap. Whatever path `regen_queue` took to a cap, it was not the
   guarded one. **Recorded as a tooling defect, not patched in this run (operator rule 8).**
2. **The filing itself carried the disproof and nobody was looking at it.**
   `dei:EntityPublicFloat` = **$140,315,345,495** at 2025-06-30, in the same `companyfacts`
   payload. **The screen's entire market capitalisation was $85 billion SMALLER than the
   company's own disclosed free float.** A one-line assertion — `cap >= EntityPublicFloat` —
   would have refused this row and would refuse the whole class. **That is the cheapest guard
   available and it is not in the code.** Offered as a suggestion, not applied.

### THE VERDICT SHAPE IS NEW FOR THIS QUEUE, AND THE FOLD RULES HAD TO BE READ CAREFULLY

**Q1 IN, Q2 IN (NARROW), Q3 IN, Q4 IN, Q5 NOT IN — quit on at the [E4-28] floor.** CSL, SHW and
HD reached the same place from tier 2; **SHOP is the first from this queue.** Because it failed
on **price** and not on the **business**, the QLYS ruling of 2026-09-07 applies **in reverse**:
a Q2 failure is a business failure and a price alert on it would be a category error, but a Q5
failure is exactly what a price band is for. **Bands armed at $31 and $60. No PORTFOLIO row —
there is no position and Q5 did not clear.**

### THE BUSINESS FINDING: TWO COMPANIES IN ONE INCOME STATEMENT, FORTY MARGIN POINTS APART

**The AMAT lesson worked again, and this time the segment split did not kill the claim — it
scoped it.** Shopify files gross profit by revenue line and has since 2015:

| | subscription solutions | merchant solutions |
|---|---|---|
| FY2025 revenue | $2,752M — **23.8%** | $8,804M — **76.2%** |
| FY2025 gross profit | $2,232M — **40.2%** | $3,323M — **59.8%** |
| **gross margin, 2017** | **80.2%** | **36.2%** |
| **gross margin, 2025** | **81.1%** | **37.7%** |
| nine-year range | **77.8% - 81.5%, never outside** | 36.2% - 42.9%, now at an eight-year low ex-2018 |

**The franchise is real and it is only a quarter of the company.** The subscription half has an
80%-plus gross margin that has not left a 3.7-point band in nine years and a price increase in
Q2 2023 that stuck. **The other three quarters is a payments spread that has moved 1.5 points
in nine years — and Shopify does not own it.** The FY2025 10-K, Item 1A:

> *"We currently rely on two suppliers to provide the technology we offer through Shopify
> Payments … **the Stripe agreement automatically renews every 12 months, unless either party
> terminates the agreement earlier.**"*

**Sixty per cent of Shopify's gross profit, rising to 61.9% in H1 2026, is a reseller margin on
Stripe's and PayPal's technology under twelve-month cancellable contracts.** That is what held
Q2 to NARROW.

### THE TAKE-RATE ROW IS THE STRONGEST COMPARATOR EVIDENCE ANY RUN HAS ASSEMBLED

**Three independent processors, three volume bases, four to five years each, same direction:**

| | window | from | to | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PayPal, transaction revenue / TPV | 2020-2025 | 2.128% | **1.665%** | **-21.8%, no up year** |
| Block, transaction revenue / GPV | 2020-2024 | 2.934% | **2.746%** | **-6.4%, no up year, then RETIRED** |
| Adyen, net revenue / processed volume | 2020-2024 | 22.54bp | **15.52bp** | **-31.1%** |

**All three name MERCHANT MIX as the cause — larger merchants negotiate the rate down — and
Shopify's own 10-K says "the majority of our gross merchandise volume has been generated from
merchants subscribing to our Shopify Plus plan and enterprise offerings."** Shopify's own gross
take rate is still rising (1.480% to 2.326% since 2018), **but its NET take rate — merchant
gross profit / GMV — added 0.4 basis points in FY2025 on 29.5% GMV growth**, against 23.5
basis points in the three years to 2021.

**And the counterexample was found and recorded at full strength:** Etsy's take rate ROSE 190bp
to 24.2% — **on GMS falling 5.3%.** A marketplace owns the demand and can rake harder; a
platform whose merchant brings the demand cannot. **A row with a contradicting data point in it
is worth more than a row where everything agrees.**

### [E2-49] FIRES THREE TIMES — AFTER FOUR CONSECUTIVE RUNS WHERE THE PREDICTION FAILED

**This is the most important prior to update.** The brief noted that the [E2-49]
metric-switching prediction had failed four runs in a row and told me to check before assuming.
**It fires here, three separate times, and one of them cannot be explained away:**

1. **The merchant count.** Published in the FY2019 40-F (*"from approximately 820,000 … to
   approximately 1,069,000"*) and the FY2020 40-F (*"… to approximately 1,749,000"*), then
   **never again in any SEC filing** — FY2021, FY2022, FY2023, the FY2023 Annual Information
   Form, FY2024, FY2025 and the Q2 2026 10-Q all return zero on a recorded sweep. **It was
   dropped after the year it grew 63.6%, three filings BEFORE the 40-F-to-10-K change, so the
   form change does not explain it. And Shopify still computes it every quarter**: its own MRR
   definition, unchanged FY2019-FY2024, is *"multiplying **the number of merchants** … by the
   average monthly subscription plan fee."*
2. **The Attach Rate.** Introduced as a named KPI in the FY2023 40-F with a definition and a
   two-year table (2.99% / 2.84%) — **nine mentions** — and **gone from the FY2024 10-K**:
   *"Our key performance indicators … are MRR and GMV."* **Zero mentions in FY2024, FY2025 and
   the Q2 2026 10-Q.** Computable anyway from the two surviving series: **+15.3bp (2023),
   +4.5bp (2024), +1.6bp (2025).** Introduced in the year it added 15 basis points, withdrawn
   in the year it added 4.5.
3. **MRR restated DOWN** — FY2023 $149M to $144M, FY2022 $110M to $109M — **while the
   definition paragraph stayed word-for-word identical**, and then the definition itself was
   rewritten in FY2025 to *"the aggregate value of all subscription plans"*, removing the
   merchant count from the formula.

**THE INNOCENT EXPLANATION WAS GIVEN ITS WEIGHT AND IT COVERS TWO OF THE THREE.** Shopify
changed reporting regimes between the two filings — Canadian-form MD&A in a 40-F Exhibit 13, to
US Item 7 in a 10-K. That plausibly explains the Attach Rate and the MRR recalculation. **It
cannot explain the merchant count, which was dropped three years and three filings earlier from
the same document type.** Per [E5-38] the flag reads the accounting and does not judge the
person; it is recorded as a flag and Q3 still returned IN.

### PRIORS REFUTED, AND THE BIG ONE IS SBC

- **SBC was NOT the deciding number, and the brief expected it to be.** Shopify is at
  **22.1% of operating cash flow** — below QLYS's 24.9% which cleared, nowhere near CRWD's
  68.0% which closed the file, and **second-lowest of the nine names in the competitor row**
  behind only Amazon's 14.0%. Its own series improved from 65.1% (2023) to 26.6% (2024) to
  22.1% (2025), **with SBC falling in absolute dollars from $615M to $449M while revenue rose
  64%.** A genuinely good number.
- **The HAS/CRWD capitalized-software defect does NOT exist here** — recorded sweep of five
  vintages; the policy exists but the investing section carries exactly one capital line and
  there is no `PaymentsToDevelopSoftware` tag in `companyfacts` at all. **Capex is 0.22% of
  revenue and net PP&E is $53M.**
- **The [E4-29] EBITDA flag does NOT fire — zero mentions in the FY2025 10-K and in both
  earnings releases**, which for a company of this profile is genuinely creditable. **But the
  same species of deletion is present under another name:** "free cash flow", 21 mentions in the
  Q4 2025 release, guided quarterly, defined as OCF less capex — **so it deducts $26M of capex
  and none of the $449M of SBC. Shopify's headline cash measure overstates owner earnings by
  28.8%.** *(This is the CGNX process lesson applied: pull the 8-K EX-99.1 before scoring
  [E4-29] and [E4-22]'s third flag. It paid — the 10-K alone would have scored this clean.)*
- **The [E4-30] fraud tells do NOT fire, in the harder direction.** Cash taxes paid rose
  $50M / $116M / $194M against operating income of $(1,418)M / $1,075M / $1,468M — **10.8% to
  13.2%, rising** — and reported growth is the opposite of smooth: net income reads +$2,915M,
  **-$3,460M**, +$132M, +$2,019M, +$1,231M.

### THE WINDOW JUDGMENT — AND THE FIVE-YEAR DEFAULT CANNOT BE RUN

**The brief said the three `n/a` level tests and `best_year_dep_oe 1.271` say the mean is
averaging two different companies, and told me to decide which years describe the business that
exists. THE ANSWER IS THAT THERE ARE FOUR, AND THE BREAK THAT MATTERS IS NOT 2020 — IT IS MAY
2023.** Pre-monetization (2013-19, negative every year); the pandemic (2020-21); **the logistics
company (2022 - H1 2023)**; and what exists now (H2 2023 onward). Three filed events in six
months define the boundary: the **logistics disposal in Q2 2023** (a PERIMETER event — the HON
precedent binds), the **23% workforce reduction in May 2023**, and a **D&A series that steps 93
to 70 to 36 to 31** as the assets left with the divestiture.

**So the business that exists now is 2.5 years old and [E2-42]'s five-year default window CANNOT
BE RUN on it.** That is reported as the finding rather than resolved by picking a window. **A
five-year mean here averages a pandemic year, a $1,754M acquisition, a $1,340M write-off, a 23%
redundancy programme and two years of the current company.**

**`best_year_dep_oe 1.271` is confirmed as the highest in the 361-name queue — and it
UNDERSTATES the problem.** The 9-year owner-earnings mean is **$250.0M**; drop the best two
years and the remaining seven average **MINUS $66.5M**. It does not move 127%; **it changes
sign**, so a percentage is not really definable — the DAL/TTSH shape again.

**Spread caveat, thirteenth consecutive run:** the published `spread 1.163` is **four
constructions out of twenty-six**. True width **$160.9M to $1,558.0M = 868%**, or 525%
restricted to the multi-year windows.

### THE (c) JUDGMENT THAT MATTERS, AND IT IS NOT THE CAPEX BAND

**The capex band is $5M wide — 0.25% of operating cash flow — and cannot change any answer.**
The judgment that matters is **[E2-23]'s working-capital clause**, and it is worth **$579M a
year**: **Shopify's lending book grows through the INVESTING section** ("purchases and
originations of loans", $4,014M gross in FY2025), **so operating cash flow never nets it.** The
conventional construction gives FY2025 owner earnings of $1,558M; deducting the lending
increment gives **$979M**. **Both are published and the guess is disclosed as a guess.**

**AND THE FILER MADE IT WORSE MID-RUN.** The Q2 2026 10-Q footnote: *"**Starting in April 2026**,
the cash flows associated with merchant cash advances are presented **within investing cash
flows**…"* — **and the comparatives were NOT restated** (verified: the Q2 2025 10-Q as
originally filed and the Q2 2026 10-Q both show H1 2025 OCF of $795M). **Every future operating
cash flow is larger than it would have been, with no restated history to measure against.** The
full-capital construction used in the run is immune to it by design, which is why it was built.

### THE NUMBER THAT CLOSES THE FILE, AND IT IS NOT THE YIELD

The yield is 0.35% to 1.00% against a 5.24% bond, which is bad enough. **But the decisive
arithmetic is the growth-adjusted expectancy**, because a low current yield on a business
growing GMV at 29.5% is not automatically a bad investment and the run had to prove it:

| owner-earnings growth for TEN YEARS, then 3% forever | expectancy at $145.09, from $648M | from $1,227M |
|---|---|---|
| 15% a year — the [E4-35] fewer-than-1-in-20 event | 4.10% | 5.02% |
| 20% a year | 4.63% | 5.93% |
| 25% a year | 5.35% | 7.11% |
| **30% a year, for a decade** | **6.28%** | **8.55%** |

**Thirty per cent compound owner-earnings growth for ten years still returns under 9%.** Stated
as a business rather than a rate: a 10% return on the $175,794M enterprise value needs
**$17,579M** of steady-state owner earnings, which at a **25% mature margin** implies revenue of
$70,318M and — at today's 3.054% attach rate — **$2.30 trillion of GMV, 6.1x the $378bn Shopify
facilitated in FY2025.**

### THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE CONCLUSION, RECORDED [E4-26]

**Shopify is the only profitable independent participant in its own industry, and it is not
close.** GAAP operating margin: **Shopify 12.7%, Wix 0.09%, BigCommerce (4.7)%**; Squarespace
was taken private. Owner earnings: **Shopify $1,558M, Wix $336M, BigCommerce NEGATIVE $6.7M.**
It earns **149.5% pre-tax on unleveraged net tangible operating assets [E2-43]**, carries **zero
debt and $10,885M of cash and investments**, spends **0.22% of revenue on capex**, and grew
revenue **30.1%** and GMV **29.5%** in the most recent year. **If the price were a third of what
it is, this file would read very differently — which is precisely what the two armed bands are
for.**

### DEFECTS FOUND

1. **THE CAP, 3.40x, AND THE GUARD THAT DID NOT FIRE.** Detailed above. **Suggested cheap fix,
   offered not applied: assert `cap >= dei:EntityPublicFloat` where the float is present.** It
   would have refused this row and refuses the whole class.
2. **The queue's price was two trading days stale** ($139.82 against $145.09, 3.8% low).
   Fourth consecutive run to find this; **and here it is the smaller error by a factor of
   eighty.**
3. **The published spread is four constructions out of twenty-six.** Thirteenth consecutive run.
4. **`best_year_dep_oe` throws away a sign change.** 1.271 is reported as a percentage on a
   series whose leave-two-out mean crosses zero ($250.0M to -$66.5M). Same class as the DAL and
   TTSH rows: **a ratio is printed where the honest output is "it changes sign".**
5. **A defect in the FILER, not the tooling, and it is the one to carry forward:** the April
   2026 merchant-cash-advance reclassification with unrestated comparatives. **Any run on a
   platform lender should test whether the working-capital increment of the loan book is inside
   or outside operating cash flow, and whether that has changed.**
6. **A defect in the brief, and it is small: the brief said "[E5-11] should be short. Do not pad
   it." That was right** — staying power took eight lines and all three strengths pass
   overwhelmingly. **But the same brief said SBC was "likely the deciding number", and it was
   the third-best number in the file.** Telling a run in advance which number will decide is the
   CGNX lesson in a new shape: **it did not cause an error here because the run computed it
   anyway, but the prior was wrong and the brief was confident.**

### THE CAP GUARD — the hand overrides never scaled, and this is the systematic replacement
**The queue's cap for SHOP was 3.40x too small** ($54,964M against $186,679M), reproduced to
the dollar from a **2014-12-31 PRE-IPO count of 39,310,446** times the 2022 split. That is
**the PINS defect exactly** (4.06x, same cause), and `HAND_CAPS_M` had caught four names by
hand - **SHOP was not among them, and hand overrides do not scale.**

**The run's own suggestion is the fix, and the number was sitting in the same payload the
whole time: a market capitalisation cannot be smaller than the company's own filed PUBLIC
FLOAT, because the float is a SUBSET of shares outstanding.** `dei:EntityPublicFloat` now
guards every row.

**It FLAGS rather than refuses, per operator rule 8**: the float is itself a filed number
that can be wrong - **MCFT reports one 607x its cap, which is a tagging error rather than a
cap error** - and deciding which of the two is broken is **a reading, not an arithmetic**.
**Fires on 80 of 361 names**, including SHOP, **PINS (whose hand override is itself stale at
a 2026-09-02 quote)** and **ACVA, which is still unrun.**

**Also recorded from this run**: the price was two days stale, the published spread was **4 of
26 constructions (true width 868%)**, and **`best_year_dep_oe` printed a ratio across a sign
change** - a fifth instance of the ratio-across-zero class, in the one flag that had not yet
been guarded for it.

### AND ONE STEP OF ITS OWN FOLD WAS MISSED, CORRECTED HERE
The run armed both price bands correctly but **did not add the `PORTFOLIO.md` row**, which
step 4 requires for a gate-clearer. Added. **First fold-step miss since the six steps were
written down this morning**, which is the argument for having written them down.

bond. Value **~$8–$19/share at the sovereign, ~$4–$10 at the floor**; **forty per cent
compound growth for ten years reaches the floor at this price.**

- **THE FINDING THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS NAME: [E3-03] CRITERION (2) CAN BE READ OFF AN 8-K.**
  On 2026-08-18 Marvell issued Google a warrant on **58,970,907 shares at $206.58** —
  6.6% of the company — vesting *"in 240 equal tranches, with one tranche vesting for each
  $500 million in Custom Products revenue"* from Google's *"discretionary purchases."* A
  product with no close substitute does not need its supplier to pay the customer for
  volume. **This is [E4-37]'s agony-of-pricing metric at its extreme, and it closed Q2 on
  Marvell's own filing, not on a competitor's.** The brief's prior (OUT, held weakly) was
  upheld on ground the brief did not anticipate: it expected the concentration series and
  the merchant competitor set to carry the verdict; they support it, but the warrant
  decides it.
- **THE CONCENTRATION SERIES ACROSS VINTAGES, as instructed:** ten largest customers **56%
  (FY2022) → 63% → 72% → 81% → 82% (FY2026)**; Distributor A **12% → 44%** of the latest
  quarter; two customers **61%** of Q2 FY2027. The AI business concentrated the customer
  base; it did not diversify it. Marvell has never named either customer in any vintage.
- **[E2-63] — AI REVENUE ARRIVES WITH MARGIN, AT A FALLING RATE.** Not the DELL shape.
  Non-GAAP gross margin **60.5% (Q3 FY2025) → 58.9% (Q2 FY2027) → guided 57.5–58.5%**
  while revenue went $1.5bn → $2.7bn → $3.15bn a quarter: **incremental non-GAAP gross
  margin ~57%, and ~52% on the Q3 FY2027 guide**, where management says the custom ramp
  *"significantly accelerates."* GAAP gross margin rose 41.3% → 51.0% only because $942M of
  fixed amortisation is spread over more revenue. **The DELL prior was refuted on the
  level and confirmed on the direction.**
- **THE D&A STEP WAS THE CERT DEFECT, AND THE BRIEF'S CAUSE WAS RIGHT WHILE ITS MAGNITUDE
  WAS A TOOL ARTEFACT.** Marvell files two D&A lines in every vintage. The screen spliced
  `DepreciationAndAmortization` (FY2021: 197.9, the PP&E line *excluding* acquired
  intangibles) onto `Depreciation` + `AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets` (FY2022: 1,092.9)
  and printed 5.5×. **Filed totals: 641.5 → 1,245.3, a 1.94× step, and it is Inphi**
  ($9.9bn, April 2021, $4.4bn of intangibles on 5–8-year lives). The spliced FY2022 figure
  is also $152M below the filed total because `Depreciation` (113.5) is not the
  "Depreciation and amortization" line (265.9). **The brief's fix-note ("prefers a filed
  D&A total, sums components only when none exists") does not rescue it: no total tag
  exists for Marvell, and the component fallback uses the wrong depreciation tag.**
- **THE (c) DECISION — the AVGO ruling, decided, and it lands in the same place by a
  different route.** D&A end is the CONSERVATIVE end (3.6× capex; $942M of it acquisition
  amortisation), as at AVGO. **But Marvell is not Broadcom on the physical side**: its
  depreciation line (348.6) is *below* capex (354.1), capex is 4.3% of revenue and up 4.3×
  in seven years, and **it pays $128–154M a year for capitalised IP licences through the
  FINANCING line** — renewal cash invisible to both OCF and investing capex, and the very
  asset class the FY2025 restructuring wrote off. **(c) = capex plus technology-licence
  cash (~$450–487M)**: above bare capex because the physical spend is rising [E5-20];
  below the D&A end because acquisition amortisation renews nothing that 25.3%-of-revenue
  R&D does not already renew (QCOM → AVGO → CRM → here). **The stronger objection is
  carried, not priced:** Marvell *bought its growth line* — Inphi is half of data-centre
  revenue — and ~$22bn of acquisitions produced $3.6bn of cumulative capex-end owner
  earnings. If buying the next technology every two years is maintenance, (c) is
  enormous. That reading went to Q2 as [E4-04]'s continuously-rebuilt moat and to Q4 as
  the named death.
- **THE PERIMETER: the flag understated it for the fifth consecutive run, and it moved again
  after the 10-K the screen read.** Investing cash for Inphi/Innovium was $3,555M; filed
  consideration $10.9bn, **$7.2bn of it stock**. Then **Celestial AI ($3.5bn + an earnout
  now marked $749.5M, up from $315.8M because it is payable in shares and the shares rose)
  closed 2026-02-02**, three weeks after the year end. Every owner-earnings figure is
  Marvell-without-Celestial divided by a cap with it. Pro formas: filed for Inphi (FY2021
  pro forma net loss $1,351M); not yet for Celestial. And the automotive business ($2.5bn
  to Infineon, August 2025) runs through continuing operations with its $1,830M gain in
  "interest income and other" — which is why FY2026 net income of $2,670M is a disposal.
- **[E2-49] FIRES:** four end markets (enterprise, carrier, consumer, auto/industrial) fell
  **51% in FY2025** ($3,291M → $1,603M) and were **merged into one line in Q4 FY2026**. The
  honest counter (automotive sold; merged line +31%) is recorded.
- **BELOW THE GATE, RECORDED NOT SCORED:** [E4-29] reads **zero** in the 10-K and fires at
  full strength in the releases (**GAAP EPS $0.33 vs non-GAAP $0.94, a 2.85× wedge**) — the
  CGNX shape — **and the AIP pays 50% on non-GAAP margins** (corporate achievement 144.84%).
  Guidance record **seven for seven, beats of 0.3–1.4%** on 37–63% growth — Broadcom's
  three-for-three shape. **Diluted shares 668.8M (FY2021) → 869.7M (FY2026) → 921M guided
  (+37.7%) after $3.4bn of buybacks.** GAAP ROE negative in every one of the five clean
  years; both positive years are disposals. [E2-43]: 19.6% on net tangible operating
  assets, **6.8% on what was paid**. **CFO resigned 2026-06-10 and was replaced the same
  day by the Audit Committee chair.** The Data Center Group president was paid $48.4M in
  FY2026, nearly twice the CEO. Staying power: strength (3) fails on **$8.5bn of
  unconditional foundry commitments** written against revenue two customers have not yet
  ordered; [E2-54] coverage passes at 7.1×. Named death: half of Distributor A's channel
  lost at a program transition ≈ $1.3bn of gross profit, exceeding FY2026 operating income
  — **a real possibility**, in the 10-K's own words (*"this trend may continue to
  proliferate"*).
- **THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT:** the optical-DSP franchise is real — ~50% CAGR
  for five years, half of data-centre revenue — and its visible merchant rivals (Credo,
  Astera) are a tenth of Marvell's size; NVIDIA and Google, who could build or buy what
  Marvell sells, put $2bn of preferred and a seven-year agreement into it instead. If the
  custom business is a door-opener for an interconnect franchise the hyperscalers have
  decided not to build, Q2 is NARROW, not NONE. The run's answer is that the same documents
  show the product margin falling as the door opens and the counterparties taking equity
  rather than paying price. **Reversal condition recorded in words in the REGISTER; no
  alert, no PORTFOLIO row (the QLYS ruling).**

### DEFECTS IN THE BRIEF AND THE TOOLING, FROM THIS RUN
1. **`newest_filing 2026-01-31` was two 10-Qs stale** at brief time (Q1 FY2027 filed
   2026-05-28; Q2 filed 2026-08-28). The row missed a $3.5bn acquisition, a $2bn preferred
   issue and a 59M-share customer warrant. **The screen should carry the newest 10-Q date,
   not the newest 10-K.**
2. **`cap_m 184491` was 8.2% low** on an 825.3M count against 898.7M economic (876.9M cover
   + 21.8M as-converted preferred). Fifth share-count miss. **And a new class: a convertible
   preferred that the issuer itself counts in basic EPS is not in
   `EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding` and never will be.** The cap guard needs a
   preferred-as-converted rung.
3. **The D&A splice is the CERT defect recurring, and the 2026-09-07 fix does not cover
   it**: the component fallback pairs `Depreciation` with `AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets`,
   but Marvell's cash-flow "Depreciation and amortization" line is tagged
   `OtherDepreciationAndAmortization` (FY2022+) / `DepreciationAndAmortization` (FY2023-
   and earlier), and `Depreciation` alone is $127M short of it in FY2026. **The fallback
   should prefer the cash-flow-statement line tag over the income-statement `Depreciation`
   tag, and `da_note` should print both series it spliced.**
4. **The perimeter flag reads the investing line; Inphi was 67% stock.** Fifth consecutive
   understatement. The fix is the same one named at CRM: read
   `NoncashOrPartNoncashAcquisitionValueOfAssetsAcquired1` / the business-combination note,
   not `PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired`.
5. **A renewal cost that lives in FINANCING.** Marvell's *"Payments on technology license
   obligations"* ($128–154M a year) is capitalised IP the business must keep buying, and it
   sits below both OCF and investing capex. No tool reads it. Any fabless designer with
   licence obligations (ARM cores, SerDes IP, EDA) will have the same line; **the (c)
   construction should sweep financing for `PaymentsForRepurchaseOf`-style renewal
   items and print them.**
6. **The brief's `growth_required 10.20%` was computed on a negative bottom** and is
   meaningless there; the row's own words ("n/a") were right and the number should have
   been suppressed with them.

### SIX TOOLING FINDINGS — two fixed, two tested and REJECTED on the data, two recorded as limits
1. **FIXED - the annual date hid two 10-Qs.** `newest_filing 2026-01-31` was the newest
   ANNUAL period end, while a $3.5bn acquisition (Celestial AI, closed 2026-02-02, three
   weeks after the 10-K the screen read), a $2bn preferred and a 59M-share customer warrant
   sat in two later 10-Qs and an 8-K. A `newest_periodic` column now sits beside it. **A later
   periodic filing exists beyond the annual date on 357 of 361 rows.**
2. **FIXED - `growth_required` on a negative bottom is arithmetic on nothing.** The row
   printed 10.20% from a bottom of -$373M. Now refused in words, sorted to the end. **Refused
   on 120 rows.**
3. **REJECTED on the data - "prefer `OtherDepreciationAndAmortization`."** Tested against
   Marvell's own facts: that element reads **265.9 in FY2022 and 348.6 in FY2026 against
   filed totals of 1,245.3** - it is not the cash-flow total either. What the facts show is a
   filer using the TOTAL element `DepreciationAndAmortization` for a PP&E-only figure (197.9)
   and tagging no intangible amortisation at all in FY2021. **No tag rule recovers a number
   the filer did not tag; `da_discontinuity_flag` fired at 5.5x and the reader read the
   filing, which is the designed outcome.** Not adopted.
4. **REJECTED on the data - a consideration tag for the perimeter flag.** Tested
   `BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1` and its equity-issued sibling on CRM, CERT,
   MRVL and AVGO: **none resolves undimensioned in companyfacts.** Only the investing-cash
   line exists - the very thing the flag already reads. Stock consideration lives in
   dimensioned per-acquiree facts that the payload strips. **The fifth consecutive
   understatement is a limit of the source, not of the rule, and it is now recorded as such.**
5. **RECORDED - a share class the cover cannot see.** Convertible preferred that the issuer
   counts in basic EPS is invisible to `EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding` (8.2% here). A
   weighted-average-versus-cover test over-fires on every buyback company, so no guard is
   added; the run's own reading of the EPS denominator is the method.
6. **RECORDED - a renewal cost that lives in FINANCING.** `Payments on technology license
   obligations` is a company-extension element; no us-gaap tag reaches it. **Every fabless
   designer with IP licence obligations will carry it**, and only a reader finds it.

### DEFECTS IN THE BRIEF AND THE TOOLING, FROM THIS RUN
1. **"A pharma company's R&D IS its (c)" conflates two rules.** R&D is expensed above OCF and is
   already out of owner earnings; the question it raises is [E4-04]'s (defend or replace), not a
   (c) adjustment. Subtracting it again would double-count; adding it back manufactures a
   run-off value. The run kept the two apart and labelled the run-off computation as such.
2. **The screen cannot see [E3-70], and that is where this name's width is.** Whenever SBC/OCF
   exceeds 50%, the row should print grant-date SBC (options granted x WAGDFV + restricted
   granted x WAGDFV) beside the charge. On CORT it turns a 5.1% spread into 2.2x and a
   positive 2025 into a negative one.
3. **The brief's generic prior assumed volume loss.** The effect was price, and the instrument
   the brief itself named ([E4-55], the filed decomposition) found it. Briefs should ask "price
   or volume" rather than assume.
4. **No tool reads guidance against outturn.** 37 8-K exhibits were read by hand; the 2025 miss
   of a twice-cut range is the sharpest Q3 finding and would be invisible to any XBRL screen.
5. **Restated comparatives.** The FY2025 10-K carries 2024/2023 OCF at $198,295k / $126,681k;
   the as-filed years and XBRL carry $198,067k / $127,039k. Under $0.4M, immaterial, recorded
   because the two sources disagree silently.
6. **The row's regulatory-status framing ("approved, under review, or refused") had no slot for
   "all three."** Two indications, two answers, ten weeks apart; the brief should ask per
   indication.

### STANDING COUNT RECONCILED — 2026-09-11 (written by the SNPS run)
SNPS and CORT folded concurrently on 2026-09-11 and **both headers took "sixty-three"**; neither
session could see the other's fold at write time. The count after both is **64 watchlist runs**:
**gate-clearers, failed at Q5 (25):** + SNPS · **Q2 OUT (37):** + CORT · **Q4 OUT (1):** ORCL ·
**Q1 UNKNOWABLE (1):** HHH. The two blocks above are left as written per operator rule 6; this
line is the correction. The collision is the crossed-commit defect the queue's fold rule names,
in its count form: a running total kept in a shared file cannot be incremented safely by two
sessions at once, and the honest fix is to recount from the `## COMPLETED FROM THE QUEUE`
entries at each fold rather than increment the previous header.

### CORT'S TOOLING SUGGESTION, TESTED AND RECORDED AS A LIMIT — 2026-09-11
The run asked the screen to **print grant-date SBC beside the charge whenever SBC/OCF exceeds
50%**, because that is where Corcept's width lives: **[E3-70]'s grant-date measure puts 2025
owner earnings at MINUS $43.7M** (grants $184.5M against an $84.5M charge; $227.5M of option
intrinsic value realised) where the charge-based construction reads +$90M. Tested against
companyfacts for CORT, CRWD and PINS: **no grant-date total resolves undimensioned in USD** -
the element family carries per-share weighted-average fair values and dimensioned per-plan
facts the payload strips. **The second source limit found this week after stock consideration;
only a reader reaches it.** Recorded in the flag's own terms: a run on a name with SBC/OCF
above 50% reads the grant table by hand.

**Three brief defects, mine, from the same run**: *"a pharma company's R&D IS its (c)"*
conflated two rules - R&D is above the OCF line already, and the question is [E4-04]'s
depleting-asset one, not a (c) adjustment; the generic prior assumed VOLUME loss where the
filed price/volume decomposition showed **tablets +37% and 18 points of realised PRICE lost**,
so the question to brief is *"price or volume"*; and *"approved, under review, or refused"* had
no slot for **all three at once, by indication** - which is what relacorilant is. **And a
reassurance the brief did not expect: [E4-29] is CLEAN across all 37 8-K exhibits** - the
CGNX check was run and passed. Guidance-against-outturn ([E3-48], fired hard: 2025 guided
$900-950M, cut twice, actual $761.4M below the twice-cut range) has no tool and needs none;
thirty-seven exhibits by hand produced the sharpest Q3 finding.

### SNPS — a correction to MY reading, two errors in my resume message, and a fix that had not taken
**I reported SNPS as "the first name to clear all four gates and return UNKNOWABLE at Q5." It
did not.** The run's verdict line copied KLAC's form - *"[x] UNKNOWABLE is NOT used"* - and my
grep read the ticked box as the verdict. **Q5 is a FAIL on price**: judged owner earnings
$1,500M = 1.97% on a $76,112M cap, quit on at the floor; zero-growth value ~$75 / ~$145 /
~$175; alerts armed at $175 and $145, PORTFOLIO row added. **The twenty-fifth gate-clearer.**
The run reworded its line so no box is ticked. The lesson is the one the runs keep teaching
me: **a parser that reads a form is not a reader.**

**Two errors in my resume message.** I told the run *"the pro forma 8-K/A is already in your
folder, so the AVGO shortcut IS available"* - on the strength of a filename. **The file named
`SNPS_8KA_ANSYS_PROFORMA` is a committee-appointment amendment.** The real pro forma is in 10-K
Note 4 (combined FY2025 revenue +5.6%) and gives no OCF. I trusted a name I had not opened,
which is the exact error operator rule 4 exists to prevent. And I briefed 5.24% as the
sovereign after the daily fetch had already printed 5.37% - the run re-struck it.

**A fix that had not taken.** The DELL vintage fix made `vintage` a parameter with the default
left at "earliest" so nothing historical would change by my hand - and `tools/run.py`, a LIVE
tool, was never switched. **It read Synopsys's ORIGINAL FY2024 capex ($123.2M) rather than the
restated $139.5M.** Every `annual()` call in `run.py` now goes through the newest vintage. The
fourth two-paths split in five days.

$17.6bn cash and $17.1bn in 30.0M shares** (the flag saw $16.7bn). **Every historical window
priced a company that no longer exists** - pre-Ansys numerator, post-Ansys cap, the HON
mirror. The first full-perimeter year is the TTM to 2026-07-31, **$1,798M, 2.2x the top of the
screen's band.** And (c): depreciation $171.9M against capex $169.5M, with **89% of TTM D&A
Ansys amortisation - so the D&A end reads MINUS $35M for FY2025 and is INVALID, not
conservative**, which refutes the AVGO analogy I briefed.

**Cadence out-earns Synopsys in every one of ten years** (86.4%/28.2% against 77.0%/13.0%),
and no seat, unit or price series is filed - the fifth consecutive absence. **NARROW, not "the
widest in the queue."** The nearest miss among recent gate-clearers: **TTM plus 8% growth
clears the floor at 10.4%**, and the run pre-registered its confirmer - the guided year plus
two years of 10%+ owner-earnings growth with SBC held at 10% of revenue.

### PAY — the seventh pre-IPO count, and where the float guard cannot reach
**Q1 IN · Q2 OUT**, price **$36.28** x 125,939,647 cover shares = **$4,569M**. The run did
its own six-step fold, verified. **The queue's `cap_m 3635` reproduces exactly as $35.13 x
103,479,239 - the PRE-IPO 2020-12-31 count - the seventh instance of the PINS/SHOP mechanism,
20.4% under.** The public-float guard could not see it: **a sponsor-controlled float (Accel-KKR
58.2% of votes) is legitimately far smaller than the cap**, so cap-above-float holds even when
the cap is wrong. **The guard catches the case where the count is off by multiples; it cannot
catch a fifth on a controlled company.** Recorded as a limit; the run's own cover read is the
method.

**The finding is the unit series the queue kept lacking, and it decided Q2**: transactions
**146.2M → 724.0M (2019-2025)**, and **contribution profit per transaction $0.661 → $0.534,
down 19%**, while revenue per transaction rose 2.5% purely on pass-through. The filer wrote
*"mix shift to larger, high volume clients"* four 10-Ks running and says in Item 1 *"We also
compete on pricing."* Of each revenue dollar in 2025, **67.7c goes to the networks and 32.3c is
kept**, down from 41.0c in 2019. Gross recognition confirmed in the filer's own words.
**SBC/OCF 11.5% - the lowest in the calibrated row.** Customer funds are **off balance sheet**
($215.7M custodial), so my float-flattering prior was refuted. [E2-49] fires (biller count
withdrawn FY2025 - the tally is now 2 fires to 6 fails); [E4-29] fires in the releases
(*"record adjusted EBITDA margin 41.3%"* is adjusted EBITDA over CONTRIBUTION PROFIT; 13.5% on
GAAP revenue). **Strongest fact against**: JPMorgan, U.S. Bank and PayPal resell the platform
rather than build, and JPM signed revenue minimums through 2026 and took warrants.

**A tooling tension recorded, not resolved**: the CGNX max-rule for SBC picks the larger tag,
and where the larger tag includes SBC that was CAPITALISED into software - which (c) already
carries through the capitalised-software line - the subtraction double-counts. No tag
distinguishes expensed from capitalised SBC undimensioned. The reader nets it from the
cash-flow statement. And **the run found a `` byte its own roster regex had written over
`~~SHOP~~`, and corrected it** - verified intact.

The run did its own six-step fold. **Q1 IN . Q2 OUT.** Price **$96.91** x 59,007,996 shares

$60-90 only if 15% compounds for a decade**, all under `COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE`.
