question loss: the write-early protocol and a scratchpad of drafted sections carried it.

### WHAT THE RUN FOUND, IN THE ORDER THE BRIEF ASKED

1. **The perimeter is 44-74% larger than the flag, and this filer hides consideration in a
   THIRD place.** Naturium $333.0M and rhode $897.5M by Note 3 ($1,230.6M against the $857M
   investing line); **$57.6M of the sellers' own deal expenses were assumed and paid through
   operating cash flow** ("Acquisition-related seller expenses (47,100)" is a debit inside
   OCF, the reverse of CERT); and the rhode earnout went **$7.1M -> $64.7M -> $80.8M** in
   eleven months, **$73.7M expensed and added straight back as non-cash**, to be paid in cash
   out of financing in three tranches to September 2028, up to $200M. The OCF-based numerator
   carries a purchase-price debit it should not and will never see the earnout credit it
   should. The March year-end straddles both closes: **no fiscal year on file describes the
   company that exists**, and the 10-K's own pro forma (rhode from 2024-04-01) is the nearest
   thing.
2. **The tariff-year instrument split down the middle.** $58.5M of IEEPA tariffs (4.4% of
   legacy sales), a global price increase on 2025-08-01, gross margin 71.3% -> 69.1% -> 69.4%
   -> 71.0% -> 72.7% -> 72.7% ex a $50.1M refund. **The price stuck and the margin recovered
   in three quarters.** The filed unit-volume line, positive every year and quarter on record
   and 85% of FY2025's growth, **went negative in the quarter of the increase and stayed
   negative for four**: -$19.4M, -$1.8M, -$18.0M, -$11.7M. Legacy brands +2.2% for FY2026,
   +0.03% post-increase. PLPC passed 87% through and kept its units; e.l.f. passed it through
   and lost them. That is Precision Steel's series and it decided the gate.
3. **No cost advantage is filed.** "Asset-light", "low costs", "remain cost competitive": no
   number, no peer, no unit cost, no speed-to-market metric in five 10-K vintages. The gross
   margin (70.7% at $7) is the outcome and the competitor row shows it is entirely spent:
   L'Oreal Consumer Products earns 21.4% with the heavier cost base, EL 5.2% under $813M of
   restructuring, e.l.f. 4.5% (8.0% ex earnout). The share e.l.f. took came from Coty Consumer
   Beauty (-22.1%, every mass trademark impaired, exit under review) and Revlon (Chapter 11).
4. **[E3-03](2) fails on the company's own pitch**: "$9 versus a prestige item at $42" is a
   statement that the customer substitutes; the risk factor names price, BOGO, private label
   and celebrity brands, and the company then bought a celebrity brand. **[E4-23] recorded at
   Q2**: a quarter of revenue depends on a named founder. **[E4-04]**: advertising 9.2% -> 22.1%
   of sales to hold a seasonal pipeline; two brands bought as replacements.
5. **Below the gate, the brief's priors on Q3 were confirmed, CGNX-shape.** [E4-29] does not
   headline the 10-K and is the third bullet of every one of thirteen releases; the definition
   excludes SBC ($86.9M), the earnout ($57.6M) AND cloud-software amortisation (a cash cost);
   the bonus plan has been on Adjusted EBITDA since the IPO and paid 200% in a year GAAP net
   income fell 77%; PSUs vest on net-sales CAGR. SBC/OCF 57.1 / 53.6 / 40.9% to the dollar.
   Nine guidance raises, one cut (the class-action date), one withdrawal.
6. **(c) is a classification, not a haircut, and it runs the other way from [E5-20].** D&A of
   $79.4M holds $35.0M of retail-display amortisation and $13.3M of cloud-software
   amortisation whose cash (~$66M/yr) is spent through OCF working capital ("prepaid expenses
   and other assets (67,401)"), plus $35.5M of acquired-intangible amortisation. The D&A end
   triple-counts; (c) judged at PP&E capex, OCF already conservative for this filer.

### PRIORS REFUTED, PRIORS CONFIRMED
- **Refuted: "growth is units, not price" as a description of the current business.** It was
  true through FY2025 and is the opposite since August 2025; the company files the split.
- **Refuted: that a consumer company either files unit data or it does not.** e.l.f. files a
  dollars-of-volume-effect line every period; it is not a unit count but it is the honest
  series, and it was enough to decide the gate.
- **Confirmed: the perimeter flag understates** (sixth consecutive), the earnout is invisible
  from both ends of the cash-flow statement, and [E4-29] fires in the releases not the 10-K.
- **Confirmed and then some: Q2 was genuinely open**, and the instrument returned a split
  answer; the verdict rests on the volume half, which the framework says is the honest one.

### THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE CONCLUSION, RECORDED [E4-26]
e.l.f. Cosmetics is No. 1 by units in US mass cosmetics with 29 consecutive quarters of
growth; it passed a 4.4%-of-sales tariff through in three quarters and its gross margin is now
above the pre-tariff level; the incumbents it took share from are writing off their brands
and leaving. A business that does that to Coty and Revlon has something. The finding is that
what it has is not the thing [E3-03] names, and the filed volume line is the evidence.

### DEFECTS IN THE BRIEF AND THE TOOLING, FROM THIS RUN
1. **`acq_note` reads the investing line; the seller-expense debit inside OCF is a new
   hiding place** (the reverse of CERT's addback). Suggest the tool print the
   "Acquisition-related seller expenses" class of OCF lines alongside the investing line when
   the flag fires.
2. **The D&A break the CERT run found has a second instance**: the FY2025 vintage moved
   "Non-cash lease expense" out of "Depreciation and amortization" (FY2024: 35,913 -> 30,167,
   the difference 5,746 being the new line). Same tag, changed content; the screen's OE@D&A
   for FY2023-24 is on the restated series and for FY2020-22 on the old one.
3. **The D&A end is INVALID in the generous-to-the-bear direction on any filer that
   capitalises fixtures or cloud costs into other assets**: the cash is in OCF working
   capital and the amortisation is in D&A. The (c) default [E3-44] presumes investing-section
   cash. Suggest a flag when amortisation of deferred charges or "retail product displays"
   exceeds PP&E depreciation.
4. **efts.sec.gov returned 403 on every transport** for the who-names-the-subject sweep;
   data.sec.gov and Archives worked with the same User-Agent. Recorded as a blocked rung, not
   a finding.
5. **The brief's "$1 price increase across the line" is not how the filing states it**: the
   10-K says "raised prices globally for all products sold" with no amount; the $1 figure is
   not in any filing read and was not used.
6. **The brief was right not to say which gate would be short.** Q3, closed, carried the pay
   finding; Q4, closed, carried the (c) classification.

### THE PIPELINE MOVED TO OPUS — 2026-09-12, and the recovery differs from a timed limit
**The Fable usage cap was reached**, which is a MODEL limit rather than a timed session reset, and
**SendMessage-resume does not survive it**: the agent is pinned to that model and hits the same
429. CALX and BE were therefore **relaunched as fresh agents on Opus with their disk state handed
over as an inventory** - run file, byte count, what was already complete, and every research file,
with an instruction not to refetch. **CALX had Step 0 done and had already corrected my brief's
sovereign** (5.35% on 09-11, not the 09-10 print of 5.37%); **BE had every 10-K FY2018-25, five
10-Qs, fourteen 8-K exhibits, three DEF 14As and the 2018 424B4 on disk**, so the relaunch cost
was the writing, not the fetching. Recorded in the run-agent memory: **the write-early protocol
decides whether WORK survives; the kind of limit decides whether CONTEXT survives.**

are labelled **FINDINGS ONLY, NO VERDICT**; Q5 never opened; Q6 is NOT REACHED with the reversal
condition written in words. **No band, no alert, no PORTFOLIO row** — the QLYS ruling.

**THE BUSINESS.** A fabless vendor of fibre-access boxes and premises Wi-Fi appliances (82.6% of
revenue) plus a cloud and managed-services subscription (17.4%), sold to about 1,600 small US
broadband operators. **79.0% of revenue comes from operators with under 250,000 subscribers**, 93%
of revenue is the United States, and the 10-K names its own demand driver: *"The U.S. Federal
government has approved programs, totaling more than $40 billion… Calix has a dedicated team of
funding specialists."* First billion-dollar year in FY2025, and gross margin at an all-time 56.8%.

competitive"; **price listed second** among the bases of competition; **nine competitors named**;
and the section ends *"Many of our competitors have the financial resources to offer competitive
products at a below market price, which could prevent us from competing effectively."*

tense.** Memory costs rose; Calix imposed surcharges; and it said:

> *"Our memory surcharge programs are designed to **recover costs—not add profit**—while
> **intentionally prioritizing market-share capture** and long-term customer goodwill over
> near-term margin."* … *"cost recovery only … neutral to gross profit."*

with backlog grandfathered at the old rate. **A business with pricing power does not publicly
pre-commit that its price increase is designed not to add profit.** And it did not work as cost
recovery either: **Q2 2026 gross margin 54.6%, −230bp sequentially and −170bp y/y, and Q3 2026
guided down ~280bp to 50.5–53.5% while revenue is guided UP. Volume up, margin down, by announced
policy.** **This is the CGNX standing instruction paying for itself a second time — and note what
it means: the one Q2 test the annual report could not support was decided by a document the 10-K
does not contain.** [E4-29] itself read **clean**: zero occurrences of "EBITDA" in the 10-K, in

holder can point at three filed series that all went up.

**THREE TOOLING DEFECTS, AND THE FIRST ONE MATTERS TO OTHER RUNS.**
1. **The EDGAR full-text-search call used to test "does this peer name the subject" returns a

   twice in their latest 10-Ks.** A **silent false negative** — the worst failure mode there is,
   because a run that trusted it would have recorded "no competitor names the subject" as a finding.
   The test was re-run by downloading each peer's 10-K primary document. **Any run that has used
   that call for a naming test should re-run it from the primary documents.**
2. **`best_year_dep 0.321` reproduces on neither obvious construction.** Best-year operating cash
   flow is **39.3%** of the FY2021-25 window and **27.5%** of the seventeen years. The verdict string
   "ONE YEAR CARRIES THE WINDOW" is right in substance; the printed number comes from an unnamed

   reaches the reader without its basis.
3. **`wc_note` pointed at the wrong year and the right one is live.** The flagged 45% is **FY2022**
   ($12,111k / $27,183k = 44.6%). The material event is **H1 2026: payables +$50,936k against
   $31,146k of operating cash flow = 163.5%, without which the half's operating cash flow was about
   −$19.8M** — confirmed by the filer's own DPO of **54 days against its stated target of 25-35
   days**, funding a $46,744k inventory build. **A working-capital flag computed only on completed
   fiscal years cannot see the live half**, which is where the DELL shape actually showed up. FY2019
   is also worse than the flagged year (−$29,440k against $4,654k of OCF) and sits inside the window
   that produces the range's bottom.

**One process note worth keeping.** Three separate findings in this file came from **furnished 8-K
exhibits rather than the annual report**: the live [E4-37] pricing answer, the "More than 1,200

a Q2 test and contradicted a Q1 disclosure — so the right generalisation is not "read the 8-K for
[E4-29]" but "read the 8-K, because the annual report is twelve months behind the sentences that
settle the gates."**

**Count: 70 runs** — gate-clearers 26, **Q2 OUT 41**, Q4 OUT 2 (ORCL, ARM), Q1 UNKNOWABLE 1.

### THE FULL-TEXT-SEARCH DEFECT — DIAGNOSED, NARROWER THAN REPORTED, AND NOW GUARDED
The run reported that the EDGAR full-text-search call *"returns a well-formed zero-hit response for
every CIK."* **Tested before recording, and the endpoint is fine - the HARNESS was malformed.** The
`ciks` parameter accepts only the bare zero-padded ten digits. Measured against ADTRAN (CIK 926282)
for the phrase "Calix" in 10-Ks:

| ciks value sent | result |
|---|---|
| `0000926282` | **200, 20 hits** - correct |
| `CIK0000926282` | 200, **0 hits** - what the CALX harness sent |
| `926282` (unpadded) | 200, **0 hits** - equally silent |

**BOTH malformed forms return HTTP 200 with a well-formed empty body. Nothing errors and nothing
warns** - and *"no competitor names this company"* is exactly the conclusion a run draws from a
zero, on a question the framework treats as evidence because **a moat is a relative claim
[E3-03]**. Primary documents on disk settle it: **ADTRAN names Calix once, Cambium three times,
Clearfield once**; CIEN, HLIT, UI and COMM zero.

**Scope, checked rather than assumed**: the shared PLPC harness (`fts_lib.py`) extracts the CIK with
a ten-digit regex and passes the **bare padded digits - the correct form** - so it was not affected;
and the naming claims in the PLTR and CALX rows rest on **greps of downloaded 10-Ks**, not on
search. **The one prior naming error already stands corrected in this ledger**: the KLAC research
file's *"Applied and Lam name nobody at all"*, which the LRCX run refuted by finding seven named
companies.

**`tools/sources.py:fts_count()` now REFUSES a malformed cik** rather than passing it through, with
both failing forms named in the message - because **a guard that returns a plausible number on bad
input is worse than no guard**, which is the half-fixed `level_shift` lesson of 2026-09-07. Its
docstring carries the standing limit: **a hit count is a prompt to open the document; the naming
test is settled by reading the competitor's filing, never by a search.**

**Two lesser row defects**: `best_year_dep 0.321` reproduces on neither construction (39.3% of the
five-year window, 27.5% of seventeen years); and **`wc_note` pointed at FY2022 when the material
event is H1 2026 - payables +$50,936k on $31,146k of OCF, 163.5%**, without which the half was
about **minus $19.8M** (the filer's own DPO is 54 days against a stated 25-35 target). The flag
reads annual facts, which is the limit already written into its docstring from INOD.

**Count: 70 runs** - gate-clearers 26, Q2 OUT 41, Q4 OUT 2, Q1 UNKNOWABLE 1.

# BE FOLDED IN — 2026-09-12. SEVENTY-ONE RUNS. Q2 OUT, and the moat turned out to be the length of somebody else's interconnection queue.

`Test Runs/2026-09-12 Run - BE Bloom Energy.md` (opened 2026-09-12 by an agent killed by a model
usage cap with the research folder fully stocked but Step 0 blank; resumed the same day and **lost
nothing**, because the research folder was on disk — the write-early protocol working in the
direction it was written for). `check_framework.py` PASS; separately, **99 distinct ledger ids
cited in the run file with ZERO phantom against the 267-row ledger.**

**FAIL at Q2. Price $275.75 (2026-09-11 close, aggregator, flagged) × 294,527,346 shares = cap
$81,216M. Sovereign 5.35% USD.**

## THE FINDING: A COST CURVE THAT WENT TO THE CUSTOMER, AND THEN THE METRIC THAT SHOWED IT WAS DELETED

This is the cleanest **[E4-55]** case the project has run, and the cleanest **[E3-62]** case.
Bloom published a **real physical series** — product accepted in 100 kW systems, megawatts accepted
net, **product cost per kilowatt**, installation cost per kilowatt — in the MD&A of every 10-K from
FY2018 to FY2023. Set against the filed product revenue and product cost of revenue for the same
years it reconciles **to within $2 per kilowatt**, which is how you know the series is being read
right. What it says:

| year | MW accepted | product rev/kW | **filed product cost/kW** | **gross $/kW** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | — | — | $4,457 | — |
| 2017 | 62.2 | — | $3,292 | — |
| 2018 | 80.9 | $4,952 | $3,372 | **$1,475** |
| 2019 | 119.4 | $4,668 | $2,881 | $1,021 |
| 2020 | 132.6 | $3,911 | $2,368 | $1,402 |
| 2021 | 188.0 | $3,529 | $2,346 | $1,021 |
| 2022 | 228.0 | $3,863 | $2,453 | $1,160 |
| 2023 | 268.0 | $3,639 | $2,108 | **$1,288** |
| 2024–25 | **not filed** | — | **METRIC DISCARDED** | — |

**Cost per kilowatt fell $1,264 over six years. Price per kilowatt fell $1,313. The customer took
104% of the cost curve, and gross profit per kilowatt peaked in the FIRST year of the series.**
[E3-62] asks the question nobody asks — *"how much is going to stay home and how much is just going
to flow through to the customer"* — and Bloom's own MD&A answers it against the owner. The textile
looms: *"Nothing was going to stick to our ribs as owners."*

**Then the FY2024 10-K deleted all four metrics**, in the registrant's own words: *"We have
determined that the foregoing metrics **no longer reflect key operating metrics** … **we will no
longer report on these metrics** … trends in costs and selling prices per kilowatt are **less
representative** … These factors can **distort** the cost or revenue per kilowatt metrics.
Management relies primarily on revenue, **non-GAAP gross and operating margins**, as well as cash
flows from operating activities to manage operations."* **[E2-49] verbatim** — *"Yardsticks seldom
are discarded while yielding favorable readings … disposition of the yardstick rather than
disposition of the manager"* — and the test [E2-49] sets, whether the switch FOLLOWS deterioration,
is answered by the discarded series' own last reading: **2022 was a $107/kW INCREASE in product
cost, the only increase in seven years.** The yardstick that went was the physical one; the
yardstick that replaced it is the one management is **paid on** and the one that **deletes stock
compensation**.

## THE METRIC THAT SURVIVES THE DELETION, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT CLOSES THE FILE

**PRODUCT gross margin: 35.4% (2023) · 36.8% (2024) · 35.2% (2025) · 35.6% (H1 2026) · 36.5% (Q2
2026). FLAT WITHIN 1.3 POINTS WHILE REVENUE TRIPLED.** A business with pricing power inside a
generational shortage of its own product expands its product margin. Bloom's did not move.

**And the trap this run walked into and out of, which is worth recording as a general lesson:** the
*total* gross margin rose from **14.8% to 32.0%** over the same period, and every bull deck in the
sector cites it. **All of it is mix and the absence of impairments** — the loss-making service,
installation and electricity lines fell from 26.9% of revenue in 2023 to 12.5% in H1 2026, and the
**$130.1M (2023) and $115.3M (2022) PPA impairments** dropped out of cost of revenue. **A blended
gross margin can rise by several hundred basis points without a single price changing. Check the
segment line before scoring pricing power off the total** — this is the same defect class as the
consolidated-series problem at [E2-56], one level down.

## THE ANNUITY IS THE WORST LINE, NOT THE BEST — THE AMAT SHAPE, WORSE THAN AT AMAT

The brief predicted this and the filing over-delivered. **Service gross margin was NEGATIVE for
seven of its first eight years:** −20.9% (2018), −4.6%, −20.7%, −2.8%, −11.6%, −20.7%, −0.7%
(2024), and first turned positive in **2025 at +10.0%**, 16.1% in H1 2026. **Q2 2026: Service 18.7%
GAAP against Product 36.5% — a ratio of 0.51 against AMAT's 0.62 — and Bloom prints both numbers
itself on slide 18 of its own Q2 2026 EX-99.2.** Installation has never been profitable in any
filed year.

**The mechanism is worth carrying forward to any razor-and-blade claim**: Bloom's service contract
is a **warranty on a consumable** — it pays for fuel-cell stack replacement. Bloom has *"increased
the life of our fuel cells by over two and half times"*, which is exactly why the margin finally
turned. **The annuity is only profitable to the extent the product stops needing the annuity.** The
two lines are in direct economic opposition, and a "recurring revenue" claim that rests on a
consumable-replacement obligation should be read as a cost, not a moat, until the filed margin says
otherwise.

## THE COMPETITOR ROW'S HARDEST FACT

Seven SEC annual filers, same metric, same window, each with its accession. **Generac — a genset
packager that buys engines and bolts them to alternators — earns a 38.3% gross margin against
Bloom's 29.0%, which is Bloom's best year ever. Caterpillar earns 33.8%.** A twenty-three-year
proprietary materials-science platform with 62 PhDs earns a **lower** gross margin than the
companies assembling commodity hardware.

**And the asymmetry: Bloom is invisible in the competitive self-description of every incumbent.**
CAT, CMI and GNRC name each other reciprocally and none names Bloom; GEV's named set is turbines and
grid gear; PLUG and BLDP name no companies at all and neither uses the phrase *"solid oxide"*. **The
only filer that names Bloom Energy is FuelCell Energy, and it names it to record that *"Bloom Energy
Corporation and Altus Power, Inc. were removed"* from its compensation peer group** — while keeping
Ballard and Plug. FCEL separately attacks *"solid oxide"* on *"longer stack life … minimal
performance derate"*, which is precisely the line that made Bloom's service margin negative for
seven years. **[E3-61] caps what this can mean** — naming practice reflects materiality thresholds
as much as market reality — and the run says so rather than over-reading it.

**A methodological point worth keeping: BLDP was EXCLUDED from the row rather than forced into it.**
Ballard files a **Form 40-F under MJDS on IFRS with no US-GAAP reconciliation**. An IFRS gross
margin and an IFRS-16 cash-flow statement are a **different measurement**, and putting them in a
US-GAAP column would be the exact error the row exists to prevent. Wärtsilä and Siemens Energy file
no SEC annual report at all — **UNKNOWABLE on this shelf, not UNRESEARCHED**, per the queue's own
non-SEC-registrant ruling. **And the PROVISIONAL hold was NOT applied, with the reason stated:** the
rule exists to stop a moat being *claimed* on an incomplete row; here the row *denies* one, and the
five missing names are all larger and better-capitalised, so their absence can only make Bloom's
relative position worse. **That asymmetry in the PROVISIONAL rule had not previously been written
down and should be.**

## THE DEPOSIT PRIOR WAS HALF RIGHT, AND THE HALF THAT WAS WRONG DECIDED THE SIGN

The brief's prior was that customer deposits on AI-data-centre orders fund the operating cash line.
Read off the filed cash-flow statements, every year:

- **FY2024: CONFIRMED AND THEN SOME.** OCF +$92.0M with the deposit line supplying **+$139.9M** —
  **net of deposits, FY2024 operating cash was NEGATIVE $47.9M.** The screen's 152% `wc_note`
  reproduces exactly.
- **H1 2026: CONFIRMED TO WITHIN $1.2 MILLION.** OCF **+$300,042k** against a deposit line of
  **+$301,232k** — net of it, **NEGATIVE $1,190k.** Customer deposits went $78,207k → **$360,568k**.
- **FY2025: REFUTED, and this is the strongest single fact against the run's own conclusion.** The
  deposit line **REVERSED by $142.6M** (deposits $220.1M → $78.2M, *"a lower level of new customer
  deposits"*) **and operating cash was still POSITIVE at $113.9M** — i.e. **+$256.6M** net of the
  swing. **H2 2025 took 92% of its $437.7M of operating cash from the business itself.**

**So the DELL lesson applies but not as predicted. At DELL one working-capital line WAS the entire
owner-earnings series. At Bloom the deposit line is 45.7% of trailing operating cash — and the two
most recent half-years are composed completely differently (8% vs 100%).** The generalisable
finding: **operating cash at Bloom is not deposit-FUNDED, it is deposit-UNREADABLE half-year by
half-year.** That is a different and, for Q4, more useful defect — and it means a single-period OCF
reading on any customer-prepayment business is worthless without the line beside it. The refundable
portion of the $360,568k is **not disclosed**, and that is the one number the run wanted and could
not get.

## TOOLING DEFECTS — TWO, AND ONE IS A SILENT [E5-06] VIOLATION ACROSS A WHOLE POPULATION

**1. BOTH SCREEN BAND ENDS REPRODUCE TO THE DOLLAR AND BOTH ARE WRONG — the INTC shape, plus one
worse thing.**
- `oe_bottom_m` **−157** = the **5-year FY2021-25 mean at the capex end with SBC SET TO ZERO**
  (−156,994).
- `oe_top_m` **−111** = the **3-year FY2023-25 mean at the D&A end with SBC SET TO ZERO** (−110,936).

Two different windows, which is exactly what the INTC run found on 2026-09-07 — **and additionally
a silent violation of [E5-06]**, *"To say 'stock-based compensation' is not an expense is even more
cavalier."* **The cause is a tagging problem, not an arithmetic one: Bloom tags stock compensation as
`AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense` DIMENSIONED by expense line, so an undimensioned annual
XBRL fetch returns NOTHING and the screen substituted zero without saying so.** The omission was
**$70M–$200M a year**; with SBC included the FY2021-25 five-year mean at the capex end is
**−$255,363k, not −$157,000k**. **This is not a BE-specific bug. Any filer that tags SBC by expense
line — and multi-line filers generally must — gets its owner earnings overstated by the whole of its
stock compensation, silently.** The fix is the same shape as `cover_shares.py`'s: when the
undimensioned series is empty but dimensioned facts exist, **fail loudly** rather than default to
zero. A screen that returns a band is trusted; a screen that returns nothing gets read.

**2. THE TIER-3 TRIAGE PUT BE IN THE WRONG SUB-CLASS, and the sub-class carried a cost instruction.**
BE was filed under *"NEGATIVE ON EVERY CONSTRUCTION — bottom AND top … no owner earnings exist on
any window or either capex end. **These runs are the cheapest in the queue**: the price question is
answered before the reading starts."* **That is false on the filings: the trailing year is
+$444,206k at the capex end and +$504,275k at the D&A end.** BE belongs two rows down with ACMR,
ALKT and ACVA under **SIGN CHANGE**, whose standing instruction — *"the multi-year mean is averaging
two different businesses; the run must date the inflection and refuse the blended mean"* — is
exactly what this run had to do. **A triage note that tells a run it is cheap is the same error class
as a brief that tells a run which gate is boring.** Both were nearly costly here: the file's sharpest
material (the unit series, the service margin, the 73% customer) sits in Q1 and Q2, which the
"cheapest in the queue" label would have had the run skim.

## THE OWNER-EARNINGS WIDTH, AND WHY IT IS UNKNOWABLE RATHER THAN OUT

**Rebuilt over eight windows and both (c) ends: −$273,262k to +$504,275k. Width $777,537k — it spans
zero and CHANGES SIGN between the corpus's default five-year window and the trailing year.** With
the D&A end struck out under [E5-20] (TTM capex $113,078k against D&A $53,009k, 2.13x, on a line
being doubled to 2 GW), **−$273.3M to +$444.2M.** Cumulative FY2018-25: **negative $1,876,625k**.
Net of the deposit inflow the TTM is **+$106,772k** and FY2025 is **+$60,389k** — the first positive
year on that construction.

**[E5-11] scored, and Q4 is NEITHER of the two precedents the brief offered.**
- **NOT the ORCL shape.** ORCL failed on a contracted claim contradicted by the balance sheet.
  Bloom's balance sheet is the opposite: **$2,667,909k of cash against $2,530,341k of total debt
  principal — a NET CASH position — of which 98.8% is a ZERO-COUPON convertible due November 2030**
  with a $194.97 conversion price against a $275.75 quote, so the likely outcome is extinguishment
  into 12.8M shares rather than repayment. Current debt **$7,269k**. **[E2-54] coverage 14.7x, or
  6.8x net of deposits.** Bloom does carry a *related* ORCL defect — **$494.1M of filed performance
  obligations against $3.9–4.2bn of guided revenue, roughly 87% uncontracted, and no backlog figure
  disclosed at all** — but that is a Q2 problem about firmness, not a Q4 problem about solvency.
- **NOT the ARM shape on the current year — but the ARM shape over the life, and worse in kind.**
  TTM **SBC/OCF 24.5%**, level with CRM 23.4 and SHOP 22.1 and well under the **CRWD 68.0** that
  closed that file. **But over the whole listed life the ratio is not computable because the
  denominator is negative: FY2018 through H1 2026, Bloom generated NEGATIVE $145,920k of operating
  cash and paid its people $1,030,941k in stock. ARM at least had cash for the stock to consume.**
  **And Bloom adds a category ARM did not have: $324.4M of stock paid to a CUSTOMER in one quarter**
  — which with TTM SBC is **68.4%** of operating cash, the CRWD reading.
- **What it IS is the HHH shape**: the filed history describes a different company than the cap
  prices, **with two quarters where HHH had 26 days.** [E2-42] requires *"not less than a five-year
  test"*; the business that earned +$444M has lived for two quarters. **UNKNOWABLE, and the
  separating test was asked aloud: the resolving documents are the FY2026 10-K (~2027-02-09) and the
  FY2027 10-K (~2028-02), and THEY DO NOT EXIST YET — which is what makes it UNKNOWABLE rather than
  a work order.**

## A NEW Q3 SPECIES: $324.4 MILLION OF STOCK PAID TO A CUSTOMER, AND A $72.3 MILLION INDUCEMENT THAT IS PURE DEADWEIGHT

This has not appeared in seventy prior runs and should be watched for. Bloom issued Oracle a warrant
on 3,531,073 shares at $113.28 in connection with the AI-data-centre partnership. **Total stock
handed over on exercise: $324.4M, of which only $17.9M has yet been charged against revenue —
$306.5M sits on the balance sheet as a "Customer Consideration Asset" that will reduce FUTURE
revenue.** The accounting is correct and the disclosure is excellent. The capital allocation is not:

**Gross settlement would have paid Bloom 3,531,073 × $113.28 = $400.0M IN CASH. Bloom forwent all of
it AND paid Oracle 248,798 additional shares worth $72.3M *"as an inducement for Oracle to elect net
settlement"*, to issue 1.4 million fewer shares worth $400.1M at the implied $290.59.** The
cash-for-shares swap is a **wash by construction** — that is what a cashless exercise is — **so the
$72.3M inducement is the entire economic content of the decision and all of it went out.** The
dilution "saved" reappears in the diluted count anyway (323.3M against 287.3M basic). **[E3-50]**
names what the motive looks like — optimising a reported share count — and **[E5-44]** sharpens it:
measured at intrinsic value rather than quote, Bloom paid with the one currency it should have been
hoarding while handing back $400M of cash, holding $2.67bn it has no filed use for. **Stated with
[E4-13]'s humility clause, which is mandatory: Oracle's negotiating position is not in the filing.**

**The generalisable watch item: a revenue-generating warrant issued to a customer is stock
compensation that does not appear in stock compensation.** It lands in APIC and in a
contra-revenue asset, and no SBC line, no SBC/OCF ratio and no non-GAAP reconciliation will show it.
**Check APIC movements against the sum of SBC plus option exercises on any name whose growth arrived
with a named strategic partner.**

## PRIORS REFUTED, AND ONE PREDICTION THAT LANDED EXACTLY

**Refuted:**
1. **"Both ends of the band are negative on every construction."** False. TTM is +$444.2M to
   +$504.3M, and the screen's negative band was an SBC-omitting artifact.
2. **"Customer deposits are funding the operating cash line."** Half true. FY2024 and H1 2026 yes;
   **FY2025 no, decisively** — the deposit line reversed $142.6M and OCF stayed positive.
3. **"Check the going-concern language in the older vintages and the 424B4."** **There is none.**
   Zero occurrences of "going concern" or "substantial doubt" in the 2018 424B4 (which disclosed an
   *"accumulated deficit of $2.3 billion"*), or in the FY2018, FY2019, FY2020, FY2023 or FY2025
   10-K. Twenty-five years of losses and never one qualification.
4. **"A history of equity raises" implying a weak balance sheet.** The issuance is real (**2.61x in
   7.4 years**) but the balance sheet today is **net cash with zero-coupon debt** — the strongest
   capital structure of any name to fail in this queue.
5. **The ORCL/ARM dichotomy the brief offered.** Neither fits; it is the HHH shape.

**Landed exactly:** **[E5-20]** — the brief predicted the D&A end might be INVALID rather than
merely optimistic, and it is: capex 2.13x D&A with the filing promising more. And the AMAT service-
margin prediction, which the filing beat in severity.

## THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THIS RUN'S OWN CONCLUSION, RECORDED PER [E4-26]

**H1 2026 GAAP operating income of $254.4M and GAAP net income of $272.5M on revenue up 150% — with
NO one-off gain — and FY2025 operating cash flow that stayed positive while the customer-deposit line
drained $142.6M out of it.** A company with no franchise and no pricing power should not be able to
do that. The honest counter-reading is that the AI on-site power market is a genuinely new market in
which Bloom has a two-to-three-year delivery lead and 1→2 GW of capacity nobody else has pointed at
this socket, and that the 2018-2023 unit series describes a **different business** — a distributed-
generation vendor selling against grid parity — that no longer exists. **If that is right, Q2 is
wrong, and the reversal condition is pre-registered rather than left to hindsight: PRODUCT gross
margin materially above ~45% held for two consecutive full years on rising volume, and/or Bloom
reinstating a physical unit series.** **[E3-47]** requires the hesitation and it is recorded: *"our
most egregious mistakes fall in the omission … category."* What makes the closure cost nothing in
practice is the price — **0.55% against a ~10% floor is a factor-of-eighteen miss; the file would
close on Q5 even if Q2 had cleared.**

would be a category error. `tools/alerts.json` untouched; no `PORTFOLIO.md` row. **The reversal

sovereign **5.35%** struck fresh. **The hand override understated the cap by $17.2bn** - the eighth

### THE SBC DEFECT — A SILENT [E5-06] VIOLATION IN THE NUMERATOR, NOW REFUSED
**Both published band ends reproduce to the dollar, and both were computed with SBC set to ZERO.**
Bloom tags stock compensation as `AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense` **dimensioned by expense
line**, so an undimensioned annual fetch returns nothing after 2018 - and `sbc.get(e, 0.0)` quietly
substituted zero, **omitting $70-200M a year while reproducing the row exactly.** [E5-06] is
explicit that SBC is simply an expense. **A screen that drops it is not being conservative; it
overstates owner earnings, which is the one direction that matters when the question is whether to
buy.**

**Measured across the 361 priced names over their last five OCF years, before fixing anything:**

| SBC resolves | names |
|---|---|
| every year | **325** |
| some years | **14** (COKE 4 of 5 missing, CINF 4, BRBS 4, DJCO 3, AUBN 3 ...) |
| **no year at all** | **21** - MKL, MPLX, APLE, CTS, CVX, NEU, PM, BRK-A, EME, TDY, GENC, **BE**, SEB, SO, UTL, NWN, TG, C and three MBIN preferreds |

**`owner_earnings()` now returns `SBC_UNRESOLVED` or `SBC_PARTIAL` and the row goes UNPRICED with
the ground stated**, exactly as `CAPEX_UNRESOLVED` already did. **The queue went 361 priced to 331.**

**DOES ANY COMPLETED VERDICT REVERSE? No, and the reason is the direction of the error.** Four
affected names had been run - **MKL (Q2 OUT), BRK-B (Q5 FAIL), COKE (Q5 FAIL) and BE itself (Q2
OUT)** - and **omitting SBC OVERSTATES owner earnings, so the screen made each look CHEAPER than it
is. A failure reached on an overstated yield holds a fortiori.** MKL and BRK are priced by the
insurer sector method rather than this construction at all, and the COKE run engaged with stock
compensation directly. **The real damage is the READING ORDER: 27 of the 30 newly unpriced names
were never run and had been ranked on an overstated yield** - CVX, PM, SO, C, MPLX, TDY, EME and
twenty more. They are now unpriced with the ground stated, pending a hand read.

**And a triage defect the run named, which I should have caught**: the tier-3 note filed BE under
*"negative on every construction ... the cheapest in the queue."* It belongs under **SIGN CHANGE**.
The run's own words: *"a triage note that tells a run it is cheap is the same error class as a brief
that tells a run which gate is boring"* - the CGNX prohibition, which I wrote into the protocol on
2026-09-07 and then left standing in a triage label four lines above the same file's tier list. The
sharpest material here - the unit series, the service margin, the customer paid in stock - sits in
Q1 and Q2, which that label would have had the run skim.

**Count: 71 runs** - gate-clearers 26, Q2 OUT 42, Q4 OUT 2, Q1 UNKNOWABLE 1.

790.4M today against 565.4M in FY2019, with **33.5-40.2 million more contracted for 2027-10-15**
on the mandatory conversion of the 6.00% Series A preferred, whose $5,750M liquidation preference
ranks ahead of the common.

### THE ONE FACT THAT CLOSED THE FILE, AND IT CAME FROM THE PEER ROW RATHER THAN THE SUBJECT

Same year, same demand environment, same supply chain, same regulators, the same aircraft
customers:

| FY2025, commercial aircraft | Airbus | Boeing BCA |
|---|---|---|
| **aircraft delivered** | **793** | **600** |
| **commercial operating result** | **+€5,470M (10.4%)** | **−$7,079M (−17.1%)** |
| whole-company owner earnings, this framework's construction | **+€3,721M / +€4,552M** | **−$2,303M / −$1,314M** *(−$3,833M / −$2,844M corrected — see the defect)* |
| **net cash / (net debt)** | **+€12,171M** | **($25,878M)** at 2026-06-30 |
| unit backlog | **8,754 aircraft** | ~6,130 undelivered firm orders |

**A 27-point margin gap on the same product in the same twelve months, and 32% more deliveries by
the company that made money.** [E3-61] warns that the competitor row shows position and cannot show
conduct — *"I think you'd have to know the people involved"* — and that warning is precisely what
makes this decisive. **It removes the environment as the explanation for seven consecutive years of
BCA operating losses (FY2019-FY2025).** Air traffic, fuel, tariffs, the supply chain and the cycle
all hit both airframers; one printed 10.4% and €12.2bn of net cash.

**[E2-53] is then the gate that fails, and it is the strongest reading of franchise in the corpus:**
*"Once dominant, the newspaper itself, not the marketplace, determines just how good or how bad the
paper will be. **Good or bad, it will prosper.**"* Boeing did not prosper, and the marketplace was
not the reason. **[E5-18] from the other side:** *"if it won't stand a little mismanagement it's not
much of a business"* — Boeing's did not stand it, going to six consecutive year-ends of negative
book equity (−$8,617M in 2019 to −$3,908M in 2024, and −$23,552M at 2024-09-30) and then raising
$23,832M from the market in two days of October 2024. **And [E4-23] is the hinge:** *"if a business
requires a superstar to produce great results, the business itself cannot be deemed great"* — the
peer row is the proof that it does.

Two more failures on the registrant's own words, both in one 10-K: **[E2-44]** — *"This market
environment has resulted in **intense pressures on pricing** and other competitive factors, and we
expect these pressures to **continue or intensify** in the coming years"*, said about BCA and again
about BGS, with the substitute conceded in the same MD&A (*"they offer competitive products and have
access to most of the same customers and suppliers"*). And **[E2-59] / [E3-03](3)** — *"Since the
737-9 door plug accident in January 2024, the 737 program **may only increase production rates
and/or implement new production lines with the concurrence of the FAA**."* Prices are not regulated;
**output is.** Regulation caps a franchise and floors a commodity business; neither creates the
class, and here it caps.

### TWO TOOLING DEFECTS, AND THE SECOND IS A NEW CLASS

**(1) The published spread is a WINDOW artifact and is nineteen times too narrow — the INTC finding
replicating on the same sub-class, five days later.** `oe_bottom -4,429 / oe_top -3,392` reproduce
to within $4M and **both ends sit at the capex end** (5y_capex −3,388 max, 3y_capex −4,426 min; the
two D&A constructions are interior at −3,563 and −4,076). The advertised $1,037M "spread" measures a
three-year-versus-five-year window difference and says nothing about the (c) judgment it is read as.
**Rebuilt over eleven windows × both ends: −$10,076M to +$9,324M, a $19,399M width.** Both members
of the STEP DOWN sub-class have now been run and both found this. The triage's *"a tight spread here
is not safety"* was right in substance and wrong about the spread, twice.

**(2) THE 401(k)-IN-STOCK DEFECT. SBC THAT RESOLVES CAN STILL BE INCOMPLETE, AND NO XBRL-SIDE GUARD
CAN DETECT THAT.** This is the BE SBC-of-zero finding in a place the BE fix cannot reach, and it is
worse in one respect: the BE case failed loudly once guarded, and this one cannot be made to fail at
all from tagged data. Boeing's consolidated cash-flow statement carries **two** equity-settled
compensation add-backs:

> **Share-based plans expense** — 426 / 407 / 690
> **Treasury shares issued for 401(k) contribution** — **1,530 / 1,601 / 1,515**
> *(FY2025 / FY2024 / FY2023, FY2025 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows)*

The second is the employee retirement match **paid in shares instead of cash**, added back to
operating cash flow exactly as SBC is. `StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueEmployeeBenefitPlan` resolves
for **FY2010-12 and FY2020 only**; from FY2021 the number exists **solely in the filed statement**.
The filed series: **$195M (FY2020) · $1,233M · $1,215M · $1,515M · $1,601M · $1,530M (FY2025) ·
$855M (H1 2026)**. [E5-06] is unambiguous and [E3-70] is stricter still, so **total equity-settled
compensation was $1,956M in FY2025 against $1,065M of operating cash flow — 184%** — and the screen
subtracted $426M of it. The correction moves FY2025 owner earnings from −$1,314M/−$2,303M to
−$2,844M/−$3,833M and flips FY2022 from positive to roughly zero.

**No code change was made, and that is the finding rather than a shortfall.** The BE fix works
because a tag returning *nothing* is detectable; a tag returning *part of the truth* is not. A
refusal rule keyed on "capex exceeds SBC by more than X" would produce false negatives across the
whole queue. **What went into `Screens/floor_screen.py` is a documented note naming the class, the
Boeing instance, and the only remedy there is: read the cash-flow statement's non-cash block, every
line of it, and do not assume `ShareBasedCompensation` is the whole of equity-settled pay.** The
same exposure exists wherever a filer pays benefits in stock — Boeing also settled **pension**
contributions in shares ($3,000M / $2,048M / $952M in FY2020/21/22), which this run left out as a
conservatism against its own conclusion.

### THE YEARS CHOSEN, AND WHY THIS RANGE IS NARROW IN THE ONLY SENSE THAT MATTERS

The brief warned there was *"no stable multi-year owner-earnings figure here at all"*: **true of the
full history, and refuted for the business that exists now.** FY2019 is a **dated structural break**
rather than a matter of taste — the worldwide 737 MAX grounding of 2019-03-13 — and across that line
seven things changed and none changed back: BCA went from profit every year to loss every year; the
FAA acquired a veto over the 737 rate; debt went $13,847M → $54,098M; interest $475M → $2,771M;
weighted-average shares 579.2M → 759.8M; and the 401(k) match went from cash to stock. **Every
window is published per [E4-38]; the mean is not taken across the break.**

| the business that exists now | capex end | D&A end |
|---|---|---|
| FY2019-2025 (7y, the whole post-grounding era) | **−$6,955M** | −$7,277M |
| FY2021-2025 (5y, the corpus default window) | **−$4,807M** | −$4,981M |
| FY2022-2025 (4y) | **−$4,393M** | −$4,320M |
| FY2024-2025 (2y, post-door-plug) | **−$10,076M** | −$9,384M |
| **TTM to 2026-06-30** | **−$2,238M** | −$585M |
| *pre-break, a different company: FY2014-2018* | *+$9,129M* | *+$9,324M* |

**Range for the business that exists now: −$10,076M to −$4,320M — negative on every window, both
(c) ends, and the trailing twelve months.** [E4-25]'s *"too wide to reach a conclusion"* applies to
the full range and **not** to the post-break one, which is the entire value of dating the break.
**The D&A end is INVALID under [E5-20] for a reason more specific than capital intensity:** capex is
1.51× depreciation in FY2025 and 1.72× in H1 2026, and Boeing's real renewal spending is not on the
capex line at all — it runs through R&D ($3,180M) and through ~$31.2bn of capitalised deferred
production costs and tooling sitting in inventory. **The $1,953M depreciation charge contains nothing
for the eventual replacement of the 737.** Windage count: one.

### THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THE BRIEF ASKED: YES, THE CUSTOMERS ARE FUNDING THE OPERATING CASH

| $M | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 | **H1 2026** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| operating cash flow | 5,960 | (12,080) | 1,065 | **+1,185** |
| change in advances and progress billings | +3,365 | +4,069 | (723) | **+4,660** |
| change in accounts payable | +1,672 | (793) | +724 | **+1,381** |
| **OCF EXCLUDING BOTH LINES** | **+923** | **(15,356)** | **+1,064** | **(4,856)** |

**In the six months to 2026-06-30 Boeing reported +$1,185M of operating cash flow while taking
$6,041M of additional money from its customers and suppliers. Excluding those two lines the business
consumed $4,856M of cash in half a year.** Advances stand at **$64,059M**. The queue's `wc_note` is
confirmed exactly: accounts payable moved −$3,783M in FY2021 against operating cash flow of
−$3,416M, **111%**.

**[E3-52] read in both directions is the real finding.** Float and deferred taxes are *"liabilities
without covenants or due dates attached … the benefit of debt … but saddle us with none of its
drawbacks."* Customer advances share that covenant-free, long-dated **form** and differ in the one
way that matters: **they are discharged by building aircraft, and on the loss-making programmes the
cost of building exceeds the cash received. That is what a reach-forward loss IS. This is the inverse
of float** — money already spent, against an obligation costing more than the cash.

### A FOURTH SURVIVAL SHAPE, ADDED TO THE ORCL / ARM / BE SET

Boeing carries **both** of the first two and is also a fourth thing.

- **The ORCL feature (contracted not to stop) is present:** $15,229M of airplane financing
  commitments of which **$11,904M is to customers Boeing itself believes are below investment
  grade**, $6,711M of accrued *"Forward loss recognition"*, and $64,059M of advances discharged at a
  negative margin.
- **The ARM feature (earns nothing after paying its people) is present and WORSE than ARM's.** ARM's
  finding was stock compensation equal to 97% of operating cash flow over its whole listed life.
  **Boeing's equity-settled compensation was 184% of FY2025 operating cash flow — the highest ratio
  this queue has recorded.** Boeing pays its retirement match in stock.
- **The BE feature (too little filed history) is absent:** 18 years of filed annual history, nothing
  UNKNOWABLE for want of evidence.
- **THE FOURTH: THE CASH IS SPENT UNDOING PAST WORK.** ORCL's cash bought datacentre assets that
  might yet earn; ARM's went to the engineers who build the next architecture; BE's bought a factory
  with too little history to judge. **Boeing's goes to its own defects:** $14,891M of cumulative 777X
  reach-forward losses (launched 2013, first delivery now 2027, zero delivered), $964M on the 767,
  ~$5,000M of BDS fixed-price development losses in FY2024 alone, **$10,882M of adverse cumulative
  catch-up adjustments in three years**, $1,300M of abnormal production costs, $1,500M of cash
  concessions to 737 MAX customers, $443M of 737-9 customer considerations, $689M to the DOJ and the
  families, and $1,696M still accrued as concessions owed. **None of it builds anything.** The
  framework had no category for a business whose principal use of capital is remediation; it has one
  now.

### THE FLOOR STATEMENT, WHICH IS THE CLEANEST IN THE QUEUE

A negative numerator has no growth rate, so the question inverts into dollars. **Boeing must earn
$8,899M of owner earnings to yield the 5.35% sovereign at $210.45, and $16,633M to clear the ~10%
[E4-28] floor. The most it has EVER earned in eighteen filed years is $13,398M — FY2018, on 806
deliveries, 579M shares and $13,847M of debt. Repeat the best year in Boeing's history exactly and
the buyer today receives 8.05% — below the figure the corpus quits on; 7.79% on the full equity
claim including the preferred. The floor requires 24% more than the best year ever, on 31% more
shares.** A round-number value range was **refused rather than invented**, because there is no
positive owner-earnings value to state. Neither bar applies: the normal method needs a value and the
screamer test needs a conservative case, and the price sits above the whole range — [E4-01]'s third
outcome.

### THE TAIL-TRIAGE CORRECTION EARNED ITS KEEP ON THE FIRST RUN AFTER IT WAS WRITTEN

BA sat under **STEP DOWN** with *"a tight spread there is not safety"*. The brief passed that along
as *"a statement about the arithmetic"* and — correctly, per the correction inserted the same day —
told the run that **every gate was open**. That mattered: the brief's own expectation was that the
file would close at **Q4**, and it closed at **Q2**. The material that closed it — the peer row, the
FAA concurrence sentence, the registrant's own pricing-pressure language, the delivery series — all
sits in Q1 and Q2. **A brief or a label that had aimed the effort at Q4 would have produced a
correct verdict on the wrong gate, and the hard sequence would have been broken to get there.**

### PRIORS REFUTED

1. **"IN NARROW on the duopoly, and I want it attacked" — refuted, and by the peer row rather than
   by Boeing's numbers.** The duopoly IS a franchise; Airbus is the one holding it. That is a
   stronger and less comfortable finding than "the moat never existed."
2. **"Q4 is where I expect this to close" — refuted on location, confirmed on substance.** Q4 is
   indeed OUT (gruesome on [E4-20]'s literal words; [E2-54] coverage negative in three of four
   recent periods; [E5-11] strengths 1 and 3 failed), but Q2 fails first and the hard sequence puts
   the verdict there.
3. **"There is no stable multi-year owner-earnings figure here at all" — true of the full history,
   refuted for the business that exists now.**
4. **The queue cap being wrong for a ninth time — refuted.** It was right.

### THE STRONGEST SINGLE FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT **[E4-51]**

**Airframe manufacturing is a thin-margin leg for everyone.** Lockheed Aeronautics **6.9%** (down
from 10.3% in FY2023, carrying a $950M classified reach-forward loss in FY2025), Northrop
Aeronautics Systems **6.3%** (a $477M B-21 LRIP loss provision), Pratt & Whitney **7.9%**, Embraer
Commercial Aviation **2.7%**. Where the peers earn 10%+ at company level they earn it on aftermarket
and electronics — RTX Collins 16.3%, HEICO Flight Support 24.1%, TransDigm 47.2%, Embraer Services
& Support 15.5% — **exactly the leg Boeing sold $10.55bn of in October 2025.** So the whole industry
takes reach-forward losses on new airframe programmes, and Boeing's are partly a genre feature
rather than purely a moat failure. **The verdict rests on the gap between a thin positive and a deep
negative: nobody else's airframe leg is at −17.1%, and the one direct comparable is at +10.4% on 32%
more deliveries in the same twelve months.** That reading is also why the file carries eight written
reversal conditions instead of being forgotten.

### DEFECTS IN THE BRIEF

Two, both small, and one is arguably a virtue. **(1) The brief asserted the run should "check that
SBC resolves for every year you use" — it does, for all 18 years, and the check passed while the
subtraction was still wrong by $1.5bn a year.** A resolution check is not a completeness check, and
the brief inherited that conflation from the BE fix. **(2) The brief said "Boeing has issued a great
many shares recently; the count is the first thing to get right," implying the queue's cap would be
wrong again.** It was right. Framing a prior as a near-certainty is the mirror of telling a run which
gate is boring — it invites the run to find what it was told to find. The brief's own instruction to
re-strike and verify is what caught it, so the protocol worked and only the framing was loaded.

**Count: 72 runs** — gate-clearers 26, Q2 OUT **43**, Q4 OUT 2, Q1 UNKNOWABLE 1.

### THE FINDING THAT ONLY A COMPETITOR ROW COULD REACH, AND IT IS THE BEST ARGUMENT FOR [E3-28] THIS PROJECT HAS PRODUCED

**Vizio Holding Corp — the only company that ever filed the SAME metrics Roku filed — raised its
monetisation per account 71.5% over the three years in which Roku's rose 1.1%, from one fifth of
the account base.** SmartCast ARPU $21.68 (FY2021) → $28.30 → $32.48 (FY2023) → **$37.17
(Q3-2024, "up 18%")**, against Roku's $41.03 (FY2021) → **$41.49 (FY2024)**.

Every single-company reading of Roku's flat ARPU has an innocent explanation available, and Roku
supplies it: *"an increasing share of Streaming Households in international markets where we are
currently focused more on scale and engagement than monetization."* **The competitor row destroys
it.** The industry's smallest, weakest and least-scaled participant was raising its take 18% a
year in the same quarters. Flat ARPU was not an industry condition. **[E2-44]'s first
characteristic — can it raise prices *"even when product demand is flat"* — is absent at Roku and
present at Vizio, and no amount of reading Roku's own filing could have established that.**

Two more from the same row:
- **Vizio's Platform+ gross margin was 57.5% (9M-2024) against Roku's advertising-only 57.8%
  (FY2025).** Roku out-scales Vizio roughly **5:1** in platform revenue and earns the **same**
  advertising gross margin. Where a moat exists, scale shows up in price or in margin. Neither.
- **Vizio's Device gross profit crossed +$115.7M (FY2021) → −$8.6M (FY2023) — the identical
  crossing in the identical years as Roku's**, with platform at 106.1% of its total gross profit
  against Roku's 104.0%. Two independent filers, one shape, one sign flip, same years. That is
  **[E2-27]** — *"viewed collectively, the decisions neutralized each other"* — not a moat.

**And the row is going dark on both sides, which is the uncomfortable part.** Vizio stopped
filing on 2024-12-13 (Form 15-12G) and Walmart discloses **three** Vizio facts: a $1.9bn purchase
price, the goodwill's segment, and an FTC consent decree to 2037. Netflix's FY2025 10-K contains
**no membership count of any kind**. Roku deleted Streaming Households and ARPU. **Three of the
four CTV filers that once published a user series have stopped.** A method that depends on
same-metric peer rows is losing its evidence base in this sector in real time, and that is worth
more than the ROKU verdict.

### [E2-49] FIRED ON ALL THREE UNIT-AND-PRICE SERIES AT ONCE — A FIRST FOR THIS QUEUE

Three different KPM sets in three consecutive annual reports, each change following a
deteriorating reading:

| filing | the Key Performance Metrics, verbatim |
|---|---|
| 10-K FY2023 | *"gross profit, Active Accounts, Streaming Hours, and ARPU"* |
| 10-K FY2024 | *"Streaming Households, Streaming Hours, ARPU, and Free Cash Flow"* |
| 10-K FY2025 | *"Streaming Hours, Platform revenue, **Adjusted EBITDA**, and Free Cash Flow"* |

**Gross profit dropped the year after consolidated margin went 50.9% → 46.1% → 43.7%. Streaming
Households and ARPU were both deleted in FY2025 — and the FY2025 10-K carries no value for either
anywhere in the document, only the words *"more than 90 million Streaming Households globally."***
Net additions had decelerated 39% → 17% → 16% → 14% → **12%** before the series ended. Those words
are consistent with **+0.3% growth and with +9%**, so **the direction of the scarce asset —
[E4-32]'s *"primary criterion of a great business"* — is now unmeasurable from the filings.**
And there is a fourth switch nobody had looked for: *"volume of streaming players sold"* fell
**−4%, −14%, −8%** across 2021-2023 (the Precision Steel shape **[E4-55]**), and in FY2024 the
basis was widened to *"volume of **all devices shipped**"*, folding in the new Roku-made TVs and
turning the sign positive.

**The [E2-49] prior's record is now: FIRED at SHOP, MRVL, PAY, ARM, CALX, BE and ROKU; FAILED at
QLYS, CRM, CORT, PLTR and INOD. Roku is the first name where the ENTIRE unit-and-price disclosure
set went in one filing.**

### THE QUEUE-RECORD SBC NUMBER, AND THE ONE BOOLEAN THAT EXPLAINS THE WHOLE FILE

**Cumulative SBC/OCF 140.2%** — ten filed years produced **$1,378,145k** of operating cash and
paid **$1,932,508k** in stock. **First in the calibrated row by 42 points** over CALX's 98.4%.
Every multi-year window exceeds 100%. Every year resolves; the zero-SBC defect of 2026-09-12 does
not touch this name, and the trend is genuinely improving (FY2024 peak $384,662k, TTM $328,038k).

**`flags_disagree: FIRES` is the file in one boolean.** `level_shift 4.23 "STEP UP"` reproduces
exactly — mean(2023-2025) $319,206k over mean(2017-2022) $75,498k on the nine-year operating-cash
series — and `level_shift_oe` refuses the ratio. **Operating cash stepped up 4.2x and owner
earnings did not step at all, because the entire step sits inside the stock-compensation add-back.**
The PLPC run of 2026-09-07 added that flag precisely to catch a name whose two series disagree,
and Roku is its sharpest instance in the queue.

### THREE TOOLING DEFECTS, AND ONE OF THEM IS STRUCTURAL

1. **`wc_note` divides one balance-sheet delta by a single year's operating cash, so on a
   near-zero year it reports the smallest movement in the statement.** Roku's 351% — the largest
   reading in the 361-name queue — is the **`Deferred revenue`** line, **+$41,402k against
   $11,795k** of FY2022 operating cash, reproduced to the dollar; without it FY2022 operating cash
   was **−$29,607k**. It *is* customer money, but the balance has never exceeded **$149.8M, 3.2%
   of revenue**, and **56% of it is not customer float at all** — it is the portion of a device's
   price allocated to *"unspecified upgrades and updates"*, i.e. cash already collected. **The
   flag missed both larger movements in the same column: FY2022's `Content assets and liabilities,
   net` at −$313,204k (7.6x larger) and FY2023's `Accounts payable` build of +$248,175k, which was
   97.0% of that year's operating cash.** Same defect family as the near-zero denominators that
   made MU and INTC re-triage as UNPRICED. The fix is not a threshold: report the delta against
   **revenue** as well as operating cash, and flag the **largest** working-capital line rather than
   one chosen tag. **No flag reads the content-asset line at all, and at Roku that line IS the
   capital expenditure** — which is why total capex is $5,280k against D&A of $68,904k, and why
   (c) is judged with the [E5-20] exception class **reversed**: D&A is the conservative end here.
2. **`oe_bottom` and `oe_top` are two different windows again**, advertised as a spread.
   `−151` is the five-year 2021-2025 mean at the capex end; `−81` is the three-year 2023-2025 mean
   at the **same** end. Found on INTC 2026-09-07, unfixed, recurs here. The real capex band inside
   the five-year window is **$272k** wide. Rebuilt over eight windows and both (c) ends the range
   is **−$189M to +$382M — it STRADDLES ZERO**, fourteen of sixteen constructions negative.
3. **THE STRUCTURAL ONE, AND IT WILL RECUR: the screen cannot see a takeover.** **Roku signed a
   definitive merger agreement with Fox Corporation on 2026-06-14** — 0.9693 FOXA shares plus
   **$96.00 cash** per Roku share, both classes alike, Roku holders taking ~27% of the combined
   company; S-4 effective 2026-09-01, **DOJ Second Request 2026-09-08**, close expected H1 CY2027,
   termination fees $866,084,000 (Roku) and $1,237,262,000 (Fox). **At FOXA's 2026-09-11 close the
   consideration is $159.90, so the $154.93 quote is a 3.1% merger spread and not an
   owner-earnings price.** Neither the queue row nor the brief carried it, because the screen reads
   XBRL and **Item 1.01 of an 8-K has no XBRL.** **A `merger_flag()` testing for an 8-K Item 1.01
   or a DEFM14A since the last 10-K would have caught it, and the blind spot applies to every name
   in the queue that gets taken over.** This is the cheapest guard on the list and it is not built.

entry here** — the exact failure the FOLD rule of 2026-09-07 was written to stop, running in the
opposite direction this time (queue entry present, reading-list entry missing, instead of the
reverse). Its queue-fold edits were also still sitting **uncommitted** in the shared working tree
when the ROKU fold began; they were committed separately under their own title (`9abe450`) rather
than swept into a ROKU-titled commit. **The count below therefore advances by two, and BA's

### THE TIER-3 TRIAGE HAS A SECOND HALF TO ITS CORRECTION

The correction of 2026-09-12 fixed the *wording* of a label that told five runs which gate to
skim. **It did not notice that four of the fifteen tier-3 names were never labelled at all** —
SWK, ARM, CALX and ROKU appear in the roster and in no sub-class. **Three of those four have now
been run and all three closed at Q2 on the business**, which is the opposite of what the labelled
classes predicted for a tier defined by arithmetic. **An unlabelled name in a labelled list reads
as "nothing here", which is the CGNX error delivered by omission rather than by wording.** SWK is
the one still live.

### WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT, AND THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT

No alert band and no `PORTFOLIO.md` row — the QLYS ruling; a Q2 failure is a failure on the
business. Four reversal conditions are in the run file, and **the first one names a document that
does not exist**: an audited Streaming Household count on the withdrawn definition, showing the
base still compounding.

**Stated as [E4-51] requires**, the best case against the OUT verdict: **advertising gross margin
expanded ~650bp year on year to 62.4% in Q2 2026 on 25% revenue growth**, faster than the US OTT
and digital ad markets, with advertising gross profit up 39%; the memory cost advantage is real
and filed (*"the Roku TV OS requires significantly less dynamic memory (DRAM) and storage memory
(Flash) than competing platforms, and this widening cost advantage is drawing more TV brands to
Roku"*); **Hisense and TCL were added as OEM partners in 2025**; and Roku's platform revenue of
$4,145M **exceeds Comcast's whole advertising line** ($3,712M, −9.2%) and is 2.8x Charter's
($1,468M, −17.6%), growing while both of theirs fall. **The verdict stands because [E3-03](2)
asks about substitutes, not about this year's margin** — and because Roku's own risk factors
concede that *"at times our existing licensed Roku TV partners have chosen to work exclusively
with, or divert a significant portion of their business with us, to other operating system
developers"*, Charter's 10-K lists Roku as one of six interchangeable surfaces (*"Xumo, Apple TV,
Roku, Vizio, LG and Samsung TV"*), and Roku ships its own channel onto Fire TV, Samsung TVs and
Google TV. **The 650bp were earned inside a category still taking share from linear television,
which is a surfing run [E3-51]; the test that separates a moat from a wave is whether the position
can be PRICED, and the Vizio comparison says it cannot.**

### A NEW DEFECT CLASS: SBC THAT RESOLVES CAN STILL BE INCOMPLETE
**The BE defect was SBC that did not resolve. This is SBC that resolves and is a quarter of the
truth.** Boeing settles its 401(k) match in stock - **$1,530M in FY2025 - and no SBC element
contains it.** Verified here: it sits under the generic equity-statement tag
**`StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueOther`** ($1,233M / $1,215M / $1,515M / $1,601M / $1,530M for
FY2021-25) while every SBC tag the screen reads returns **$427M**.

**NO GUARD IS ADDED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS WHY.** `DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized` is the
obvious candidate: **181 of the 331 priced names file it, and it exceeds the SBC tag on 24 at 5% of
operating cash and 9 at 10%.** But **Boeing's is settled in STOCK while AMAT's ($320M) and DAL's
($1,400M) are settled in CASH, and nothing in the tags distinguishes them.** A cash match is an
operating expense already correctly inside operating cash flow; a stock match is a non-cash add-back
that must be subtracted. **A flag firing on all three would be wrong twice out of three times**, and
operator rule 8 forbids the tool deciding which. **Written into `sbc_annual`'s docstring as a
reading task instead**, with the confirmed cases named on both sides. Direction, for anything already
run: an understated subtraction overstates owner earnings, so **AMAT, the twenty-first gate-clearer,
looked cheaper than it is and its failure on price holds a fortiori.**

**And a defect in my brief, which the run named precisely**: I wrote *"check that SBC resolves."*
**Resolution is not completeness** - the check passed while the subtraction was wrong by $1.5bn a
year. I also wrote *"eight runs have found the queue's cap wrong,"* which framed a prior as
near-certain; **it was right this time.**

**69,649,196** economic shares (Class A 64,657,388 + Class B 4,991,808, summed on the note 14 charter
reading, cover of 10-Q acc. `0001628280-26-054832`) = **$5,014.7M**, against a queue row of $2,979M.
Sovereign 5.35% (Treasury, 2026-09-11). Q3 and Q4 built and recorded as non-governing; Q5 headed
`COMPUTATION — NOT A CLEARANCE`.

### THE GHC PROBLEM IN ITS LISTED-SUBSIDIARY FORM — AND THIS TIME IT WAS FOUND FIRST

ACM Research is a Delaware holding company whose operating business is **ACM Research (Shanghai),
STAR Market 688082.SS**. The brief named the GHC and BAM/BN precedents and asked what share of owner
earnings belongs to ACMR's own holders. **The filings answer it in four places, all read:**
- **Net-income attribution: 77.2% (FY2025)**, 77.7–79.9% in FY2022–24.
- **Ownership: 82.5% (FY2022) → 82.1% → 81.5% → 74.6% (FY2025) → 73.2% (2026-06-30)** — the September
  2025 private offering (38,601,326 shares at RMB 116.11, net $623.0M), ACM Research's own sale of
  4,801,648 Shanghai shares at RMB 160.00 on 2026-02-06, and 2,431,900 Shanghai options exercised by
  Shanghai employees on 2026-05-12.
- **Parent-only statements (Rule 4-08(e)(3), note 20):** registrant operating cash +$7,555k (2025);
  **90.5% of registrant net income is an equity-method pick-up**; registrant cash $96,184k.
- **Cash by jurisdiction (note 2):** at 2025-12-31 **8.5% of the group's $1,132.6M sat at the registrant**;
  52.6% in mainland China behind SAFE approval and fixed deposit terms; 37.2% in Hong Kong inside
  CleanChip — **which ACM Research sold to ACM Shanghai in December 2019 for $3.5M, before the STAR
  IPO**. **Restricted net assets of $1,675,187k exceed ACM Research's entire equity.**

**The difference from GHC is the useful part.** GHC's distortion was a mandatorily redeemable NCI — a
liability. ACMR's is an **ordinary minority in a listed subsidiary that keeps issuing its own shares**,
so it shows up as a *falling percentage* and a *rising APIC* (the subsidiary issues above book, so ACM
Research's equity went from $904.6M to $1,464.4M in FY2025 without an ACMR share being sold). **The
dilution looks like value creation in the consolidated balance sheet and like dilution only in the
ownership footnote.** Combined with the registrant's own issuance, **a 2024 ACMR share's look-through
claim on the operating business is 0.812 as large nineteen months later.**

### Q2 OUT, ON FOUR FILED GROUNDS

1. **[E3-03] criterion (2)** — the 10-K names nine substitutes (Lam, NAURA, SCREEN, SEMES, TEL, Kokusai,
   Applied, Suzhou Jingtuo, and *"recent entrants of local equipment suppliers"*) and concedes
   competitors may *"offer bundled discounts … that we cannot match."*
2. **[E3-46]** — on the KLAC/AMAT/LRCX row formula, **ROUNTOA 4.9% (10.3% ex-cash), last of eight filers
   and half of Axcelis's 10.2%**; operating margin 12.1%; services and spares at most 8.4% of revenue.
3. **[E2-44] both halves** — gross margin **−5.7 points in FY2025, the first full year after the
   2024-12-02 Entity List designation, while revenue grew 15.2%**; and **cumulative operating cash of
   −$32.7M** over eight years of 43%-a-year revenue growth.
4. **[E2-59]** — **99.63% of revenue from mainland China**; "Other Regions" revenue fell **$16.8M → $6.4M →
   $3.3M**; the 10-K attributes growth to customers' drive *"to achieve a greater share of the global
   semiconductor market"*; state grants; a Pudong state vehicle holds 5% of the US parent; and the
   Lingang production centre is held on a **land-grant tax covenant dated 2027-07-09**.

**Why NONE and not NARROW like ACLS**: ACLS had no captive threat, a filed price range that rose through
the bust, a 31.9% aftermarket and a diversified customer list. ACMR fails all four distinctions.

### A UNIT SERIES EXISTS — THE FIRST IN THIS COHORT SINCE ACLS

Cumulative tools delivered, Item 1 of every 10-K: **annual delta +55 (FY2020), +90, +155, +385 (FY2023),
+355, +315 (FY2025), ~310 annualised (H1-2026)**. The definition widened twice (FY2020, FY2023), so only
FY2023 onward is one series — **and on it units have fallen three years running while revenue per
delivered tool went $1.45M → $2.20M → $2.86M.** Either a genuine mix climb into ECP/furnace/PECVD, or
[E4-55]'s Precision Steel shape. Carried to Q6 rather than resolved.

### Q4, RECORDED: A FIFTH SURVIVAL SHAPE

**Owner earnings are negative on every one of nine windows, at both (c) ends, and on the trailing twelve
months** — −$104.2M to −$26.0M consolidated, **−$82.0M to −$20.5M attributable to ACM Research**, TTM
−$146.0M to −$54.5M. **The range is $78M wide and does not span zero**, which is the unusual thing: [E4-25]'s
*"no useful conclusion"* is the verdict for a range that straddles the answer, and this one does not.
Added to the ORCL / ARM / BE / BA set: **growth refilled by selling the subsidiary** — net cash on the
balance sheet, negative owner earnings, and the refill valve is equity issued at a register the US
holder cannot own or vote in. **Partly ARM's shape, and worse**: ARM's SBC consumed 96.6% of positive
operating cash; **ACMR's cumulative SBC of $135.9M was paid against cumulative operating cash of −$32.7M
— out of financing, not operations.**

### Q3, RECORDED: THE FLAGS CONVERGE ON MARKET VALUE, NOT ON THE NUMBERS

No honesty disqualifier: *Kain v. ACM Research* dismissed with prejudice 2022-01-10; the FY2022 adverse
ICFR opinion (two material weaknesses) remediated by 2023-12-31 with no restatement; Armanino's 2023 exit
was from all public-company audit, with no disagreement. **But [E4-52] convergence:** a **$4bn revenue
target**; **adjusted EBITDA** as a 10-K key measure since FY2017 **and a Bank of China covenant at 5x
EBITDA** — [E5-41]'s *"higher borrowing power"* written into a loan; **NEOs holding options on ACM Shanghai
stock (CEO 1,250,000)**, which puts management on both sides of subsidiary dilution; a CEO option vesting
on **market capitalisation** ($1.55bn / $2.55bn / $3.55bn tranches), which issuance moves; the Class B
sunset defeated by a market-cap level in 2020; and **serial issuance at two registers**. **The accounting
reads clean after 2023; the convergence is in the incentives and the capital structure.**

**[E4-29] ran the INVERSE of CGNX:** zero EBITDA mentions in the three 2025–26 earnings releases, 24 in the
FY2025 10-K. **The standing instruction to read the EX-99.1 before scoring [E4-29] should be symmetric —
read both, because the flag can live in either.**

### PRIORS REFUTED OR MOVED
- **Refuted in part — "the customer list" as the Q2 killer.** Concentration broadened: three customers
  87.6% (2018) → 43.8% (2022) → **one customer above 10% in H1-2026**. The Q2 verdict rests on the
  substitutes, the returns number, the margin and the regime — **the customer list is the weakest of the
  grounds, not the strongest.**
- **Refuted — the tier-3 label.** "SIGN CHANGE — recoveries" describes the reverse of ACMR's series (the
  positive years are the early ones) and the queue's two ends come from two different windows.
- **Moved — the AMAT service-margin analogy.** It does not transfer: ACMR files no service line and its
  blended bucket is at most 8.4%. **ACMR is not evidence for or against the AMAT finding; it lacks the leg.**
- **[E2-49] metric-switching: did not fire** — the 10-K's four key measures are unchanged FY2017–FY2025.
  Record now **seven fires, six failures** (fired SHOP, MRVL, PAY, ARM, CALX, BE, ROKU; failed QLYS, CRM,
  CORT, PLTR, INOD, ACMR).
- **Export controls: ACMR does NOT resemble AMAT's BIS position** — no settlement, penalty or denial order;
  ACM Shanghai is a **designated party** the world may not supply, which is a supply-chain constraint
  rather than an enforcement matter.

### THE STRONGEST SINGLE FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT **[E4-51]**
**ACMR's ~353M ACM Shanghai shares at the filed February 2026 transfer price (RMB 160.00 ≈ $23.05) carry a
quoted value of roughly $8.1bn — against ACMR's own $5.0bn cap**, before any registrant cash. A
sum-of-the-parts buyer calls that a 38% discount. **It is a spread between two quotes, not a yield**; the
stake cannot be distributed (*"Stockholders of ACM Research may never directly own equity interests in ACM
Shanghai"*); and the only way the registrant has ever realised it is by selling Shanghai shares, which
lowers the 73.2%. And it prices a company with negative owner earnings at ~$11bn in Shanghai, which is
the quote [E2-28] tells an owner to sell into.

### THE ROOT CAUSE OF EVERY COMMIT CROSSING, FOUND AND FIXED
SWK staged the deletion of a 5.7MB dump it had committed, **and that staged deletion landed inside MY
commit `83d56f7`, titled for ACMR** - even though I had staged only my own file by name. **Tested in two
fresh repositories: `git add mine.txt && git commit` produced a commit containing both `mine.txt` and
the other session's `theirs.txt`; `git commit -- mine.txt` contained only `mine.txt` and left the other
file staged for its owner.** The rule every brief carried - *"commit your own files by name"* - chose
what a session added and never excluded what another had. **That is the root cause of all six crossings
recorded in this tree.** FOLD step 6, the overnight prompt and the run-agent memory now require
**`git commit -F <msgfile> -- <paths>`**. The six crossings already made stay recorded.

### CORRECTION, 2026-09-12 23:37 — my Item 2.01 claim was wrong, tested against its own motivating case
In the SWK fold I recorded that **8-K Item 2.01 "is the item that marks" a closed divestiture** and
called it *"a measured addition for the next session."* **It was not measured. I measured it now, and
it fails on the case that motivated it.**

- **SWK's CAM sale closed in April 2026, and Stanley filed ZERO Item 2.01 8-Ks after its 10-K.** It
  announced the sale under **Item 7.01 (Regulation FD)**, on 2026-04-06 and 2026-04-20. **Item 2.01 is
  required only for a SIGNIFICANT disposition**, so a completed sale below that threshold is disclosed
  another way and never reaches it. **The approach is structurally incomplete, not merely noisy.**
- **It also throws false positives from filer mistagging.** Across the 331 priced names, Item 2.01
  fires on 19. One is **PAY's filing of 2026-08-03 - which is its Q2 earnings release**, *"Paymentus
  Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results,"* tagged 2.01 where it belongs under 2.02.
  **PAY's run therefore did NOT miss an acquisition**, and its verdict needs no addendum.
- **It does catch significant completions correctly**: it fired on **HHH's Vantage acquisition of
  2026-06-05**, the event that made HHH the queue's only UNKNOWABLE.

**Incomplete AND unclean is no basis for a guard, so it is NOT built and NOT wired into the queue.** It
joins the source limits: **a closed perimeter event is reliably found only by reading the 10-Q and the
press releases, and the item number on an 8-K is not a dependable index to it.** The lesson is the one I
keep having to relearn: I wrote a recommendation as though it were a finding, and the first test of
its motivating case refuted it.

### TOOLING DEFECTS
1. **The queue price can be one event stale, and the brief carried it.** The pre-check struck ACVA at a close taken before an

   1.01s across the queue is for the next session to measure, not for this fold to assert (the Item 2.01 lesson of 2026-09-12).
2. **The screen counts seller float as owner earnings.** `wc_note` fired correctly (285%) and the row still carried the float inside
   both ends. For settlement businesses (auction houses, payment processors that hold funds on balance sheet) the ends are not owner
   earnings until the payables and receivables lines are removed; only a reader sees which filers are in the class.
3. **Operating cash omits floorplan credit losses** where finance receivables sit in investing. No tag-level guard can see the

4. **The D&A end double-counts capitalised SBC** — its amortization sits inside D&A ($6.2M FY2025) while the SBC line already carries
   it. A new variant of the acquired-amortization defect (SWK, ALKT).

   neither operating cash nor cash capex. The BOEING lesson in a third form: resolving is not complete.
6. **`cap_flag`'s two-date comparison, confirmed a second time** (ALKT defect 1): float struck at $16.22, cap at $6.76-equivalent.
7. **`oe_bottom` / `oe_top` from different windows and different (c) ends — the sixth instance.**
