### THE DEAL CHECK SAW THIS MERGER AND FILED IT AS SOFT, AND THE EXHIBIT FIXES IT
**A merger is announced in an 8-K Item 1.01 days before any proxy or 425 exists**, so the Copart deal sat
in the soft note that says *"a merger and a credit agreement look identical."* The run suggested the
merger-agreement exhibit, **EX-2.1**, as the marker. **After tonight's Item 2.01 failure, it was tested on
its motivating case FIRST:**

| filing | exhibits | EX-2.1? |
|---|---|---|
| ACV merger with Copart, 2026-09-10 | EX-10.1, **EX-2.1**, EX-99.1, EX-99.2 | yes - correct |
| ACV's own $50M buyback, 2026-05-13 | EX-10.1 | no - correct |
| Stanley's $1.0bn credit facility | EX-10.1, EX-10.2 | no - correct |
| ACMR's $150M share sale | EX-10.1, **EX-5.1** | no - correct |

**Then swept across all 122 soft names: EX-2.1 on 18 filings at 16 names, and every one of the 16 reads
as a real M&A agreement** - plans of merger, equity, asset, stock and unit purchase agreements. **No false
positive. That is the precision Item 2.01 lacked.**

**IT DOES NOT SAY WHICH SIDE, and that is deliberately left to the reader.** EX-2.1 is filed by the target
and the acquirer alike. **A regex classifier was tried and was wrong where it committed - it called Enerpac
and Embecta targets when both are the buyers.** Read by hand, **ACVA and Bowman (BWMN, a take-private) are
being acquired, so their quotes are spreads**; most of the rest are buying or selling a business, which
changes the perimeter instead. **`deal_note` now reports "M&A AGREEMENT ON FILE" when EX-2.1 is present,
says READ IT because the side decides the finding, and uses the exact regex the sweep validated.** Tested
on six known cases, all correct. **EX-5.1 marks a registered securities offering, debt or equity (25 names),
and is recorded rather than wired, because it rarely changes a verdict.**

**Survival-shape numbering, to reconcile when FLNC reports**: ACVA named a sixth shape, **"the borrowed
balance sheet"** (its cash is customers' money, which reverses in the same downturn that raises loan
losses), and the concurrent FLNC run named **"the treadmill"** as a sixth.

**Count: 77 runs** - gate-clearers 26, Q2 OUT 48, Q4 OUT 2, Q1 UNKNOWABLE 1.



## UPDATE 2026-09-12 - FLNC: Q2 OUT, an integrator of other people's cells on other people's balance sheets
`Test Runs/2026-09-12 Run - FLNC Fluence Energy.md`. **Q1 IN, Q2 OUT, file closed; Q3 recorded UNKNOWABLE, Q4 recorded OUT.**
Price **$9.93** x **184,596,369 economic shares** (Up-C: 143,163,588 Class A + 41,432,781 Class B-1, 10-Q cover
`0001868941-26-000029`) = **$1,833.0M**; sovereign **5.35%** (Treasury, 2026-09-11, struck fresh). Queue cap `1949` was
**6.3% high** on a stale price; the count behind it was right. The run did its own six-step fold.

### THE ROW WAS READ AS UNLABELLED, AND THE LABEL TURNED OUT FACTUALLY RIGHT
Unlike BE, FLNC really is negative on every construction: **-$183M to -$101M** on the 3-, 4- and 5-year windows, the TTM and
both (c) ends. **It was still the wrong instruction**, and this run is the cleanest proof of the correction of 2026-09-12:
every reason the number is negative is a Q1, Q2 or Q4 finding the label would have had the run skim.

### THE FINDING - five things that sit behind the negative sign
- **Q1, the asymmetric cost curve.** Fluence buys cells (the FY2025 10-K: *"including battery cells from China"*) and rents
  contract manufacturers. Its price per GWh falls with cell cost (*"lower average price per GWh ... as the cost of lithium-ion
  batteries has continued to decline"*, FY2025 MD&A) while cell-cost rises on signed fixed-price contracts land on Fluence
  (FY2022 supplier repricing, gross margin -5.2%; 9M FY2026 *"increases in battery prices"*, gross margin 6.5%, Q3 5.1%). On
  two-year GWh windows the customer took **~83%** of the cost decline - better than BE's 104%, but the sharper finding is the
  asymmetry: falls passed on, rises absorbed [E3-62].
- **Q2, the substitutes, from both sides.** Fluence names Tesla, Wärtsilä, Sungrow and CATL; **Eos's 10-K names Fluence**;
  Fluence's own risk factor says Chinese integrators price below it. **Tesla's energy segment went 18.9% -> 29.8% gross margin
  (2023-25) on 46.7 GWh while Fluence went 13.1% -> 6.5% on 5.0 GWh.** Stem exited battery hardware; Powin went bankrupt.
- **Q2, the borrowed moat.** The strongest bull input - bankability - is the sponsors': performance guarantees and $100.0M of
  supply-chain-finance guarantees from AES and Siemens, and a risk factor that says a reduction in the Founders' ownership *"may
  prompt business partners to reprice"*. The Founders sold 23.0M shares at $21.00 in May 2026 [E4-23].
- **Q4, the treadmill.** Customers and suppliers lent **$1.13bn** of working capital from FY2021 to 2026-06-30 and cumulative
  operating cash was still **-$1,092.0M**. Deferred revenue is **$1,014.0M, 2.8x cash**, discharged at a 5-13% gross margin
  below ~$350M of overhead. FY2024's only positive operating cash was **payables +$370.1M (the screen's 464%) and accruals
  +$160.2M**.
- **Q4, the perimeter (the ACMR question in Up-C form).** Class A owns **77.55%** of LLC owner earnings, then pays corporate tax
  on its share and owes the Founders **85% of basis-step-up tax savings (TRA: $165.1M on $194.2M, unrecorded)**. The yield is
  unchanged by the split (whole-LLC count against whole-LLC earnings); the TRA is a claim on the success case only.

### PRIORS REFUTED OR CONFIRMED
1. **"Q2 OUT on criterion (2)" - confirmed**, and named precisely: the filed price mechanism is the proof of substitution.
2. **"The customer took the cost curve" (the BE analogy) - modified:** ~83%, not 104%; the asymmetry is the finding.
3. **"2 Item 1.01 8-Ks" - refuted:** one revolver amendment and its clerical 8-K/A. It was covenant relief (first 3.50x
   leverage test moved to 2027-01-01).
4. **"Powin (bankrupt - check)" - confirmed from a filing** (Ameresco 10-K: Chapter 11 on 2025-06-10, $26.7M of deposits
   stranded) - and it became **the strongest fact against the verdict**, not for it.
5. **"BE's deposit shape or BA's" - both, by question:** BE's for the operating cash (unreadable in any period), BA's for the
   economics (advances discharged by building), at a thin positive margin that does not cover overhead.
6. **"A battery-cell supplier dispute and a cybersecurity/US-content controversy" - partly:** the supplier dispute is filed
   (largest module vendor repriced a signed agreement, 2022; $19.5M settlement); a June-July 2026 cyber incident is filed; no
   U.S.-content controversy was found, only PFE-compliance uncertainty now said to be resolved.
7. **The metric-withdrawal prior [E2-49] FIRED** - Free Cash Flow headlined in FY2024 (+$71.6M, the payables year), absent in
   FY2025, and **redefined in Q2 FY2026 to add back supply-chain financing** ($70.8M). **Tally: ten fires (SHOP, MRVL, PAY, ARM,
   CALX, BE, ROKU, SWK, ACVA, FLNC), seven failures (QLYS, CRM, CORT, PLTR, INOD, ACMR, ALKT).**

### THE REBUILT RANGE
**-$183M to -$101M** (5y capex end to 3y D&A end); TTM -$160.1M to -$150.1M; the screen's `-184 / -101` reproduce within $1.2M
from **different windows and different (c) ends - the seventh such pair**. [E4-41] normalises down (FY2023 $19.5M supplier
settlement; 9M FY2026 $18.9M of 45X credits, IEEPA refunds, a $39.4M receivables sale). If the supply-chain-financing footnote
is read literally, TTM owner earnings are -$262M to -$252M. **SBC resolves and is complete** (the question the BE and BA runs
made standing).

### THE SURVIVAL SHAPE - THE SIXTH (ACVA's BORROWED BALANCE SHEET), IN A FIXED-PRICE FORM: THE TREADMILL
The ACVA run folded the sixth shape earlier the same night (commit 42bcdbe). Fluence belongs to it - liquidity lent by customers that runs
backwards when orders slow - **with a performance obligation ACV's float does not carry**: each deposit dollar costs ~95 cents to
discharge before overhead, on contracts exposed to cell prices, so the borrowed balance sheet must keep growing to stand still.
Named death: an order slowdown (customer money back to its FY2024 level is -$701M against $365M of cash) plus a cell-price margin
shock on $3.1-3.4bn of next-twelve-month backlog. **A real possibility**; the likeliest permanent loss is dilution, not a filing.
Recorded as the sixth shape's second instance, not a seventh class, so the register stays countable.

### Q3, RECORDED
No integrity finding. **UNKNOWABLE on the open SEC formal investigation** (revenue recognition, capitalised software, related-party
service contracts), in a daily-execution gate case with a revenue-recognition material weakness in three consecutive 10-Ks.
Converging flags [E4-52]: FY2025 revenue $337M below the floor of a twice-cut range; Adjusted EBITDA as the guided and paid
yardstick; the FCF redefinition; the except-for pattern. **AES is owner, customer (24.5% of FY2025 revenue on "preferred
purchasing conditions") and guarantor at once**; a July 2026 Delaware derivative suit names AES. In management's favour: the
2025 bonus paid 0% on every financial metric and the 2024-26 PSUs were forfeited, with no discretion used.

### THE STRONGEST SINGLE FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT [E4-51]
**Powin, a competitor Fluence itself once named, went bankrupt in June 2025 and stranded a customer's deposits.** In a market where
the buyer pre-pays and relies on the integrator for a decade, a sponsor-backed, 19.3-GWh integrator may not be a close substitute for
a weak one - and record orders followed. It does not reverse the verdict because the bankability is the sponsors', and the customer's
power over Fluence's price is filed regardless of how safe Fluence is.

3. **`wc_note` names payables but cannot see customer deposits or supply-chain finance** - the larger lines in this file.
4. **The owner-earnings ends are from different windows and (c) ends a seventh time.**

- **Q1, what it is.** A reseller buying from ~280 suppliers (ten = 68.8% of purchases) at a **~9.5% direct margin after

  verified by reading); Newegg names all of them. Micro Center is private; its only EDGAR trace is as a REIT anchor tenant.

### FOUR TOOLING CHANGES FROM NEGG, AND ONE OF THEM REPAIRS A FIX OF MINE FROM AN HOUR EARLIER
1. **`best_year_dependence` refuses a near-zero POSITIVE mean.** It guarded `mean <= 0`, and Newegg's +$0.11M
   slipped through to print 9,918% - **the fifth instance of the ratio-near-zero class**, and the same gap
   `level_shift` had. Refused on 3 names; the ordinary-compounder and ANF regression cases are unchanged.
2. **MY OWN MISLABEL, corrected.** The working-capital note I wrote an hour earlier called the average of
   ABSOLUTE operating cash "a five-year average". Newegg's reads $21.1M that way; **the signed mean is minus
   $12.9M.** It now says "typical |OCF|".
3. **AND THAT SAME NOTE NEVER REACHED A BRIEF.** The queue truncates it to 150 characters, and my version put
   its conclusion last, so **NEGG's cell ended "...against a typi" and the one sentence that mattered - that
   the ratio means nothing - was cut off.** The week's recurring defect, a diagnostic that never reaches the
   reader, introduced by my own longer wording. **Rewritten conclusion-first ("RATIO MEANINGLESS"), the
   `IncreaseDecreaseIn` prefix dropped (18 characters), the cell widened to 260. All 13 near-zero notes now
   survive through their last word**, matching the original measurement exactly.
4. **`name_change_note()` - a prompt for a different company's history under the same CIK, with its precision
   stated.** The SEC's `formerNames` record caught NEGG exactly. **Measured before building**: raw it fires on
   **101 of 331**, mostly noise (Cisco, Walmart and ADM show a "former name" identical to the current one;
   many are rebrands). Dropping normalised-identical names and rebrands that share a word leaves **41; read
   by hand, about 26 are genuine perimeter events** (de-SPACs, spin shells, reverse mergers like NEGG, TECX
   and ARMP, mergers like Helix into Hornbeck) **and ~15 are rebrands the filter misses. About 60% precision -
   stated in the note itself.** Only reading separates a harmless de-SPAC from a reverse merger into an
   operating shell.

**The queue is regenerated with all of tonight's changes**: 16 M&A agreements (EX-2.1), 23 live deal forms,
41 name changes, 13 near-zero working-capital notes, 3 refused best-year readings.

### SBC/OCF - THE CALIBRATED ROW HAS NO PLACE FOR THIS NAME
Operating cash is negative in every period on file (cumulative −$283.5M), so **SBC ÷ OCF is refused in words** - the same rule
written into `level_shift` and `growth_required`. At ARM, stock pay ate the owners' share of real operating cash; **at Rigetti
there is no operating cash to eat - stock pay is added to a loss, and the loss is paid for by selling more stock.** Substitute
stated: SBC was 169% of cumulative revenue. **The row's companion for pre-revenue names should be SBC ÷ revenue, or equity issued ÷
cash consumed (2.4x here) - not built.**

is locked by the **74.7% controlling shareholder** rather than by the customer [E2-59].

### THE DISCONFIRMING READ THAT MADE THE VERDICT HARDER AND THEN SHARPER [E4-26]
The blended fee-rate fall is **MIX, not third-party erosion.** BWS - BN's own insurer - is **$108bn of FBC generating $234M of
fees, 23.4bp** ($92bn and $167M in FY2024). **Ex-BWS the FY2025 rate is 99.1bp and is not falling.** That **defeats** the claim
that BAM's customers are forcing its price down, and it **does not rescue criterion (2)** - 99.1bp is still fourth of ten, and
KKR's and APO's blended rates are depressed by exactly the same mechanism (Global Atlantic, Athene), so a like-for-like
ex-insurance row would lift them too. **What it does instead is sharpen the mix finding: $48.6bn of the firm's $87.3bn of H1 2026
gross inflows - 55.7%, and 70% of the entire $69.4bn increase in Fee-Bearing Capital - came from the controlling shareholder's
insurance balance sheet at a quarter of the third-party price.** The growth carrying the $1-trillion plan is, in the most recent
filed period, **majority related-party capital.**

### THE SURVIVAL SHAPE - A NINTH: THE WAREHOUSE
**Not one of the eight.** ORCL contracted not to stop building; ARM's stock pay ate the owners' cash; RGTI sells equity as
revenue; ACVA/FLNC/NEGG borrow a balance sheet. **BAM lends one - to its own funds' deals.** *"The Company earns fees in
connection with bridge financing and **bears the risk associated with syndicating the commitment**"* (10-Q Note 15): **$3.3bn
(end-2024) -> $6.6bn (end-2025) -> $8.0bn (2026-06-30)**, plus $433M of fund guarantees, against **$3.1bn of corporate
liquidity - 2.6x**, with **no filed maturity schedule**. The commitments grew **2.4x in eighteen months in a benign market**,
which is [E4-40]'s exposure-not-experience exactly. **It carries the FIFTH shape's feature - distribution above owner earnings
[E2-60] - in a debt-funded rather than divestiture-funded form**: dividends plus buybacks were **127-179% of owner earnings in
every filed period**, funded by cash ($3,545M at end-2022 to $404M at end-2024), then $2.5bn of notes in 2025 and $1.0bn in April
2026, then $655M of related-party deposits. **The register now stands at NINE.**
**Why the business still survives its own named death:** the near-term cash requirement that fails [E5-11]'s third strength is, in
the main, **the dividend and the buyback - both discretionary.** Cutting the payout releases ~$3.2bn a year immediately while fees
keep arriving on $298bn of committed capital under 10-12 year terms. **[E2-54]**'s coverage test passes at 9-24x with no maturity
before 2030. **The mechanism breaks the distribution, not the company** - insolvency a low-level possibility, the dividend path
breaking a real possibility.

### THE STRONGEST SINGLE FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT [E4-51]
**87% of the fee base is long-dated or perpetual; a closed-end client literally cannot leave for a decade; the listed-affiliate
MSAs *"cannot be terminated without BN's consent"*; and the third-party fee rate is 99.1bp and is not eroding.** The lock is real
and it is stronger than most brands. The verdict turns on the distinction that the lock is on money *already committed*, never on
the next dollar - and nine filers compete for the next dollar, three of them growing faster at an equal or higher price.

### A RESUMED RUN - WHAT THE DRAFTS ON DISK COST AND WHAT THEY NEARLY COST
The killed session left Q3, Q4, Q5 and Q6 written but never appended, with five unresolved placeholders and **two lines that
presupposed a verdict Q2 had not reached**:
1. Q3's weight case read *"[E3-43]'s original form governs **once Q2 has found no franchise**."*
2. Q4's verdict ended *"**if this Q4 were governing**, strength (3) would need the commitment maturity schedule … before an IN
   could be written without a caveat."*
**The second is the more dangerous, and it is a protocol defect as well as a smuggled conclusion**: an IN carrying a caveat is
UNRESEARCHED by the framework's own thin-evidence rule, so the draft's Q4 was only writable as IN *because* Q2 was assumed to have
closed the file first. **Q2 was decided from the filings and the peer row before either line was read back**, and both were
rewritten with the correction recorded in place rather than repaired silently. The Q4 caveat was replaced by a **reason** - the
verdict rests on the coverage test and the contractual fee term, not on the missing schedule, and the failing cash requirement is
discretionary - with the schedule recorded at Q6 as a reopening condition instead.
**The verdict the drafts presupposed and the verdict reached agree. That they agree is not what made the rewriting unnecessary;
the rewriting was done anyway, and the CGNX prohibition is why.**

### THE BLOCK, TESTED
The 2026-09-02 note called BAM and BN *"asset managers with fee streams and consolidated funds."* **For BN that was wrong on the
facts:** BN is a holding company whose own definition is *"ownership interests in our Asset Management, Wealth Solutions and
Operating Businesses"*, with an **audited parent-only balance sheet** (40-F Note 1, three columns) and a separate SEC filer for
every leg. **Measurable.** What the note was right about, again: no five-year window on one perimeter exists.

### HOW A HOLDING COMPANY'S Q2 WAS ASKED - a method finding for the next multi-leg name
The BRK run found a moat at the level of the whole (a funding structure no leg carried); the L run asked the question where the
earnings are. **BN needed both, in that order:**
1. **The whole-level claim first**, because BN makes one in writing (the *"Brookfield Ecosystem"*, *"five distinct advantages for our
   franchise"*). Tested on the one number BRK's whole-level moat rested on - **the cost of the permanent capital** - and on the
   attacker's test. **It fails on both:** BN's own risk factor says competitors *"may have … a lower cost of capital"*, BWS has the
   highest life and annuity cost of funds of four filers, and Apollo-Athene and KKR-Global Atlantic run the same system at larger scale.
2. **Then the legs, weighted three ways** (segment book equity, cash reaching the Corporation, quoted market), **because each single
   weight flatters a different leg**: book puts real estate at 43%, market puts BAM at 44%, cash puts the fee engine at 37%. **The three
   legs carrying 84-87% on every basis were rowed; the three carrying 12-16% were read from the parent's filing and not rowed**, with the
   directional reason stated (the parent's own text puts them in regulated, contracted or highly competitive classes) and each row named
   as a reversal work order.
**Why the BAM row transferred as a floor, not a ceiling:** at BN the fee engine's "conferred" durable leg is partly **BN paying itself**
(BWS's $243M of fees to Brookfield; BEP and BIP's $466M of IDRs to BAM). A fee paid between two controlled legs cannot be a customer's
judgment about substitutes, because at the parent there is no customer.

6. **The brief's prior 4, spread vs cost of float - resolved to cost of funds**, which is [E3-69]'s own quantity for a spread writer and
   the name four filers use; the spread is shown beside it because that is where BWS's number is built differently.

### Q4 IN NUMBERS, BECAUSE THEY ARE THE STARKEST IN THE MINI BERK TRACK
Look-through owner earnings at BN's share **about $0 to $1.1bn a year, bottom nil ($12M)**, against DE of $6.0bn. **BEP's operating cash
was below its depreciation in FY2024 and FY2025** ($1,147M against $2,425M in FY2025, with $6,587M of capex). **BPY's operating cash was
negative in two of three years** while it paid $800M to its redeemable and special LP holders. IFRS return on common equity **2.37% /
1.13% / 2.66%**. **The marks and the cash disagree by a factor of three:** parts at their own marks ~$45 a share; owner earnings plus
investments at book ~$9-17. **Named death: the internal funding loop in reverse** (BWS holds $20.4bn of Brookfield-related assets against
$12.7bn of capital), ~25% of common equity at risk - a real possibility; Corporation failure a low-level possibility on 15-year recourse debt.

## UPDATE 2026-09-13 - SONY: Q2 OUT, a conglomerate judged per segment, and a spin-off perimeter rebuilt rather than averaged across
`Test Runs/2026-09-13 Run - SONY Sony Group.md`. **Q1 IN, Q2 OUT, file closed; Q3 recorded IN with an EBITDA-pay history and a live
buyback flag; Q4 recorded (survives; the named death is the owner's return); Q5 headed COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE; Q6 recorded with
nothing armed.** Price **¥3,632** x **5,843,334,871 shares** (July 2026 Share Buyback Report treasury count, 6-K `0001104659-26-094573`,
walked through August by hand) = cap **¥21,223bn**; sovereign **JGB 30-year 3.995%** (Japan MOF, 2026-09-10). **The first WAVE 5 name
and the first of its eleven foreign 20-F filers.**

### THE SKIP REASON, TESTED
The triage called SONY a *"foreign 20-F filer ... [with] too few annual periods because their XBRL history is short."* **Half right.**
Companyfacts carries IFRS annual facts back to FY3/21, so the history is not short; **what it lacked on 2026-09-13 was the FY3/26 20-F
itself** (latest 20-F accession in the facts: `0001193125-25-143137`), and **what it could never supply is the perimeter**: the
consolidated operating cash flow before the spin-off runs the insurer's and bank's policyholder and deposit flows through operations
(FY3/23 consolidated OCF ¥314.7bn against ¥415.5bn for the industrial business alone; FY3/25 ¥2,321.7bn). **A mechanical owner-earnings
line on the XBRL would have been an insurer-contaminated number.** The skip reason was a prompt to read the filing, which is what it
turned out to need.

### THE PERIMETER - HOW A DISCONTINUED OPERATION WAS HANDLED (the CNR rule, a new form)
- **What the filing says:** partial spin-off of Sony Financial Group decided 2025-05-14, executed **2025-10-01** by dividend in kind
  (¥955,700M), **16.40% retained** and equity-accounted; discontinued operations, **comparatives re-presented three years deep**.
- **Where a longer window came from:** Sony published an unaudited *"Condensed Statements of Cash Flows"* separating *"Sony without
  Financial Services"* in Item 5 of every 20-F. **The two bases differ by one intra-group flow** - the FS dividend to the parent, counted
  in the separated schedule and eliminated in continuing operations - so FY3/21-FY3/23 were rebuilt by removing it, and **the splice was
  measured in both overlap years before use** (residual ¥24.1bn, 2.2%, in FY3/24; ¥1.1bn in FY3/25). **Method note for the next
  spin-off filer:** look for the company's own separated schedule before refusing a window; measure the splice; state the residual.

### THE CONTENT TRAP - a (c) defect the D&A default would have made silently
Sony classifies film, TV, catalog and game-content additions **inside operating cash flow** (Note 27(1)), **and** its cash-flow
*"Depreciation and amortization"* **includes content amortization** (Pictures D&A ¥517.8bn in FY3/26). **The [E3-44] default applied to
reported D&A would have charged content twice** - once as cash inside OCF, again as (c) - understating owner earnings by ~¥400-600bn a
year. The run used D&A less content amortization at the D&A end. **This is the RESUME STATE's ELF finding ("the D&A end of (c)
triple-counts on filers that capitalise displays or cloud costs") in a new and much larger class: every studio, label and publisher
that capitalises content into operating assets.** A tooling screen cannot see it; the reader must check where content cash sits.

### HOW A CONGLOMERATE'S Q2 WAS DECIDED - the third precedent, and where it sits
GHC (no leg passes -> OUT), HAS (profit overwhelmingly in the franchise leg and the rest eating no capital -> IN), BRK (a group-level
structural moat carries substitutable legs -> IN). **SONY is the case between them:** two NARROW legs (Music; G&NS, generation-contingent)
at **54.6% of five-year segment profit**, three legs that fail [E3-03] or [E4-04] at ~45% **and the largest capital programme** (I&SS
¥265.3bn of ¥804.9bn FY3/26 capex; Pictures content additions ¥100bn a year above amortization), no filed group-level moat, and the
whole's ROE down five years running. **Decided OUT on the conjunction, with no numeric mix threshold invented** - none exists in the
corpus, and the verdict names the two filed facts it rests on.

### PRIORS REFUTED OR CONFIRMED
- **"The spin-off was planned for around October 2025" (the brief's memory):** confirmed, with the retained 16.40% and the three-year
  re-presentation the memory lacked.
- **"Sony is a franchise because PlayStation and Music are":** the legs, yes (NARROW each); the security, no.

  Adjusted EBITDA as its KPI *while it was beating its target by 21%*, toward operating income; the candor pattern. One more failure
  for that ledger; runs folded since the RESUME STATE are not recounted here.
- **The CGNX companion rule paid again:** the FY3/25 and FY3/26 20-Fs no longer print Adjusted OIBDA in the MD&A (the FY3/24 20-F headlined it), but every segment page of the
  FY2025 and Q1 FY2026 results decks does; the 10-K/20-F alone would have under-read [E4-29].

### THE SURVIVAL SHAPE - A TENTH: THE CAMOUFLAGE
Not one of the nine (ORCL, ARM, BE, BA, SWK, ACVA/FLNC/NEGG, CNR, RGTI, BAM's WAREHOUSE). **The company does not die; the owner's
return does**, because two franchise legs' cash is recycled into legs that must re-win a race every cycle and the consolidated series
hides the rate earned on the recycling **[E2-56, E2-27]**: ROE 22.0% -> 13.0% in five years while equity nearly doubled and ¥1.90tn went
to acquisitions and investments outside (c). **It carries BAM's second feature in part** - cash distributions (¥657bn in FY3/26; up to
~¥704bn planned) at or above five-year owner earnings - funded by the working-capital release and net cash, not a warehouse. **The

## UPDATE 2026-09-13 - TM: Q2 OUT, the best volume car company in the row, and its own bridge says the savings did not stay home
`Test Runs/2026-09-13 Run - TM Toyota Motor.md`. **Q1 IN, Q2 OUT, file closed; Q3 recorded (no integrity disqualifier at board level,
four converging prompts, a live buyback flag); Q4 recorded (survives; the named death is the owner's return); Q5 headed COMPUTATION - NOT
A CLEARANCE; Q6 recorded with nothing armed.** Price **¥3,031** x **11,813,621,960 shares** (20-F cover walked through the self-tender
result, the Q1 FY2027 summary and the August repurchase notice) = cap **¥35,807bn**; sovereign **JGB 30-year 3.995%** (Japan MOF,
2026-09-10). **The second WAVE 5 name.**

### THE SKIP REASON, TESTED
*"Foreign 20-F filer ... too few annual periods because their XBRL history is short."* **Right in effect, wrong in cause.** Toyota moved
from US GAAP to IFRS with the FY2021 20-F, so `companyfacts` holds `ifrs-full` annual facts for FY2020-FY2025 only, and **the FY2026
20-F filed 2026-06-10 had not been ingested by 2026-09-13** (SONY found the same lag). The filings themselves hold **ten years of the
two-way Non-Financial / Financial Services cash-flow statement**, on two bases, and the run read all ten, measuring the basis gap in the
overlap year (3.5% of free cash) rather than splicing blind.

### THE QUESTION THE BRIEF ASKED, AND WHY IT HAD TWO ANSWERS
*GM and F failed Q2 on excess-capacity language; does Toyota's filed cost and margin record differ?*
- **Yes, relatively.** On an all-charges-in basis (Toyota's segment measure is IFRS operating income with the ¥1,380bn tariff and
  ¥845bn of recall provisions inside it; GM's is EBIT-adjusted and Stellantis's is AOI), Toyota's automotive margin **led the eight-name
  row in each of the last three fiscal years** and its five-year pooled **8.22%** beat every volume peer's comparable figure (GM 5.39%
  with GM Financial inside, VW about 5.6%, Ford 1.46%, Honda automobile -0.62%). GM and F failed at the bottom of this row; Toyota sits at
  the top of its volume half.
- **No, absolutely.** The [E2-58] exception is a cost advantage *"both wide and sustainable"*. Not wide: GM (8.60%) and Stellantis (9.61%)
  beat it on their own adjusted measures, and the width is roughly the EV write-offs the peers took and Toyota did not (yet: LF-ZC was
  cancelled in May 2026 with the cost unquantified). Not sustainable: **Toyota's own 20-Fs attribute every year's operating-income change
  to named causes, and the "Effect of cost reduction efforts" line summed to -¥645bn over FY2017-FY2026** (gross value-engineering
  savings of ¥240-265bn a year consumed by materials); **exchange rates contributed +¥1,685bn to a decade in which operating income rose
  ¥912bn**; the margin fell 11.20% -> 6.11% in two years while leading.
- **The method finding:** a Japanese filer's consolidated operating-income bridge is the place to run [E3-62]'s second step (*"how much
  is going to stay home"*) directly, year by year, from the company's own attribution.

### PRIORS REFUTED OR CONFIRMED
- **"Toyota is the exception to the commodity doctrine":** refuted on the doctrine's own two words, while confirmed as a relative leader.
- **"The captive-finance separation will change the picture as at GM and F":** refuted in direction. Toyota's lender earned 12.4% of
  seven-year pre-tax (GM's 89.9% in its latest year); the industrial business carries itself. The lender's share does rise when the
  industrial margin falls (8.2% -> 16.6% over FY2024-FY2026).
- **"A group take-private may be live":** completed 2026-06-15. TMC's cost: ¥3.66tn self-tender at a 10% discount to market to absorb
  Toyota Industries' 9.15% cross-holding, ¥800bn of 8.6% compounding preferred in the buyout vehicle (stated purpose: *"to invest the ample
  cash that the Company has accumulated"*), ¥1.26tn received for its 24.66% Toyota Industries stake; **net about ¥3.2tn out**. The
  chairman co-invests in the vehicle (6-K 2026-03-30); managed by an outside-director committee; the amount is not in TMC's exhibits.
- **The [E2-49] metric-withdrawal prior:** did not fire (the FY2020 depreciation-method change was announced with its ¥173.2bn effect).
- **The CGNX companion rule:** read and clean; EBITDA appears zero times in the 20-F and in both 2026 results releases.

### Q3, RECORDED
Binary gate (daily execution; Financial Services at 8.1x assets to equity). **[E4-22]'s cockroach fires at full strength**: certification
testing failed at four group companies (Hino 2022, Daihatsu 2023, Toyota Industries and TMC itself 2024; at TMC the regulator's on-site
work found eight more cases than the company's review), Hino's US criminal resolution effective 2025-03-19 with the penalty unquantified
in TMC's 20-F. Against it, the filed root cause names management (*"The management teams were responsible for what happened"*) and every
matter carries dated remediation. Other prompts: strategic shareholdings sold only *"once it obtains consent from the issuer"* ([E3-66]);
chairman pay +8% in a year operating income fell 21.5%, with market capitalisation in the bonus formula ([E4-27]). **Buyback flag:** the
¥3,067 tender valued the company near ¥40tn against this run's ¥20-35tn floor range; guidance record conservative (FY2026 operating income
guided ¥3,800bn, delivered ¥3,766bn).

### THE SURVIVAL SHAPE - AN ELEVENTH: THE PASS-THROUGH
Not one of the ten (ORCL, ARM, BE, BA, SWK, ACVA/FLNC/NEGG with FLNC's "treadmill" variant, CNR, RGTI, BAM's WAREHOUSE, SONY's CAMOUFLAGE).
**Nearest to the tenth, sharing its death and not its mechanism**: the company does not die, the owner's return does, but there is no
franchise leg funding a race and nothing is hidden. **A business that spends more than depreciation every year to hold unit volume
(industrial capex 1.53x D&A over ten years on +0.7% a year units) in an industry where every competitor does the same [E2-27], and whose
own filed savings are passed through to input costs, expenses and customers [E3-62].** The return exposure is **likely** (margin 6.11%,
break-even volume in a *"significant rise"*, FY2027 operating income guided ¥3,400bn against ¥5,353bn two years earlier); the lending tail
is **a low-level possibility** ([E3-24]'s 10%-of-loans-losing-30% arithmetic gives ¥1.17tn, 2.9% of TMC equity). **The register now
stands at ELEVEN.** *(The run first drafted the name "the treadmill"; renamed before commit because FLNC's fold already used it.)*

### THE STRONGEST SINGLE FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT [E4-51]
Toyota's all-in automotive margin is the highest in the filed row in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026, while Honda, Ford, Stellantis and GM wrote
off EV programmes. The file's answer is that the lead sits inside the peers' excluded charges and halved in two years, but the fact is
filed and favourable.

### TOOLING AND DOCUMENT DEFECTS

### THE QUESTION THE BRIEF ASKED: DOES THE MOTORCYCLE RECORD SHOW WHAT THE CAR RECORD DOES NOT?
- **Yes, on every filed measure.** Motorcycle segment margin 14.3 -> 18.2% FY3/22-26 and never below 9.9% in eleven filed years;

  generation capabilities"* will fund the automobile transition. The motorcycle class is NARROW, not WIDE: Hero files 28.7% of India's

### THE SURVIVAL SHAPE - THE TENTH (THE CAMOUFLAGE), IN A DECLARED FORM. NO NEW SHAPE.

**The company does not die; the owner's return does**, because a franchise leg's cash is recycled into a leg that must re-win a race each

### THE SOVEREIGN, THE HARD INPUT - AND HOW TO REPEAT IT FOR UMC
- The **Ministry of Finance** issues; the **Central Bank of the R.O.C. runs the auctions "on behalf of the Ministry of Finance"** and
  publishes each result (`cbc.gov.tw/en/cp-448-...`; the 30-year A15105 on 2026-05-26 at 1.8140% weighted average). That is the issuing
  authority's print, but it exists only on auction days.
- **The Taipei Exchange publishes the daily Treasury Yield Curve**: POST `https://www.tpex.org.tw/www/en-us/bond/govDaily2` with
  `date=YYYY/MM/DD&fileCode=Curve&response=json` lists the month's files; each `Curve.YYYYMMDD-E.xls` carries the 2/5/10/20/30-year EBTS
  benchmarks and fitted zero curves. 2026-09-11: 30-year 1.886% (below the 20-year's 2.101%), fitted 30-year zero 2.18-2.19%.
- **The CBC's NT$/US$ closing rate** (`cbc.gov.tw/en/lp-700-2.html`) is the issuing-authority FX. **Nothing was added to
  `tools/sources.py`.** The gap to USD is ~3.5 points, the widest in the queue; the floor makes it decision-irrelevant.

### THE QUESTION THE BRIEF ASKED: DID SHARE AND MARGIN HOLD THROUGH THE NODE TRANSITIONS?
- **Yes, tested and not assumed.** Gross margin 48.7% (2015) -> 59.9% (2025), operating margin 37.9% -> 50.8%, revenue x4.5 against UMC's
  x1.6 and GlobalFoundries' x1.17 (2019-25); 54.4% gross margin in the 2023 downturn (units -21%) above every peer's best year; revenue
  per wafer +21% that year (mix-confounded, stated). **Customers' filings carry the substitute test**: Broadcom ~95% of wafers, AMD all
  of 7nm and below, Intel's own leading products *"exclusively manufactured by TSMC"*. The attacker's test [E2-45] has been run and filed:
  Intel Foundry -58% operating margin in 2025.
- **And the record does not overturn [E4-04].** The full row reads *"rule out companies in industries prone to rapid and continuous
  change"*; TSMC's own 20-F uses that description of its industry and says its position depends on remaining *"a technology leader"*;
  capex exceeded depreciation in every year including the 2023 downturn; and the last leading-edge incumbent's filed margin fell 26 points
  in nine years after a lapse. **A ten-year record of staying on the wave is [E3-51]'s surfing run at its best.** This is consistent with
  the INTC run (the process node wholly replaced every generation) and SONY's I&SS leg, and it is the line the KLAC run drew between
  defending a platform and re-buying a node.

`Annual Meetings/2023 Annual Meeting.txt`, section 26: Berkshire *"bought a substantial position in Taiwan Semiconductor, and ... sold
almost the entire position within a few short months"*; Buffett: *"one of the best managed companies and important companies in the

manufacturers would be a structural change requiring a written case. **It is the single most relevant corpus passage for this name and
no brief mentioned it; future briefs for any name Berkshire has owned should point to the transcript.**

The filing gives no maintenance/growth split. It gives a 5-year machinery life, capex above depreciation in all eleven years **including
the downturn year**, and Q2's finding that holding position means re-buying the node, which is [E2-23]'s *"fully maintain its long-term

### THE SURVIVAL SHAPE - A TWELFTH: THE ADDRESS
Not one of the eleven (ORCL, ARM, BE, BA, SWK, ACVA/FLNC/NEGG with the treadmill and pendulum variants, CNR, RGTI, BAM's WAREHOUSE, SONY's

prints *"no overlapping OCF/D&A/capex annual facts"* purely because of the **USD-unit filter and the US-GAAP tag names** (RESUME STATE
section 9). TME, read for the row, shows the *lag* cause instead: its FY2025 20-F is in companyfacts for one dei fact only.

### THE BRIEF'S TRAPS, CHECKED
- **Issued vs outstanding (ERIC):** does not fire - the cover count is outstanding (issued 209,485,215 less treasury 3,652,688).
- **Beneficiary certificates:** no dividend, distribution or liquidation right (Articles 9.6) - excluded from the cap; 69.3% of votes.
- **Currency:** cap converted at the ECB reference rate of the quote date; every yield EUR over EUR (the ATLKY defect guarded).
- **Social costs on share-based pay:** the 20-F does not itemise the share-linked charge; it sits in the Note 5 payroll-tax line and the
  Note 20 accrual (87, 64, 64, 169, 84, 7, 57, 217, 217 for 2017-2025; 142 at June 2026), with quarterly amounts only in the furnished
  updates. Kept inside OCF; the accrual build subtracted at the high end.

### WHAT THE RUN FOUND THAT THE PRIOR (v3.0, 2026-07-15) RUN DID NOT
The five-pack called the moat "NARROW, WIDENING" on three price rises "with low churn" and priced owner earnings from net income in
dollars. Under v4.1: **churn has not been reported since 2021**; the price rises were **parallel across the industry** (WMG, Deezer); the
largest supplier states that **every service carries all content and a listener needs one subscription**; the royalty split that widened
the margin is **renegotiated every one to three years** with owners who took **50-64% of the revenue increments**; and the widening rests
on two profitable years in ten. The label side is a **bilateral oligopoly** - WMG says it has *"limited ability to increase our wholesale
prices"*, Spotify says the majors have *"market power"* - a negotiated split, not a franchise on either side.

### FOR THE OPERATOR
- **A proposed thirteenth survival shape, THE TENANT**, distinguished from TM's PASS-THROUGH (no capex race; the pass-through is
  contractual, to named suppliers, at renewal). Register it or fold it into PASS-THROUGH - a naming call, not a gate change.

## UPDATE 2026-09-13 - MBGL: Q2 UNKNOWABLE, a 45%-margin data business whose one substitute no filing measures
`Test Runs/2026-09-13 Run - MBGL Mobility Global.md`. **Q1 IN, Q2 UNKNOWABLE, file closed; Q3 recorded (no disqualifier, overlay, five
converging disclosure flags); Q4 recorded (would read IN on survival; THE DOWRY proposed); Q5 headed COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE; Q6
recorded with nothing armed.** Price **US$20.16** x **294,821,320 shares** = cap **US$5.94bn**; sovereign **USD 30-year 5.35%** (US Treasury,
09/11/2026). **The first Q2 UNKNOWABLE in the register.** **Register count at the fold, read from the register: 92 runs.**

### THE SKIP REASON, TESTED - A MISLABEL, NOT A 20-F
The triage called MBGL "Mercedes" and filed it with the 20-F names. **The ticker is Mobility Global Inc.**, S&P Global's former Mobility
segment (CARFAX, Polk, automotiveMastermind, Market Scan), distributed 1-for-1 to S&P Global holders on 2026-07-01. companyfacts had nothing
annual to price because the registrant had filed one 10-Q; **the audited history (combined cash-flow statements 2023-2025) is in the Form
10-12B/A Information Statement under MBGL's own CIK**, which the brief's pre-check did not list. No cash-flow statement exists for the
perimeter before 2023, so the five-year default window is two years short and was not filled from segment lines.

### THE BRIEF'S QUESTIONS, ANSWERED FROM THE FILED RECORD
- **What closed:** a pro rata spin-off; the EX-2.1 that fired `deal_note` is the Separation and Distribution Agreement. **Control:** widely
  held, one BlackRock 13G, no 13D. **Pending:** nothing; the quote is not a spread. The Tax Matters Agreement fences combinations, issuance and
  buybacks of 20% or more until 2028-07-01.
- **Predecessor history:** S&P Global's 10-K carries a Mobility segment from 2022-02-28 and IHS Markit's 10-Ks a Transportation segment, neither
  with cash flows; the Form 10 carries the only cash-flow statements. 2025 revenue cross-checked: Form 10 $1,750M, S&P Global segment $1,747M.
- **Separation debt:** $2.0bn of notes (2029/2031/2036) paid out as a $2.0bn dividend to S&P Global; revolver undrawn; cash $186M.
- **The ongoing relationship:** TSA up to 18 months, tax and employee agreements, non-exclusive IP cross-licences, reciprocal data licences the
  company calls *"not material to us"*.
- **Competitor row:** Experian's AutoCheck is not segmented in any filing and Experian's IR site blocked the fetch; Cox, J.D. Power and CDK are
  private; CarGurus and Cars.com file 10-Ks and sit well below CARFAX on margin. ACV Auctions is a channel, not a competitor - its 10-K and
  OPENLANE's name AutoCheck beside CARFAX.

### WHY UNKNOWABLE AND NOT IN OR OUT
- **For IN:** CARFAX at 43-45% before acquired amortization, capex ~1% of revenue, unleveraged net tangible assets ~$68M; a data estate grown
  from 17bn to 38bn records since FY2016; company-compiled revenue growth near 10% a year through a decade of flat vehicle sales; a 2013 dealer
  antitrust complaint that shows customers once believed there was no close substitute.
- **For OUT:** two wholesale registrants offer AutoCheck beside CARFAX; Listings (14%) is a follower on three registrants' lists; B2B (35%) is
  no franchise on its own competitor list and falling margin.
- **What decided it:** the missing peer is the ONLY direct competitor in the product that carries the claim (unlike CTAS, TSCO and EFX, where a
  private peer was one of several and a filed unit series carried the verdict), and **the unit disclosures are a frozen "more than 40,000" dealer
  floor and a monthly report-view figure that fell from "more than 31 million" (TTM Sep-2025) to "more than 28 million" (TTM Dec-2025)** while
  growth became "primarily driven by price increases". An IN needed three narrowing assumptions; an OUT needed the opposite three. The deciding
  record - a defined CARFAX unit and price/volume series over two to three standalone years - does not exist yet.

### REFUTED OR NARROWED PRIORS
- **"A spin-off with a short record is the HHH shape"**: refuted for the business, kept for the company. HHH's forward entity was not its filed
  entity; MBGL's business is the filed perimeter with a new balance sheet and head office. Q1 is IN; the too-little-history feature applies only
  to standalone costs, which Q4 bridges from the company's own estimates.
- **"Registrant-named substitutes fail criterion (2)" (the ACVA rule)**: narrowed. It held at ACVA because the returns agreed with the list;
  at MBGL they do not, and the gate cannot be closed OUT on the list alone.
- **"Data businesses are capital-light, so the D&A end is fine"**: confirmed here, with the maintenance cost located in operating expense
  (data acquisition and advertising), which is why (c) is small.

### NEW FOR THE OPERATOR
- **The first Q2 UNKNOWABLE in the register.** It turns on the framework's own line - *"Where a competitor's data is unavailable, say so and
  hold the moat class PROVISIONAL"* - applied where the unavailable competitor is the only direct one. If the operator reads the queue's CTAS,
  TSCO and EFX "row limit" practice as covering this case, the verdict would move to a narrow IN; the run file states the distinction.
- **A proposed survival shape, THE DOWRY** (it would be the fifteenth, after THE TENANT and THE PATRON, both unregistered): a spun-off business
  carrying debt sized by the departing parent and paid to it, so the leverage was chosen by the party that left with the cash.
- **Spin-off runs should read the parent's Investor Day 8-K and every DRS version:** the unit metric that moved (report views) moved between
  the first DRS and the second, and the standalone-cost and tax guidance lives only in the Investor Day deck.

### TOOLING AND SOURCE DEFECTS FOUND
- **`deal_note()` labels every EX-2.1 "plan of merger or acquisition"**; a spin-off's Separation and Distribution Agreement fires it. The
  instruction to read is right; the label invites a spread treatment.
- **The brief's filing inventory missed the Form 10-12B, 10-12B/A and three DRS filings** under the subject's own CIK.
- **S&P Global's 10-Q dates the notes "May 19, 2026"; MBGL's 10-Q says "May 29, 2026".** Immaterial; recorded.
- **experianplc.com is behind Incapsula bot protection**; the EFX run's transcription of AR 2026 is the only on-disk copy of Experian figures.
- **EDGAR full-text search through `fts_count()`: 48 calls, no HTTP error**; hits used as prompts, the naming documents opened.

## UPDATE 2026-09-13 - IHG: Q2 OUT, a hotel flag that pays owners more each year to fly it
`Test Runs/2026-09-13 Run - IHG InterContinental Hotels.md`. **Q1 IN, Q2 OUT, file closed; Q3 recorded (no disqualifier, gate case, buyback flag,
converging flags); Q4 recorded (would read IN on survival; THE FLAG proposed); Q5 headed COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE; Q6 recorded with nothing
armed.** Price **US$153.83** x **146,997,788 shares** = cap **US$22.6bn**; sovereign **USD 30-year 5.35%** (US Treasury, 09/11/2026). **The first hotel
company run in this project, and the last of the eleven foreign 20-F filers in wave 5.** **Register count at the fold, read from the register: 93 runs** (IHG adds one Q2 OUT).

### THE SKIP REASON, TESTED - TAG NAMES, AND A COVER COUNT THAT WOULD HAVE MISPRICED IT ANYWAY
- IFRS in US dollars; companyfacts holds eleven annual USD periods to FY2025. **Not short history, not the unit filter, not lag: `run.py`'s US-GAAP tag
  names**, exactly as at GFS.
- **Had the tags resolved, the cap would still have been 12.1% too high.** The 20-F cover "outstanding" figure is the prior year's issued count including
  treasury shares, repeated unchanged (164,711,854 for FY2024 and FY2025; 187,717,720 for FY2020 and FY2021 in dei). **ERIC's trap, in a worse form: issued, and a
  year stale.** The true count comes from the Total Voting Rights 6-Ks and the daily buyback reports, less the employee trust.
- **The brief's premise that the London line trades in pence is out of date:** it has traded in US dollars since 2026-01-02.

### THE BRIEF'S QUESTIONS, ANSWERED FROM THE FILED RECORD
- **System Fund separation:** the fund's cash sits in consolidated operating cash flow in three places (its result, its non-cash add-backs, its deferred-revenue
  float) and its capex in investing; IHG even pays the fund interest on the cash it holds (*"System Fund interest | 20 | 25"*, H1 2026). **Separated, the fund
  supplied $118-182M a year of the consolidated cash in 2023-25.**
- **SBC resolves in two places:** operating and System Fund lines; the ifrs companyfacts tag carries only the operating line (47 of 72 in 2025).
- **Key money:** inside operating cash flow at IHG and at all five peers. $61M (2019) to $237M (2024) to $179M (2025). Judged ~30% maintenance of unit volume
  from the removals replacement ratio; both ends displayed.
- **Owner earnings, five-year default:** $468M / $555M central / $593M; $339-673M across nine windows with and without 2020-21.
- **Competitor row:** Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, Wyndham, Choice from their 10-Ks, companyfacts cross-checks matched; Accor not an SEC filer.

### WHY OUT AND NOT UNKNOWABLE
- **For IN:** removals of ~1.5% underlying imply hotels stay in the system for decades; 66% of room nights come through the loyalty programme; the system grew
  through 2020; fee revenue fell less than RevPAR.
- **Against, and decisive:** the customer is the hotel owner, who owns the building and can re-flag it at term; IHG's own risk factor says renewals may be on
  worse terms; IHG pays rising key money, cut owners' loyalty assessment in a good year, and grew its fee business partly by negotiating revenue out of the
  owners' fund; its share of the branded systems' rooms fell for six years; a peer (Choice) raised its filed royalty rate through 2020 and 2025. **The documents
  that decide criterion 2 exist and were read; they agree.**

### REFUTED OR NARROWED PRIORS
- **"Asset-light franchisor = MCD-class franchise" is refuted as a transferable prior.** McDonald's passed Q2 because it keeps the land at the end of every term;
  IHG owns 17 of 6,963 hotels. **The land, not the franchise contract, carried MCD's criterion 2.** Any future franchisor run should ask who owns the site first.
- **"Fee resilience in 2020 shows pricing power" is narrowed:** fee revenue fell less than RevPAR at every hotel company in the row by a similar ratio (0.87-0.93
  of the RevPAR decline for IHG, Hilton, Wyndham, Marriott); fixed per-room technology fees, not a price rise, are the cushion.
- **The [E2-49] metric-withdrawal prior fired here** (TGR removed from the LTIP after 2020; adjusted FCF re-presented upward). The running tally is not
  restated: the reading list records it as stale, and later folds have moved it.

### NEW FOR THE OPERATOR
- **A proposed survival shape, THE FLAG** (it would be the sixteenth, after THE TENANT, THE PATRON and THE DOWRY, none registered): a brand flown over a building
  someone else owns, re-flown at term, whose take is set by rivals bidding for the same buildings and whose leverage is sized on the EBITDA that rivalry permits.
  **The register is unchanged.**
- **No single list of registered survival shapes exists on disk** (GFS noted it; this run rebuilt it again from the register and found ACMR's run numbering a
  shape "fifth" that the reading list numbers differently). A one-page shape register would stop every run rebuilding it.
- **The hotel row is now on disk** (`Test Runs/_research 2026-09-13 IHG/peers/`): five 10-K rows with royalty rates, contract terms, key money, loyalty and
  verbatim competition language, for any later run on MAR, HLT, H, WH or CHH.

### TOOLING AND SOURCE DEFECTS FOUND
- **`run.py` / `sources.annual()` US-GAAP tag names** block every IFRS filer, USD or not (confirmed on two USD filers, GFS and IHG, where no other cause is present).
- **`dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding` can be stale and can include treasury shares on a 20-F cover**; a screen should never take it as outstanding for a
  foreign private issuer without the Total Voting Rights or share-capital note.
- **The ifrs SBC tag misses System Fund (or any segregated-fund) share-based cost**; SBC "resolves" in the tag and is still incomplete.
- **The BoE database has no 30-year par gilt series in the codes tried** (`IUDLNPY` is 20-year); GBP 30-year from the DMO was not fetched, and did not matter
  because the earnings currency is USD.

stock-price flags); Q4 recorded (would read IN on survival; THE PERMIT proposed); Q5 headed COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE; Q6 recorded with nothing
armed.** Price **US$170.19** x **589,585,682 shares** = cap **US$100.3bn**; sovereign **USD 30-year 5.35%** (US Treasury, 09/11/2026). **The first of

### THE SKIP REASON, TESTED - A REAL TAG GAP, THE WRONG CORPUS LABEL
- **The gap is real and it is presentation:** from the FY2023 10-K, *"Purchases of property and equipment"* is folded into *"Other investing activities,
  net"* on the face of the cash-flow statement and appears only in the MD&A FCF reconciliation ($33M in 2025, 0.27% of revenue). `PaymentsToAcquire
  PropertyPlantAndEquipment` therefore ends at FY2022 and `run.py` priced three years.
- **The [E5-20] label does not fit:** D&A exceeds capex in five of six listed years; the renewal cost of this business is expensed (product development,
  marketing, a $1.7bn hosting commitment). **The D&A default [E3-44] applies, and the (c) band is under 5% of owner earnings in every window.** The skip reason's
  generic wording ("the corpus calls it INVALID for this class") was written for railroads and attaches to every missing capex tag; the next seven names in
  the row (AMZN, NVDA, CL, SPGI, TOST, EQIX, DLR) should test which case they are before assuming the exception.

### THE BRIEF'S QUESTIONS, ANSWERED FROM THE FILED RECORD
- **Share classes:** A and B identical in dividends and liquidation (20 votes on B), summed; **Class H excluded** (9.2M, held by a wholly-owned subsidiary,
  "issued and zero shares outstanding" on the balance sheet, though the cover calls it outstanding); Class C zero.
- **Customer funds:** unlike PAY, **the host funds never touch operating cash** - their swing is financing and their cash is restricted cash. Operating
  cash carries the unearned-fee float and the interest on held funds; owner earnings are shown with each removed.
- **SBC:** resolves to the dollar; **49.6% of OCF since the IPO year, 31.7% ex-2020** - below CRWD's 68.0% in the calibrated row, rising four years.
  Withholding on net settlement counted with buybacks, not subtracted twice. $16.4bn of repurchases and withholding since 2022 cut the count 6.6%.
- **Taxes:** the 2023 $2,897M valuation-allowance release and the 2025 $213M allowance are non-cash; set aside.
- **Regulation:** New York City's Local Law 18 (September 2023) - *"Prior to September, New York City represented approximately 1% of Airbnb global
  revenue"*; *"Approximately 80% of our top 200 markets by revenue already have some form of regulation"* (Q3 2023 letter); EU STR Regulation from May 2026;
  Spain €65M proposed fine; Italy $957M settled for 2017-23. The 10-K quantifies no other market.

### WHY OUT AND NOT UNKNOWABLE
- **For IN, stated at full strength:** brand and performance marketing 13.0% of revenue against Booking's 30.4%; cut from $1,140M (2019) to $723M (2021)
  while GBV rose $38.0bn to $46.9bn; 2020 bookings -37% against Booking -63% and Expedia -66%; recovered first.
- **Against, and decisive:** criterion 2 is what the customer thinks. Airbnb's 10-K says hosts often cross-list and guests compare sites; Expedia's 10-Ks name
  property managers listing on Airbnb, Vrbo and Booking.com; Booking.com's homes listings nearly doubled since 2019 to ~3.9M and reached ~36% of its room
  nights; the take rate has been flat for three years below Booking's, and the 15.5% single host fee is take-rate-neutral by design, introduced because
  cross-listed homes look cheaper elsewhere. **The documents that decide criterion 2 exist and were read; they agree.**

### REFUTED OR NARROWED PRIORS
- **"Direct demand = franchise" is narrowed:** marketing efficiency is a measured advantage in how demand is acquired, not evidence the customer sees no
  substitute. The fee conduct is the test, and it is defensive.
- **"Funds payable is the owner-earnings trap" is narrowed for marketplaces that ring-fence host money:** the separation still has to be done, but here it
  moves owner earnings ~6-18%, not the sign.
- **"Stock compensation is the centre of the file" did not hold** at 31.7-49.6% of OCF; the franchise question closed it.

### NEW FOR THE OPERATOR
- **A proposed survival shape, THE PERMIT** (it would be the seventeenth, after THE TENANT, THE PATRON, THE DOWRY and THE FLAG, none registered): the
  product is a use of other people's property that governments permit, cap or withdraw market by market, while making the platform enforce the rules and
  collect and pay the tax. Nearest are THE PATRON (but the permit-giver pays nothing) and THE FLAG (but supply is lost to the regulator, not a rival bid).
  **The register of shapes is unchanged; added to the index as proposed.**
- **The OTA row is now on disk** (`Test Runs/_research 2026-09-13 ABNB/peers/PEER_ROW.md`): Booking, Expedia (with Vrbo's last segmented year) and Trip.com
  2019-2025, with take rates, units, 2020 collapses, marketing, SBC/OCF, float treatment and verbatim competition language - for any later BKNG, EXPE or TCOM run.

### TOOLING AND SOURCE DEFECTS FOUND
- **`tools/sources.py:fts_count()` does not guard the phrase:** a phrase that already carries quote marks returns an inflated count (98 against 2 for
  "Local Law 18" in Airbnb's filings). It guards the CIK only; same defect class as the CALX harness.
- **`run.py` / `sources.annual()` read capex from one tag**; a filer that moves capex into a combined investing line and the MD&A reconciliation goes
  unpriced, and the skip reason then names the wrong corpus case.
- **`Screens/cover_shares.py` sums a subsidiary-held class** the balance sheet excludes (Class H here); the tool's MULTIPLE CLASSES warning is right, but the
  "outstanding" cover wording does not identify it.
- **Airbnb's shareholder letters are mostly images**, but their text layer carried the outlook, fee and regulation passages this run quotes.

## CL — Q1-Q4 IN, Q5 below the [E4-28] floor by 0.65 points (commits `ea8e241`, `a0f392b`, `32f5edb`, `cf49823`, `c0b0ece`). Alerts armed $75.61 / $50.77.
**The first consumer-staples franchise the queue has carried through all four business gates, and the clearest case yet of a
moat that is real, top-of-row profitable, and has not widened in eleven years.** Resumed on 2026-09-18 from a run killed at a
session limit on 2026-09-13; the scheduler was rate limited for the five days in between and nothing had touched the file.

### THE FINDINGS
- **Q2 IN, class NARROW, and the three findings that keep it out of WIDE are recorded rather than waived.** Colgate reports its
  own primary moat metric in the same MD&A sentence every year, and read across twelve 10-Ks it says something the company's
  commentary does not: **global toothpaste share 44.4% (2014), 44.7% (2015), then down every year to 39.4% (2021), then back to
  41.3% (2025)** — still **3.4 points below its 2015 level** — while **advertising went from 9.4% of sales (2016) to 13.3%
  (2025)**. **[E4-32]'s direction test fails across the decade** and is satisfied only across 2022-2025, and the re-widening was
  bought with 3.9 more points of every sales dollar. It is also a **dollar** share by the company's own definition, not a unit
  share, so the pricing below flatters it.
- **The physical series [E4-55] is the sharpest single table in the run.** Filed components summed 2016-2025: **worldwide volume
  +7.7 points, price +38.0, FX -20.4**; the Oral, Personal and Home Care segment, 77% of sales, **+2.9 points of volume in ten
  years**. Dollar sales rose 34%; units did not move. **And the price was mostly devaluation recovery, not [E2-44] pricing
  power**: Latin America priced **+76.8 against FX of -56.2** and Africa/Eurasia **+76.2 against -62.6**, recovering roughly
  80-85% of the currency loss and no more, while the three hard-currency regions priced at about **1% a year** (North America
  +12.9, Europe +11.0, Asia Pacific +17.2 against FX -16.8, so **+0.4 points of dollar price in ten years**).
- **[E4-37]'s inverse metric is firing, in the home market, on the filed record.** North American net selling price was
  **-1.9% in 2024 and -0.2% in 2025** — two consecutive years of price given back — with volume **-9.3 points over 2021-2025**
  and advertising at 13.5% and 13.3% of sales. *"it's not a great business when you have to have a prayer session before you
  raise your prices a penny."*
- **The counter-evidence is in the file at full strength and it is strong:** in 2022 and 2023 Colgate put through **+9.5% and
  +10.0%** of worldwide price and its **global toothpaste share ROSE, 39.4% to 41.1%**. That is [E2-44] criterion (1) passing in
  the hardest conditions the decade offered, and it is why the verdict is IN rather than OUT.
- **The competitor row, ten peers, is the reason the verdict holds.** PG, Unilever, Haleon, Kenvue, Church & Dwight,
  Kimberly-Clark, Clorox, General Mills, J.M. Smucker and Freshpet, on the same metrics and the identical net-tangible-operating-
  assets construction used on the subject. **CL and PG top the row on returns on capital and nobody else is close**
  (CL 61.5-91.0%, PG 77.8-91.7%, KMB 24.5-37.4%, CLX 25.4-67.6%). **And the physical series is poor across the ENTIRE row** —
  Kenvue negative in all three filed years, Clorox -10 then -7, Kimberly-Clark negative three straight years, General Mills'
  tonnage negative in four of six — with Unilever the only peer positive in each filed year. **Every branded staple in this row
  grew dollars on price 2021-2024 and gave some back in 2025.** That is a finding about the industry, not about Colgate.
- **Q2 is graded by segment because the segments grade differently, and the weights are filed.** Oral Care is 44% of sales and
  carries the verdict. Pet Nutrition is 23% and is held **PROVISIONAL** because **Nestlé Purina and Mars are not SEC
  registrants and cannot be measured from any primary filing** (the General Mills sweep across six 10-Ks returns zero hits for
  "Purina", zero for "Mars" whole-word and zero for "Hill's"). **Personal and Home Care are 33% and criterion (2) is NOT shown
  for them** — the company claims global leadership only in liquid hand soap, and the filing names private label as a source of
  competition for *"certain of our products"*. **Hill's is the best two-sided record in the file**: volume **+31.7** points and
  price **+49.1** with FX of only -3.4.
- **Q3 IN as an overlay, not a gate**, on **[E3-43]**'s own rule now that Q2 returned a franchise, but scored harder because the
  class is NARROW. No integrity disqualifier: no SEC action, no restatement, no auditor change, no qualified opinion, no matter
  naming an officer or director, and **zero instances of EBITDA across every Colgate file on disk, earnings releases included**.
- **The sharpest Q3 finding is [E2-56]'s camouflage, exact.** About **$2.4bn** into a skin-health adjacency in 2018-2019
  (EltaMD and PCA SKIN $730M, Filorga $1,711M) **while the core's own share was falling from 44.0% to 39.4%**, and **$2,211M of
  it written off in three charges** (2021, 2022, 2025), each followed by a statement of continued belief and **no post-mortem
  filed anywhere** ([E2-57]). A consolidated 79-101% return on tangible operating capital hides a 90%-plus loss on $2.4bn.
- **Q4 IN, [E4-20] GREAT, and [E5-11] scores 2 of 3 with the fail written as a fail.** Owner earnings per diluted share
  **$2.70 (2016) to $4.29 (2025), +5.3% a year**, on net tangible operating assets that did not grow. **Strength 2 FAILS:**
  $1,370M of cash is not *"massive liquid assets"*, and the 10-K points at an *"undrawn revolving credit facility supporting our
  commercial paper programs"*, which is exactly **[E5-39]**'s kindness of strangers. Strengths 1 and 3 pass comfortably.
- **Q5: the business is IN and the price is not.** **On every window the owner-earnings yield is below the thirty-year
  Treasury** — 3.83% / 3.92% / **4.05%** / 4.67% / 5.26% against **5.29%**. Adding the realised +5.3%/yr growth, granted at face
  value, gives **9.35% on the [E2-42] default five-year window: 0.65 points below the ~10% floor**. **The price already assumes
  about 5.95% a year of perpetual growth** — the best decade the filings show, repeated forever and slightly bettered, when 1.1
  points a year of that decade came from the share count and the rest from pricing this run showed was mostly devaluation
  recovery. Value **roughly $50 to $75 a share** on the default window against a quote of **$87.73**.

### REFUTED OR NARROWED PRIORS
- **"The killed session's 41.3% toothpaste share and +38.0 points of price show a franchise": narrowed, and the direction
  reversed the reading.** Both figures are correct and both are in the file, but the eleven-year share series the brief did not
  carry shows a **decline of 3.4 points from 2015**, and the regional price split shows the +38.0 is **devaluation recovery in
  soft-currency markets**, not [E2-44] pricing. The prior became the reason the class is NARROW rather than WIDE.
- **"Advertising rising from 9.4% to 13.3% of sales is investment or the cost of holding position — to be read, not assumed":
  read, and it is the cost of holding position.** Share is lower than when the spending was lower.
- **"Whether the skin-health write-downs are a Q3 or a Q4 item": settled at Q3 and at Q2.** They are [E2-56]'s camouflage at Q3

### THE FINDINGS

- **Q2 IN, class NARROW, and the verdict is carried by ONE segment out of four.** Ratings is **48.5% of continuing segment

- **THE METHOD FINDING, and it is the one to keep: FORM NRSRO IS A COMPLETE COMPETITOR ROW FOR AN INDUSTRY WITH PRIVATE
  PARTICIPANTS.** Every nationally recognised statistical rating organisation — **including Fitch, which is inside Hearst, and
  Kroll, and A.M. Best, and Egan-Jones, none of which files financial statements anywhere** — must file an **annual Form NRSRO
  certification on EDGAR**, and Item 7A of that form carries **its own count of credit ratings outstanding by class**. An EDGAR
  full-text search over form type **NRSRO-CE enumerates the entire industry: exactly TEN registrants in 2026.** Nine report a
  count. So the row is not "as many as I could reach"; it is **all of them**:
  **S&P Global Ratings 1,077,798 (49.4%) · Moody's Investors Service 684,055 (31.3%) · Fitch Ratings 266,519 (12.2%) · DBRS
  73,491 · Kroll 52,055 · Egan-Jones 14,348 · A.M. Best 8,385 · Japan Credit Rating Agency 5,361 · Demotech 451.** Top three
  **92.9%**. **This pattern generalises to any SEC-registered-intermediary industry** — broker-dealers, transfer agents,
  municipal advisors, security-based swap dealers — **where registration carries a public disclosure exhibit, and it is worth
  checking before any future run marks a moat PROVISIONAL on "the competitor is private".**
  **Two limits on the row, both stated in the run:** S&P's count is **85% government and municipal** (916,817 of 1,077,798), a
  low-fee class, so the units overstate the lead — S&P is 49.4% of units but about 52% of the S&P/Moody's revenue pair; and
  **Fitch left Item 7A blank in its 2026 certification**, checked page by page with two extractors and for form-field values, so
  its figure is a year old.

### THE PERIMETER, AND WHAT IT TEACHES THE NEXT RUN

**Two perimeter events sit inside any window: the IHS Markit merger of 2022-02-28 and the Mobility spin of 2026-07-01.** The
10-Q filed 2026-07-28 does **not** present Mobility as discontinued operations — that starts in Q3 2026 — so **every filed
financial statement of S&P Global describes a company that no longer exists.** **The subtraction is nevertheless already on
EDGAR, in a filing that looked routine: the 8-K/A of 2026-07-06, accession `0001104659-26-080571`, items 7.01/9.01**, whose
EX-99.2 is an **Article 11 unaudited pro forma income statement for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and Q1 2026 plus a pro forma balance
sheet**, ex-Mobility. **It is a better source than the spun entity's own Form 10**, because the Form 10's *combined* statements
charge Mobility with allocated corporate overhead that **stays with the parent**, while the pro forma's discontinued-operations
column is scoped to what actually leaves — and note (a) says so. **Standing lesson: after a spin, look for the parent's 8-K/A
pro forma before rebuilding anything by hand.** The run carried **three perimeters** and never blended them inside one mean
([E4-25], [E4-38]).

- **Toast Capital**: a capped first-loss guarantee, cash cost already inside operating cash, sector method not owed; **$46M of loans held for investment** appeared in
  H1 2026. **The float** is payroll float; restricted cash is Toast's own collateral.

### Q3 FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING
- **[E4-29] fires in the pay.** The bonus is *"Funded based on Recurring Gross Profit (RGP) and Adjusted EBITDA performance"* (DEF 14A, 2026-04-23). Adjusted
  EBITDA was $633M against GAAP operating income of $292M. **RGP excludes the hardware line altogether, which lost $220M**: the metric the bonus is funded on does not
  bear the cost of buying the position the business depends on.
- **Guidance beaten every time in FY2025** (Adjusted EBITDA guided $510-530M, delivered $633M): [E3-48] weight and [E5-30]'s ratchet, both carried.
- **The H1 2026 buyback** ($486M, 19M shares, about $25.60) was 4.5x the half-year SBC charge and fails buyback condition (2) on this run's arithmetic.
- **Two amortisation prompts for the FY2026 10-K**: D&A fell $35M to $22M and commission amortisation fell $48M to $46M in H1 2026 while both bases grew; no change
  in estimate disclosed. Owner earnings are built on cash and are immune.
- **[E2-49] did not fire**: the prior now stands at six fires and six failures.

### REVERSAL CONDITION, IN WORDS (fold step 4; nothing armed, no PORTFOLIO row)
Reopen Q2 only on a filed broad-based price increase that holds without a fall in net adds; a disclosed churn or retention figure; the concession sentence leaving
the 10-K; or Toast's own share estimate moving toward dominance while the filed rivals shrink.

### DEFECTS IN THE BRIEF (eight) AND IN THE KILLED SESSION'S Q1 (four)
The brief dated the $61M warrant repurchase to FY2025 (it is FY2024); quoted a capex series mixing two definitions; inferred capitalised SBC from a $1M gap when the
filed figure is $12M; called payroll float merchant float; attributed all $91M of credit-loss expense to Toast Capital ($62M is); omitted NCR Voyix and included
Olo; missed the 2026 loans held for investment; and its prior 2 (the bank bears the credit risk) was wrong, as it feared. The killed session's Q1 misdated the
self-description change (twice in six months, not once in eighteen), misnamed the float, omitted the guarantee cap, and put interest income outside operating cash.
All four corrected in a dated note; nothing edited.

### ONE THING TO KEEP
**For any business selling to small merchants, search the 8-K exhibits for letters to customers before scoring [E2-44](1) or [E4-37].** Here the company filed
its own pricing test, with a date, a price and an apology.

### WHY Q2 CLOSED, ON SNOWFLAKE'S OWN RECORD (the PLTR run's Snowflake figures were not imported)
- **The company says its lock-in is falling, by its own choice.** FY2026 10-K Item 1A: open formats like Apache Iceberg mean *"there is less customer 'lock in'
  when our products are used in external environments"*, and *"Our support of open data formats may also reduce switching costs between us and our competitors."*
- **Its suppliers are its largest competitors.** *"We currently offer our platform on the public clouds provided by AWS, Azure, and GCP, which are also some of our
  primary competitors. Currently, a substantial majority of our business is run on the AWS public cloud"*; costs and gross margins depend on *"the prices we are able
  to negotiate with these public cloud providers"*. Their segment margins are 24-41%.
- **Price is a competitive factor and efficiency is passed on.** *"We compete based on various factors, including price"*; it may not *"offer as many discounts or free
  services as our competitors"*; and every 10-K since FY2022 says efficiency gains let customers *"consume fewer compute, storage, and data transfer resources to
  accomplish the same workloads"* [E3-62].

  (FY2024-26)**, the lowest of six software filers in the row (MongoDB 13-17%, Elastic 9-15%, Datadog 21-23%, Teradata 17-19%, Palantir 27-47%), while its stock pay
  (34-42% of revenue) is the highest.
- **The full-strength case, recorded first**: realised capacity prices rose **8% (FY2021), 4% (FY2022) and 3% (FY2024)** by discount discipline and dearer editions;
  retention 125-126%; RPO $9.8bn; product revenue +37% in Q2 FY2027; Teradata, the shrinking legacy incumbent, names Snowflake; growth needs no balance-sheet capital
  because customers prepay. **No list-price increase was found in 23 documents swept.** Retention has fallen from 178% (FY2022) to 125%, and the company forecasts
  further decline. **[E4-04]** engaged in its own words, including a new FY2026 risk: *"Frontier AI model providers may seek to vertically integrate their offerings
  by expanding into the data storage and management layers"*.

### REVERSAL CONDITION, IN WORDS (fold step 4; nothing armed, no PORTFOLIO row)

### FOR THE OPERATOR
- **A reverse recapitalization puts two companies under one set of companyfacts keys, and the screen reads the earliest vintage, which is the shell.** Proposal only: flag

- **`tools/sources.sovereign()` served a stale cached row a fourth time** (09/17 5.29%; the Treasury's 09/18 figure is 5.34%).

### ONE THING TO KEEP
**A de-SPAC's tagged history can belong to two companies, and a de-SPAC can buy a third.** Read the basis-of-presentation note before any tagged year is used, and the
deal filings before the price is used.

  regulatory cost in three years [E2-57, E5-33]; the count rose 10.8% in three years net of buybacks [E5-15].

shares issued to the controller on 2026-09-11); sovereign **USD 30-year 5.34%** (US Treasury, 09/18/2026). **The fifth and last of wave 5's "no share count from dei"
names. Register count at the fold, read from the register: 113 runs** (BZFD adds one Q2 OUT).

### THE PRIOR THE BRIEF ASKED TO BE ARGUED AGAINST, AND HOW IT FARED
The brief expected the hard question to be whether a publisher can hold a franchise against the platform owners who control distribution. **Half right.** The platform
record is real (Facebook hours 428M, 184M, 58M in 2021-23; the founder's 2023 memo: *"slow to accept that the big platforms wouldn't provide the distribution or
financial support"*; AI summaries that *"provide answers directly on the search results page"*). **But the question was not hard, and the platforms were not the
decisive substitute**: the paying customers were. Branded-content buyers keep 41-50% of their spend a year, Amazon (28% of revenue) sets the commission, and People
Inc., the competitor BuzzFeed's own 10-K names, grew its Digital revenue 11.4% a year at a 27.7% segment margin through the same search decline while BuzzFeed's
continuing revenue fell 17.2% a year.

### WHY Q2 CLOSED, ON SIX INDEPENDENT RECORDS
- **The advertisers' vote, on the company's own metric**: net branded content advertiser revenue retention 50%, 41%, 48%, 41% (2023 to the twelve months to
  2026-06-30); branded advertisers *">40"* to *">20"*.
- **The company's own Item 1A**: *"expanded consumer choice significantly, resulting in traffic fragmentation and increased competition for advertising"*; AI search
  weakening *"our leverage in negotiating content licensing or access terms"*.
- **The platform record** (the brief's prior), above.
- **The unit series [E4-55]**: advertising revenue per measured hour $0.53, $0.37, $0.32, $0.33 (FY2022-25, -37%) while hours fell 12%; H1 2026 $0.28 against $0.32.
- **Amazon sets the commission**: *"less supplemental bonuses from our affiliate partners"* cut FY2025 affiliate revenue.
- **The row** (PPLI Digital segment, ZD Digital Media segments, NYT, TDAY, AREN; Vox, Bustle and Condé Nast private): BuzzFeed last on growth and on owner cash
  (-12.1% of revenue FY2022-25). **[E4-04] fires independently**: the basis replaced four times in five years (Facebook video, owned sites, a studio, *"an AI-app
  incubator"*).

### THE SKIP REASON, FROM THE FILED RECORD
- **A dimensioned three-class cover with an empty class**, the DASH kind, the Class C zero tagged `ixt:fixed-zero` in the 10-Q and `ixt-sec:numwordsen` in the 10-K;
  charter unmoved (DE). **Like PATH, the `a8bc84f` owner earnings were negative at every end; like PUBM, its capex end omitted capitalised software.** The row's tally is
  complete (dated note under the wave 5 table): in all five names the label meant a per-class cover that companyfacts drops, never a missing count.

### WHAT CHANGED WHAT THE QUOTE MEANS
- **A sale of control on 2026-05-26** to Byron Allen's LLC under Nasdaq's *"financial viability exception"*, with no shareholder vote: 40M shares at $3.00, of which
  $100.0M is a note due 2031 from an LLC that *"currently holds no assets other than the Shares"*, secured by 33.33M of them; then 4.2M shares at $1.44 and 1.7M at $1.06
  at recent closes. Allen holds 53.5% and appoints six of nine directors. **The count is right; what 40M of the counted shares were paid with is the part that changes the
  price's meaning** (about $56M of cap if the collateral shares are treated as an unexercised option).

### Q4 AND (c)
- **Owner earnings on the continuing perimeter**: -$35.0M five-year (a splice of two vintages), -$28.3M four-year, -$27.9M three-year at the capex end, -$32.4M at the
