### THE PRIOR THE BRIEF ASKED TO BE ARGUED AGAINST, AND HOW IT FARED
The brief named its own likeliest error: that a small, low-multiple, family-controlled appliance company is the kind of name a framework built on Berkshire's corpus
would look kindly on. **It was wrong, and the filings refute it at Q2, before the family or the multiple is reached.** The family (81.0% of the vote), a long-lived
brand and a ROTCE-based pay plan are real; none of them makes a buyer unable to find a substitute, and the filer says in its own risk factors that the buyer can.

### WHY Q2 CLOSED, ON FOUR INDEPENDENT RECORDS
- **The filer's own Item 1A**: the industry *"does not have substantial entry barriers"*; customers are *"sourcing, or expanding the extent of sourcing ... directly from
  manufacturers in Asia"*; *"we compete with our retail customers, who use their own private label brands"*; retailers *"have a large selection of ... suppliers from which
  to choose"*. Walmart 29%, Amazon 19%, top five 62%, all on purchase orders.
- **The price line follows the cost line, both ways [E2-44, E3-43, E3-62]**: the revenue bridge in every 10-K FY2019-25 shows +$42.9M of price in 2022 that did not restore
  the margin, then **-$28.1M (2023) and -$30.6M (2024), *"lower average selling prices reflecting lower costs"***. The savings went to the buyer the year they appeared.
- **Units and rank [E4-55, E4-32]**: revenue $603.7M (FY2020) to $606.9M (FY2025), flat nominal; *"#1 small kitchen appliance brand ... based on units sold"* (FY2020-23) to
  *"#1 ... national brand"* (FY2024) to *"#2 ... national brand ... and grew to #4 by dollars sold"* (FY2025); Amazon's buying -23.6% in 2025.
- **The row** (SN, SPB HPC segment, NWL H&CS segment, LCUT as a channel peer; De'Longhi, SEB, Donlim foreign; Conair, Sensio, Versuni, Gourmia private; private label
  unsegmented): HBB is **better run than Spectrum's and Newell's appliance segments and than Lifetime** (5.8% five-year operating margin against segment margins of
  -17.3% to 3.7% and a 3.5% five-year average), and **not the leader**: SharkNinja's kitchen categories alone are $3,367.1M, growing about 27% a year on a 49.0% gross
  margin, taking share from both sides. Spectrum is divesting its segment. **A competent operator in a category with no moat is [E2-37]'s remarkable textile company.**

### THE SKIP REASON, FROM THE FILED RECORD
- **The label was right: the cap really was broken, in two layers.** (1) A per-class dimensioned cover, the META/PATH/PUBM kind, two classes, no empty class, so
  companyfacts carries only `EntityPublicFloat`. (2) The undimensioned `us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding` carries **100 shares at 2017-06-30**, the pre-spin
  NACCO-subsidiary capitalisation, and zeros after. **$27,000,200 / (100 x $31.605) reproduces the 854,301%.** The code that wrote the triage row is not on disk; the
  current `shares_outstanding()` refuses the stale fact (550 days), but `Backtests/scripts/bt17_microcap.py` `shares_asof()` does not and returns exactly 100 for HBB.
- **Unlike PATH and BZFD, the `a8bc84f` owner earnings were positive at every end**, so the count was the only thing that kept HBB unpriced.

### WHAT CHANGED WHAT THE QUOTE MEANS
- **$36.5M of IEEPA tariff refunds in Q2 2026** (after the Supreme Court's ruling of 2026-02-20 that IEEPA does not authorise tariffs), booked in cost of sales under a gain
  contingency model and called *"non-recurring"* by the filer. The price went from $23.87 on 2026-08-05 to $31.42 two sessions later and to a two-year high of $34.00 on
  08-17. **A twelve-month yield at face value is 21.7%; without the refund 13.1%; on the five-year default 6.4%.** [E4-41] removes it.

### Q3 FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING (recorded, not governing)
- **The 2020 Mexican-subsidiary restatement** (FY2017-19; *"certain former employees"*; two material weaknesses, one in the income-tax process; remediated by FY2021;
  a $10.0M insurance recovery in 2022 that sits inside FY2022 operating profit and inside the 2022 guidance test). [E4-22]'s first flag, fired and remediated.
- **[E4-29] clean in all 28 releases (no EBITDA), and the adjustment lives in the proxy instead**: the 2025 short-term plan paid on operating profit of $47,327,405 against
  $36,579K reported [E2-57, E4-27]. Mitigated by a ROTCE override (up to -40%) and Class A stock restricted for 10 years; ROTCE carries 30-33% of both plans, [E2-01]'s
  own yardstick. **A run that reads only the 10-K and the releases scores this company clean on adjusted earnings; the pay table is where the except-for is.**
- **Guidance against outturn [E3-48]**: three of eight directional calls FY2022-25 hit. **[E2-49] fired mildly** on the rank's changing basis (the "national brand"
  qualifier arrived the year before the fall). Tally: nine fires (SHOP, MRVL, PAY, ARM, CALX, BE, PUBM, BZFD, HBB) and six failures.
- **Candor [E2-26, E2-69]**: both of the filer's own adjustments (the 2022 recovery, the 2026 refund) remove a favourable item. The General Counsel left "effective
  immediately" on 2026-06-18 after fifteen months with no reason given: a prompt for the next 10-Q, not a finding.

### Q4 AND (c)
- **Owner earnings**: **$27.0-27.3M five-year (FY2021-25)**, $45.7-47.6M three-year, $13.2-13.5M seven-year, $55.7M twelve months without the refund. The spread is working
  capital in named years (2020's pandemic and ERP inventory build, 2022's supply-chain build, 2023's release, the supplier-finance programme) that nets out over five:
  the five-year mean matches after-tax operating profit ($27.5M). (c) is the D&A default [E3-44]; capex $2.3-3.4M a year; the band is $0.3M wide.
- **Good, not great**: about 20% pre-tax on roughly $185M of capital employed, flat; ROE 41% (2020) to 15% (2025) as retained cash paid down the revolver.
- **Named death**: a large customer moves a category to its own label or buys direct, while a tariff or freight shock goes unpassed. Walmart is $178.3M; losing it at a
  25.7% gross margin turns a $36.6M operating profit into about a $9M loss. **A later instance of shape #19 THE SHELF as the mechanism, with #11 THE PASS-THROUGH as a
  feature** (index updated); no new shape.

### REVERSAL CONDITION, IN WORDS (fold step 4; nothing armed, no PORTFOLIO row)
Reopen Q2 only if the revenue bridge shows a positive price contribution in a year of falling costs in three years of four; the unit rank returns to #1 on an unchanged
basis and the dollar rank rises, for two 10-Ks; gross margin holds above 26% excluding windfalls for three years with Walmart's and Amazon's shares held; the
no-entry-barriers sentence is withdrawn with a reason; and revenue grows at least as fast as SharkNinja's kitchen categories for three years.

### FOR THE OPERATOR
- **`Backtests/scripts/bt17_microcap.py` `shares_asof()` has no staleness test** and returns a nine-year-old pre-spin share fact (100) for HBB. Whether any backtest
  panel priced a spin-off registrant on such a fact has not been tested. Recorded, not changed (tooling is not this run's to alter).
- **`tools/sources.sovereign()` was current this time** (09/18, 5.34%), after eleven stale readings recorded by earlier runs.
- **Seven defects in the brief** are listed in the register entry and the run file; the largest is that the triage history says the count "did not resolve" when it
  resolved to 100, and that the priors omitted the tariff refunds that doubled the price.

### ONE THING TO KEEP
**When a filer publishes its own revenue bridge, read the price line against the cost line before reading any rank or margin.** Hamilton Beach's bridge answered the
franchise question in two rows: when costs fell in 2023 and 2024, $58.7M of price went back to the buyer the same year. A moat keeps the saving; a supplier returns it.


## UPDATE 2026-09-19 - LCID: Q2 OUT, the most efficient car on sale, sold for half of what it costs to build, and funded by the shareholder who chairs the board
`Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - LCID Lucid Group.md`. **Q1 IN; Q2 OUT on the business, file closed; Q3 recorded (a GATE case on daily execution and leverage; IN on the
binary with converging flags); Q4 recorded (OUT: owner earnings negative on every window and both (c) ends; gruesome); Q5 headed COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE; Q6
recorded with nothing armed.** Price **US$4.09** (2026-09-18 close, aggregator flagged; the split-adjusted series matched on the post-split basis by the April 2026
offering prices in the 10-Q, $8.11 and $8.32) x **394,070,176** (the Q2 2026 10-Q cover, `0001628280-26-052606`, one class) = cap **US$1,611.7M**; sovereign
**USD 30-year 5.34%** (US Treasury, 09/18/2026). **The second of wave 5's "cap rejected as a broken input" names. Register count at the fold, read from the register:
115 runs** (LCID adds one Q2 OUT).

### THE PRIOR THE BRIEF ASKED TO BE ARGUED AGAINST, AND HOW IT FARED
The brief named its own likeliest error: that a pre-profit, capital-consuming carmaker is an easy close, and asked the run not to let that shortcut Q1 (the
non-vehicle revenue) or the choice between OUT and UNKNOWABLE. **Half right.** The close did come, but at Q2 on Lucid's own pricing record, not at Q4 on the losses;
and Q1's look at the non-vehicle revenue found the thing the prior did not anticipate: **the one technology licensee (Aston Martin) and the largest identifiable
customer (the Saudi government) are both in the controlling holder's circle**, and no licensing revenue from an unrelated party appears in any filing read.
UNKNOWABLE was argued at Q1 ([E3-31]'s *"subject to constant change"*) and refused, because the business the filings show can be judged on the record; the
future programmes were put outside the circle so that they could not be used later to rescue it.

### WHY Q2 CLOSED
- **Every car cost more to build than it sold for, in every year**: cost of revenue per car delivered $376.8k, $322.6k, $169.0k, $164.8k (FY2022-25), then
  **$202.4k in H1 2026**, against $75-98k of revenue per car; gross margin -92.8% (FY2025), -107.4% (H1 2026), negative even before the write-downs.
- **Prices were cut to sell more** [E3-03] criterion 2, [E2-44], [E4-37]: FY2023 deliveries +37%, revenue -2%, *"pricing and incentives offered"*; FY2024 *"a lower
  average selling price"*; vehicle revenue per delivery $96.9k to $73.5k.
- **The row** (eleven names, eight with figures): Lucid last in every year, -258.7% operating margin in FY2025 against Rivian -66.5% and Ford Model e -67.1%; about
  $221k of operating loss per car against Rivian's $85k. **My recomputation of Lucid reproduced the RIVN run's row to the decimal**, which checks both runs.
- **[E4-04] and [E4-23]**: each programme buys a replacement; the engineer-CEO who personified the efficiency claim resigned in February 2025.

### THE SKIP REASON, FROM THE FILED RECORD
- **The label was wrong in both words.** The sanity guard fired on its **lower yield bound**, from the correct post-split count: -176.3%, -161.1% and -192.4% on the
  `a8bc84f` owner earnings over a $1,911.2M cap at the 2026-08-31 close. Nothing was broken; the guard caught a real finding.
- **The HBB layers do not exist here** (one class, one undimensioned dei fact). **The reverse split (1:10, 2025-08-29) is real** and leaves unadjusted pre-split
  counts in companyfacts' dei series, which make the `a8bc84f` `share_count_shift()` read 0.1308.
- **The general lesson for the tooling**: a range guard on the quotient cannot tell a broken denominator from a business that consumes more than its market value.
  **Had the stale pre-split count been used, the yield would have been about -22.6%, inside the guard, and the broken input would have passed.** The guard's
  label should say "outside range: read", not "broken input".

### Q3 FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING (recorded, not governing)
- **The controller is on every side**: Ayar (PIF), 56.69% as converted, five of nine directors and the chairman, is the DDTL lender (SOFR plus 5.75%, $1.7bn drawn,
  liquidity covenant removed), the holder of three preferred series, the buyer of common, the backstop of the converts (prepaid forwards, with Lucid paying Ayar a
  fee), a customer through its government, and a shareholder of the licensee.
- **The preferred's claim grows about 18% a year, not 9%**: 9% in kind times a *"Relevant Percentage"* stepping up to 150.4% at 60 months and 208.4% at 108 months
  (Series C Certificate of Designations). **My first draft said 9%; the certificate corrected it**, and the filed six-month movement of Series A and B ($203.4M,
  8.8%) confirms it. **A run on any company with a preferred of this kind should open the certificate, not the 10-Q summary.**
- **Terms not unfair on the day, by the company's own accounting**: the Series C was booked at $292.4M against its $550M price, a $142.2M gain to Lucid. The finding
  is the common's position behind the escalating claim, not a term.
- **[E2-49] fired, a new form of it**: the 2026 production guidance (25,000-27,000) was reaffirmed on 2026-04-03 and in the 8-K of the 2026-04-14 financing, then
  appears in no later release or 10-Q read. **Not withdrawn in words; allowed to lapse.** The call transcripts were not read. Tally: ten fires (SHOP, MRVL, PAY, ARM,
  CALX, BE, PUBM, BZFD, HBB, LCID) and six failures.
- **[E3-48]**: the SPAC forecast table (135.3 thousand units and $13,985M revenue for 2025) against 17,840 and $1,353.8M; the year's first production guide missed in
  2022, 2023 and 2025, the last revision met every year. **[E4-27]**: the Midsize pay milestone missed its date and was credited at 85% because the later date "was
  planned".
- **The proxy's scored free cash flow ($(4,400)M) does not reconcile to its own Annex B ($(3,800.1)M)**; the gap runs against the executives, so it is a reading
  problem, not a pay flag.

### Q4
- **Owner earnings**: -$3,327.8M (five-year, capex end), -$3,660.8M (four), -$3,639.5M (three), -$5,407.3M (twelve months); the D&A end also negative everywhere.
  **H1 2026 operating cash (-$2,407.9M) exceeded all of FY2024's.** Gruesome; none of [E5-11]'s three strengths; [E2-54]'s coverage test failed absolutely.
- **Named death**: shape **#8 THE EQUITY IS THE REVENUE with #14 THE PATRON as a feature**, the same pairing as RIVN; no new shape. The $3.0bn pool covers about two
  quarters at the H1 2026 burn and about three on the plan-adjusted rate; every path in the filings requires another raise by 2027.

### REVERSAL CONDITION, IN WORDS (fold step 4; nothing armed, no PORTFOLIO row)
Reopen Q2 only if gross profit is positive before and after write-downs for four consecutive quarters with revenue per car level or rising; vehicle revenue per
delivery rises in a year when deliveries rise, with no MD&A attribution to pricing and incentives; operating profit is positive for a full year and return on
capital employed is positive in two consecutive 10-Ks; capex is funded from operating cash for two years without a new raise from the controller; and the row
still places Lucid at or above the luxury peers once their annual reports are pulled.

### FOR THE OPERATOR
- **The survival-shapes index was missing two instances its runs had named**: RIVN (#8 with #14's feature) and TSLA (#11 with #14's feature). Both are added by this
  fold, dated and attributed to their run files, with LCID beside RIVN.
- **The sanity guard's wording** ("a broken input and never a finding") was wrong for LCID; whether it is wrong for SOUN and BIRD is for their runs.
- **The Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Porsche annual reports** are the one named work order that would complete the luxury end of the carmaker row for any future run.

### ONE THING TO KEEP
**When the owner earnings are more negative than the market value, the guard that calls the quotient "broken" is describing the business, not the data.** Lucid's
common is quoted at $1.6bn and consumed $3.3-5.4bn a year; the controlling holder, not the customer, is the source of the cash, and its claim grows ahead of the
common at about 18% a year.

## UPDATE 2026-09-19 - SOUN: Q2 OUT, the voice-AI company whose own 10-K says its function is given away free, and whose revenue doubled while the businesses it owned shrank
`Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - SOUN SoundHound AI.md`. **Q1 IN; Q2 OUT on the business, file closed; Q3 recorded (a GATE case on daily execution; IN on the binary
with converging flags); Q4 recorded (OUT: owner earnings negative on every window and both (c) ends; gruesome); Q5 headed COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE; Q6 recorded
with nothing armed.** Price **US$5.93** (2026-09-18 close, aggregator flagged; corroborated by the LivePerson closing terms, an implied VWAP of about $7.08 against
late-August closes of $6.74-7.16) x **444,109,844** (the Q2 2026 10-Q cover, `0001840856-26-000022`, Class A plus Class B summed after reading the charter) = cap
**US$2,633.6M**, **about US$2.87-2.89bn pro forma** for the 36,894,839 shares issued to LivePerson's noteholders on 2026-09-04 and the unfiled 3.0-5.8M to its
stockholders; sovereign **USD 30-year 5.34%** (US Treasury, 09/18/2026). **The third of wave 5's "cap rejected as a broken input" names. Register count at the fold, read
from the register: 116 runs** (SOUN adds one Q2 OUT).

### THE PRIOR THE BRIEF ASKED TO BE ARGUED AGAINST, AND HOW IT FARED
The brief's likeliest error: that a loss-making, acquisitive, heavily stock-paid AI company is an easy close. **Half right.** The close came at Q2, not at Q4, and not
for free: the franchise case had real evidence, all from SoundHound's own documents or a rival's: design-win stickiness (*"very unlikely that a customer will change
complex technology until a product model is revamped"*), multi-year renewals with a carmaker and restaurant chains, per-unit royalties, and **Cerence, the auto voice
incumbent, naming SoundHound among competitors that *"have had some success selling into our customer base"***. Revenue guidance was met in every year FY2022-25. All of
it proves [E3-03]'s criterion 1 (needed or desired). Criterion 2 is answered by the filer itself.

### WHY Q2 CLOSED
- **The filer's own words on substitutes** [E3-03] criterion 2: alternatives *"offered at significantly lower costs or free of charge"*; rivals able to make the function
  *"available at lower cost or free of charge within the larger offering"*; carmaker contracts with *"annual price reduction commitments"*. Its own release celebrates
  displacing an incumbent voice assistant: in this field incumbents are displaced, which is the switching cost failing. Cerence's 10-K carries a near-identical paragraph,
  so it is the industry's condition.
- **The growth was bought and the owned businesses shrank**: reported revenue $45.9M to $168.9M (FY2023-25) through SYNQ3, Amelia and Interactions; **the filer's own pro
  forma, $153.6M to $143.5M (FY2023-24) and $225.6M to $211.7M (FY2024-25)**; Legacy SoundHound alone about $45.9M to $30.7M in FY2024. Then LivePerson, revenue down
  53% since FY2022, bought in September 2026.
- **Contracted revenue is thin and falling**: GAAP RPO $79.5M to $60.0M in two quarters, $37.3M due within a year against $203.2M of TTM revenue.
- **[E4-04]**: R&D 58% of revenue, and the capability that changed the field is rented (*"large language models like OpenAI's ChatGPT"*); five acquisitions since January 2024.
- **The row** (Cerence, LivePerson, Five9, NICE): SoundHound last on every margin and cash column; five-year owner cash -176.3% of revenue against NICE +14.7%.

### THE SKIP REASON, FROM THE FILED RECORD
- **The label was RIGHT in both words, by the HBB mechanism through the LCID bound.** Per-class dimensioned dei cover (A and B), so companyfacts carries only the
  **SPAC shell's 17,461,000 of 2022-03-09**; `bt17_microcap.shares_asof()` returns it; over it the `a8bc84f` owner earnings give -97.4% to -125.2%, tripping the lower
  yield bound; over the correct count, -3.5% to -4.9%.
- **The instructive contrast**: LCID's correct count tripped the same bound on a real finding; SOUN's stale count tripped it on a broken input. The guard cannot tell
  them apart, and **would have missed SOUN's broken cap had the stale count been somewhat larger**. The LCID fold's recommendation (label the guard "outside range:
  read", not "broken input") is strengthened, not weakened.
- **A NEW DEFECT CLASS for the tooling: the de-SPAC's first year.** companyfacts carries two FY2021 operating-cash values for this CIK, the shell's -$0.864M and Legacy
  SoundHound's -$66.2M; the screens read the earliest vintage, so the shell's number sits inside the five-year owner earnings (about $13M a year too small in magnitude)
  and the current `working_capital_flag` fires on the shell's 2021. **Any SPAC-merged filer whose early years straddle the merger may carry the shell's cash flows**; it
  is untested whether any backtest panel priced a de-SPAC on a shell year. **Not fixed here** (the run does not change tooling); recorded for the operator.

### Q3 FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING (recorded, not governing)
- **A "backlog" that was mostly a forecast**: *"cumulative subscriptions & bookings backlog"* $661M at FY2023 against GAAP RPO of $12.7M, 52 times; the footnote:
  *"Subscriptions backlog refers to potential revenue achievable ... assuming a 4-year ramp up ... and assuming a successful full roll out"*. Dropped from releases after
  Q2 2024 while still rising, so it is the projections flag [E4-22, E3-48], not [E2-49].
- **[E2-49] fired**: *"positive adjusted EBITDA"* for 2025, promised on 2024-02-29, absent from every later release; 2025 adjusted EBITDA -$58.4M. The Q4 2023 promise
  was missed the same way (-$3.7M). Tally: eleven fires (SHOP, MRVL, PAY, ARM, CALX, BE, PUBM, BZFD, HBB, LCID, SOUN) and six failures.
- **Material weaknesses in every annual report FY2023-25 and every 2026 10-Q**, reaching *"substantially all accounts and disclosures"*; three late-filing notices; the
  *Liles* action survives on internal-control statements.
- **Stock paid to creditors [E5-44]**: 36,894,839 shares (about $261M on the agreement's terms) for $373.7M face of LivePerson's secured notes; the S-4 shows the price
  was cut from $284M to $250M of enterprise value after *"the non-renewal by a large LivePerson customer"* and attrition *"higher than were forecasted"*.
- **Pay**: half of the 2022 executive PSUs on a $15 and $20 share price [E3-50]; the FY2025 bonus paid 100% on revenue (met with acquired revenue) and 0% on adjusted
  EBITDA.

### Q4
- **Owner earnings**: -$125.4M to -$135.4M (five-year), -$142.0M to -$157.3M (three-year), -$208.5M to -$237.0M (TTM); worse as the window shortens. RSU grant value
  $168.2M against an $83.1M charge in FY2025 [E3-70].
- **Named death**: shape **#8 THE EQUITY IS THE REVENUE with #2 as a feature**, and **#21 THE ROLL-UP proposed** (pending the operator): reported growth bought with the
  acquirer's shares from the owners and creditors of shrinking businesses while the owned businesses shrink; it lasts as long as the quote will buy the next one.
  About 15-19 months of cash at the filed burn; the company's liquidity plan names the ATM.

### REVERSAL CONDITION, IN WORDS (fold step 4; nothing armed, no PORTFOLIO row)
Reopen Q2 only if the filer's pro forma shows the businesses owned throughout growing in two consecutive annual reports with LivePerson included; a filed price
increase holds, or the "annual price reduction commitments" and "free of charge" language leaves Item 1A, with gross margin before acquired amortisation rising two
years; GAAP RPO grows faster than revenue for four quarters and contract assets fall as a share of revenue; owner earnings (stock pay at the larger of charge and grant
value) are positive for a full year with no ATM sales; ICFR is clean two years running; and SoundHound's five-year owner cash per revenue dollar reaches Cerence's and
Five9's.

### FOR THE OPERATOR
- **A proposed survival shape, #21 THE ROLL-UP**, added to the index as proposed; it is argued apart from #8 (how losses are funded) and #10 (no strong leg's cash is
  recycled, only a share price).
- **The de-SPAC first-year defect** above, for whoever next touches `floor_screen.annual()` or the backtest panels.
- **The next SoundHound document that matters**: the Q3 2026 10-Q, the first to carry LivePerson, the post-closing share count and the cash LivePerson delivered.

### ONE THING TO KEEP
**When a company's growth is bought, ask for the filer's own pro forma before reading the headline.** SoundHound's release said *"Record Annual Revenue of $169
Million, Up Nearly 100%"*; its own 10-K's acquisitions note showed the same businesses owned throughout had shrunk two years running.

## UPDATE 2026-09-19 - BIRD: Q1 UNKNOWABLE, the shoe company that sold its shoes, kept its listing and bought one GPU lease
`Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - BIRD Allbirds.md`. **Q1 UNKNOWABLE, closed without prejudice; Q2 recorded (would be OUT); Q3 recorded (a GATE case on daily execution;
IN on the binary with nine converging prompts); Q4 recorded (would be OUT: owner earnings negative on every window and end; gruesome); Q5 headed COMPUTATION - NOT A
CLEARANCE; Q6 records reopening conditions and arms nothing.** Price **US$2.30** (2026-09-18 close, aggregator flagged; corroborated at the 06-18 RSU grant value,
the proxy's 05-07 price and the 09-02 Form 4s) x **11,809,193** (the Q2 2026 10-Q cover, `0001437749-26-028446`, Class A plus Class B summed after reading the
charter) = cap **US$27.2M**; sovereign **USD 30-year 5.34%** (US Treasury, 09/18/2026). **The fourth and last of wave 5's "cap rejected as a broken input" names,
and the last name in the wave 5 table. Register count at the fold, read from the register: 117 runs** (BIRD adds one Q1 UNKNOWABLE, the queue's fourth after HHH,
RGTI and DJT).

### WHAT THE SHARE BUYS
- **Not Allbirds.** The footwear business, trademarks, customer lists and inventory went to an affiliate of American Exchange Group on 2026-06-09 for $40.7M; the
  registrant is **Smartbird, Inc.** since 2026-06-15. On 2026-03-30 the plan was a sale and dissolution; on 2026-04-15 it was a GPU pivot under a $50M (now $100M)
  convertible facility, named "NewBird AI"; by August a managed dedicated-cluster model with no pay-as-you-go pricing.
- **One contract**: $2.758M of NVIDIA-based servers leased 36 months to a subsidiary of QumulusAI, Inc. (itself a filer reporting going-concern doubt that it says
  its plans will alleviate), about $3.7M of payments with a purchase option, booked as $2.758M revenue and $2.758M cost. **The lease earns about 19%; the notes that
  funded it cost about 19.5%**; continuing overhead was $10.7M in Q2 alone.
- **In the filer's own words, *"no historical information relevant to that business"*.** That sentence decided the verdict's kind: UNKNOWABLE, as HHH, RGTI and
  DJT were, with the [E3-31]/[E4-46] OUT case (the filer's own *"rapid technological change"*) recorded and named as the first to run on any reopening.

### THE PRIOR THE BRIEF ASKED TO BE ARGUED AGAINST, AND HOW IT FARED
The brief's likeliest error: a streak of Q2 closes on consumer brands. **The brief was more wrong than it feared, in a direction it did not name**: the brand is no
longer the registrant's, so a Q2 on it would have judged American Exchange Group's asset. The brief's own guard (*"do not let the Q2 argument substitute for Q1"*)
is what caught it. **The franchise case was still argued, because the brief asked**: brand strength, direct-to-consumer data, 41-53% gross margins. **The owners
ran [E2-45]'s attacker's test live**: 91 parties contacted, IP-only bids of about $30M and $30-40M, and the winning $39M bought the trademarks, the inventory
($38.9M at book) and receivables with about $26.5M of payables assumed. **A brand that fetched about the value of its shoe stock was not a franchise at the end.**

### THE SKIP REASON, FROM THE FILED RECORD
- **Four readings tested; three confirmed, one refuted, and a fifth found.** (a) per-class cover plus a stale **pre-IPO** count (56,508,441 of 2021-09-30);
  (b) the **1-for-20 split** of 2024-09-04, mixed vintages in companyfacts' weighted averages, and the house rule's split factor turning the stale count into a
  quarter of the true one; (c) the **lower yield bound** trips on the correct count as well (-237% to -299%); (d) no shell year; **(e) the numerator was a sold
  business**: the triage divided the footwear business's FY2021-25 losses, from 10-K facts not yet recast, by the market value of the company that had sold it.
- **A NEW DEFECT CLASS for the tooling: the completed disposition.** Nothing in the screens reads a sale of the whole operating business between annual reports:
  the continuing/discontinued split reaches companyfacts only as half-year facts, and `ocf_continuing()` acts only on annual facts, so every registrant that sells
  its business and keeps its listing is priced on the sold business until its next 10-K. **Not fixed here** (the run does not change tooling); recorded for the
  operator. The 8-K Item 2.01 route was already tested and rejected as a signal (RESUME STATE item 5).
- **The house split rule has a blind spot beside it**: it corrects a count measured before a split, but not one measured before an IPO. Any backtest anchor that
  fell back to a pre-IPO balance-sheet count would be understated by the IPO's shares and the converted preferred, and then scaled by any later split. Untested
  whether any panel did.

### Q3 FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING (recorded, not governing)
- **A dividend estimate given before the vote, against the outturn**: the merger proxy anticipated *"approximately $1.34 per share"*, and the fairness opinion was
  given on that figure and on a dissolution the proxy said would not happen; the board paid **$0.31**, on a record date by which the new ATM shares took part.
- **The sale proceeds, headed for owners on 2026-03-30, funded a new business by 2026-04-15**; the proxy's stated reason is that stockholders *"continue to have their
  shares listed and traded on Nasdaq"*; no filing sets the new business's expected return against the cash in owners' hands [E2-30, E5-24].
- **20.5% of the count granted as service-vested RSUs in one half-year** (the CEO's inducement award alone 13%), against a proxy "burn rate" of 5.3% [E4-27, E3-70].
- **Adjusted EBITDA in the 10-Q** [E4-29]; the ATM signed thirteen days after a +582% day (a prompt only [E3-50]); two candor prompts [E2-26].

### Q4
- **Owner earnings** of the sold business: -$85.2M to -$86.8M (five-year), -$68.6M to -$76.4M (three-year), about -$51M to -$54M (TTM). **The business the share
  buys**: about -$36M a year at H1 2026's continuing rate, against about $34M of cash.
- **Named death**: shape **#8 THE EQUITY IS THE REVENUE with #6 THE BORROWED BALANCE SHEET as a feature**; the mechanism is a conversion price set at 93% of the
  lowest ten-day VWAP, so the $8.25M of notes alone are about a third of the count at $2.30. No new shape proposed.

### REOPENING CONDITION, IN WORDS (fold step 4; nothing armed, no PORTFOLIO row)
Two audited years of the AI-infrastructure business; several customers, none above half of revenue; contracts earning above the cost of the money that bought
the hardware, after overhead, with the floorless notes gone; owner earnings (stock pay at the larger of charge and grant value) positive for a full year with no
ATM sales; and leases renewed across a hardware generation at filed rates. On reopening, run the Q1 OUT case first.

- **The wave 5 table is fully struck with BIRD.** The orchestrating session writes `WATCHLIST COMPLETE.md`; this run did not.
- **The next Smartbird documents that matter**: the annual meeting of 2026-09-30 (3.5M more plan shares; conversions above 19.99%) and the Q3 2026 10-Q.

**Before judging a business, check that the ticker still owns it.** Every figure a screen held for BIRD described a shoe company; the share had become a claim on

aggregator flagged; corroborated by the Q2 2026 10-Q repurchase prices) x **4,302,549,243** (the Q2 2026 10-Q cover, `0001628280-26-050503`) = cap
**US$379.7bn**; sovereign **USD 30-year 5.34%** (US Treasury, 09/18/2026). **WAVE 6, the first of the five ordinary businesses the triage dropped. Register
count at the fold, read from the register: 118 runs** (KO adds one Q5 close: Q1 4, Q2 83, Q4 2, Q5 29).

### WHAT THE 2020s FILINGS SAY ABOUT THE CORPUS'S MOST-CITED FRANCHISE
- **The case against was built first, from the filer's own text**: substitutes on the shelf and *"powerful buyers"*; currency cutting operating income 9%, 8%, 11%
  and 12% in 2022-25; US unit cases level; weight-loss drugs and sugar taxes named in Item 1A; energy ceded to Monster under a non-compete; the bottler keeping part
  of each price rise; BodyArmor written down $1.72bn.
- **What refuted the OUT case was the head-to-head, not the history.** North America price/mix compounded about +49% over 2021-25 on level cases, and segment
  operating income rose from $3,331M to $5,070M; in the same country and years PepsiCo's beverage volume fell and its margin with it. Worldwide cases 29.3bn to
  33.8bn in ten years. Operating income on the tangible capital that earns it: 67-89% (FY2021-25). **Nothing before FY2016 was used.**
- **A correction to a number carried in this file since the PEP and COKE runs**: KO's 31.5% return on NTOA (FY2025) is right on the standard formula, and on that
  formula PepsiCo is level with it (32.9%). The formula counts $18-20bn of bottler stakes, whose income sits below operating income; without them KO's figure is
  67%. **The standard formula understates a company whose bottlers are equity stakes.**

### THE PRIOR MOST LIKELY WRONG, AND HOW IT FARED
The brief's warning (operator rule 9) was that a corpus reader has an incentive to clear Coca-Cola. **The favourite hypothesis survived Q2 on 2020s evidence, and
the file then closed on price**, which is the verdict the incentive argues against: the same franchise the corpus bought at a price assuming 1.2% growth against a
9% bond (VERIFICATION, CASE 2) is priced today to need 2.6% just to match a 5.34% bond and 7.2% forever to reach the floor, against a filed 4-6%.

### A TOOLING FINDING: TWO $6BN ONE-OFFS INSIDE OPERATING CASH, THE REVERSE OF THE COKE CASE
- **The COKE run found a perpetual royalty in FINANCING, outside operating cash, which flattered the screen. At KO two one-offs sit INSIDE operating cash and
  depress it**: the $6.0bn IRS deposit (2024; the 10-K tax note says the $3,262M of 2024 tax payments *"does not include $ 6.0 billion paid in relation to
  invoices"*) and $6,069M of the $6,173M fairlife milestone (2025; the rest, $104M, in financing). `tools/run.py KO` therefore prints five-year owner earnings of
  $7.8-8.4bn and three-year $6.3-7.2bn, about $2bn a year below the adjusted $10.0-10.9bn. **The error runs the conservative way here, so no verdict turns on
  it**, but any screen ranking KO by yield ranked it about a quarter too dear. **Not fixed** (the run does not change tooling): the same class as the resume note's
  "a diagnostic that exists but never reaches the reader". A screen would need an operating-cash outlier guard that sends a reader to the MD&A liquidity
  paragraph, where both items are named.
- **Three smaller operating-cash items a TTM reader would take at face value**: the receivables factoring programme ($14.7-21.9bn of receivables sold a year; the
  outstanding balance is not disclosed, so its lift is unmeasurable), transfers of surplus pension assets into company cash ($523M, $332M), and tax-credit
  partnerships whose cost sits in investing while the benefit sits in operating cash. The TTM's $16.3bn of operating cash would have printed a 3.6% yield.
- **`tools/run.py` read the Q1 2026 cover** (*"share basis: dei cover-page count as of 2026-04-28"*) when the Q2 10-Q of 2026-07-29 was on file; immaterial here
  (the count barely moved), recorded as the known companyfacts lag. `Screens/cover_shares.py` read the right filing.

### Q3 FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING
- **The except-for flag [E2-57] fires in the headline metrics and in the pay plan together.** Releases lead with *"Comparable Currency Neutral Operating Income
  (Non-GAAP)"*; FY2024 operating income fell 12% GAAP while that measure grew 16%. The annual incentive pays on organic revenue and comparable currency-neutral
  operating income; the PSU free cash flow is adjusted to exclude *"impacts resulting from the application of the tax court rulings"*. The mitigation is

  undistributed equity income +$0.75-0.95bn shown apart. SBC resolves in 7 of 7 years. D&A end admissible, capex end the default (capex about 2x D&A for three years).
- **Named death: stagnation, and a new shape proposed, #22 THE HABIT** (added to `Screens/SURVIVAL SHAPES - index.md`, pending the operator): the franchise is a
