| active fixed income | 20.79 | 19.44 | 17.55 | 17.23 | 17.06 | 16.95 |
| active multi-asset | 19.21 | 17.94 | 15.28 | 13.55 | 12.42 | 12.03 |
| non-ETF index | 3.83 | 3.80 | 3.79 | 3.52 | 3.52 | 3.47 |
| private markets | 70.49 | 66.71 | 69.64 | 77.36 | **89.85** | 80.06 |
| cash management | 6.61 | 12.01 | 13.05 | 13.01 | 12.76 | 12.72 |

**Every organically owned line fell. The only two that rose did not rise on price:** cash
management's 2021 figure is a zero-rate fee-waiver artefact and the series has fallen since 2023;
private markets rose because **GIP and HPS were bought**. **Ex private markets the total fell 15.74
to 13.64bp.**

### THE REFUTED PRIORS
1. **"BlackRock is the cheapest manager on the row, so the row shows its strength."** Wrong question.
   15.22bp against TROW's 39.4 and BEN's 40.5 is a fact about *product mix*, not about franchise. What
   the row actually shows is **six independent filers, with six different definitions and six
   different fiscal calendars, all falling at once**: STT -14.4%, IVZ -30.8% on its own gross yield,
   TROW -11.3% ex performance fees, BEN -3.1%, BAM -8bp, BLK -6.6%. A franchise is a claim about the
   customer's alternatives, and the customer is getting a better price every year from everybody.
2. **"The blended rate has been flat for two years, so the compression is over."** It is flat because
   $28.3bn bought a 90bp book. Strip it and the rate fell 13.4% over four years.
3. **"Scale is the moat."** [E3-62]'s second step decides it: ETF average AUM **+60.3%** while the ETF
   price fell **17.1%**. The savings went home to the customer. An advantage that shows up as volume
   at a price you cannot raise is scale, not franchise.
4. **"An asset manager's reported operating cash flow is its owner's cash."** Not for a fund
   consolidator. **GAAP operating cash of $3,927M in 2025 understates the owner's cash by $3,536M**,
   because the consolidated funds' securities purchases sit in OPERATING while the outside investors'
   subscriptions sit in FINANCING. The filer publishes the separation; the run used it.
5. **"D&A is the conservative end of (c)."** Here it is the *wrong* end: **68.8% of 2025 D&A is
   amortisation of intangibles bought in GIP, Preqin and HPS** - a purchase price already paid in
   shares that are already in the share count. The corpus default [E3-44] runs backwards for a serial
   acquirer of intangible-heavy businesses, and this is the third instance in three days of a D&A tag
   misreading a filer, after IBM's lease ROU amortisation and DIS's TFCF/Hulu amortisation.

### THE FINDING THAT WAS NOT IN THE BRIEF
**The pay scorecard.** The 2026 proxy prints the "2025 NEO Pre-Set Performance Scorecard", and under
*Financial Performance - Priority 1: Drive profitable growth* the scored measures begin: **"Next
12-Month P/E Multiple (including relative premium)"** and **"Total Shareholder Return"**. **[E3-50]**
describes exactly the premise the corpus *"adamantly disagree[s]"* with - that a manager's job is to
encourage the highest stock price possible - and names the next step, *"unadmirable accounting
stratagems"*. **Writing the forward price/earnings multiple, and the relative premium to peers, into
the CEO's pre-set pay formula is that premise formalised.** It converges with three other flags
[E4-52]: an adjusted-EPS gap that grew from $1.60 to **$12.78** in one year; the same adjusted
operating margin being the metric the 10-K says is used *"to determine the long-term and annual
compensation of the Company's senior-level employees"*, while it adds back **$738M of compensation
paid to retain the people the company bought**; and a buyback announced as a **dollar quantity**
rather than as a price condition. GAAP return on average equity fell 14.7% to 10.7% and GAAP EPS fell
$42.01 to $35.31, while adjusted EPS rose 10% and the CEO was rated *Far Exceeds* with $45.0M of pay,
the incentive up 24%. **[E2-01] was written to prefer the first number.**

**And the credit, recorded as plainly:** BlackRock prints the BPIP payout matrix in advance and
reports the prior cycle's outturn against its own pre-set target - **$716M of average annual organic
revenue growth against a $640M target, 43.4% against 41.5%, payout 116.6%**. That is **[E2-49]**'s
*pre-set, long-lived and small bullseyes* and the **[E3-48]** artifact done properly. Against it: the
adjusted-margin bullseye was **raised from 41.5% to 44.0% while the GAAP margin fell eight points**.

### DEFECTS FOUND
1. **`tools/sources.py:_get()` defaults to `WEB_UA` = `Mozilla/5.0`, and `www.sec.gov/Archives`
   answers it with HTTP 403.** Every primary-document fetch in this run failed until `headers=SEC_UA`
   was passed. The default is wrong for the rung of the evidence ladder the framework uses most.
   **Fix: default to `SEC_UA` for any `sec.gov` host.** Changes no number; removes a trap that costs
   every new run a failed call.
2. **`cik_for("BLK")` returns the right CIK and a two-year history, silently.** CIK 0002012383 files
   today and its `companyfacts` begins at **FY2024**, because the holding company was created in
   October 2024 at the GIP closing; 2009-2023 sits under CIK 0001364742, now **BlackRock Finance,
   Inc.** `name_change_note()` returned an **empty string**. A single-CIK XBRL pull returns two years
   and no error - the same defect class as `level_shift` and `working_capital_flag`: a diagnostic that
   never reaches the reader. **Fix: fire `name_change_note()` on a `formerNames` entry that differs in
   corporate form, or have `annual()` refuse when fewer than five annual periods resolve.**
3. **The brief's instruction to find the CIK myself was load-bearing.** Any run that had taken a CIK
   from a brief would have built a two-year series for a seventeen-year filer.
4. **Two defects in the fold script itself, found and fixed while folding and recorded in its
   header.** `rindex()` on the string "## COMPLETED FROM THE QUEUE" lands on an inline mention - there
   are several inside register entries and one inside the FOLD section, which sits AFTER the
   WRITE-EARLY heading, so the window search then failed outright; headings must be matched
   line-anchored. And percent-formatting cannot be used to build a register entry, because the text is
   full of literal per-cent signs. **Any session copying a prior fold script inherits both.**
5. **Delegating the competitor row to a helper agent exhausted the session limit**, and only the
   write-early rule saved the partial peer file. The coordinator's correction - fetch peer data
   in-session - is the right rule for a run this size. **Every figure in the recovered peer file was
   re-read in the filing text by this session before use**, and the six ETF prospectus accessions were
   recovered by matching on-disk file sizes against EDGAR's own filing indexes.
6. **No defect in the brief's framing of the fee-rate test.** It named the decisive series before the
   data was pulled and the data confirmed it. The instruction *not* to inherit BAM's conclusions
   mattered: the two managers reach the same verdict for different reasons - BAM's rate falls on
   related-party mix, BlackRock's on customer substitution at a commodity price.

### ONE THING TO KEEP
**Aladdin is the only part of this company that is not a commodity, and it is 8.2% of revenue.** The
brief was right that it might behave differently, and half right about how: the contracts are
long-term and recurring and organic ACV grew 16%, but the fees are *"generally determined using the
value of positions on the Aladdin platform"* - market-linked like everything else. At $1,981M it
cannot reclassify the other 91.8%. **If Aladdin ever exceeds a fifth of revenue with organic ACV
growth above 15%, this file should be run again from Q1** - that is refutation test 6 at Q6.

### THE HONEST SUMMARY
**This is a very good business and it is not a franchise.** It survives everything Q4 can model,
earns a high return on the tangible capital it uses, consumes no capital to grow, and has the most
reliable revenue line in the queue. **And owner earnings per share are flat to 12.5% lower than four
years ago on 40.3% more assets under management.** At $1,069.78 the buyer pays 1.13% of the $15.3
trillion for the right to earn 0.152% a year on it, which is nine years of gross fees before a single
cost. The owner-earnings yield is **2.74-3.21% against a 5.34% government bond**, and the honest
pre-tax expectancy of **3.51-4.12%** misses the ~10% floor by **five and a half to six and a half
points**. **[E2-53]** is the line to remember: *"Once dominant, the newspaper itself, not the
marketplace, determines just how good or how bad the paper will be."* **The largest asset manager
that has ever existed does not determine its own price.**

### TRV (The Travelers Companies) - run 2026-09-19, FAIL at Q2, OUT on the business
**MINI BERK insurance track, WAVE 6.** Price US$374.62 (2026-09-18), 208,575,022 shares off the
10-Q cover of 2026-07-17 (0000086312-26-000145, count at 2026-07-10), cap US$78,136M, sovereign
5.34% (US Treasury 30-year, issuing authority). Run file
`Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - TRV Travelers.md`.

**WHAT THE RUN FOUND.** Travelers is the purest insurer this track has met - no operating leg at
all - and it is a good business by the one measure the corpus nominates for the class: **its cost of
float over 2016-2025 was NEGATIVE 1.73% a year**, so it was paid about $907M a year to hold a mean
$52.4bn of other people's money while the long bond pays 5.34% to borrow. **[E3-69]**: *"a low cost
of funds signifies a good business."* It is nevertheless **not a franchise**, on three independent
grounds, and the file closes at Q2.

**REFUTED PRIORS.**
1. **The brief's MKL prior did not transfer, and that is the most useful thing here.** Markel's
   current-accident-year combined ratio was 99.3 / 101.1 / 100.3, so its reported underwriting
   profit *was* prior-year releases. **TRV's is below 100 in nine of ten years** - 95.2 / 100.2 /
   98.8 / 96.3 / 96.2 / 96.3 / 97.5 / 97.4 / 94.2 / 92.3, mean 96.44 - so its underwriting profit is
   real. **The same test that killed Markel clears Travelers, and Travelers still fails Q2 for
   different reasons.** A test that only ever fires one way is not a test.
2. **The brief asked what filed retention and renewal price change did together in personal lines.
   Neither is filed as a number.** The 10-K gives five adjectives and the furnished supplement
   carries no retention table for any segment; the quantified series lives only in earnings-call
   slides. **The substitute is better than what was asked for:** the policies-in-force series, which
   TRV publishes annually and quarterly, and which **[E4-55]** says is the honest series anyway -
   domestic personal policies 9.2M (2022 peak) to 8.4M (2025), **down 800,000 or 8.7%**, while net
   written premium per policy rose **50.6%** since 2021 and the quarterly decline accelerated
   monotonically through 2025.
3. **A prior TRV session had died in this tree at about 10:43 the same day**, uncommitted, having
   fetched seven 10-Ks, the proxy, the Q2 2026 supplement and a substantially complete CNA
   extraction. **All of it was usable and the CNA cell of this run's peer row rests on it.** The
   write-early protocol paid off *across* sessions, which the protocol does not currently claim.

**THE THREE GROUNDS FOR THE Q2 OUT.** (i) Two of three **[E3-03]** criteria fail on the filer's own
words - ~2,600 licensed US P&C companies in an industry it calls *"highly competitive in the areas
of price"*, with captives and self-insurance named as substitutes; and *"approximately one-half of
the states require prior approval of most rate changes"* against a standard that rates be *"not
excessive"*. **[E2-59]**: regulation caps a franchise and floors a commodity business, and creates
neither. (ii) **The competitor row, extended from MKL's through the CB run to thirteen names on the
current-accident-year basis, puts TRV TENTH** and fourth of the six standard-lines peers it actually
competes with, 6.0 points behind Chubb: KNSL 80.60, ACGL 86.99, CB 89.50, WRB 89.84, HIG-BI 92.28,
PGR 92.57, RLI 93.08, AXS 94.10, CNA 94.89, **TRV 95.54**, ALL 96.94, CINF 97.28, MKL 100.27.
(iii) **[E2-58]'s single exception - a cost advantage wide and sustainable - is held by Progressive
at a 21.5% expense ratio and Allstate at 21.4% against TRV's 28.5%**, seven points wide, in exactly
the lines TRV is growing.

**THE Q3 FINDING WORTH CARRYING TO OTHER INSURERS.** TRV reports net favourable prior-year
development in nine of ten years. **The mechanism, from the note 8 triangles: workers' compensation
released 20-24% of eight consecutive accident years to pay for general liability strengthening of
7-28% in eight consecutive accident years, plus commercial automobile, plus an asbestos charge every
year.** **[E2-56]**'s Pro-Am effect applied to reserves - and the fuel is measurably running out
(24.4% released on AY2016, 0.1% on AY2023), taking 1.6 points a year of reported combined ratio with
it. **The general test this suggests for any reserve-driven filer: the consolidated development
number is a NET of two opposite trends, and the line-level triangle is where the trend lives.**
Candor lands above the industry and below **[E2-67]**: TRV publishes the triangles (GAAP-mandated)
and voluntarily names the direction of its asbestos error, but never aggregates the triangles into
the sentence they support.

**TOOLING DEFECTS.** Two, both in the same family. `us-gaap:GeneralAndAdministrativeExpense` and
`us-gaap:ReinsuranceRecoverables` both stop at TRV's 2014, replaced by
`SellingGeneralAndAdministrativeExpense` and `ReinsuranceRecoverablesOnPaidAndUnpaidLosses`. **The
first draft of `arith.py` therefore printed a twelve-year table containing one row, 2014, and a mean
computed from it - without erroring.** `tools/sources.py:annual()` documents this exact defect
(added 2026-08-27 after Apple) and the fix is a tag UNION; the prompt is that a run-local script
repeats it, and that a single-row series is indistinguishable from a company with one year of filed
history, which is survival shape #3. Second: the recoverables break makes 2014 return $4,067M
against 2015's $8,910M, a concept break that would have put a spurious -4.06% into the first row of
the cost-of-float table; **no tool detects a level discontinuity at a tag boundary**, and one would
qualify under the tooling test because it removes friction from a check the run had to do by hand.

**SECTOR METHOD DEFECTS - three, none amended, all named per PRIME RULE 5.** (a) Step 1's
deferred-tax rule has **no sign**: **[E3-71]** values a deferred tax LIABILITY as an interest-free
loan, and TRV carries a $1,041M net deferred tax ASSET created by bond marks - the ordinary case for
any insurer holding bonds at market in a rising-rate world, not an exotic one. (b) **CONVENTION 5
guards the LOW side of the ratios and has no language for the high side**, and the high side is
where the method can flatter: at 3.08x investments to equity the **[E5-46]** gross-asset
construction produces **$103.2bn against a $78.1bn market capitalisation, 1.32x**, which a run that
did not stop to ask what funds the assets could report as a screamer. This run wrote that language
itself. (c) **The cost of float has no stated SIGN CONVENTION.** Every previous name had an
underwriting loss in some years; TRV has a gain in nine of ten, so the ratio is negative throughout,
and "cost of float 1.73%" versus "minus 1.73%" inverts the central economic fact about the company.
This run adopted **negative = paid to hold the money** and said so in the table header; the document
should carry it.

**THE NAMED DEATH: shape #11 THE PASS-THROUGH, with shape #7 THE LONG TAIL ON A SHORT CYCLE as its
feature. No new shape proposed.** Quantified from exposure not experience **[E4-40]**: 2017's own
realised 100.2 current-accident-year ratio on 2025's premium is a $3,395M swing, plus one event
inside the disclosed $3.0bn corporate catastrophe retention, is about $6.4bn against $7,796M of
pre-tax income - **the company survives at break-even and the owner's return falls to 2017's $7.58 a
share, a 2.0% yield on today's price**, with the next soft market arriving after the reserve cushion
is spent and with the catastrophe load doubled from 3.1 to 8.4 points. A real possibility.

**BELOW THE GATE, not a clearance:** honest pre-tax expectancy **5.28% (ten-year mean) to 6.44%
(five-year)** on a $78,136M cap against the ~10% floor **[E4-28]** - the BRK shape, above the bond
and below the floor, at a much lower quality of business. **Nothing armed.**

## UPDATE 2026-09-19 — CCB: THE FIRST BANK THE PROJECT HAS EVER RUN. Q2 OUT, and the moat was refuted from the CUSTOMERS' filings

**Coastal Financial Corporation (CCB), CIK 0001437958, WAVE 6**, run under the operator ruling of
2026-09-19 that the five banks are run. **Q1 IN · Q2 OUT on the business · Q3, Q4 and Q6 RECORDED,
NOT GOVERNING · Q5 did not open** and appears only as `COMPUTATION — NOT A CLEARANCE`, where the
name **also** fails the ~10% floor. Price **US$45.97** (2026-09-18), **15,286,327 shares** from the
Q2 2026 10-Q cover of 2026-08-03 (`0001437958-26-000061`), cap **US$702.7M**, sovereign **5.34%**
(US Treasury 30-year, 2026-09-18). Run file
`Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - CCB Coastal Financial.md`.

**THE FINDING, and it is a method finding as much as a company finding: a sponsor bank's moat
cannot be evidenced from the sponsor's own filings, and this run went and got the customers'
instead.** Coastal rents its charter to 28 financial-technology firms (CCBX: 48.1% of loans at
2025-12-31, 52.9% at 2026-06-30, 67% of 2025 consolidated pre-tax income). EDGAR full-text search
for `"Coastal Community Bank"` across **all** filers returned 113 hits since 2025-01-01, of which 45
are Coastal's own and the rest identify partners Coastal never names: **Dave Inc. (20), Prosper
Marketplace and Prosper Funding (21), Upbound Group (5), TriplePulse (3)**. Then:
- **Dave Inc.'s FY2025 10-K:** *"our partnerships with Evolve and Coastal, **our two bank
  partners**."* Coastal's largest identifiable partner is deliberately dual-sourced to a competing
  sponsor bank.
- **Prosper Marketplace's FY2025 10-K:** personal loans at **WebBank**, only the credit card at
  Coastal — and an amendment that *"**reduces the program fee percentage that the Company pays to
  Coastal by 0.75%**"*. The customer negotiated Coastal's price down, in writing, in its own filing.
- Coastal's own 10-K concedes it: a partner *"could terminate a relationship with us for many
  reasons, **including being able to obtain better terms from another provider**."*
**[E3-03] criterion 2 fails on the record, not on inference**, and the one metric that measures what
Coastal actually sells has fallen three years running on the filer's own non-GAAP table: **net BaaS
loan income per dollar of average CCBX loans 9.71% → 9.09% → 8.41%**, with the partner's share of
CCBX interest income up from **40.4% to 47.0%**. [E4-32] reads that DOWN. Class **NONE**.

**THE COMPETITOR ROW INVERTED THE BULL CASE, which is the third time a row has done that in this
tree (after HOG and CHE).** Eleven filed peers. Coastal's headline 7.14% NIM is second-highest in
the row and it is the accounting — the filer's own reconciliation cuts the CCBX margin to **3.50%**.
**And on the price of BaaS deposits Coastal is the worst in the row: 3.52% for CCBX deposits against
Pathward's 0.09% and The Bancorp's 2.06%** (TBBK, with 95% of average deposits from fintech, says
its NIM fell to 4.31% *"driven by the shift … to a greater percentage of fintech loans, for which we
primarily earn fee income"*). **The classic banking-as-a-service prize is free deposits, and Coastal
is not getting it.** Its cheap money (1.56%) belongs to the community bank — the half that is not
growing.

**THE PRIOR THAT SURVIVED, and it is the strongest fact against this run's conclusion.** The brief
asked for *"any regulatory agreement or consent order."* There is none: **zero hits for "consent
order" in six annual reports, FY2020–FY2025**, and both Company and Bank *"well capitalized."*
Against the row that is a real relative advantage, and it is **[E3-02]** vindicated — Coastal did
not *"mindlessly imitate the behavior of their peers"*, and the peers were caught: **Green Dot**, a
Federal Reserve consent order *"including a $44 million civil money penalty"*; **Customers
Bancorp**, a Written Agreement plus a Pennsylvania consent order; **Metropolitan Bank**, consent
orders from both the FRB and NYDFS in 2023, after which it exited the business. It does not promote
the name ([E2-37]), and it is a permission re-earned at every examination, not a property ([E4-04]).

**THE EVENT NO BRIEF COULD HAVE KNOWN, because it is one quarter old: the indemnity failed.** Q2
2026 net loss **$42.1 million**, ROE **−33.10%**, from *"a $22.8 million provision for credit losses
and a $46.0 million valuation adjustment to the credit enhancement asset, **both related to one
partner, not expected to be fully collected under its indemnification arrangement**"* — **$68.8
million pre-tax, 1.26% of assets, 14.8% of equity, about a point off every capital ratio** (CET1
12.43% → 10.86%). **That is [E3-29]'s mechanism proved at 9.66 : 1, not at twenty to one**:
*"mistakes that involve only a small portion of assets can destroy a major portion of equity."* The
credit enhancement asset — a receivable from private fintechs — fell $177.657M → **$154.346M**, and
the only collateral behind it is partner cash reserve accounts of **$72.2M**, a figure disclosed
**annually only**: no 10-Q carries it, including the one that wrote $46.0M off. Checked against the
Q1 2026 and Q3 2025 10-Qs — it is a standing **disclosure limit, not concealment.**

**THE COCKROACH SEQUENCE [E4-22], and it is the cleanest example of that rule this tree has
produced.** The FY2024 10-K disclosed **material weaknesses in internal control over financial
reporting *"related to the control environment and the risk assessment and control activities
components of the COSO framework associated with accounting and financial reporting for information
provided by Banking-as-a-Service ("BaaS") partners"***, which forced a **restatement of FY2023 and
six quarters** — partner accounting policies differing from Coastal's, and interchange booked gross
where Coastal *"acts as an agent"* (Note 23; *"Neither of these misstatements had any impact on
consolidated pre-tax or net income"*). Declared **fully remediated at 2025-12-31** with a *"formal
Partner ICFR Program"*, **attested by Baker Tilly** — and **five months later the same failure class
(reliance on one partner's promises) produced the $68.8 million charge.** The controls were
remediated; the exposure was not.

**PRIORS REFUTED BY READING, and recording them is the point.**
1. **Metric-switching [E2-49] looked live and is not.** The same closed year carries different
   ratios across filings (2023 efficiency **45.92%** in the FY2023 10-K, **44.66%** in the FY2025
   10-K; NIM 7.10% then 6.88%). That is the yardstick-disposition tell — and it is **Note 23's
   restatement**, disclosed and audited, and it made the **older** figures look **better**. The
   positive condition is met instead: the proxy publishes the incentive plan's four goals, weights,
   three thresholds **and the outturn — three of four missed and published as missed** (ROA 1.17%
   target / 1.05% actual; core deposits 19.21% / 10.08%; gross loans 12.88% / 7.55%).
2. **The [E4-29] EBITDA flag is clean, and the CGNX rule was applied properly** — all four furnished
   8-K EX-99.1 earnings releases were pulled before scoring. **EBITDA appears zero times** in the
   10-K, in all four releases and in the proxy. **And every non-GAAP measure Coastal publishes makes
   the reported figure worse** (CCBX margin 9.00% → 3.50%; CCBX yield 15.87% → 8.41%). Under
   **[E2-69]** — judge deviations by direction — that is the candor case, not the flag.
3. **Serial issuance [E5-15] does not fire.** The one step in the count is a **$98.0M raise in
   December 2024 at about $67 a share against $29.38 of book (~2.3×)** — [E5-44] in reverse, and
   accretive. No dividend has ever been paid and no share was repurchased in 2025.
4. **The aggregator price was corroborated from primary documents, which is new here.** The CCBX
   President's Forms 4 report Coastal shares at **$41.80 on 2026-08-03** and **$46.85 on
   2026-09-01**, both code F (tax withholding, not sales), bracketing the $45.97 quote. **A Form 4
   is a primary-document price check and it costs one fetch** — worth adding to the habit.

**WHAT THE INCENTIVE PLAN CANNOT SEE [E4-27].** 65% of the measured 2025 bonus weight is growth and
asset-based return; board discretionary is 25% and paid at 100%; and the **net-charge-off metric
scored 100% of target in a year of $196.8 million of consolidated net charge-offs**, because — the
proxy's own footnote — *"Net charge-off goals are based on community bank data only as CCBX
charge-offs are reimbursed by our CCBX partners."* The community bank charged off **$27 thousand**.
The plan cannot see the risk that produced the 2026 loss.

**THE GOVERNANCE SEQUENCE, recorded under [E3-57]/[E2-30] and NOT as an [E5-16] conduct finding.**
2026-05-12, the CCBX President adopts a 10b5-1 plan for up to 15,000 shares. The quarter to
2026-06-30 carries the $68.8M. **2026-07-22, the CFO resigns after ten months** — hired 2025-10-01 at
$500,000 annualised with RSUs and PSUs granted at a $110.59 stock price — *"to pursue a position as
the Chief Executive Officer of a banking subsidiary of a privately held company in the financial
technology sector"*, with the **65-year-old retired predecessor made interim CFO**. **2026-07-29, one
day before the loss is announced, the board makes its chairman Executive Chair on a five-year
agreement at $750,000** — a partner in the law firm the Company paid **$1.3 million** in FY2025 —
alongside an existing CEO on $874,000. 2026-07-30, the loss is reported. With Queyrouze and Stines
resigning in 2025, that is **five executive changes in twenty-four months** in a business the
framework had just classed have-to-be-smart-every-day. At the 2026 annual meeting the 11.34% holder
and bank-M&A principal **Steven D. Hovde was re-elected 6,374,067 to 6,372,171 — 50.007%.** The CEO,
sixteen years in the job, owns **0.26%**.

**THE ARITHMETIC THAT MATTERS MOST, and it required a new CONVENTION.** The ordinary owner-earnings
construction was **refused with reasons** — 2025 operating cash flow was **$254.6M against $47.0M of
net income** because $6.69bn of loans ran through held-for-sale; property purchases were $8.4M
against $4.74bn of assets. So, per **[E5-37]** and exactly as the insurer sector method does for
float, the metric set was selected by business type first, and the measure is **[E2-01]**'s own
return on equity capital employed, **plus a (c) equivalent labelled CONVENTION: `(c) = Δassets ×
the Tier 1 leverage ratio`** — the equity a bank must retain to hold its capital ratio while it
grows; corpus anchor **[E2-60]**'s third dimension of maintenance, *"its financial strength."*
- **ROE 17.24% → 18.24% → 16.41% → 14.11% → 10.17% → −12.04%** (H1 2026, as filed), recomputed
  independently and matching within 0.15 points in four of five years.
- **Pre-tax income flat for three years — $57.1M, $57.3M, $61.2M — while average equity rose 73%.**
- **(c): $316.0M of capital required 2021–25 against $204.4M earned — a $111.6M shortfall.** Equity
  rose $350.7M against cumulative net income of $204.4M, so **$146.3M was bought from new
  shareholders.** Five-year mean owner earnings **−$22.3M**, three-year **−$10.9M**, and **−$11.5M**
  excluding the distorted 2021. **Gruesome [E4-20]**, with [E4-43] applied so as not to over-read it:
  it was in the *good* class in 2021–23 and is not now.
- **Staying power [E5-11]: 2 of 3**, and the failure is strength (3) — the one the corpus calls the
  killer. $1,008.4M of cash, zero FHLB and zero discount-window borrowings at every year-end,
  $48.1M of total borrowings, $1.12bn of contingent capacity — against **$3.29bn of the $4.86bn of
  deposits belonging to CCBX**, demand-withdrawable and tied to terminable programme agreements,
  with **estimated uninsured deposits up from $641.3M (15.5%) to $1.35bn (27.7%) in six months.**

**THE STRESS [E3-24] SPLIT THE COMPANY IN TWO, which is the most useful thing in the file.**
**(A) The community bank passes the corpus's own bank test at the corpus's own parameters:** 10% of
the $1,982.5M community-bank book at 30% severity = **$59.5M** against a year's pre-tax of
**$61.2M** — *"the company would roughly break even"*, the exact 1990 Wells Fargo result. Non-owner-
occupied CRE plus construction is 170.9% of the Bank's total risk-based capital against the 300%
interagency threshold. **This bank does not die of loans. (B) It dies of counterparties:** with the
enhancement worth nothing for one year at FY2025 volumes, pre-tax $61.2M becomes **−$126.4M**,
equity $463.4M → **$368.6M**; **a second such year: $273.8M and 5.02% of assets, through the 5%
well-capitalised line.** Graded on the partner that already failed: **one partner = 14.8% of equity,
three = 44.5%, five of twenty-eight = 74.2%. Likelihood: A REAL POSSIBILITY** — not low-level,
because it is the filed record of the most recent quarter; not likely, because the Bank may
*"declare the agreement in default, take over servicing"* and *"retain the full yield."*

**SURVIVAL SHAPE #25 — THE INDEMNITY, proposed, added to `Screens/SURVIVAL SHAPES - index.md` by
this fold**, with **#11 THE PASS-THROUGH as a feature**: *the balance sheet holds the assets and the
legal losses, and the losses have been contracted away to counterparties smaller and
less-capitalised than the lender, so the reported credit quality is a receivable from the borrowers'
own promoters; the promise is booked as income on the way in and reversed as expense on the way
out.* It is #6 inverted (Coastal lends its balance sheet rather than borrowing one) and #13 inverted
(Coastal is the landlord, and its rent is being negotiated down).

**BELOW-GATE: IT FAILS THE FLOOR TOO.** Honest pre-tax expectancy **8.71%** on the best single year
the company has ever had and **7.42%** on the five-year mean, both below the ~10% [E4-28] quit-on
figure, and **negative** on the retention-adjusted construction. Above the bond (337bp over 5.34%),
below the floor — the Berkshire configuration. Price/book **1.52×**. **Nothing armed**: a Q2 OUT
failed on the business, so the QLYS ruling of 2026-09-07 gives a reversal condition in words —
Coastal's partners ceasing to dual-source, observable in **their** 10-Ks.

**WHAT THE FRAMEWORK NEEDS IN ORDER TO RUN A BANK — four gaps, for the operator, because four more
banks are queued (ACNB, SOFI, JPM, TFC).**
1. **Q2 has no passable form for a bank, and the corpus says so itself.** **[E3-43]** classes a bank
   as *"a business, unlike a franchise"* — which is *why* **[E3-29]** raises Q3 to gate weight — and
   **[E3-03]** criterion 2 requires *no close substitute*, which no deposit-taker in a metropolitan
   market has ever had. Read literally, **every bank stops at Q2**, and the corpus bought banks.
   **This run did not use that reasoning**; it closed Q2 on Coastal's own and its counterparties'
   filed facts. But the general question is structural and needs a ruling (PRIME RULE 5). The two
   candidates: (a) Q2 for a bank is a *local-deposit-franchise* test, which Coastal's community-bank
   half passes; (b) **[E3-29]** creates an explicit exception class in which Q2 returns NARROW and
   the decision moves wholly to Q3 and Q5. **(b) has the better textual support and the worse
   discipline.**
2. **The evidence ladder stops too soon for a regulated filer.** The **FFIEC Call Report** (the only
   public data on the private sponsor banks that are Coastal's real competitors — Cross River,
   WebBank, Evolve, Column, Lead, Sutton, Celtic, Thread) and the **Federal Reserve / state banking
   department enforcement registers** (the only place a supervisory action becomes public) are both
   outside the six rungs. Their absence turned the industry's most important competitor comparison
   into a stated limit and the supervisory record into an absence claim reading *"no instance found
   in SEC filings."*
3. **Owner earnings needs a declared form for balance-sheet businesses, as float got one.** The
   CONVENTION above should be adopted with a ledger row or refused.
4. **A ruling on whether `COMPUTATION — NOT A CLEARANCE` may carry a floor verdict.** This run found
   a second, independent, sufficient reason not to buy and recorded it as a note beside the Q2 FAIL
   rather than as the fail line.

**TOOLING FINDING, and it is a live trap for any future financials screen:** the screening layer
builds owner earnings from **operating cash flow**, which for a bank measures growth, not earnings.
**CCB 2025: operating cash flow $254.6M against net income $47.0M — 5.4×**, because $6.69 billion of
loans ran through loans-held-for-sale. **Any screen that priced a bank that way priced it at roughly
five times its earnings.** The 2026-09-01 triage dropped financials as a class, which accidentally
avoided it; if financials are ever screened, the construction must change first. *(No screen output
for CCB exists on disk to check against — the 2026-09-01 triage priced it with a financial flag and
then dropped it, and the pricing script is still not committed, which is the HBB finding of
2026-09-19 again.)*

**DEFECTS IN THE BRIEF, recorded as the operator asked.** (i) It said to strike CCB **"in the WAVE 6
table"** — **CCB is not in that table.** The table is the eleven businesses the 2026-09-01 triage
dropped, and adding a twelfth row would falsify its own "eleven" and the 151-of-151 reconciliation.
CCB appears in the WAVE 6 section only in the operator-ruling sentence and in the
`#### EXCLUDED UNDER THE OPERATOR'S BANK DIRECTIVE` subsection, and **it was struck in both places
with a dated note**. (ii) The brief's list of banking-as-a-service comparables (*"Pathward, Live Oak,
Customers Bancorp"*) omitted **The Bancorp (TBBK)**, which is the closest comparable that exists and
which **Coastal's own proxy names in its compensation peer group** — and TBBK turned out to carry the
single most illuminating sentence in the row (its NIM falling *because* it shifted to fee-based
fintech lending, which is the structure Coastal has not adopted). **Live Oak is not a BaaS bank at
all** — it is a digital SBA lender with zero hits for "BaaS" in its 10-K — and it is in the row as a
digital-lender comparable, labelled as such. (iii) The brief was otherwise accurate, and its two
best instructions both paid: **[E3-03] criterion 2 tested against what the filings say about a
partner moving sponsor banks** produced the verdict, and **the instruction to read the reserving
record against subsequent charge-offs** produced the finding that the company-wide charge-off rate
is meaningless as read while the community bank's is 40–701× covered.

## AIG (American International Group, Inc.) - run 2026-09-19 - Q1 IN, **Q2 OUT on the business**
Run file: `Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - AIG American International Group.md`. WAVE 6, MINI BERK insurance track, sector method with both
amendments. Price US$75.33 (2026-09-18, aggregator, flagged); 522,893,169 shares off the Q2 2026 10-Q cover (`0000005272-26-000076`);
cap US$39,389M; sovereign 5.34% (US Treasury 30-year, 2026-09-18). Q3 and Q4 recorded, not governing; Q5 a computation only; no band.

### WHAT THIS RUN ADDS TO THE INSURER PANEL
- **The MKL/CB decisive series separates Chubb from AIG more sharply than any other measure in either file.** Current-accident-year
  combined ratio including catastrophes, 2016-2025, from the filer's own published points in four 10-Ks, every row re-added to the reported
  ratio: **100.4 / 113.2 / 110.2 / 100.8 / 104.4 / 96.4 / 93.7 / 92.0 / 93.2 / 92.2.** Above 100 in five of ten years; ten-year mean
  **99.65 against Chubb's 92.3**. The same hurricanes in 2017: Chubb 97.9, AIG 113.2. The same pandemic year: Chubb 97.4, AIG 104.4.
- **A new Q2 shape for the panel: the manager-made turnaround.** Same licences, same brand, same markets: five years above 100, then five
  below 94 in four of them. [E2-36]'s corporate Pygmalion rather than an excisable cancer, and [E4-04]/[E4-23] then close it, because the
  two executives who performed the turnaround leave on the filed record (Zaffino off the board 2026-09-15; Hancock, CEO of General
  Insurance, retiring 2026-12-31). Chubb's key-person question was open; AIG's is answered by its own first half-decade.
- **The competitor row now has AIG, TRV and HIG Business Insurance in it** (`Test Runs/_research 2026-09-19 AIG/peers/row_out.txt`): on the
  current-accident-year basis 2021-25, KNSL 80.60, ACGL 86.99, CB 89.50, WRB 89.84, HIG-BI 92.28, RLI 93.08, **AIG 93.50**, AXS 94.10,
  TRV 95.54, MKL 100.27. AIG is 7th of 10 in its best five years. **My TRV figures (96.3 / 97.5 / 97.4 / 94.2 / 92.3) match the TRV run's
  own, computed independently the same afternoon**, which is a cross-check on both files.
- **Reserving candor, read two ways.** AIG names every adverse line in words each year and publishes ten triangles, and its 2025 Investor
  Day deck prints its predecessors' *"2008 – 2018 $33B underwriting loss"* - a candor point. But its headline prior-year figure is struck
  after the NICO cessions: 2024 was **$254M adverse before the cover** and is reported as $368M favourable. [E2-67]'s scorecard is not
  published, as at Chubb.
- **The NICO adverse development cover is the panel's most direct evidence of what a non-franchise reserve book costs:** the pre-2016 US
  long-tail book has paid **$32.6bn against the $25bn attachment**, with $8.9bn still to pay, the excess funded by Berkshire.

### THE REFUTED PRIORS
- **"Check what AIG still holds in Corebridge" - it holds nothing.** Corebridge bought back $750M of stock from AIG on 2026-02-17 and AIG
  sold its last 25.5M shares on **2026-05-07** (Q2 2026 10-Q, Note 1). The carrying basis the brief asked about was the fair value option
  inside an equity-method line (2024-06-09 to 2026-03-31), then an equity security, then nothing.
- **"Management changed completely since 2008" - true, and it is changing again right now**, which the brief did not mention and which
  became the centre of Q2: a new CEO from 2026-02-16 (from Aon's presidency, not from underwriting), the executive chair gone on
  2026-09-15, the General Insurance CEO gone on 2026-12-31.
- **"A five-year window on one perimeter may not exist" - confirmed, and it bore on Q3 and Q5, not Q1, Q2 or Q4.** The consolidated
  statements carry continuing operations for 2023-2025 only, and 2023 still holds Validus Re and Crop Risk Services; the General Insurance
  segment series is continuous and is what Q2 used.
- **"Large adverse reserve charges in the 2010s" - confirmed from the rollforward**: prior-year development of $5,788M adverse in 2016,
  $1,565M in 2017, $1,429M in 2018 (FY2018 10-K).
- **The death candidate:** the brief listed catastrophe, long-tail reserves and the portfolio. The filings support long-tail reserves;
  the catastrophe exposure is small **net** (1-in-250 worldwide $2.5bn, 4.8% of equity) because AIG cedes 40.9% of gross reserves and
  buys a large catastrophe programme. The dependence on reinsurers' annual renewal is the [E5-39] item instead.

### DEFECTS FOUND
- **Tooling: `.gitignore` does not cover the `tenk_*.txt` / `tenq_*.txt` names** that the CB fetcher and this run's fetcher use for
  stripped filings (the patterns match `*10-K*`, `*10K*`, `*10k*`, `*10-Q*` and so on). The CB run's five stripped 10-K/10-Q files entered
  history that way. This run did not commit its stripped filings; the pattern is left for the operator to extend, not edited here.
- **Process: something other than this run wrote into this run's research folder** during the run (stripped AIG 10-Ks for FY2017,
  FY2019 and FY2024, and fresh copies of FY2021 and FY2023, at 15:37-15:40). Same EDGAR documents, no harm done, and not committed; but a
  second writer in a run's folder is the precondition for the crossings the fold rule exists to prevent.
- **`tools/sources.py:cik_for()` returns a `(cik, name)` tuple**, not a CIK string; a script that formats it as a number fails. Not a bug,
  a signature worth knowing.
- **Sector method gap 1 - CONVENTION 4 cannot be built on a consolidated balance sheet that still holds a life insurer** (AIG before
  2024-06-09: life receivables and DAC corrupt two of five terms). This run used average net loss reserves from the rollforward as the
  float proxy for the ten-year cost of float and confessed it; the two agree in direction for 2025 (-5.69% against -5.06%).
- **Sector method gap 2 - retroactive reinsurance has no rule.** AIG's ratios and cost of float exclude the development ceded to NICO
  and the deferred-gain amortisation; the consideration paid for the 2017 cover is outside the General Insurance ratio entirely. A filer
  that has sold its reserve deficiency looks cheaper to fund than it was. The run disclosed it rather than adjusting for it.
- **Sector method pointer: "Schedule P"** - the method cites the statutory Schedule P triangles; this run (like CB) used the 10-K Note
  triangles, which are GAAP, net, undiscounted and by line. Schedule P was not pulled.

### ONE THING TO KEEP
The price is the strongest fact against the verdict: **0.97x book and 12.0% pre-tax on 2025 adjusted earnings with the excluded
restructuring put back** - above the ~10% floor that quit Chubb. A Q2 OUT on a cheap insurer is [E3-47]'s omission risk by definition;
the Q6 reversal conditions (current-accident-year ratio under 95 through FY2028 under the new management; a top-half row position; no
adverse excess-casualty development on AY2021+; expense ratio under 29%) are the written test of whether it was the wrong close.

### AIG ADDENDUM - the replication, two corrections (same session, after `4ed4627`)
- **Two agents ran AIG** (commit `c7132f3`); the second reproduced every core figure independently and refused to overwrite the committed run. **Its findings are folded, checked first**: an eleventh year (2015, current-accident-year 99.4; eleven-year mean 99.6, five of eleven above 100); a proxy-against-10-K candor inconsistency (the board letter's *"For the first time since 2008, we generated more than $2 billion in underwriting income"* against the filer's own $2,048M in 2022 and $2,349M in 2023); component 2 nearly nil; restructuring excluded in every year 2021-2025; and a below-gate floor computation averaging 9.36%.
- **Correction 1 - my Q3 scored [E4-30] on smoothness alone.** The cash-tax half fires and is explained: cash taxes 34.3% -> 18.3% -> 8.5% of pre-tax income (2023-25; the first two include Corebridge), on a valuation-allowance release.
- **Correction 2 - my Q4 summed alternative shocks within one reserve line** ($5.05bn). Like-for-like with CB it is **$2.8bn, 6.8% of equity and 52% of adjusted pre-tax income, against Chubb's 3.7% and 23%**. A defect worth keeping for every insurer run: **the filer's sensitivity table lists alternatives, not a scenario; sum one per line.**
- **Sector-method gap, sharpened:** about $13.2bn of AIG's covered long-tail losses are NICO's (paid or open), so CONVENTION 4 float prices Berkshire's credit as AIG's funding.

## ACNB (ACNB Corporation) - run 2026-09-19 - Q1-Q4 IN, FAIL at Q5 on price. The SECOND bank the project has run and the FIRST to clear the business gates.

**Verdict line: Q1 IN / Q2 IN (NARROW, direction MIXED) / Q3 IN at GATE weight / Q4 IN (GOOD, not great) / Q5 OUT ON PRICE, quit on at the ~10% [E4-28] floor / Q6 IN.** Price **US$64.57** (2026-09-18 close, aggregator flagged) x **10,169,930** shares (10-Q cover, accession `0001628280-26-054143`, issued-versus-outstanding checked: 11,079,210 issued, 909,280 in treasury) = cap **US$656.7M**. Sovereign **5.34%** USD, **US Treasury** 30-year par yield, 09/18/2026. Register entry **128**.

**THE ONE THING THIS RUN ADDS TO THE PROJECT'S METHOD, and it is not about ACNB: for a bank, the competitor row should be built from the FDIC Call Report FIRST.** The SEC row - ten PA/MD holding companies over five years, one stated specification - took most of this run's peer effort and it was the FDIC row that decided the question. The Call Report is better on every count that matters here: it is **the issuing authority** rather than a redistribution; it covers the **private and mutual banks an SEC row structurally cannot see**, which is exactly the class ACNB's own 10-K names as its deposit competition; it is **bank-level** rather than holding-company-level, so the holding company's subordinated debt does not contaminate the margin; and it **publishes net interest margin, cost of funding earning assets, the efficiency ratio and return on equity directly**, so they need not be reconstructed from tagged data on eleven different tagging conventions. The mechanics, recorded so the next bank run can reuse them: `banks.data.fdic.gov/api/locations` filtered by `STALP` and `COUNTY` enumerates every banking office (712 across ACNB's nine counties, reducing to **56 distinct insured institutions**), and `banks.data.fdic.gov/api/financials` with `search=CERT:<n>` and `filters=REPDTE:<yyyymmdd>` returns `NIMY`, `INTEXPY`, `EEFFR`, `ROE`, `ROA`, `ROAPTX`, `DEPUNINS`, `DEPNIDOM`, `COREDEP` and `NTLNLSR` per institution per quarter. **Two API traps, both hit and both fixed in `Test Runs/_research 2026-09-19 ACNB/fdic_row.py`: `api.fdic.gov` 404s - the host is `banks.data.fdic.gov`; and a `CERT:(a OR b OR c)` filter silently returns institutions outside the list, so CERTs must be requested one at a time and the result filtered client-side.** Also note the `CERT` field is a **string** in `locations` and an **integer** in `financials`.

**WHAT THE FDIC ROW FOUND, and it both made and qualified the Q2 case.** ACNB Bank is CERT 7506. At 2026-06-30 it carries a **4.553% net interest margin against a 56-bank market median of 3.746%**, a **1.274% cost of funding earning assets against a median of 1.685%**, a **50.54% efficiency ratio**, **14.53% ROE**, **1.80% ROA** and **0.012% of net charge-offs**. Against the eleven banks that actually compete for the same deposits and buildings it is **first on net interest margin, first on funding cost among everything above a billion dollars, first on efficiency and first on return on assets**, and Citizens & Northern - same size, same state, same business - is charging off **0.880%, seventy-three times as much**. Of the 56, exactly six combine a margin above 4% with funding below 1.5%, and **ACNB is the only Pennsylvania- or Maryland-headquartered community bank above $1bn among them**. Bank of Bird-in-Hand, the fast-growing private Lancaster County bank the SEC row could not see, funds at **2.75%** - more than twice ACNB's cost - which is the answer to whether the advantage is an artefact of comparing ACNB only with listed companies.

**AND THE FINDING THAT CORRECTS THE SNAPSHOT. The five-year Call Report panel says the advantage is not what the 2025 numbers suggest.**

| | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | 2026-06-30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ACNB cost of funding earning assets | 0.231% | 0.109% | 0.334% | 1.048% | 1.412% | 1.274% |
| median of the 56 institutions | 0.232% | 0.383% | 1.599% | 2.174% | 1.928% | 1.685% |
| **ACNB advantage, points** | **0.00** | **0.27** | **1.27** | **1.13** | **0.52** | **0.41** |
| **ACNB rank, cheapest of 56** | **28th** | **3rd** | **2nd** | **3rd** | **9th** | **8th** |
| ACNB NIM advantage over the median | **-0.10** | +0.12 | +0.78 | +0.68 | +0.92 | +0.81 |

**In 2021, with the risk-free rate at zero, ACNB was the 28th cheapest funder of 56 - exactly the median - and its net interest margin was BELOW the median. There was no visible advantage at all.** What the record actually shows is **not a permanent cost advantage but a LOW DEPOSIT BETA**: the market's cost of funds rose 194 basis points from 2021 to 2024 while ACNB's rose 82; as the market's came back down 49, ACNB's came down 14. **A lag is worth most when rates are high, which is when it matters for margin - and it compresses on the way down as it expanded on the way up.** So **[E2-58]**'s one exception, *"a cost advantage that is both wide and sustainable"*, is met on a **64-basis-point cycle average** across 2021-2025 - about **$13 million a year pre-tax, a fifth of pre-tax income** - and **not** on the 127-basis-point 2023 peak. The composite points the other way and is still widening: from 10 basis points below the market median in 2021 to 81 above it in mid-2026. **Class NARROW, direction MIXED, and the two limbs are written as pointing opposite ways on purpose.**

**REFUTED PRIOR, mine and worth recording: I expected a community bank's Q2 to fail, because deposits and loans are commodities and [E2-58] says the exception is rare.** The filings refuted it. What I had not expected is *where* the advantage lives: **ACNB is not a better-paid lender at all** - its total earning-asset yield of 5.61% in 2025 is BELOW Orrstown's 6.13% - **it is a cheaper funder, and the whole franchise is one line of the income statement.** That is also why the class is NARROW and why the Q4 death is a funding event rather than a credit event.

**THE CONVENTION, AND THE ONE MODIFICATION CCB'S VERSION NEEDED.** This run adopted the CCB construction of the same day - four measures of [E2-01]'s *"earnings rate on equity capital employed"*, with **ROTCE as [E2-43]'s governing denominator** for a five-time acquirer and the goodwill wedge on its own line, plus the **(c) equivalent = Δassets x the Bank's Tier 1 leverage ratio** - and found that it needs the **CNR split**. ACNB's 2025 asset increase of $833,296k contains **$877,450k that arrived on 2025-02-01 in the Traditions acquisition and was paid for with $83,649k of issued stock, not with retained earnings.** Unsplit, (c) is $90,996k and "owner earnings" is **minus $53,945k** - which is arithmetic about a stock issuance dressed up as arithmetic about earning power. **Split, the organic record is the mirror image of Coastal's and is the check that the construction is not tuned to a result: five-year organic (c) of $20,406k against $164,171k earned, a $143,765k SURPLUS, where CCB's identical construction produced a $111.6M shortfall.** The balance sheet SHRANK in four of the five years. **This company does not retain earnings to grow; it issues shares to buy growth and pays the earnings out** - a 45% five-year payout, and 89% of H1 2026 earnings returned including a $0.50 special dividend. **Standing ruling for SOFI, JPM and TFC: the bank CONVENTION requires the CNR split whenever the filer bought anything inside the window.**

**THE SHARPEST SINGLE FINDING, and it is a finding about a model rather than about a number: ACNB's own interest-rate simulation cannot see the risk the balance sheet carries, and [E4-40] says exactly why.** The filer discloses that a **plus-or-minus 200 basis point twelve-month ramp moves its net interest income by at most 1.1%**, against policy limits of 5% and 10%. That model is correct for a rate shock and it runs on **historical deposit betas** - on *experience*. **The exposure is different in kind: $600,711k of deposits paying ZERO and $336,504k of savings paying 0.03% while the 30-year Treasury pays 5.34%. Nothing has to happen in the rate market for that to reprice. The depositor simply has to notice.** Repriced to 3.0%, it costs **$28,015k pre-tax - 38.0% of annualised pre-tax pre-provision earnings - with market rates completely unchanged.** The mild form, simple convergence of the deposit cost to the market median, costs **$10,259k at today's 41bp gap and $16,014k at the 64bp cycle-average gap**, taking ROE from 13.76% to roughly 11.5% and 10.4%; combined with a 25%-severity loss on a fifth of the non-owner-occupied CRE book ($41,654k), a year's earnings goes to approximately zero with the company solvent and well capitalised. **[E4-40]'s warning is that a benign loss history late in a good cycle is *"not only useless, but actually dangerous"*, and here the filer's own risk model is the benign history in equation form.**

**NEW SURVIVAL SHAPE PROPOSED: #25 THE SLEEPING DEPOSITOR**, with **#11 THE PASS-THROUGH** named as the mechanism so the index stays honest if the proposal is refused. The argument against #11: in every #11 instance the gain flows to the **customer or the supplier because a rival bids it away**; here it flows to the **supplier of the raw material** - the depositor - and **no rival has to do anything at all**, because the substitute has been on the table at a 400-basis-point advantage for three years and the counterparty only has to read its own statement. Against #19 THE SHELF: no concentrated intermediary takes the margin (the twenty largest depositors are 7.2% of the book). Against #22 THE HABIT: Coca-Cola's habit is a purchase the customer enjoys and pays a premium for, whereas **this habit costs the counterparty money every day it persists.** Its distinguishing feature, and the reason it is worth a number: **there is no observable event.** #11 narrows when a competitor cuts price and you can watch it happen; #25 narrows one account at a time, silently, and shows up only in the funding-cost line two quarters later. **Tells checkable on any deposit-taker: a large noninterest-bearing balance priced at zero by inattention rather than by contract; a disclosed cost of funds far below the market median with no contractual reason; a rate table showing savings at 0.03% while the sovereign pays five per cent; and an interest-rate sensitivity model built on historical betas, which therefore cannot see it.**

**THE [E3-02] CONFORMITY TEST, answered four ways, and it answers in ACNB's favour on everything except the deal-making.** The flag **fires on M&A**: four of the eleven row names bought a bank inside eighteen months (Orrstown/Codorus Valley 2024-07-01, Citizens & Northern/Susquehanna 2025, Peoples Financial/FNCB 2024, ACNB/Traditions 2025-02-01). It is **refuted on every place the industry was actually lax.** **Credit:** net charge-offs of 0.13 / 0.06 / 0.16 / 0.08 / 0.08 / 0.02 / 0.02 / 0.01 per cent across eight filed years, and 0.012% now against C&N's 0.880%. **Duration, where the 2023 failures happened:** held-to-maturity securities are $63,288k of amortised cost against $56,576k of fair value, an unrecognised loss of **$6,712k, 1.98% of tangible common equity** - mark the whole portfolio and tangible equity falls from $338,479k only to $331,767k, because **88% was kept in available-for-sale where the loss already sits in equity, and $2.8M of it was crystallised ON PURPOSE in December 2025 with an 8-K about it.** **CRE concentration against the regulatory thresholds:** non-owner-occupied CRE plus construction plus multi-family was **239.0% of the Bank's total risk-based capital at 2025-12-31 and 231.6% at 2026-06-30**, inside the **300%** level of the 2006 interagency guidance's second criterion (whose 36-month growth limb *is* met on the acquisition, but the guidance requires both limbs), and **construction alone, ~$116,680k against ~$397M of Bank total risk-based capital, is ~29% against the 100% level of the first criterion** - and the filer volunteers that sentence, which nothing requires it to do. **Funding:** uninsured and non-collateralised deposits 17.7% then 18.1% of Bank deposits (21.1% on the FDIC's broader definition) against **40-50% at JPMorgan, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and PNC in the same nine counties**, with liquidity covering 329.7% of them.

**THE RESERVING RECORD, which is a bank's only substitute for [E2-67]'s table, and it resolves the one flag that matters for a bank.** [E2-50] fired: **the 2024 CECL assumption change released $2,763k of pre-tax income, 6.8% of that year's total, in the one year when reported EPS would otherwise have FALLEN from $3.71 to about $3.53 rather than risen to $3.73 - while the allowance ratio fell from 1.23% to 1.03% and nonaccrual loans rose from $3,011k to $5,871k.** What answers it is the direction of the error over eight years: **the allowance has been 3.1x / 2.8x / 7.3x / 10.6x / 18.7x the net charge-offs actually taken in the three years that followed it, in every testable window.** [E2-50]'s risk is UNDER-reserving and ACNB's error has run conservative every time, so the 2024 release reads as **a late correction of a demonstrably over-large reserve, taken in a convenient year** - not as a reserve built in order to be released. **[E2-67]'s exact artifact does not exist for a bank and the absence is stated rather than scored.**

**Q3 AT GATE WEIGHT, and two contrasts with runs folded the same day.** [E4-29] **reads clean with the count given**: `grep -c -i ebitda` = 0 in the 10-K, 0 in the Q2 10-Q, **0 in all FOUR 8-K EX-99.1 earnings releases** (the CGNX companion rule was followed) and 0 in the proxy, with "adjusted EPS", "adjusted earnings" and "adjusted net income" also at zero. **[E3-50] does not fire** - the pay metrics are net interest margin and return on average equity, and TSR appears only inside the mandated Item 402(v) table, **the exact inverse of the BLK run's finding one day old that "Next 12-Month P/E Multiple (including relative premium)" is scored as a financial-performance measure.** [E4-30]'s cash-tax tell **fires and reads benign** (25.2 to 16.4 to 11.5% of pre-tax, against a flat 20.5 / 21.2 / 20.2% book rate, a current/deferred split of $5,777k/$3,626k disclosed in Note 15, and a rate reconciliation whose largest line is 1.5 points). **[E2-57] fires at the pay formula**: $1,582,358 of after-tax merger costs added back to net income and ROAE for award purposes - **and the same passage discloses an offsetting $3,479,192 securities-loss adjustment against the executives and nets the two to +$146,790 in public, which is [E2-49]'s pre-set bullseyes and the candor case demonstrated in one paragraph.** **[E2-72] is recorded as UNTESTABLE rather than scored either way: ACNB's 10-K carries no shareholder letter and a CEO letter, if one exists, lives in a glossy annual report that is not an SEC filing.**

**CAPITAL-ALLOCATION FLAG LIVE, and the sharpest instance is not a bank.** **[E5-44]** runs the wrong way on every deal: ACNB issued 2,035,246 shares at $41.10 ($83,649k) when its own tangible book value per share was $29.37 - **paper at 1.40x its own tangible book to receive $44,688k of tangible net assets, i.e. 1.88x** - diluting tangible book value per share by about $15M, 6% of pre-deal tangible equity, and the 2020 and 2017 deals have the same shape. But the instance that reads on management rather than on arithmetic is **$7,800,000 of CASH in February 2022 for Hockley & O'Donnell Insurance Agency: the insurance segment's pre-tax income four years later is BELOW its pre-purchase level - $920k (2021), $1,312k, $1,701k, $1,528k, $853k (2025) - on revenue that rose from $5,928k to $9,482k.** The revenue arrived and the earnings went backwards. Against the flag, and recorded: the Traditions deal **is** earning ($13.2M of pre-tax in eleven months; pro-forma 2025 net income $48,943k against $37,051k reported; H1 2026's 18.21% ROTCE is the best figure in the five-year series), and **[E5-08]'s second condition passes on filed prices - 38,203 shares at $42.73 and 17,140 at $46.36 in Q4 2025 and 179,407 at a weighted-average $50.79 in Q2 2026, every share below $51 against a $64.57 quote, which is better execution than this run's own valuation would have managed.**

**WHY IT FAILED, IN ONE SENTENCE.** Honest pre-tax expectancy is **8.4% at the bottom boundary [E5-34], 9.3% at the centre and 10.7% at the top**, against the **~10% floor [E4-28]** - pre-tax owner earnings of $41.9M to $53.6M on a $656.7M capitalisation is a 6.43-8.15% pre-tax yield plus 2.0-2.5% of growth - so **ACNB is above the bond on every construction and below the floor, the Berkshire case named in the operator protocol, and the third name to land there on 2026-09-19 after CB and GFF.** Value roughly **$45 to $65** against **$64.57**; the screamer test's answer is *above the whole conservative range and inside the full range*, which is *no useful conclusion*; and the floor needs **1.85-3.57% growth in owner earnings per share for ever** against diluted EPS of **minus 3.5% a year since 2022** and tangible book value per share of **plus 6.9% a year** - the record supports the assumption on tangible book and refutes it on EPS, **and the difference between the two is the acquisitions.** Windage ONE, at Q4.

**THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT [E4-26, E4-51], and it is about my arithmetic rather than the company: the two most recent quarters earned $13.7M and $15.2M, so if that is the run rate the company is at 11.4x earnings and 1.93x a tangible book compounding at 6.9% a year, the expectancy is 10.7%, and this file says BUY.** It does not, because [E5-34] prices against the bottom boundary and [E4-18] forbids narrowing until the answer appears - **but two record quarters are thin evidence for a peak and thin evidence for a run rate alike, and a reader who prefers the newer perimeter reaches the opposite verdict from the same file.**

**ARMED, because this is a PRICE failure and not a business failure** (the QLYS ruling of 2026-09-07 cuts this way): **bands $58.70** (the centre case meets the floor) **and $51.50** (the bottom boundary meets the floor), each **a prompt for a full re-run and not a purchase**, both VOID if any Q6 falsifier fires; plus a `PORTFOLIO.md` row, **unranked, watch-list only, no position held and none proposed, pre-committed SIZED DOWN if it ever clears.** **Q6's discriminating observation is stated in advance so it cannot be back-fitted: if the funding advantage narrows while the sovereign FALLS it is the low-beta lag and it is aberrational; if it narrows while the sovereign is FLAT or RISING the depositors have noticed and it is permanent** - from 2025 to mid-2026 the 30-year was roughly flat and the advantage fell 11 basis points, which is mildly adverse and not yet decisive.

**TOOLING DEFECTS, four.** (1) **`tools/sources.py:_get()` still defaults to `WEB_UA` = Mozilla/5.0 and `www.sec.gov/Archives` answers it with HTTP 403** - the BLK run found this earlier today and it is confirmed a second time; every primary fetch here passed `headers=SEC_UA`, and the default is wrong for the rung the framework uses most. (2) **There is no FDIC Call Report helper anywhere in `tools/`**, and for a bank it is the best available instrument; the recipe and the two API traps are recorded above and in `Test Runs/_research 2026-09-19 ACNB/fdic_row.py`. (3) `tools/run.py` has no construction for a bank and was not used - which is why the CONVENTION had to be written twice in one day, once by CCB and once here. (4) **The brief was clean**: it named the evidence and the priors and no expected verdict, and it did not tell any gate it would be boring. The one thing it could not anticipate is that the decisive competitor evidence would come from outside the SEC entirely.

## UPDATE 2026-09-19 — SOFI: THE THIRD BANK. Q2 OUT, and the moat was refuted from the CUSTOMER'S filing again

**SoFi Technologies, Inc. (SOFI), CIK 0001818874, WAVE 6**, run under the operator ruling of
2026-09-19 that the five banks are run. **FAIL at Q2, OUT on the business.** Q1 IN; Q3 and Q4
written and marked RECORDED, NOT GOVERNING; Q5 did not open and appears only as
`COMPUTATION — NOT A CLEARANCE`. Price **US$16.96** (2026-09-18 close, aggregator, flagged,
corroborated against nine SEC-filed Form 4 transaction prices of $17.28–$18.00), shares
**1,291,570,324** off the Q2 2026 10-Q cover of 2026-07-31 (accession `0001818874-26-000054`),
cap **US$21,905.0M**, sovereign **5.34%** (US Treasury 30-year, 2026-09-18, struck fresh).
`Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - SOFI SoFi Technologies.md`.

**THE HEADLINE FINDING, and it is the CCB method working a second time on the same day in a
different industry.** SoFi's Q2 2026 10-Q says *"the exit of a large client that fully
transitioned off our platform prior to December 31, 2025"* — Technology Platform accounts
**160.0m → 134.8m**, segment revenue **−23%**, contribution profit **−65%**, technology services
fees **−$76.3M** in the half. **The client names itself in its own 10-K. Chime Financial, Inc.,
accession `0001795586-26-000013`:** *"Historically, transactions have been processed by Galileo
Financial Technologies, LLC … However, **as of the end of 2025, we have transitioned our members'
transactions to being processed by ChimeCore**,"* built to *"reduce or eliminate reliance on
third-party vendors in areas such as transaction processing, financial ledgering."*
**The substitute was not a rival vendor — it was the customer, who is also SoFi's closest
competitor in digital consumer banking, with 9.5 million ACTIVE members.** And a second
counterparty priced SoFi down in writing: **Dave Inc., accession `0001193125-26-085370`** —
*"In January 2023, we executed an amended agreement with Galileo that **significantly reduced
processing fees**"* — the identical finding the CCB run made on Prosper hours earlier.
**Two banks, two days' work, and in both cases the moat was refuted from the counterparties'
filings rather than the subject's. That method is now the most productive thing this project
does on a financial.**

**WHAT IS LEFT OF THE SEGMENT IS BEING PROPPED BY INTERNAL TRANSFERS, AND THE FILER CONCEDES THE
CONSTRUCTION.** Note 17: intercompany fees inside Technology Platform were **$27,805k in Q2 2026
against $18,182k in Q2 2025**; strip them and external segment revenue fell from **$91.7M to
$56.7M, 38.1%, in one quarter.** The accounts-metric footnote says in terms: *"We **include
intercompany accounts** on the Galileo platform as a service in our total accounts metric to
better align with the Technology Platform segment revenue reported in Note 17 … **which includes
intercompany revenue.**"* **Contribution margin went 32.1% → 13.9%.**

**THE METRIC THAT CANNOT FALL — a new instance of a pattern this project keeps finding, and the
sharpest yet.** SoFi's two most-quoted numbers are defined verbatim as cumulative *"since our
inception through the reporting date, **whether or not the members are still registered for such
products**"* and *"whether or not such loans have been paid off."* **"Member growth up 35% to a
record 13.7 million members" is the first line of every earnings release, New Members carries 15%
of the annual bonus weight, and the number is arithmetically incapable of declining.** Chime, in
the same business, reports **Active** members. **[E4-55]** asks for the physical series; the only
non-cumulative segment series SoFi publishes is the one that fell 16%. *(Compare the ULTA
finding — "active" members redefined — and the BLK finding — a blended fee rate held up by
purchased mix. This is a third mechanism in the same family: not a switched metric and not a
bought average, but a metric whose DEFINITION forbids bad news.)*

**THERE IS NO DEPOSIT FRANCHISE, AND THE NUMBER IS 0.28%.** Of $45,543.2M of deposits at
2026-06-30, **$45,416.3M — 99.72% — are interest-bearing**, at an average cost of **3.40%** in
FY2025. Noninterest-bearing deposits are **$126.9M**. Against the competitor row: Pathward pays
**0.09%**, The Bancorp 2.06%, Coastal's community bank 1.56%, Capital One 3.21%, Ally 3.56%,
LendingClub *(now filing as **Happen, Inc.**)* 3.83%, Synchrony 4.10%. **SoFi's 5.85% net
interest margin is asset mix, not moat: Synchrony earns 21.1% on equity while paying a WORSE
4.10% for its money, and SoFi earns 6.27% at 3.40%.** This is **[E2-58]**'s commodity end, whose
one exception is *"a cost advantage that is both wide and sustainable"* — SoFi's is 30 basis
points better than Ally's and 331 worse than Pathward's.

### THE THREE NUMBERS THAT CHANGE HOW THE COMPANY READS

**1. Cumulative net income MINUS $265.5M. Cumulative operating cash flow MINUS $27,435.0M.
Cumulative fair-value write-up on the balance sheet PLUS $2,027.1M.**
Operating cash flow is negative in **all seven filed years**, because personal-loan originations
are classified held-for-sale and run through *operating* (−$5,270.9M in 2025, −$7,000.5M in H1
2026), funded by deposit inflow inside *financing*. **The CCB cash-flow finding inverts and
holds: Coastal's operating cash flow was 5.4× its net income and measured growth; SoFi's has no
sign at all.** And the cumulative unrealised write-up above unpaid principal — $1,153.6M at
2024-12-31, $1,937.1M at 2025-12-31, **$2,027.1M at 2026-06-30, 18.3% of equity** — **is larger
in absolute terms than the entire cumulative earnings record of the company, which is negative.**
**That is not a charge of impropriety. It is the plainest possible statement of where the
reported profit lives: on the balance sheet, as an estimate, not in the bank.**

**2. [E2-50] LANDS ON THE VALUATION NOTE, NOT ON A RESERVE TABLE — and that is the fifth
framework gap.** **$46.60bn of $47.93bn of loans are at FAIR VALUE**, $36.6bn of it Level 3 at
**3.49× book equity**; the allowance for credit losses is **$56.5M**. There is no reserve, so
there is no reserve-development table, so **[E2-67]**'s candour benchmark has no artifact to
test. The pen writes the **discount rate** instead: personal loans at 2026-06-30 carry a coupon
of 12.89%, an assumed annual default rate of 4.77%, a 25.77% prepayment rate and a **discount
rate of 4.97% — 37 basis points BELOW the 30-year Treasury**. At 2025-12-31 it was **4.5%**, down
from 5.3%, i.e. **84 basis points below the sovereign**, and the reduction was itself a source of
income. **And the exit price is being estimated in a channel the company has not transacted in:
personal-loan whole-loan cash sales were $0 in H1 2026 against $1,313.3M in H1 2025, and no
securitization transfer qualified for sale accounting in FY2025 or either half-year** other than
Loan Platform Business ones.

**3. THE (c) CONVENTION PASSED A SECOND INDEPENDENT TEST, AND THE EQUITY ACCOUNT CONFIRMS IT BY A
DIFFERENT ROUTE.** CCB's convention — **(c) = Δassets × the Tier 1 leverage ratio** — applied
unchanged: **$7,096.4M of capital required against $358.8M earned, 2022–2025, a $6,737.6M
shortfall**; four-year mean "owner earnings" **−$1,684.4M**, three-year **−$1,424.6M**.
**Independently: equity rose $6,698.9M between 2021-12-31 and 2026-06-30 on cumulative net income
of $682.2M, so $6,016.7M — 89.8% — came from selling shares.** A convention that reproduces
itself from the equity account on two very different banks is worth adopting. *(One refinement:
for a consumer lender risk-weighted assets bind before total assets, and the RWA cross-check —
ΔRWA × the Tier 1 risk-based ratio — gave the same answer to within 1% on FY2025. Either
denominator works; the run should state which.)* **[E2-01]'s primary test: 6.85% pre-tax on
average equity capital in the best year the company has ever had**, and below the 5.34% sovereign
in five of the six periods.

### Q3 AT GATE WEIGHT, AND THE CONTRASTS WITH CCB AND ACNB ARE INSTRUCTIVE

**[E4-29] fires here as hard as it has fired anywhere in this project, and it is a BANK.**
Adjusted EBITDA of **$1,053.9M against net income of $481.3M**, adding back **$234.2M of
depreciation and amortization** and **$262.1M of share-based expense** — the two things the

**[E4-35] in its purest published form.** From the Q4 2025 release: *"Over the medium term,

**[E3-48] WAS RUN AND IT FAVOURS MANAGEMENT, and this is recorded in full because the rule

**THE INCENTIVE READ [E4-27] IS THE SHARPEST Q3 FINDING AFTER [E4-29], AND IT IS A THREE-BANK

**[E3-02] CONFORMITY FIRES, WHERE COASTAL PASSED AND ACNB PASSED ON EVERYTHING BUT M&A.** In the

took on digital-asset custody obligations for eight-tenths of one per cent on the gross.

**WEAK ACCOUNTING FIRES ON A GOODWILL TEST, AND IT IS CHECKABLE ON ANY FILER.** **$1,364.5M of

4%); the annual test at 2025-10-01 was **qualitative**, and so was the **Q2 2026 test**, taken

profit. The same unit was impaired by **$247.174M in 2023** for the same kind of reason, and the
