### THE STRESS, AND THE HONEST ANSWER IS THAT IT SURVIVES EVERYTHING

**[E3-24] run three ways on the loans SoFi owns the risk of.** 10% of loans at 30% severity:
**$1,438.0M on the whole $47.9bn book** — a $630M pre-tax loss against its best run-rate, 10.1%
of equity after tax; **$783.1M on personal loans alone, at which the company ROUGHLY BREAKS
EVEN — the exact 1990 Wells Fargo result on the corpus's own parameters.** Pushed to 20% at 50%
on the personal book: $2,610.2M, 18.4% of equity. **Reversing the ENTIRE $2,027.1M cumulative
fair-value write-up costs 14.3% of equity; the filer's own +200bp shock costs $1,563.4M, 14.9%;
the two together 19.8%.** **At a $4bn pre-tax loss — five times its best annual earnings — Tier 1
risk-based capital is still 12.31% and Tier 1 leverage 10.84%.** **IT DOES NOT DIE OF CREDIT OR
OF MARKS, and the $3.19bn of equity raised in 2025 is exactly why.**

**Staying power scores 3 of 3, where Coastal scored 2 of 3, and the difference is a single
number: uninsured deposits.** Coastal's went from 15.5% to 27.7% in six months; **SoFi's are
about 3% — the filer states *"approximately 97% of our total deposits were insured"*** — through
a reciprocal Insured Deposit Program giving up to $3 million of coverage. Add **no unrealised
AFS loss** (amortized cost $3,993.3M against fair value $3,993.3M — the thing that killed three
banks in 2023), $3.1bn of cash, Tier 1 leverage 16.5% holdco and 13.3% bank. **The balance sheet
is the strongest fact against this run's verdict and it is stated as such.** The one near-term
item is **$428.0M of 2026 convertible notes maturing 2026-10-15**, trivially covered.

**SO WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS, AND IT IS A NEW SHAPE.** The business earns **6.85% pre-tax on equity
capital** while growth requires equity equal to **15–19% of every new dollar of assets**, so
growth cannot be funded from earnings and is bought from new shareholders — **89.8% of the equity
added since 2021.** Meanwhile the reported profit that makes the shares saleable is, to the
extent of **$2,027M**, an unrealised write-up on assets the company keeps and funds, with
cumulative operating cash flow of **minus $27.4 billion**. **The company does not fail; the
per-share claim stops compounding.** On the company's own guided 30% asset growth, holding Tier 1
leverage requires roughly **$3.0bn of new capital a year against $0.65–0.80bn of earnings — about
130 million shares a year at $16.96, ten per cent of the company, annually.**

**NEW SURVIVAL SHAPE PROPOSED: THE MARKED BOOK** — *earnings recognised at origination as an
unrealised write-up on an asset the lender keeps rather than sells, so the reported profit is a
valuation and not a receipt; the cash never arrives, because the asset is retained and funded
with deposits; growth consumes regulatory capital ten to twenty times faster than the valuation
earns it; and the gap is closed by issuing shares while the reported growth holds. The company
survives very large credit and rate shocks — the equity raised to grow is also the equity that
absorbs them — but the owner funds the growth twice, once in the dilution and once in the return
foregone.* Distinct from **#8 THE EQUITY IS THE REVENUE** (there the customers do not pay; here
they pay all of it and the company is GAAP-profitable), from **#2** (there the employees take the
operating cash; here the cash never exists), from **#11 THE PASS-THROUGH** (there the gain goes
to customers or suppliers; here *the gain is an estimate that has not yet been collected from
anyone*), from **#24 THE BOUGHT AVERAGE** (there a falling unit price is concealed by purchased
mix; here the unit price is fine and the *cash conversion* is absent) and from **#25 THE
INDEMNITY** (there the loss is contracted away to a counterparty and booked as income; here
there is no counterparty at all — the loss is retained and the *income* is the lender's own
discount rate). **Tells checkable on any filer: cumulative operating cash flow far more negative
than cumulative net income with the gap in one held-for-sale line; a cumulative fair-value
write-up larger than cumulative earnings; asset growth times the regulatory capital ratio
exceeding net income for several consecutive years; and equity growth exceeding retained earnings
by an order of magnitude.** **#2 and #11 are carried as features so the index stays honest if the
proposal is refused.**

### WHY IT FAILED ON PRICE TOO, AND WHERE IT DIFFERS FROM EVERY BANK BEFORE IT

**SOFI IS BELOW THE BOND ON EVERY CONSTRUCTION.** CCB and ACNB both landed *above the bond,
below the floor* — the Berkshire configuration named in the operator protocol. **SoFi does not.**
Honest pre-tax expectancy at $16.96: **3.69%** on the annualised H1 2026 run-rate (the most
favourable honest figure in the file), **2.40%** on FY2025, **0.16%** on the four-year mean,
**minus 7.69%** retention-adjusted — and **even the company's own Adjusted EBITDA yields 4.81%
against a 5.34% sovereign.** **To reach the ~10% floor from the current run-rate needs 39.5% a
year for three years, which is almost exactly the company's own published 38–42% target: at this
price the buyer is paid nothing for three years even if management delivers it.** P/B 1.98×,
P/TB 2.32×, 28.3× the company's own guided 2026 adjusted EPS of about 60 cents.

**THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT [E4-26, E4-51].** *SoFi is the only digital-first
consumer bank in the United States to have reached scale, profitability and a national charter
at once. It gathered $45.5bn of deposits in four and a half years at a cost below Ally's, 97% of
them insured, with no unrealised securities loss; it raised $3.19bn above three times book and
retired converts with high-priced shares; it now runs more capital than any peer in the row, so
the next several years of growth can be funded more cheaply than the last. It has been profitable
for eight quarters, beaten raised guidance, published pre-set targets and cut its own payout,
reports effective ICFR with a Big Four attestation, has no consent order in five annual reports,
and discloses Level 3 assumptions quarter by quarter beside realised charge-offs — more than most
banks do about their reserves. Its realised personal-loan charge-off rate of **2.62% is 215 basis
points BELOW its own assumed 4.77%**, so the marks may be conservative. And the $575.9M
third-party origination fee business converts the same customer acquisition into capital-free
revenue, which is the answer to the capital problem.* **That case is not wrong about the capital,
the liquidity, the deposit insurance or the disclosure. It is wrong about "only": Chime has 9.5m
active members with no charter and built SoFi's own technology in-house; Synchrony earns 21.1% on
equity paying more for its money. Scale reached is not scale defended, and 6.85% pre-tax on
equity is the number that says which one this is.**

**NOTHING ARMED, no `PORTFOLIO.md` row** — the QLYS ruling: a name that failed on the **business**
gets a reversal condition in words. The breaker is pre-committed and in the run file:
**noninterest-bearing deposits rising from 0.28% to above 10% of total deposits WHILE the cost of
interest-bearing deposits falls more than 100 basis points below Ally's in the same year** —
i.e. the "primary banking relationship" claim finally showing up in the funding cost the way it
does at Pathward and at Coastal's community bank. Both numbers are in the average-balance table
of every 10-K.

**FOUND AND FIXED: `tools/sources.py:fts_count()` returned a well-formed ZERO for every query
that passed `forms` as a Python list.** That is the **identical silent-false-negative class** the
function's own docstring was written to prevent in the parameter beside it (the CALX defect of
2026-09-12), and it could defeat that guard. Measured on `"Calix"` before the fix:
`forms=['10-K']` → **0 hits**; `forms='10-K'` → **306**; `forms='10-K,10-Q'` → **622**; and
`cik='0000926282', forms=['10-K']` → **0**, where the no-forms call returns 40. The list
urlencodes to `forms=%5B%2710-K%27%5D` — a Python repr — and EDGAR answers **HTTP 200 with an
empty body and no warning.** **This run reported "0 hits in 10-Ks" for `"SoFi"`, `"SoFi
Technologies"`, `"Galileo Financial Technologies"` and `"SoFi Bank"` — four false negatives on
the question the framework treats as evidence, because a moat is a relative claim** — and caught

**Fixed: a list, tuple or set is coerced to the comma-joined string the endpoint expects; a bad
FORM NAME still fails loudly with HTTP 500.** Verified after the fix at 306, 622 and **20**, the
last matching the figure the docstring records as correct. **This is the fifth consecutive
session whose defect was a guard that read one side of its own input** (`level_shift` four times,
the `cik` half of `fts_count` once, and now the `forms` half of the same function). **The rule
worth naming: when a guard is added to one parameter, test the parameters beside it.**

**CONFIRMED A THIRD TIME TODAY: `tools/sources.py:_get()` still defaults to `WEB_UA` =

**(d) ONE COLUMN IN THE FDIC ROW IS A TRAP AND IT IS FLAGGED, because the row is now a standing

therefore measures only the $1.28bn at amortized cost. The real figure is in the MD&A — a

**$359.9M of delinquent-loan sales in 2025.** **A reader ranking the row on that column would
conclude SoFi runs the cleanest consumer book in America; it is the accounting election, not the

**AND A NEW FRAMEWORK GAP, THE SHARPEST OF THE SIX: THERE IS NO RULE FOR A BANK HELD INSIDE A
HOLDING COMPANY THAT ALSO OWNS SOMETHING ELSE.** **[E2-56]** says judge segment by segment;
**[E2-43]** says pick the denominator by the question. **Neither says whether a bank holding
company is judged on the BANK's return on the bank's equity or the GROUP's return on the
shareholder's, and at SoFi those are 15.41% and 6.27% — more than two to one.** Both are right and
they answer different questions. **Candidate rule, offered and not adopted: report BOTH, name the
capital sitting outside the bank in dollars and as a percentage of consolidated equity, and let
the difference be the finding. SoFi's is $3,798,271k, 34.3%.** It would have changed nothing at
Coastal or ACNB, whose holding companies are essentially their banks. **It will bite hard on JPM
and TFC.** **And the fixable half of gap 2 is now concrete: the missing ladder rung has an address
— `banks.data.fdic.gov/api` — ACNB built the harness, this run reused it in twenty minutes, and it
belongs in `tools/`.** The OCC and Federal Reserve **enforcement** registers remain unpulled on all
three banks.

## JPM (JPMorgan Chase & Co.) - RUN 2026-09-19. ALL FOUR BUSINESS GATES IN; FAIL AT Q5 ON PRICE.
*The narrative fold. The register entry with the price, the share count, the cap, the sovereign and the
PASS/FAIL line is in `Screens/WATCHLIST RUN QUEUE.md`, entry 130. Run file:
`Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - JPM JPMorgan Chase.md`.*

**THE FOURTH BANK THIS PROJECT HAS RUN, the SECOND to clear the business gates, and the largest company it
has ever priced** ($929,488M). WAVE 6, under the operator ruling of 2026-09-19 that the five banks are run.

**THE FINDINGS, in the order they mattered.**

**1. The first thing the run tested about the franchise, it refuted.** A bank's franchise is the price of
its money, and ACNB - the only bank to have passed Q2 before this run - passed on exactly that: a cost of
funds 64 basis points below the median of its own 56-bank market over five years. **JPMorganChase FAILS
that test. On one uniform specification across all six holding companies, from their own tagged annual
data, it is THIRD of six on the cost of total deposits in every one of five years** (five-year means:
Wells Fargo 0.927%, Bank of America 1.066%, **JPMorgan 1.202%**, Morgan Stanley 1.699%, Citigroup 1.902%,
Goldman Sachs 2.958%). The FDIC Call Reports confirm it independently at six dates: JPMorgan Chase Bank NA
is third of the four universal banks on cost of funding earning assets at every date, 21bp behind Bank of
America and 42bp behind Wells Fargo at 2025-12-31, and only **23.2% of its deposits pay nothing** against
27.5% at Bank of America and 27.3% at Wells Fargo. **The largest deposit franchise in America is not the
cheapest one.**

**2. So where the pass came from is a DIFFERENT form of [E2-58]'s single exception, and naming which form
is the general result.** *"a cost advantage that is both wide and sustainable … By definition such
exceptions are few."* JPMorgan's is on the **expense line**: a 52% overhead ratio against Bank of
America's 61.65%, Citigroup's 64.7% and Wells Fargo's 66%; five-year means 55.40 / 64.66 / 67.52 / 69.20;
**a 9.65-point gap on a $182,447M revenue base, about $17.6 billion a year of pre-tax income, and
WIDENING** (JPMorgan 59 to 52 while Bank of America went 67.03 to 61.65). Five-year mean ROTCE **20.80%,
first of six in four of five years**, with a worst year (18%) above every peer's best year but Morgan
Stanley's. **After four banks the usable rule is: [E3-03] criterion 2 is passable for a bank ONLY through
[E2-58]'s exception, and the exception has at least two independent forms - the price of the liability
(ACNB) and the cost of the platform (JPM). A bank with neither is OUT.**

**3. [E2-59] bites on a dated, quantified event and it is the 2023 acquisition.** JPMorgan Chase Bank NA
held **11.30% of all United States domestic insured deposits at 2022-12-31** on the FDIC's own numbers, so
the ordinary interstate-merger route to a $200bn bank was closed; what opened was an FDIC receivership
auction, and Note 34 records it: *"acquired certain assets and assumed certain liabilities of First
Republic Bank … from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ('FDIC'), **as receiver**."* The
**$2,775 million after-tax bargain purchase gain was granted by the regime, not won from customers**, and
is scored that way rather than as moat evidence. The regime sent the bill too: a **$2.9 billion FDIC
special assessment** in 2023 expense.

**4. The refuted prior on deposit share, and it is the sharpest [E4-32] finding.** The run expected the
largest bank in America to be gaining share. **It is not. Domestic deposit share went 11.77% (2021), 11.30%,
11.68%, 11.44%, 11.67%, 11.65% (2026-06-30) - twelve basis points BELOW end-2021 after absorbing a
$92 billion deposit base.** Bank of America's fell 71bp over the same window, so JPMorgan won relatively;
but the franchise did not widen on the measure that matters most to it. Investment-banking fee wallet share
fell 9.1% to 8.4% and the loan-syndication rank slipped #1 to #2 globally and in the U.S.

**5. Q3 was the gate and the closest precedent on disk was AGAINST the company.**
`Framework/v4/VERIFICATION - the two cases that decide the deletions.md` rejects Citigroup at mid-2007 at
Q3 on its filed Legal Proceedings. JPMorganChase's record is long and bad in absolute terms: a **2015
GUILTY PLEA to federal antitrust**, a **2020 DOJ Deferred Prosecution Agreement** over precious-metals and
Treasuries spoofing, an EURIBOR infringement re-imposed in December 2023, a **$31.5M Indian
money-laundering fine**, the **$290M Epstein settlement**, and **NEW March 2024 OCC and Federal Reserve
consent orders over the completeness of trade-surveillance data - the SAME failure class as the 2020 DPA,
three and a half years later, which fires [E4-22]'s cockroach rule at full strength.**
**The gate was decided by an artifact the run NAMED and then WENT AND GOT from the issuing authority
rather than recalling: the Federal Reserve's own enforcement-actions file, all 2,889 actions.** Thirteen
entity actions against JPMorgan Chase & Co. since 2003, nine of them orders, **ZERO still open**, five
civil money penalties totalling **$878,932,500 - the largest of the six** - and the 2024-03-08 order
**terminated 2025-12-04, twenty-one months**. Run across the row: **Citigroup and Wells Fargo each still
have an OPEN order at the same date.** That is [E5-22]'s operative test - *"the failure that counts is they
didn't act when they learned"* - answered by the supervisor's own termination dates, and it is why this run
does not reach the Citigroup conclusion, which rested on LIVE matters. **A reader who scores $879 million
of central-bank penalties and a criminal antitrust plea as a disqualifier has a defensible reading and the
run file says so.**

**6. [E3-02] conformity, tested at the one moment in twenty years when it could be tested against a
control group that actually died.** At **2022-12-31**, before anything was public, from the FDIC Call
Reports of all seven institutions: **JPMorgan Chase Bank NA carried held-to-maturity securities at 1.40x
equity - the LOWEST of the seven - against Silicon Valley Bank's 5.91x, Bank of America's 2.81x, Wells
Fargo's 1.84x, First Republic's 1.63x and Citibank's 1.60x** - and the lowest assets-to-equity at 10.5x.
Its own filings put the HTM unrealized loss at $36,762M, **13.9% of common equity**; the same mark at
Silicon Valley Bank was of the order of its whole equity. **It did not imitate, and the peer it most
conspicuously did not imitate is Bank of America, whose ROTCE has since run 6.2 points below it.**

**7. [E2-50] reserves, and the answer is conservative by a wide margin.** Cumulative provision 2019-2025
**$54,408M against cumulative net charge-offs of $41,302M - 31.7% MORE reserved than lost** - with the
allowance covering the following year's charge-offs at **2.72x or better in every single year** and 10.76x
in 2020. **[E2-67] is met in SUBSTANCE and NOT in form: JPMorganChase publishes no reserving back-test,
and the one in the run file was built by the reader from the published series.** The one honest criticism
is the CB run's #23 THE CUSHION applied here: the **-$9,256M provision of 2021** is 15.5% of that year's
pre-tax income and the reason 2021 shows the window's best ROTCE of 23%.

**8. The segment answer to the brief's question, and it is the named death.** On the filer's own capital
allocation: **AWM 40% on $16.0bn, CCB 32% on $56.0bn, CIB 18% on $149.5bn - and Corporate about 3.7% on
$120.9bn, 35.3% of the common equity.** The filer says why in one sentence: *"Any capital that the Firm has
accumulated in excess of these current requirements … has been retained in Corporate."* **All three
operating segments earn far above any plausible cost of their allocated capital; a third of the equity
earns a bond return because the Federal Reserve requires 11.5% of $1,981,692M of RWA and the Firm holds
$288,469M, an excess of $60,574M.** That is **PROPOSED SHAPE #27 THE LICENCE**: each additional point of
required CET1 moves $19,817M from the 18-40% businesses into the 3.7% one, about $2.9bn a year pre-tax,
and the owner has no vote. Likelihood **LIKELY**, and it runs both ways - Corporate's allocation falls to
$98.4bn on 2026-01-01.

**9. Why it failed at Q5, and the one judgment the failure rests on.** Honest pre-tax expectancy
**7.54% at the bottom boundary [E5-34], 9.62% centred, 11.06% at the top**, against a 5.34% sovereign -
**above the bond by 2.2 to 4.3 points and below the ~10% floor**, the fifth name on this track to land in
that configuration after KO, CB, GFF and ACNB. Value range **~$200 to ~$340 a share against a $349.67
quote**; 3.08x tangible book; the **Screamer test [E4-01]** returns the third outcome, narrowly - above the
whole range. **THE STRONGEST FACT AGAINST THE VERDICT: on the record the business has DELIVERED, the price
clears the floor.** Diluted EPS compounded 6.85% a year 2021-2025 and tangible book per share 10.30% a
year 2020 to mid-2026, against the 3.24% to 5.46% of perpetual growth the quote requires. **The entire Q5
failure rests on one judgment - that the 82.5% rise in net interest income from $52,311M (2021) to
$95,443M (2025), on 52.3% of the revenue, was the federal funds rate and not the business, and cannot
happen again from the same starting point.** [E4-41] requires that break to be named and removed; the run
names it. **And the board bought 8.9 million shares at $317.28 in December 2025, inside the top quarter of
this run's optimistic case: the disagreement is one year of multiple expansion, not an order of
magnitude.**

**10. The LIVE CAPITAL-ALLOCATION FLAG, which binds position size and not the discount rate [E4-13].**
**$31,640M of buybacks in 2025 at 2.57x tangible book against $9,898M at 1.65x in 2023 - three times the
dollars at 1.6 times the price** - under a programme that states it *"does not establish specific price
targets or timetables"*, the exact inverse of **[E5-25]**'s standard of publishing both conditions as
numbers in advance. **[E5-24]**'s first law inverted: *"what is smart at one price is dumb at another."*
The counter-argument is strong and is stated in full at Q3: the alternative use is Corporate at 3.7%, and
a share bought at 2.57x tangible book in a 20%-ROTCE business returns about 7.8% on the cash - better than
3.7% and better than the bond. **The run's answer is that [E5-08] asks for a material DISCOUNT, and 7.8%
on cash spent is a fair price, not a discount.**
**And [E4-27]: the CEO's entire equity award is in PSUs paying maximum at ROTCE >= 18% and zero below 6%,
and the five-year buyback programme accounts for roughly 3.8 points of the reported 20% ROTCE.** Recorded
under **[E5-38]** as a fired flag and explicitly NOT as a venality finding.

**11. Two facts that belong in any future bank run because they are unusual.** **Zero net common shares
issued in five years** - the issued count is 4,104,933,895 in all six filings read, identical to the share,
while the outstanding count fell 12.8% and the $192 billion First Republic acquisition was paid in cash and
a note. And **[E3-48] answered in the company's favour**: the 2025 outlook printed in the FY2024 10-K
guided NII to ~$94.0bn, NII ex-Markets to ~$90.0bn, adjusted expense to ~$95.0bn and the Card charge-off
rate to ~3.60%; the outturn was **$95,443M, $92,591M, $95,640M and 3.31% - guided conservatively and beaten
on three of three measurable items.** The projections flag fires on the practice ([E5-30]: a guidance
culture is a ratchet, and two of the three metrics are non-GAAP) and is answered on the record.

**12. A METRIC-SWITCHING finding the reader loses by [E2-56].** JPMorganChase went from **FOUR reportable
segments to THREE** with effect from January 2024: **Commercial Banking - which the brief asked about as a
segment with its own filed return on equity - no longer exists as a reporting unit**, folded into a
$149.5bn CIB reporting a blended 18%. The switch was announced ahead with restated comparatives and a
named management change, and did not follow deterioration, so it is [E2-49]'s candor case - **but the
separate series a reader needed is gone.**

**TOOLING DEFECTS AND BRIEF DEFECTS FOUND.**
- **`tools/sources.py:_get()` still defaults to `WEB_UA` and `www.sec.gov/Archives` answers HTTP 403 -
  the THIRD confirmation in one day** (BLK, ACNB, JPM). Every primary fetch in this run passed
  `headers=SEC_UA`. It is a one-line fix: default to `SEC_UA` for any `sec.gov` host.
- **`tools/sources.py` has no helper for the two regulator endpoints that decided two gates today.**
  ACNB and JPM both hand-rolled them. Two functions - `call_report(cert, dates)` and
  `enforcement_actions(name)` - would get the same numbers sooner without adding a step, which is the test
  CLAUDE.md sets for tooling.
- **The evidence-ladder gap CCB reported is CLOSED for two of its three rungs.** The FDIC Call Report API
  and the Federal Reserve enforcement file are both one HTTP request from the issuing authority and both
  decided gates. **RECOMMENDATION: add one rung between "SEC EDGAR primary documents" and "company IR
  site" - *the prudential regulator's own published data for the sector*.** The rung still genuinely
  missing is the **OCC** register (`apps.occ.gov` returned HTTP 404 twice) and **NCUA Form 5300**.
- **BRIEF DEFECT 1: the brief says JPM is "the third bank this project has run." It is the FOURTH** - CCB,
  ACNB and SOFI all ran 2026-09-19. The count matters because the deliverable asked whether the banks now
  run have settled the Q2 question.
- **BRIEF DEFECT 2: the brief says "two banks have already met [E3-03] criterion 2 differently." Only ONE
  had** - ACNB. CCB's Q2 was OUT and SOFI's Q2 was OUT. JPMorgan is the second.
- **BRIEF DEFECT 3: the brief says "JPM is not in the WAVE 6 table" and instructs a strike "in the
  operator-ruling sentence and the excluded subsection." Both halves are wrong: JPM IS a row in the WAVE 6
  table (unlike CCB and ACNB), and it is NOT in the excluded subsection, which names only CCB, ACNB and
  SOFI.** The fold struck the table row itself and recorded the discrepancy beside the ruling rather than
  editing it out.
- **ONE ERROR OF MY OWN, corrected in an addendum rather than by editing history (operator rule 6):** Q1
  states Level 3 ASSETS are $76,139M and 21.5% of common equity. **That is the Level 3 LIABILITIES figure;
  Level 3 ASSETS are $33,732M, 9.5% of common equity.** The Q1 sentence is left visible, the correction is
  at the head of Q4, and every subsequent calculation uses the corrected figures.

## OTTR (Otter Tail Corporation) - run 2026-09-19 - Q1 IN, **Q2 OUT on the business**
*Two companies in one registrant, and the filer publishes the pounds.*
**The name was run because this project's own bookkeeping was wrong.** OTTR sat in
`## PRE-RUN, EXCLUDED FROM THE QUEUE (14)` at the head of `Screens/WATCHLIST RUN QUEUE.md`, which
asserts a run already existed. **It did not. No run file for OTTR existed anywhere on disk** -
verified at 19:44 EDT by `ls "Test Runs" | grep -i ottr` and again for `otter`, zero hits of any
date, before anything was fetched. One of fourteen names on that list was wrong; **the other
thirteen were not checked by this fold and somebody should check them.**

**Verdict line: Q1 IN / Q2 OUT / Q3 UNKNOWABLE, Q4 UNKNOWABLE, Q5 and Q6 all RECORDED, NOT
GOVERNING.** Price **US$87.42** (close 2026-09-18), **41,985,580 shares**, cap **US$3,670.4M**,
sovereign **5.34%**. Register entry **131**.

### What the run found, in order of how much it changed my mind

**1. THE COMPETITOR ROW REFUTED MY PRIOR, AND THE BRIEF'S.** The brief said the PVC pipe earnings
"exploded after 2021 and have since fallen back." **They have barely fallen back - and every other
listed participant's have collapsed completely.** Uniform GAAP consolidated operating margin,
FY2019-FY2025, each cell from that filer's own 10-K:

| | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **OTTR Plastics segment** | 15.5 | 18.4 | 34.9 | 51.6 | **60.9** | 58.7 | **54.7** |
| Westlake (WLK) | 8.1 | 5.7 | 23.8 | 19.3 | 5.8 | 7.2 | **-14.1** |
| Atkore (ATKR) - **co-defendant** | 11.7 | 13.6 | 27.3 | **31.5** | 25.4 | 19.5 | **0.8** |
| Olin (OLN) | 2.9 | -13.0 | 20.8 | 19.0 | 10.4 | 4.5 | **0.1** |
| Advanced Drainage (WMS) - **HDPE, the named substitute** | -5.7 | 17.4 | 14.9 | 23.4 | 25.5 | 22.6 | 20.3 |

**I wrote the case FOR the exception before the case against it [E4-51], and the thing that
decided it was not the litigation.** It was the filer's own unit series.

**2. THE PHYSICAL SERIES IS THE WHOLE ANSWER, AND OTTER TAIL PUBLISHES IT [E4-55].** Chaining the
volume percentages the filer states in its own MD&A every year (+1.7%, -19%, -14%, +27%, +8%),
**pounds of PVC pipe sold in 2025 are 2.8% BELOW 2020** - index **0.972** - while Plastics
operating income went from **$37,823k to $231,079k, 6.1x**. **The price per pound is 2.12x its
2020 level and that is the entire gain.** **Two disjoint chains of the filer's own disclosed
percentages agree to within 1%**: the volume chain (0.972) with the revenue index (2.059) implies
a price index of 2.119, and the independent price chain (1.821 x 1.66 x ~0.948 x 0.88 x 0.85)
gives 2.12. This is the Precision Steel lesson exactly - *"dollar revenue flattered by pricing is
how a shrinking franchise hides; the physical series is the honest one"* - **except that here the
filer hands you the honest series, which is a candor point in its favour [E2-26] and the thing
that closed the gate against it.**

**3. THE 2021 TRIGGER IS A HURRICANE, AND THE FILER SAYS SO.** The 82.1% price rise was *"largely
due to the combination of PVC resin **supply constraints** ... negatively impacted ... by
**production disruptions caused by extreme weather events in the Gulf Coast region** of the U.S."*
**[E3-51]**: the advantage lives in the wave, not the surfer. On **[E4-36]**'s four causes of
extreme success it is cause four, which is the one the corpus lists because it is not ownable.

**4. THE UNEXPLAINED RESIDUAL IS WHERE [E3-61]'s LIMIT BITES, AND THE FILINGS NAME THE
MECHANISM.** The row shows position; *"it cannot show conduct."* In the quarter to 2026-06-30
Northern Pipe Products and Vinyltech **paid $103.5 million** to settle all three US classes in
`In re: PVC Pipe Antitrust Litigation`, No. 1:24-cv-07639 (N.D. Ill.) - alleging the defendants
*"conspired to fix, raise, maintain and stabilize the price"* of PVC pipe by *"improperly
exchang[ing] confidential information through OPIS"* - **charged to the Plastics segment on the
face of the income statement, which put the quarter into a $7.6 million net loss.** A **DOJ
Antitrust Division grand jury subpoena is live** and on 2026-07-01 the DOJ moved to extend its
discovery stay to **2026-12-31**. A **British Columbia class action is unsettled**. A
**shareholder derivative demand of 2025-05-20 is unanswered**.

**THE CO-DEFENDANT'S FILING IS ON THE EVIDENCE LADDER AND IT DATES THE ALLEGED PERIOD.** Atkore's
FY2025 10-K (`0001628280-25-054049`) describes the identical case with detail Otter Tail's own note
does not use: conduct *"between **approximately 2021 and the present**"*, through *"a weekly report
called **'PVC & Pipe Weekly'** published by defendant Oil Price Information Service, LLC"*, and
**OPIS's own preliminarily-approved settlement obliges it *"to pay certain monies and to COOPERATE
WITH PLAINTIFFS."*** Atkore has **not** settled. **The alleged period begins in 2021. The Plastics
margin was 18.4% in 2020 and 34.9% in 2021.**
**I made no finding of wrongdoing and the framework forbids one: [E5-38]** (a fired flag is not a
venality finding), **[E5-22]** (penalty size is not seriousness in either direction), **[E5-17]**
(*"Charlie and I would not have spotted it"*). **The Q2 finding is about the SOURCE OF THE MARGIN,
which is the question Q2 asks**, and **both branches fail**: a market outcome every peer has
already lost, or **[E2-59]**'s administered price where *"the moat belongs to the regime"* and
*"That day is gone"* is how it ends. **There is no third branch in which this is a durable
advantage the company owns, which is why the gate closes regardless of how the litigation ends.**

**5. AND MANAGEMENT TAKES THE SAME SIDE, IN WRITING, TWICE.** FY2025 10-K Item 1: *"our earnings
growth rate has exceeded our long-term targeted growth rate **primarily due to market conditions
within the PVC pipe industry** ... we expect these industry conditions to **gradually normalize
through 2027** ... we expect earnings and cash flow generation within our Plastics segment to
**moderate from current levels**."* And the MD&A: *"We anticipate earnings from our Plastics
segment will **continue to decline through 2027**."* **Under [E3-03] that settles it: you cannot
call a franchise something whose owner tells you it will normalise.**

### The regulated half: handled by the framework's own definition, not by argument

**[E3-03] criterion 3 disqualifies a rate-regulated utility outright, and the filer's own first
sentence about itself supplies the evidence:** *"Our utility business operates as a regulated
monopoly ... **However, we are subject to extensive regulation.**"* Every dollar of the **$470.1
million** revenue requirement (MN $209.0M, ND $225.6M, SD $35.5M) was set by a commission at an
allowed **ROE of 9.48% / 10.10% / 8.75%** on an equity ratio the commission chose. **And two of the
three tariffs write the cap in as legal text: North Dakota returns 70% of earnings above a 10.20%
ROE to customers; South Dakota returns 50% above 8.75% and 100% above 9.50%.**
**[E2-44] fails on both characteristics** and the second fails by an order of magnitude: **$1,921
million of Electric capex planned for 2026-2030 against $97.6 million of segment net income in
2025 - 19.7 years of the segment's entire earnings, spent in five.** That is not a criticism of
management; it is what a regulated utility is.
**ROW B, five utility peers and fourteen jurisdictional allowed-ROE cells, from their own 10-Ks**
(AVA Alaska 11.45%, BKH Nebraska Gas 9.85%, **OTTR ND 10.10%**, NWE Colstrip 10.00%, ALE SWL&P
9.80%, AVA WA 9.80%, **ALE Minnesota Power 9.65%**, NWE MT electric 9.65%, NWE MT gas 9.60%, IDA
Idaho 9.60%, AVA ID/OR 9.4-9.6%, **OTTR MN 9.48%**, NWE Great Falls 9.20%, **OTTR SD 8.75%**):
**there is nothing to own, because the variable that sets the return is not a competitive
variable.** Otter Tail's Minnesota 9.48% is **below ALLETE's Minnesota Power at 9.65% before the
same commission**, and its South Dakota 8.75% is **the lowest cell in the table and has not been
reset since August 2019.**
**One cell of Row B is a fact about the asset class: ALLETE was taken private and its last 10-K is
FY2024** - and this project's own `PREPPED READING LIST` already lists ALE under *"taken private /
merged / renamed"*, which is independent confirmation from inside the repository.

### Q4: the arithmetic is a second, independent reason, and it is not close

**[E5-20] was applied PER HALF and the split is stated, because a single consolidated (c) would be
wrong in both directions at once:** Electric capex/D&A is **3.00x**, so the D&A end is **INVALID**
for 75.8% of the assets; the Manufacturing Platform's is **0.61x**, so **[E3-44]/[E2-41]**'s D&A
default is there the *higher* and therefore the *conservative* figure.
**The (c) judgment was built from the filer's own 2026-2030 plan BY CATEGORY**, which most filers
do not publish: Electric renewal (Renewable Generation and Storage **$645M**, which replaces the
coal fleet the MPUC ordered retired, plus Distribution **$268M** plus Other **$153M**) / 5 =
**$213.2M**, plus Manufacturing Platform **$129M** / 5 = **$25.8M**, total **$239.0M a year, 2.02x
consolidated D&A of $118.1M**. **$171.0M a year of Transmission was EXCLUDED as growth - the one
generous choice in the file, and it is disclosed in the same paragraph.**

**Owner earnings over five annual windows plus the TTM plus an escrow-adjusted TTM, three (c)
constructions, and the whole set repeated on two independent boom-normalisations - THIRTY-NINE
cells - and every single one is below the ~10% [E4-28] floor, including the cells the framework
declares INVALID for being too generous.**
- **As filed: -$163.0M to +$297.9M, i.e. -4.44% to 8.12% of the market cap. IT SPANS ZERO.**
  Strike the invalid D&A column and the legitimate band is **-4.44% to +4.54%**.
- **WITHOUT THE PLASTICS BOOM, shown separately and never silently dropped [E4-25, E4-41]**, against
  a **2017-2020 baseline of a 16.7% mean margin over four filed years untouched by it**, on two
  methods (actual revenue at the pre-boom margin; pre-boom dollars scaled by the pounds index):
  **-$71.9M to +$164.9M, and -1.96% to +0.91% with the invalid column struck.** **Strip the boom and
  treat the utility as the framework says a utility must be treated, and this company produces
  owner earnings of approximately NOTHING.**

**A READING FINDING WORTH CARRYING TO OTHER RUNS.** The Q2 2026 cash-flow statement adds back the
**$103,500k** settlement as a non-cash item, and **the $73,500k actually paid into the settlement
escrow in June 2026 appears NOWHERE as an outflow**, because the statement reconciles *"Cash, Cash
Equivalents **and Restricted Cash**"* and the escrow sits inside the ending balance (ASU 2016-18).
**A further $30.0M left in July 2026.** So filed H1 2026 operating cash of $182,711k overstates the
cash available to owners by $73.5 million. **The TTM is shown both ways and the adjusted row is the
honest one. This is not an accounting criticism - the presentation is what the standard requires -
it is a reason the framework insists on the detail lines [E3-27], and any run meeting a litigation
or regulatory escrow should check the same line.**

**SBC RESOLVES and is COMPLETE** - eighteen filed years FY2008-FY2025, **none zero**, so the
SBC-of-zero defect recorded on 2026-09-12 does not bite. **[E3-70] was checked rather than
assumed**: there are **no options** (restricted stock and performance shares only), and the fair
value of vested awards (**$3.6M restricted + $5.5M performance = $9.1M**) **equals the $9,119k
charge**, so the market-value uplift is nil. SBC is **2.36%** of operating cash and shape #2 does
not apply.

**Staying power [E5-11]: (1) PASS on the Electric half only** (six consecutive years of Electric
segment increase, $66.8M to $97.6M); **(2) PASS with the escrow deducted** (from $386.2M of cash to
roughly $248M unrestricted after both tranches); **(3) FAIL, and it is the one the corpus says
usually kills** - H1 2026 capex **$324,755k** against operating cash **$182,711k**, a **$142.0M
shortfall in six months funded by $170,000k of new long-term debt**, against a filed plan of
**$467M for 2026 and $574M for 2027** and the filer's own sentence that *"**Debt financing will be
required** in the five-year period from 2026 through 2030."* **[E5-39]**: the plan depends on the
debt markets being open for five consecutive years.
**And the run says plainly that the company does not fail: [E2-54]'s coverage test clears
comfortably at 2.14x on total capex and 3.22x on the (c) judgment**, the equity layer is **62.8% -
HIGHER than the 52.5-53.5% the commissions themselves authorise** - **$805M of $1,107M** of debt is
due beyond five years at rates at or below the sovereign, and **there have been 87 consecutive
years of dividends.**

### Q3: two flags fire hard, five findings go the company's way, and none of them promotes the name

**[E2-49] METRIC-SWITCHING FIRES WITH EXACT TIMING, and this is the sharpest Q3 finding in the
file.** The operational form of the test is to compare the headline metric across successive
filings. Counted on three consecutive 8-K EX-99.1 releases:

| release | accession | occurrences of "adjusted" |
|---|---|---|
| Q4/FY2025, Feb 2026 | 0001466593-26-000002 | **0** |
| Q1 2026, May 2026 | 0001466593-26-000049 | **0** |
| **Q2 2026, Aug 2026 - the quarter of the charge and the loss** | 0001466593-26-000068 | **18** |

**Three new non-GAAP yardsticks arrived at once** - Adjusted Net Income, Adjusted EPS, Adjusted ROE
- **plus a second parallel guidance range, and the adjusted range of $5.68-$6.08 sits $0.46 ABOVE
the pre-settlement guidance of $5.22-$5.62** while GAAP guidance was cut to $3.84-$4.24. A
shareholder reading only the adjusted number is told 2026 is a **better** year than originally
promised, in the year the company paid $103.5 million and lost money in a quarter. **The arithmetic
reconciles and the release states the $1.84 reconciling item, which is credit due - but [E2-49]'s
own carve-out is that a switch *"announced ahead with reasons"* is the candor case, and this one
arrived WITH the loss.** **[E2-57]** fires on the same event: *"you must count the runs scored
against you in all nine innings"*, and the $103.5 million is the cost of **the way the Plastics
segment earned its money**, not a flood or a fire. **And the Adjusted ROE excludes the charge from
the DENOMINATOR as well as the numerator, worth 380 basis points on the filer's own statement** -
which is what **[E2-01]**'s *"without undue leverage, accounting gimmickry"* clause is pointed at.

**FIVE FINDINGS IN THE COMPANY'S FAVOUR, and [E2-37] governs every one of them** - *"a good
managerial record is far more a function of what business boat you get into than how effectively
you row."*
1. **[E2-30]'s second behaviour DID NOT FIRE**, and it is the behaviour the corpus treats as near
   inevitable. A company whose earnings tripled on a commodity spike, holding **$386 million of
   cash, bought nothing** - goodwill flat at **$37,572k for six consecutive years** - **issued
   nothing** (+1.24% of shares in five and a half years, all employee plans), and **repurchased
   nothing**. The windfall went **68.5% into capital expenditure, 20.0% into dividends** and the
   rest onto the balance sheet. **[E3-40]'s loss of focus, the vector the corpus says worries it
   most, is absent.**
2. **[E4-29] IS CLEAN, AND THE CGNX COMPANION RULE IS WHAT MADE THE ANSWER TRUSTWORTHY.** The word
   EBITDA appears **zero times** in all three earnings releases **and zero times in the proxy**, and
   its three appearances in the 10-K are all inside the goodwill-impairment valuation methodology.
   **This is the exact inverse of Cognex: clean 10-K and clean releases.**
3. **[E3-48]'s outturn record: four consecutive years of guiding LOW and beating by 72.5%, 79.0%,
   35.8% and 11.4%.** In February 2022, having just reported $4.23 for 2021, they guided 2022 to
   **$3.78-$4.08 - below the year just finished** - and delivered **$6.78**. **The beats shrink in
   exactly the pattern a reverting commodity price predicts, which is a second independent
   confirmation of the Q2 finding: management has never been able to forecast the plastics price,
   which is what a price you do not control looks like from the inside.**
4. **The pay did not follow the windfall.** CEO non-equity incentive compensation was **$1,403,783 /
   $1,473,907 / $1,471,194** for 2023/2024/2025 - **flat, +4.8% over two years** - and total CEO pay
   is **2.5% of net income**. The **utility president is paid on Electric Platform ROE, not
   corporate ROE**, so the man running the regulated business was not paid on the PVC price:
   deliberate design, and it is right. *(The corporate officers were paid on a Corporate ROE
   inflated by the windfall, and the proxy calls 16% ROE *"utility sector leading"* - **[E4-41]** is
   the answer to that boast.)*
5. **[E3-54]'s retention test passes at $1.98 of market value per $1 retained**: $959,689k retained
   2021-2025 against a market value that went from **$1,766.8M** (41,469,879 filed shares x a $42.61
   close on 2020-12-31, split-invariantly, no splits in ten years) to **$3,670.4M**. The filer's own
   TSR table: $100 -> **$219.89** against EEI **$143.83** and Nasdaq $186.96.

**[E4-52]: I record a PRESENTATION convergence and explicitly REFUSE to call it an allocation or
financing one.** Three flags point one way - the standing 7-9% EPS growth target, the metric switch
and the except-for adjustment - all toward a smoother, higher earnings picture at the exact moment
the windfall reverses. **But the lollapalooza is a confluence acting *in favor of a particular
outcome*, and the outcome is missing: no capital was raised on the flattered number and nothing was
bought with it.** That distinction is the whole read, and drawing it is the difference between
reading the flags and scoring them.

**[E2-01] ROE on average equity, 2019-2025: 11.5 / 11.6 / 19.0 / 25.7 / 22.1 / 19.4 / 15.6.** The
pre-boom level is **11.5%** and the decay is three years old. **[E2-43]'s denominator adjustment is
immaterial and that is itself the finding**: goodwill plus intangibles are **$42.2M, 2.3% of
equity**, because **there were no acquisitions** - book equity is very nearly tangible equity.

**[E2-56]'s Pro-Am question, answered segment by segment as the row requires:** the cash from a
**123.9%** pre-tax-on-assets business is being invested in a **4.3%** business, and what the
retention buys is the allowed ROE - **8.75%, 9.48% and 10.10%, every one below [E5-40]'s ~12%
"quite satisfactory" mark for retained utility capital.** **Stated with [E4-13]'s humility clause,
and the finding is about the STRUCTURE, not the people:** this company generates cash in a business
that cannot use it (Plastics takes $8M of capex a year, and adding capacity is what compressed its
own price) and must deploy it in a business that earns 9-10% by law. **There is nowhere better
inside the company to put it, and buying something outside the circle is the behaviour [E2-30](2)
warns against.** It binds position size and nothing else.

**One [E2-26] failure named, and it was found by building Row B rather than by looking for it:**
**NorthWestern publishes `Authorized Rate Base` AND `Year-end Estimated Rate Base` in dollars for
every jurisdiction** ($3,176.2M against $3,425.6M for Montana electric alone), so its shareholders
can compute the regulatory lag. **Otter Tail publishes the allowed *percentage* return on rate base
and the revenue requirement, and no rate base at all.** For a company whose entire stated growth
strategy is *"rate base investments"*, that is the one number a half-owner would most want.

**Found by listing amended filings, which is not in the standard sweep and should be:** a **Form
10-K/A, Amendment No. 1, `0001466593-26-000015`, filed 2026-02-23**, five days after the original,
whose *"sole purpose"* is *"correcting the date of the Report of Independent Registered Public
Accounting Firm ... **from February 19, 2025 to February 18, 2026**."* **The FY2025 annual report as
originally filed carried the PRIOR YEAR's date on Deloitte's report.** Scored against **[E2-69]**'s
direction rule - self-found, corrected in five days, reason stated exactly, fresh certifications
filed, nothing else touched - **it is the smallest possible control lapse in the candid direction
and it does not fire [E4-22]'s first flag. I went looking for a second cockroach and found none.**

**[E4-30]'s cash-tax tell read and explained rather than scored:** cash tax as a share of reported
pretax income **ROSE** through the windfall (4.0% in 2021 to **15.7%** in 2024), which is the
**opposite** of the direction that fires the flag, and the **3.4%** in 2025 is **`Energy Related Tax
Credits` of -$29,773k, -9.2 percentage points**, itemised on the filed rate reconciliation, plus a
$33,187k deferred charge. **And the earnings series is the least smooth in this week's folds**:
$95.9M -> $176.8M -> $284.2M -> $294.2M -> $301.7M -> $275.9M, then a **$7.6M quarterly loss**.

### The death: PROPOSED SHAPE #27 THE CONVERTED WINDFALL

**The company does not die. The owner's return dies.** A temporary excess return in a small
unregulated leg, caused by an exogenous supply shock the company did not create and does not
control, is being converted **dollar for dollar into permanent regulated rate base earning
8.75-10.10% by law**. The company gets larger, safer and more predictable with every dollar of the
conversion; the reported earnings then revert toward the regulated level on the company's own
published schedule; and the owner who capitalised the windfall earnings owns a utility. **Nothing
fails, no covenant breaks, no dividend is cut - the windfall is simply gone, and irreversibly,
because the money is in the ground in Minnesota and the return on it is set by a commissioner.**
**Argued explicitly against the existing shapes:** **#10 THE CAMOUFLAGE** is the closest miss and
does not fit, because camouflage requires cash recycled into legs that *"must re-win a race each
cycle"* and **the Electric segment re-wins no race** - it is not a bad business eating the good
one's cash, it is a **capped** business eating it; **#11 THE PASS-THROUGH** is present as a feature
of the plastics leg only (price -15% against input cost -14% in 2025, new capacity arriving in the
same year the price fell); **#5** does not fit (the dividend is 20% of operating cash, covered
4.8x); **#20 THE WAVE** does not fit (that is one customer's capacity cycle; this was an
economy-wide supply shock and Otter Tail's volume **fell**).
**Quantified from filed figures [E3-24]:** full reversion of Plastics operating income from
**$231,079k** to the pre-boom margin on 2025 revenue (**$70,598k**) is **-$160,481k pre-tax**,
**-$118,690k after tax** at the segment's own filed **26.0%** rate, **-$2.82 per share**, taking
FY2025 diluted EPS from **$6.55 to $3.73**. **Cross-checked against management's own forecast: that
$3.73 sits BELOW the company's 2026 GAAP guidance midpoint of $4.04**, so the reversion is not
complete even on their arithmetic. **Likelihood: LIKELY** - four years in progress on the filer's
own price series (-5%, -12%, -15%), completed already by every listed peer, and stated in the
annual report. **Tells checkable on any filer:** a segment under 10% of assets and over half of
segment income; that segment's capex a fraction of its depreciation while another's is a multiple of
its own; the filer's own price-per-unit disclosure showing the gain is all price while units are
flat or down; a five-year capital plan in the capped segment worth more than a decade of its
earnings; and an allowed return below [E5-40]'s ~12%.

### Q5, below the gate, and the double failure is the sharpest number in the file

**Honest pre-tax expectancy 4.54% at the most favourable legitimate cell, 3.43% at the [E2-42]
default five-year window, 0.91% ex-boom - BELOW the ~10% [E4-28] floor AND BELOW the 5.34%
sovereign, at MINUS 0.80 to MINUS 4.43 points over the bond.** **The only cell in thirty-nine that
clears the bond is the D&A construction the governing framework declares INVALID for a utility.**
**That double failure is rarer than a floor failure** - most names that fail [E4-28] at least clear
the sovereign - and it is **the inverse of the Berkshire case `CLAUDE.md` names (above the bond,
below the floor): OTTR is below both.**
The price needs owner earnings **2.20x larger** than the best legitimate measurement of them, i.e.
**5.46% perpetual growth at a 10% discount rate**, from a company whose 61%-of-earnings engine
management says is normalising and whose 75.8%-of-assets engine is capped by statute. **[E2-63]'s
ceiling here is not an estimate, it is legal text**: two of three tariffs return 70% and 100% of
earnings above a stated ROE to customers. Value **roughly $20-$40 a share against the floor, $35-$75
against the bare sovereign**; the price of **$87.42** is above the top of both. **SCREAMER TEST
[E4-01]**, third outcome, *above the whole range*, **with no margin subtracted to get there** and a
**windage count of ONE** (the boom normalisation, shown beside the unadjusted figures so a reader
can refuse it), plus the one generous choice disclosed. **Dividend yield 2.64% against a 5.34%
sovereign: the dividend yields 2.70 points LESS than a thirty-year Treasury.**

### Defects found, and one of them is in this project's own machinery

1. **THE PRE-RUN EXCLUSION LIST WAS WRONG** (above). One of fourteen checked, one wrong. The other
   thirteen are unverified by this fold.
2. **A SCREEN DEFECT, REPRODUCED - THE BA/INTC/ACMR/ALKT/ACVA CLASS IN A NEW VARIANT.**
   `Screens/2026-09-02 MASTER RUN QUEUE (corrected).csv` advertises OTTR at **"$94M to $298M"**.
   Both ends reproduce to within 0.5% **and BOTH COME FROM THE SAME THREE-YEAR WINDOW**, one at each
   (c) end (3y capex **$94,321k**; 3y D&A **$297,877k**). **So the advertised spread is neither a
   capex band across windows nor a window difference: it is a single window priced two ways** - and
   the run's own **[E5-20]** finding is that **the top end is INVALID for this filer**, so the band's
   upper bound is not a legitimate number at all. **The screen's bottom of $94M is $257M ABOVE the
   rebuilt bottom of -$163.0M**, because the three-year window excludes FY2020's **$371,553k** capex
   year and the TTM's **$488,584k**. **The previous five instances of this defect class were
   different-window and different-(c)-end combinations; this is the first where both ends share a
   window, and it is the most misleading form, because a reader sees a wide band and infers the
   capex judgment has been bounded when it has not been touched.**
3. **A SECOND BOOKKEEPING FINDING: OTTR NEVER PASSED THROUGH THIS FILE'S OWN `EXCL_REGULATED`
   BUCKET**, whose stated ground is *"**[E3-03]** criterion 3: a rate-regulated utility is not a
   franchise by definition"* and which excluded twelve names. OTTR arrived on the separate
   **SP400-600 mechanical screen** track (`Screens/2026-07-16 SP400-600 Mechanical Screen - full
   results.csv`, where it is labelled *Utilities / Electric Utilities*). **That is how a SIC-4911
   registrant reached a run queue that already had a rule excluding its larger half.** The run was
   still worth doing - the interesting half was the unregulated one - but the two tracks should
   agree, and a hybrid registrant needs the bucket applied **per segment**, which no screen does.
4. **`sources.py:price()` returns the latest close only** and has no dated-quote signature, so the
   2020-12-31 close needed for **[E3-54]** had to be pulled through `sources._chart('OTTR','10y')`
   and read out of the timestamp series by hand. It worked, and the split events came with it (none
   in ten years, which is what the split-invariance rule needs), **but a `price(ticker, iso_date)`
   would remove a hand step from every retention test.** Recorded as friction, not as a defect.
5. **`sources.py:_get()` defaults to a Mozilla user agent and `sec.gov/Archives` answers 403** -
   the brief warned, `headers=SEC_UA` fixed it, and it is confirmed again here.
6. **Bash heredocs with apostrophes fail** - the brief warned, it happened once on the Q2 append,

### The strongest single fact AGAINST this run's conclusion

**In 2021 Otter Tail raised the price per pound of PVC pipe by 82.1% and the pounds it sold went
UP 1.7%.** On **[E4-37]**'s inverse metric that is the yawn end of the scale - no prayer session,
no agony - and it is the single most franchise-like fact in the file. A reader who wanted to argue
for this business would start there, add the genuine end-market distinction (municipal water
funded by public infrastructure budgets, against Atkore's non-residential electrical construction
and Westlake's housing), and note that the 2024-25 volume recovery of +27% and +8% is real. **The
answer is that the same metric has already detected the downgrade in real time, which is its
stated Q6 use: by 2024-25 the same business is taking -12% and -15% on price and cannot stop it,
and the pounds are still below where they were in 2020.**


## UPDATE 2026-09-19 - TFC: THE FIFTH BANK. Q2 OUT, and the regulator's own data says it harder than the filings do

`Test Runs/2026-09-19 Run - TFC Truist Financial.md` (2,018 lines). **Q1 IN; Q2 OUT on the business,
file closed; Q3 recorded OUT at gate weight on [E3-29] and NOT on integrity; Q4 recorded IN on
survival; Q5 did not open and appears only as `COMPUTATION - NOT A CLEARANCE`, where it fails the
~10% [E4-28] floor and the 5.34% sovereign at the conservative end; Q6 recorded as the reversal
record.** Price US$48.56 (2026-09-18), 1,221,626,188 shares, cap US$59,322.2M. **Register entry 132.
Nothing armed, no PORTFOLIO row.**

### The finding that decided it, and it came from the FDIC rather than from EDGAR

The ACNB run of the same morning left a standing ruling for the banks still queued: *"the competitor
row for a bank should be built from the FDIC Call Report FIRST."* For ACNB that ruling existed
because 56 insured institutions compete in its nine counties and most are private or mutual, so the
Call Report was the only instrument that could see the row at all. **For a $556 billion bank with
1,927 branches in fourteen states the ruling does something different, and it turned out to be worth
more: every real competitor is an SEC registrant, so what the Call Report adds is a SECOND, uniform,
independent measurement on definitions no filer can choose.**

Two rows were built, nine banks and five years each — PNC, US Bancorp, Fifth Third, KeyCorp,
Regions, Citizens, and M&T and Huntington added because they are the same size class and the same
business and their exclusion would leave the row without the two banks that grew.

**Row A**, computed by this session on one specification from each filer's tagged annual statement
values and **validated against the subject's own filed figure** — this run's 2025 ROTCE of 12.28%
against Truist's published 12.7%, the gap being exactly the $290M of intangible amortisation and the
$416M deferred-tax adjustment Truist adds — put Truist **8th of 9** on the five-year mean return on
tangible common equity (11.43%, or 11.50% on the as-filed correction) and **8th of 9** on net income
available to common over average assets (0.745%).

**Row B, the FDIC Call Report, put it last.** On the regulator's own uniform definitions, **Truist
Bank (CERT 9846) has the WORST 2021-2025 mean pre-tax return on assets of the nine largest regional
banks in the United States — 0.991% against Regions Bank's 1.875% — and the WORST mean return on
equity, 7.03% against 13.86%.** It funds itself at the **4th cheapest** cost of the nine (1.341%),
runs the **5th best** net interest margin (3.113%), and carries mid-pack leverage (13.3× tangible
common equity). **The inputs are average. The output is last.** That is the whole Q2 verdict in three
lines, and it is not a judgment — it is the regulator's arithmetic.

### What the filings added on top

**[E3-03] criterion 2 fails on Truist's own words**, in Item 1: *"The financial services industry is
intensely competitive … **Many of our competitors have substantial positions nationally or in the
markets in which we operate. Some also have greater scale, financial and operational resources** …
Competition affects every aspect of our business, including product and service offerings, rates,
pricing and fees … **We expect that competition will only intensify in the future.**"* And on its own
market-share table: **number-one deposit share in exactly ONE of fourteen states (Georgia, 21% of
deposits) and FOURTH in Florida, its largest market at 22%.**

**[E2-58]'s single exception — a cost advantage "both wide and sustainable" — fails**, because
Truist is mid-pack on the cost of money on both rows. **[E4-55]'s physical series confirms the
direction:** branches **2,781 → 1,927** (−30.7%), noninterest-bearing deposits **$145,892M →
$105,092M** (−28.0%), the free-deposit share **35.0% → 26.2%**, total deposits still below the 2021
peak — in the five fastest-growing states in America across a period when nominal GDP grew about a
quarter. **Qualified honestly, because the analyst's incentive runs the other way [E4-26]: deposit
shrinkage 2021-2025 is industry-wide among the regionals that did not buy a bank** (PNC −3.6%,
KeyCorp −2.5%, Regions −5.7%, Fifth Third +1.5%), while the three that bought one grew. **That is an
industry fact, not a Truist fact, and the run records it as such.**

### The perimeter, and the answer to "how many clean years exist"

`sources.py:name_change_note('0000092230')` flagged it before a filing was opened: *"was 'BB&T CORP'
until 2019-12-06 … CHECK THAT MULTI-YEAR FIGURES ARE ONE COMPANY [NEGG, 2026-09-13]."* **Twelve
perimeter events are established with dates, and ONE clean year exists.** The merger (2019-12-06);

2022**, freezing a $3.7bn discount in AOCI so the marks would stop appearing; 20% of Truist Insurance
Holdings sold for $1.9bn and the student-loan book sold (2023); **$6,078M of goodwill impaired in Q4

### THE PERIMETER EVENT THE BRIEF DID NOT KNOW, AND IT IS TWO OF THEM

### Q3: the yardstick that was dropped, and the counterweight that was kept

**[E2-49] fires twice and one instance is the cleanest this project has found.** The FY2020 10-K:

by the fourth quarter of 2022**."* The FY2021 10-K reaffirms it again. **The FY2022 10-K contains

**[E2-57], the "except for" flag, fires at full strength inside the pay formula.** Annex A of the

**[E3-48]'s action performed from the filings.** The January 2025 guide for FY2025 was adjusted

Three of four **[E2-30]** institutional-imperative behaviours fire, including a disclosed **$30
million professional fee *"to develop an ongoing program to identify, prioritize, and roadmap …
revenue growth and expense savings opportunities beyond the Merger"*** — **[E3-58]**'s consultant

**THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS GIVEN EQUAL PROMINENCE, because [E4-26] requires the disconfirming evidence

Threshold"**, final payment **"No awards earned"**, and realised pay **60% of target** for 2022-2025.
**That is [E2-49]'s positive condition met: a pre-set, long-lived, small bullseye kept while it read

### The insurance sale: a good sale, and the run says so without qualification

**Received:** $1.9bn for 20% (2023-04-03) and **~$10.1 billion of after-tax cash** for the rest
(2024-05-06) at a **$15.5 billion implied enterprise value**, on a business earning **$580M pre-tax
on $3,372M of insurance income in 2023** with almost no balance sheet. **That is 21 to 27 times
earnings for a capital-light fee business that had been held inside a bank trading at 7 to 13 times.
It is the single best capital-allocation decision in the file.**

**Spent:** **$27.7 billion of AFS securities sold at a $6,651M pre-tax / $5.1bn after-tax loss**,
reinvested from a 2.80% book yield into 5.27%. **And the honest reading cuts against the obvious
criticism, so the run gives it first [E4-51]: the repositioning did NOT destroy tangible book value,
because the loss was already in AOCI** — the 2024 comprehensive-income statement shows **+$4,205M of
after-tax "net change in AFS securities"**, the same loss travelling out of AOCI as it travelled into
retained earnings — **and the tax benefit was real cash.** Reinvesting adds roughly **$680M a year**
of pre-tax interest income. **Any reading that calls it "$5 billion destroyed" is wrong.**

**What survives is that the repositioning was the REMEDY and the disease was the decision that
created it.** The securities book was doubled in the two years of the lowest rates in American
history and then $59.4bn of it was moved into held-to-maturity so the marks would stop appearing.
**$46.4 billion of HTM still carries a $38.1 billion fair value at 2026-06-30 — an $8.2 billion
unrecognised loss, 14.0% of common equity and 20.3% of tangible common equity, which no
repositioning has touched.** And the 2026-09-15 slide says the pattern repeats: the RAC sale *"Creates
$945MM or 22 bps of CET1 capital"*, the plan is to **"Reposition certain AFS securities to fully
offset capital created from RAC sale"**, and the 2026 buyback target is *"unchanged at $5B."*

### [E3-02] gives a hard number, because two of the nine did not do it

HTM unrecognised loss as a share of common equity at 2025-12-31, each figure from the filer's own
securities note or tagged data: **US Bancorp 15.6%, TRUIST 13.4%, Huntington 7.5%, PNC 3.5%, Citizens
3.2%, M&T 2.7%, KeyCorp 1.7%, Regions 0.1%, Fifth Third a small GAIN.** **Truist is second worst of
nine — and Regions, which has essentially none of the problem, earns the best return in the whole
row (1.875% pre-tax on assets against Truist's 0.991%).** That is the tightest link between Q2's
return finding and Q3's conformity finding, and it is the line **[E3-02]** predicts: *"the tendency
of executives to mindlessly imitate the behavior of their peers, no matter how foolish it may be to
do so."* **The JPM run of the same evening found the other end of the same distribution — JPMorgan's
HTM at 1.40× equity at 2022-12-31, the lowest of seven — so the two runs answer each other, and the
finding is recorded in both folds: among American banks in 2020-2022 the securities decision
separates the returns.**

### Q4: it survives, and the run says so without hedging

Three **[E5-11]** strengths met. CET1 **10.9%** against a **7.0%** requirement (4.5% plus a **2.5%
stress capital buffer, which is the regulatory FLOOR** — the 2025 supervisory test produced a decline
of no more than 2.5% of risk-weighted assets, and the FRB extended the next SCB to 2027-10-01).
**$207.7 billion of selected liquidity sources** against $177.6bn of uninsured deposits. **CRE
measured against the interagency guidance thresholds passes both by a very wide margin —
construction and land development 12.7% of total risk-based capital against the 100% level, total CRE
51.5% against the 300% level — with CRE office at just $2,435M, 10.3% of CRE and 0.74% of total
loans, and CRE non-performing loans down from $298M to $47M in one year.**

**[E3-24]'s own worked bank scenario, run on Truist's book, gives Buffett's own answer.** 10% of
$329,796M of loans at 30% severity is **$9,894M** of charge-offs in one year — **5.5× the worst year
in the bank's post-merger history** — against **$9.0bn** of annualised pre-provision net revenue and
a **$4,983M** allowance. **Roughly break even.** *"A year like that — which we consider only a
low-level possibility, not a likelihood — would not distress us."* A harder compound scenario (2.7%
of loans charged off, the entire HTM loss realised, PPNR down 20%) still leaves **CET1 at 9.9%
against 7.0%** and costs **19% of tangible book value per share.**

**[E2-50]'s test passes.** The allowance at each year-end covered the **next two years'** net
charge-offs **1.94× (2021), 1.37× (2022) and 1.45× (2023)**, the ALLL ratio moved in a 25-basis-point
band through a full cycle (1.34%–1.59%), and the provision has exceeded net charge-offs every year
since 2022. The one prompt — the **$813M negative provision in 2021**, about 10% of that year's
earnings, released into a loss cycle that then rose for four years — is recorded as **[E3-02]**
conformity rather than a reserving failure, because the reserve that remained proved 1.94× the
following two years' losses.

**And [E2-67]'s bank analogue was found, which the SOFI fold flagged as a structural gap from the
other direction.** Truist publishes, **every year and in dollars**, what a pessimistic macroeconomic
scenario would add to its modelled allowance: **$2.1bn (2021), $2.2bn, $2.2bn, $2.2bn, $2.4bn
(2025)** — 45% of the current allowance. It is not a development triangle and it is not a model
backtest (no standard requires one), but it is the filer stating how wrong its central estimate could
be, with the direction named. **Proposed to the operator: treat the ACL scenario sensitivity as the
bank analogue of [E2-67]'s table, and record its absence as a candor gap where a bank does not
publish one.**

### The (c) convention: CCB's form adopted, ACNB's split applied, and a third form added because Truist's filings make the first one wrong

The brief asked the run to follow the prior banks' construction *"unless Truist's filings make it
wrong, and say which."* **They do, and the failure is specific and fixable.** Truist's total assets
**fell** $19,906M in 2023 and $4,173M in 2024, and neither was a contraction of the business —
**$7,655M of it was the Insurance Holdings segment leaving the balance sheet.** So CCB's
`Δassets × Tier 1 leverage` form prints **$5,278M of owner earnings in 2024 — the highest of the six
years — in the year the company realised a $6,651M securities loss.** The form used instead is
**`Δ(risk-weighted assets) × the CET1 ratio`**, which is the binding constraint, is what the
regulator measures, and is the one the company itself uses in public (*"Creates $945MM or 22 bps of
CET1 capital"*).

**Bank owner earnings: $2,616M (RWA form, the single clean year) to $3,690M (CCB form, five-year
mean) — a 41% spread whose every dollar is traceable to whether a disposal that released regulatory
capital counts as earnings. Truist earned $21,773M over five years and had to retain $6,036M of it,
27.7%, simply to hold its CET1 ratio while risk-weighted assets grew.** And the equity account
confirms it independently, which is the check ACNB's ruling asks for: **common equity FELL from
$62,864M to $60,273M over five years while $19,951M was earned and $18,850M was paid out.**

**Recommendation carried to the operator: the convention has now passed three independent tests
(CCB, ACNB, SOFI) and been refined by a fourth. Give it a ledger row in the RWA/CET1 form with the
Δassets form as the fallback for filers that do not publish risk-weighted assets, or refuse it —
rather than let a sixth run re-invent it.**

### Below the gate, and the shape

**Yield 4.41% to 6.22% against a 5.34% sovereign — MINUS 0.93 to PLUS 0.88 points. Honest pre-tax
expectancy about 8%, below the ~10% [E4-28] floor on every construction and BELOW THE BOND at the
conservative end.** The quote needs **5.59% perpetual growth** at the conservative end from a
business whose diluted earnings per share from continuing operations went **$4.07 (2022) to $3.82
(2025)** on a 4.9% smaller share count. Value **roughly $20 to $50 a share**, and **[E4-25]** says
the width IS the conclusion. Screamer test: **above the whole conservative range.** Windage count
ONE.

**PROPOSED SHAPE, entered in the index as #29 THE BOUGHT RATIO** (drafted as 27 and renumbered at
the fold, because JPM took 27 and OTTR took 28 the same day; the collision is recorded, not
resolved): *the published return target is reached by retiring and selling the capital the return is
measured against, rather than by earning more on it; each disposal raises the ratio and lowers the
business; nothing ever breaks, and the owner's claim compounds at the rate of the share count rather
than the rate of the bank.* Argued against **#5 THE SELF-LIQUIDATING DISTRIBUTION** (the payout is a
buyback, not a dividend, and the assets sold are deliberately the **worst** ones — RAC's *"pre-tax
earnings were approximately breakeven"* on the filer's own slide), **#24 THE BOUGHT AVERAGE** (its
exact inverse: BlackRock's share count **rises**) and **#26 THE MARKED BOOK** (SoFi issues equity to
grow; Truist retires it to shrink). **Truist and SoFi are the project's first two banks that neither
fail nor compound, from opposite directions, and that pair is worth more than either finding alone.**

### The strongest fact against the verdict, and the falsifier

**On the FDIC's own numbers Truist Bank's efficiency ratio in the first half of 2026 is 52.990% —
the BEST of all nine banks. Its pre-tax return on assets has gone 0.874% → 1.248% → 1.350% in six
quarters. Its own reported ROTCE has gone 13.3% → 12.7% → 13.8% → 15.4%. Diluted EPS rose 37% year
on year in Q2 2026. And the management that produced the five-year record left on 2026-09-01 having
earned nothing on its long-term award.** If the last six quarters continue for three years, this
verdict is wrong.

**The falsifier is pre-committed [E1-02]: Truist Bank's pre-tax return on average assets, on the FDIC
Call Report, reaching the nine-bank median of about 1.42% and STAYING there for three consecutive
full years, while the noninterest-bearing deposit share stops falling.** H1 2026 is the first
half-year of such a run. **One year is not three, and the reason is [E4-17]: "those beliefs change
quite gradually."** A second, separate prediction is on the record before the fact: **if the new
CEO's "broader strategic review" produces a large acquisition paid for in Truist stock, the verdict is
CONFIRMED, not refuted, because [E5-44] says the shares given must not be worth more than the
business received — and at a quote above this run's whole conservative value range, Truist paper is
not cheap currency.**

### Tooling and brief defects

1. **An FDIC API trap, found and fixed.** `banks.data.fdic.gov/api/institutions` with
   `search=NAME:"..."` is a **full-text** match. A first pass that searched `"TRUIST BANK"` and took
   the largest match by assets returned **JPMorgan Chase Bank, CERT 628**; `"CITIZENS BANK"` returned
   **Wells Fargo Bank, CERT 3511**; `"KEYBANK"` and `"MANUFACTURERS AND TRADERS TRUST"` returned
   **nothing at all**. A row built that way is wrong and looks entirely plausible. The correct call
   is `filters=NAME:"<exact legal name>" AND ACTIVE:1`, verified against city and state, and nine
   CERTs are saved for reuse in `_research 2026-09-19 TFC/fdic_certs.json`. **The ACNB run asked for
   an FDIC helper in `tools/`; this run seconds that request and supplies a second recipe.**
2. **A data trap that caught this run's OWN Q2 table.** `companyfacts` returns the **latest** vintage
   of a restated balance-sheet date. Truist's goodwill at 2022-12-31 is **$23,233M** in the tagged
   data and **$27,013M** on the FY2022 10-K's own balance sheet — the $3,780M difference being the
   Insurance Holdings goodwill later moved to discontinued operations. **Any ROTCE or tangible-book
   computation for a filer with a discontinued-operations recast must use the as-filed capital table,
   not the tagged data.** Corrected in a dated addendum; the ranking did not change.
3. **The brief said TFC is not in the WAVE 6 table and is in the excluded-bank subsection. The exact
   opposite is true on both counts** — and this is the **fifth consecutive fold** to correct a brief
   about where a name lives in the queue, and a verbatim repeat of JPM's. **The two names that ARE
   rows in the eleven-name table are JPM and TFC; the three in the excluded subsection are CCB, ACNB
   and SOFI.**
4. **The brief said "the fourth bank".** JPM folded as register entry 130 claiming the fourth while
   this file was being written, so **TFC is the fifth** — the third consecutive bank whose brief
   mis-stated the count, corrected by counting the register rather than trusting the brief.
5. **`sources.py:_get()` still defaults to a Mozilla user agent and `sec.gov/Archives` answers 403.**
   The brief warned of it (*"three runs have now hit this"*) and every fetch in this run passed
   `headers=SEC_UA` explicitly. It is now four runs, and the default should change.
