## PAGP (Plains GP Holdings, L.P.) - run 2026-09-20 - Q1 IN, **Q2 OUT on the business**
**WAVE 7, NAME 1.** The first of the operator's three CSV lists. Register entry **133**. Price
**US$27.67** (2026-09-18, aggregator flagged) x **197,904,124 Class A shares** (10-Q cover,
`0001581990-26-000025`) = cap **US$5,476.0M**. Sovereign **5.34%**, 30-year US Treasury par
yield curve, 2026-09-18, struck from the issuing authority.

### The finding that governs everything else: the screen priced the wrong entity

PAGP sorted **first in the entire wave** because its screen `growth_required` read **-0.1381** -
the arithmetic said the price already cleared the floor with negative growth. **It does not,
and the reason is one tier down.**

`PAGP does not directly own any operating assets` (10-K FY2025, first paragraph). It owns an
**~85% limited partner interest in AAP**; AAP owns **233.0 million PAA common units, ~31% of
PAA's common and Series A preferred combined**. Look-through **~26%**. The filer states it three
more ways in the same document: FY2025 net income **$260M to PAGP against $1,426M to
noncontrolling interests (15.4%)**; partners' capital **$1,345M against $12,871M (9.5%)**;
distributions paid **$301M against $1,441M (17.3%)**.

**The screen's `oe_bottom_m 1318 / oe_top_m 1750` is the WHOLE consolidated group set against
197.9M Class A shares - one class of the top tier. An overstatement of roughly four times.**
This is the per-class denominator error of DASH, META, PATH, PUBM and BZFD **inverted**: there
the cover count was unreadable and the numerator was right; here the cover count is right and
the **numerator belongs to a wider entity**. **The general form worth carrying forward: a
consolidated numerator is only usable where noncontrolling interests are immaterial, and
`owner_earnings()` never reads the NCI lines.** Any multi-tier partnership, any
sponsor-and-MLP pair, any filer consolidating a JV it does not own outright, will price this
way. The tell is three lines long and sits in every 10-K: net income attributable to NCI,
noncontrolling interests in partners' capital, and distributions paid to noncontrolling
interests.

### Q1 IN. A taxed wrapper on about 198 million PAA common units

The filer names the design: **Economic Parity** - *"the number of our outstanding Class A shares
equals the number of AAP units we own, which in turn equals the number of PAA common units held
by AAP attributable to our ownership interest in AAP."* So one Class A share = one PAA common
unit of economics, **through an entity that "has elected to be taxed as a corporation for United
States federal income tax purposes"** and carries a $1,136M deferred tax asset.

Underneath, PAA is a crude-oil midstream business with two legs: **fee assets** (20,405 miles of
active pipeline, 76 million barrels of commercial storage, 9,680 kb/d of 2025 tariff volume,
largest in the Permian) and a **merchant book** that buys and sells physical crude - which is why
revenue is **$44,262M** and purchases are **$40,433M**. Operating income is **3.2% of revenue**.
Not simple; but every layer is stated and quantified in the filing, and [E3-31]'s test is whether
the analyst can *"realistically define what [he doesn't] know"*, not whether the chart is short.

### Q2 OUT. Two of three [E3-03] clauses fail in the filer's own words

**Clause (2), no close substitute - the filer writes [E2-58] itself:**
*"many of the areas where PAA operates have become overbuilt, resulting in an excess of midstream
energy infrastructure capacity"*, caused by *"relatively low barriers to entry"*, with rivals who
*"may be motivated to reduce transportation rates to levels approaching variable operating costs,
without regard to whether they are generating an acceptable return on their investment ... with
respect to certain of PAA's long-haul Permian pipelines."* Add *"pipelines may also face
competition from other forms of transportation, such as truck, rail and barge"* and *"existing
third-party owned pipelines with excess capacity in the vicinity of our operations also expose us
to significant competition."* **[E2-58]'s one exception is a cost advantage "both wide and
sustainable"; the competitor row shows PAA has the opposite.**

**Clause (3), not price-regulated - the filer quantifies it:** *"The majority of our pipeline
profits in the United States are based on rates that are either grandfathered in part or set by
agreement with one or more shippers. These rates remain regulated by FERC and are subject to
challenge or review and modification by FERC under the ICA."* The FERC index for July 2021-June
2026 was **revised down about 1% effective 1 March 2022**, vacated by the D.C. Circuit in July
2024, re-issued in September 2024 and is still under petitions whose *"final resolution ... could
have an adverse effect on our cash flows."* **[E2-59] exactly: the regime here is a CAP and not a
floor, and the corpus says neither creates the class.**

### The competitor row is the sharpest single artifact in this run

Ten peers, five years, one metric, every figure from the peer's own 10-K facts - **operating
income / (net PP&E + equity-method investments + net finite-lived intangibles)**, chosen because
[E3-46] makes the second question about a business a number and because margin-on-revenue is
meaningless across a set where some filers run $40bn of commodity gross through the top line and
others do not.

| | 5-yr mean FY2021-25 |
|---|---|
| **PAA / PAGP** | **5.6%** |
| HESM | 25.5% |
| MPLX | 20.1% |
| DKL | 14.5% |
| WES | 14.3% |
| EPD | 13.7% |
| TRGP | 11.8% |
| OKE | 11.6% |
| ET | 9.1% |
| KMI | 8.7% |
| GEL | 4.8% |

**Tenth of eleven. Peer median 13.7%. PAA's BEST year, 6.7%, is below every peer's five-year
mean except Genesis Energy's.** Enbridge named and excluded (40-F, IFRS, CAD). Limits stated:
EPD and ET tag no undimensioned `EquityMethodInvestments`, so their denominators are understated
and their returns flattered - correcting them moves EPD to ~12.9% and ET to ~8.8%, which does not
touch the conclusion. And [E3-61]'s limit stands: the row shows position, never conduct.

**[E4-55] on the units, and it is the whole story in two lines:** tariff volumes **8,934 -> 9,680
kb/d (+8%)**, Permian **6,731 -> 7,333 (+9%)**, while *"certain Permian long-haul contract rates
reset[] to market in 2025."* **Volume up, rate down, 5.6% on capital.** [E3-62]'s second step -
*"how much is going to stay home and how much is just going to flow through to the customer"* -
answers itself from the filer's own variance table. **That is the #11 PASS-THROUGH signature, and
it is recorded beneath the close rather than as a Q4 finding, because Q4 was never reached.**

### Priors the brief set, and what happened to each

| prior | outcome |
|---|---|
| **A. The structure may not be what the screen priced** | **CONFIRMED, and it is the run's governing finding.** Numerator ~4x too large. |
| **B. The working-capital flag names its year (2021 payables = 99% of OCF)** | **TRUE as arithmetic, REFUTED as a finding.** Payables released $1,970M; **receivables absorbed $2,179M**; net working capital was a **$227M DRAIN**. Operating cash before working capital is a stable $2.2-3.0bn across five years. |
| **C. Q2 has a regulated-price question with proportions owed** | **ANSWERED from the filing: the MAJORITY of US pipeline profit is FERC-regulated**, and the unregulated merchant leg sits in a market the filer calls overbuilt. |
| **D. Shapes #11, #5, #6, #28 to test at Q4** | **#11's signature is present and recorded; #5, #6 and #28 are UNTESTED**, because the file closed two gates early. No shape is named as this business's death. |
| **E. Q3 requires the latest 8-K EX-99.1; the industry's releases are built on a non-GAAP metric** | **CONFIRMED at full strength, recorded and NOT scored.** See below. |
| **F. Perimeter: `deal_note` says two Item 1.01s, no EX-2.1** | **THE `deal_note` WAS WRONG.** See below. |

### [E4-29] is constitutional at this filer - recorded, not scored, because Q3 was not run

*"Adjusted EBITDA"* appears **43 times** in the Q2 2026 earnings release (`0001581990-26-000023`,
2026-08-07), whose second headline bullet is *"Delivered strong second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA
attributable to PAA of $738 million."* It is not a stray usage:
- the filer's **own targeted credit profile** is written in it - *"a leverage multiple averaging
  between 3.25x to 3.75x, which is calculated as total debt plus 50% of the value of preferred
  units, divided by Adjusted EBITDA attributable to PAA"*;
- the **bank covenant** is written in it - *"Consolidated Funded Indebtedness to adjusted
  Consolidated EBITDA ... no greater than 5.00 to 1.00, which increases to 5.50 to 1.00 during an
  Acquisition Period"* (Revolving Credit Agreement of 2026-06-12, 8-K `0001104659-26-075189`);
- **D&A was $953M against $1,428M of operating income** - the excluded charge is two-thirds the
  size of the profit;
- and *"Adjusted Free Cash Flow"* of **$4,189M** for Q2 2026 against $348M a year earlier is
  mostly the **$3.9bn of divestiture proceeds**.

**[E2-54] is the corpus's answer to an EBITDA covenant** - *"a capital structure that does not
allow all interest, both payable and accrued, to be comfortably met out of current cash flow net
of ample capital expenditures"* - and it was not run here, because Q4 was not reached.

### The perimeter: four events the FY2025 statements do not carry, and a screen inference that missed the biggest

`deal_note` read *"2 8-K Item 1.01 filing(s) since 2026-02-27, none carrying a merger agreement
(EX-2.1) - most likely a credit facility or offering."* Opened, all of them:
1. **2026-05-12, `0001104659-26-059512`: the COMPLETED SALE of the Canadian NGL business to
   Keyera for ~CAD $5.328bn (~USD $3.883bn), ~$3.3bn net.** Its agreement exhibits are **EX-2.2,
   EX-2.3 and EX-2.4** - the three amendments - because the original SPA of 2025-06-17 was filed
   as EX-2.1 to the **Q2 2025 10-Q**. **A deal-perimeter test keyed to `EX-2.1` on the 8-K misses
   every transaction whose agreement was filed earlier and amended at closing.** This is the MRVL
   lesson in a new place.
2. **2026-09-14, `0001104659-26-107550`: $700M of 6.750% Series A and $800M of 7.000% Series B
   junior subordinated notes due 2056** - issued six days before this run, after the newest
   periodic filing, against a 30-year Treasury of 5.34%.
3. **The EPIC Crude / Cactus III purchase** (55% 2025-10-01, 45% effective 2025-11-01), most of
   FY2025's **$2,651M** of acquisition cash. **The company's own pro forma in that same 8-K takes
   FY2025 net income from continuing operations attributable to Class A shareholders from $152M
   to $135M, and from $0.77 to $0.68 per Class A share - dilutive on the filer's own arithmetic.**
   Recorded; **Q3 was not run and no capital-allocation verdict is written.**
4. **$484M of the FY2025 $2,931M operating cash is discontinued operations** - the Canadian NGL
   business, which no longer exists.

### One security fact - COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE

**PAGP closed at $27.67 and PAA at $25.37 on 2026-09-18.** By the filer's own Economic Parity
rule one Class A share carries the economics of one PAA common unit, so **PAGP trades at a 9.1%
premium to the identical claim one tier down**, and PAGP is the only one of the two that is a
corporate taxpayer. Recorded as a fact about two securities; no entry language, no Q5 output.

### Tooling and brief defects

1. **`working_capital_flag()` reads ONE line and never nets its matched counter-line.** On a
   commodity merchant, receivables and payables both scale with the commodity price, so the flag
   fires in every year the price moved and **names the wrong cause**. Here it named the year the
   cash was *drained* ($227M net use) as the year the cash was *made*. **Proposed fix, not made:
   where a filer tags both `IncreaseDecreaseInAccountsAndOtherReceivables` and
   `IncreaseDecreaseInAccountsPayableAndAccruedLiabilities`, report the NET working-capital cash
   effect beside the single line and refuse the "one line made the cash" string when the
   counter-line offsets more than half of it.** The likely reason they were never netted: **the
   two tags carry opposite cash-sign conventions** in the standard taxonomy (an increase in
   receivables is a use of cash; an increase in payables is a source).
2. **No guard reads noncontrolling interests.** `owner_earnings()` takes the consolidated
   operating-cash line whatever share of it belongs to the registrant's own shareholders. **This
   is a whole error class, not one name** - the three lines that detect it are in every 10-K and
   none is read. Any sponsor/MLP pair, multi-tier partnership or majority-owned-JV consolidator
   in the remaining 262 wave-7 names carries it.
3. **`PropertyPlantAndEquipmentNet` is not the tag this filer uses after FY2020.** PAGP and PAA
   report under
   `PropertyPlantAndEquipmentAndFinanceLeaseRightOfUseAssetAfterAccumulatedDepreciationAndAmortization`
   from FY2021. A capital-return screen keyed to the first tag returns **nothing** for this filer
   and drops it silently rather than refusing - the same shape as every other two-paths split
   this project has found.
4. **The `deal_note`'s EX-2.1 test, above.**
5. **The dispatch brief and `CLAUDE.md` both say the ledger is 267 rows. It is 311**, and
   `Screens/RESUME STATE ...` section 10's "286" is also now stale - the 25 survival-shape rows
   of commit `0eaeadd` landed the same day. `tools/check_framework.py` prints
   *"LEDGER 311 rows, 311 unique ids"* and PASSES. **`CLAUDE.md`'s KEY FILES table still says
   267** and should be corrected by the operator, since that same table instructs the reader to
   *"Count the file, never the pointer."*
   **And a trap inside the counting itself, recorded because my own first count fell into it:**
   `csv.reader(open('principle_ledger.csv', encoding='utf-8'))` returns **286**, not 311,
   because without `newline=''` Python translates the `
` inside the quoted multi-line
   `quote_verbatim` fields and the reader splits single rows into several. **`newline=''` is
   required**, which is what `check_framework.load_ledger()` already does and what any future
   count should copy. **A wrong count taken this way raises no error and looks entirely
   plausible** - which is the same failure shape as the `working_capital_flag()` and `EX-2.1`
   defects above: right arithmetic, wrong object.
6. **A filer drafting artifact, flagged and not smoothed (PRIME RULE 1).** The 8-Ks of
   2026-09-14 and 2026-05-12 both describe PAA as *"a wholly owned subsidiary of Plains GP
   Holdings, L.P."* **PAA's common units trade on Nasdaq and AAP holds ~31% of them**; the press
   release attached to the same 8-K states it correctly. A reader relying on the 8-K body alone
   would compute exactly the error the screen made.

### What could not be resolved, and the document that would resolve it

- **PAGP's entity-level cash tax path.** It carries a **$1,136M deferred tax asset** and pays
  corporate tax on income a PAA unitholder receives untaxed at the entity. How fast that asset is
  consumed - and therefore what fraction of the PAA distribution actually reaches a Class A
  shareholder over a decade - is not computable from the documents read. *Resolved by:* Note 15
  (Income Taxes) of the FY2025 10-K read against the deferred-tax rollforward, plus the Section
  754 / basis discussion in the Class A share tax summary. **Not fetched: the file closed at Q2
  and no valuation was owed.**
- **The split of Crude Oil Segment Adjusted EBITDA between fee-based and merchant margin.** The
  10-K describes both legs and disaggregates neither. *Resolved by:* PAA investor-day materials
  or a supplemental disclosure; it is in none of the 10-K, the 10-Q or the 8-Ks read here. **It
  does not change Q2** - both legs fail [E3-03], the fee leg on clause (3) and the merchant leg
  on clause (2).

# UPDATE 2026-09-20 — LEG: THE FIRST NAME IN THE PROJECT TO DIE BETWEEN THE SCREEN AND THE RUN
**WAVE 7, name 2. `Test Runs/2026-09-20 Run - LEG Leggett & Platt.md` (commits `e2c06dd`,
`11e67bd`). The file closes at STEP 0, before Q1 opens, and records NO framework verdict.**

**Leggett & Platt ceased to exist as a public security on 2026-08-26.** It was merged into
**Somnigroup International Inc.** — all-stock, fixed exchange ratio **0.1455** SGI per LEG,
8-K Item 1.01 of 2026-04-13 (`0001193125-26-151966`), DEFM14A `0000058492-26-000364`, closing
8-K `0001193125-26-366694` of 2026-08-26, **Form 25-NSE `0000876661-26-000712`** on 2026-08-27
and **Form 15-12G `0001193125-26-384400`** on 2026-09-08, whose line settles it: *"Common Stock,
$0.01 par value - 1 holder"*. Former LEG holders own ~8.6% of the combined company. **There is no
float, no quote and no price term, so Q5 cannot exist.**

**THE DEAL FLAG DID ITS JOB AND THE PRICING PATH DID NOT.** The screen row's `deal_note` fired
correctly — ten filings since the annual report, first 425 on 2026-04-13 — and the ROKU rule of
2026-09-12 (*"if a deal is live the quote is a spread, not an owner-earnings price - read it
before pricing anything"*) is what sent this run to the filings before it priced anything.
**But the flag has only two states, live and absent. It has no state for CLOSED.** So the
screen priced a cancelled security: cap `1257`, which the run reconstructed exactly as
**$9.20 (the suspended-trading close of 2026-08-26) x 136,588,995 (the cover of the last 10-Q
LEG will ever file, `0000058492-26-000430`) = $1,256.6M.** The $9.20 was itself only 0.1455 x
SGI. **A yield of 14.53% and a growth requirement of minus 4.53% — the row that ranked LEG
second in the whole wave-7 order — are arithmetic on a price that does not exist.**

**THE AGGREGATOR STILL SERVES THE DEAD QUOTE.** $9.20 comes back today as
`regularMarketPrice` with exchange `"NYSE"`, twenty-five days after the Form 25. Operator rule
5 already says aggregators are for live quotes only, flagged; **this is the case that shows a
flag is not enough, because the quote was not live and nothing in the response said so.**

**A TOOL CONCLUDED, AND WHAT IT CONCLUDED WAS FALSE.** `python tools/run.py LEG` printed
*"LEG: not an SEC filer... This is UNRESEARCHED, not UNKNOWABLE."* **LEG is an SEC filer** —
CIK 58492, 10-Q filed 2026-08-06. The SEC had merely dropped it from the live
`company_tickers.json` after the Form 25 and Form 15. Two faults, and the second is the worse:
the claim is wrong, and **naming a verdict violates operator rule 8**, under which tools fetch
and compute and are *forbidden to conclude*; *every flag is a prompt to read, never a score*. A
run that had obeyed the tool would have gone hunting RNS and SEDAR+ filings for a Missouri
company. **The constructive fix, offered by the run and NOT built:** absence from
`company_tickers.json` for a ticker the queue carries with a recent 10-K is a **delisting
tell**, and **Form 25 and Form 15 are clean signals** — exactly where the RESUME STATE's ninth
source limit found 8-K Item 2.01 was not. That limit was recorded as *"incomplete and unclean,
so not built"*; Form 25/15 is the artifact it was looking for.

**A THIRD DEFECT, CAUGHT INSIDE THE RUN.** A tag-stripper that replaces HTML tags with spaces
**fabricates whitespace inside every defined term in an EDGAR document**. The run's first draft
quoted `(the " Closing Date ")` and asserted the entities were `&#147;/&#148;`; both were wrong
(they are `&#8220;/&#8221;`, no interior spacing). It caught this itself and recorded the
mechanism rather than smoothing the quote — PRIME RULE 1 working rather than failing.

**THE VERDICT FORM IS THE THING FOR THE OPERATOR.** The four verdicts attach to *questions
about a business you could buy*, and **none of them describes "the security has been
cancelled"**. The run tested all four and refused each on the record: **OUT** asserts the
business fails, which is false; **UNRESEARCHED** is a work order and no artifact is outstanding,
since every artifact was fetched and they are what closed the file; **UNKNOWABLE**'s *effect*
is exactly right but its *definition* — *"evidence is in, the future is still indeterminate"* —
is false, because here the evidence is complete and the future is entirely determinate. It also
refuted four arguments for running the gates anyway, the strongest being **[E3-47]**'s omission
cost, answered rather than waved: [E3-47] concerns failing to buy what you understood **and
could have bought**, and LEG could not have been bought at any price after 2026-08-26, so the
omission is a **screening** omission, reported as the tooling defect above.

**It closed as `DEAD_OR_ACQUIRED`, which is THIS FILE'S OWN CATEGORY** — the *"Taken private /
merged / renamed"* bucket in the data-quality findings above, whose stated rule is *"A name
failing that check is recorded and closed without a full run."* Using it as the outcome of a
*run* rather than of a *triage* is confessed in the run file as a **CONVENTION** under PRIME
RULE 3. **It licenses nothing**: no gate passed, no name promoted, no number used. **Whether the
framework should carry a fifth outcome is a structural change and PRIME RULE 5 reserves it to
the operator, with a written case and quotes. Flagged, not patched.**

*Dated note beside the bucket above rather than an edit of it (operator rule 6): that list was
measured on 2026-08-31, when LEG was a filer in good standing and belonged on no such line.*
**LEG is the thirtieth name of that class and the only one ever to reach a run file, because it
died AFTER the queue was built.** *The bucket line above is left exactly as measured.*

**TWO NAMES TO RE-READ BEFORE THEY ARE RUN: ACLS and CNR**, flagged by the run as the same
class. Neither is in `_wave7_order.txt`, but **the queue's cap for any acquired name is a dead
quote by construction**, so the check is cheap and the alternative is another run spent
discovering it.

**THE SUCCESSOR IS NOT QUEUED BY THIS CYCLE. Somnigroup International Inc., NYSE: SGI, CIK
`0001206264`** — different management, capital structure, consolidation and owner earnings.
**Nothing in the LEG file carries into it**; **[E4-08]** asks durability *of a company*, and
this file's company is not that company. If it is run, it is run under its own file from its
own filings, which is the operator's queueing decision and not an unattended one.

### What was recorded and never used
Sovereign **5.34% USD**, 2026-09-18, US Treasury daily par yield curve 30Y from the issuing
authority, struck this session via `tools/sources.py` and not inherited from the brief. **Owner
earnings: none; Q4 was not written and no net-income proxy was used or contemplated.** The
operator rule 4 cross-check was performed even so — six-month operating cash flow, filed
statement *"( 10.3 )"* against XBRL **-10,300,000**, agree. *Noted and not scored, because no
gate was open to score it: final-half operating cash flow was negative, a $101M year-on-year
swing.*

# SMPL — The Simply Good Foods Company — run and folded 2026-09-20 (WAVE 7, name 3; register entry 135)

**Q1 IN. Q2 OUT, on criterion (2) of [E3-03]. FAIL, and the file closed on the BUSINESS and
not on the price.** Price **$10.13** (2026-09-18, aggregator, flagged), shares **88,460,545**
from the cover of the 10-Q, accession `0001702744-26-000023`, cap **$896.1M**, sovereign
**5.34%** (US Treasury, 09/18/2026). Run file:
`Test Runs/2026-09-20 Run - SMPL Simply Good Foods.md`.

## The finding

**A brand is not a franchise when the retailer's planogram decides the unit series.** Three
trademarks, no factory, and 49% of sales through two customers on at-will contracts with no
minimum purchase. The company's own filings close the gate:

- Atkins **retail takeaway -23.9%** in the quarter and **-22.1%** year to date, on *"known
  distribution losses"*. **A product its customers think has no close substitute does not
  lose a quarter of its consumer offtake because a retailer cut facings.**
- **OWYN is the inverse experiment and the more damning one**: down on *"poor velocities,
  **including on newly expanded distribution**"*. It was GIVEN more facings and sold less per
  facing. **The facing was the asset; the brand was not.**
- Gross margin **32.2% against 36.9%, -470bp in nine months**, on *"higher input costs"*,
  with no price response. **[E2-44]**'s first characteristic failing on the filed statement,
  and **[E4-37]**'s agony metric with no evidence the increase was even attempted.

## The competitor row is what makes it a category finding, not a company finding

**BellRing (BRBR), the only listed pure-play comparable, lost 640bp of gross margin in the
same twelve months** (28.5% against 34.9%) on +2.3% sales while SMPL fell 5.4%. **The cost
shock passed through neither of them.** That is **[E2-58]**'s equation operating one layer
DOWN from the trademarks: the contract-manufacturing and protein-input layer holds pricing
power over both branded buyers, and the branded buyers hold none over the retailer. Celsius
(+85.5%, margin flat) is the control that says this is not the whole consumer-health shelf.
Medifast (-36.0% in FY2025, from $1,598.6M in 2022 to $385.8M in 2025) is what the Atkins
path looks like run to its end in a listed registrant.

**An absence, recorded because it was looked for** (absence-claim rule): an EDGAR full-text
sweep of 2026-09-20, 10-K forms, 2024-09-01 to 2026-09-20, on `"Simply Good Foods"`,
`"Quest Nutrition"`, `"Atkins"`, `"OWYN"` and `"Premier Protein"`, **found no instance of any
competitor's 10-K naming this company or its brands**. Weight it low: the same sweep shows
BellRing's brand named only by BellRing and Post, so not naming rivals is this industry's
convention.

## REFUTED PRIORS — the brief was wrong twice and right once, and the wrongness is the finding

**1. `cap_flag` IS NOT A DATA-INTEGRITY FLAG. It is a drawdown detector wearing one's
label.** The brief called the re-strike "the first real work of the run" and said the likely
cause was a share count that is too low. **Both halves are wrong.** The cap was right; the
share count reconciles to the share (104,050,545 issued less 15,609,338 treasury =
88,441,207, against the cover's 88,460,545 thirty-three days later); and the thing that moved
is the PRICE. The FY2025 10-K cover reads *"approximately $3.5 billion based on the closing
price of **$37.75**"* as of 2025-02-28. **$37.75 then, $10.13 now: down 73%.** And the screen
used a cover a year older still ($3,300M as of 2024-02-23, the FY2024 10-K) while its own
`newest_filing` column already pointed at FY2025 — **thirty-one months of drift between the
two numbers it declared irreconcilable.**

**The general rule, for every future run that meets this flag: `cap_flag` compares a
live-priced cap with a point-in-time dollar float, so it fires on every name that has fallen
hard since its last cover date and on no name that has risen.** A run that treats it as "one
of the two is wrong" will spend fetches looking for a share-count error that is not there.
**The right first action is to read the cover's PRICE, not to recount the shares** — it is on
the same line, and it settles the flag in one look. *The brief was right about one premise and
right to say check it rather than assume it: an August-FYE filer measures cover float at the
last trading day of February, and both covers confirm it (2024-02-23 and 2025-02-28).*

**2. THE "$282M NET CASH INFLOW" NEVER HAPPENED. It is an XBRL SIGN FLIP BETWEEN VINTAGES,
and it is a NEW failure mode for the perimeter flag.**
`PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired`, FY2024, same element, same year:
**+280.4 as tagged in the FY2024 10-K (`0001702744-24-000089`); -280.4 as tagged in the
FY2025 10-K (`0001702744-25-000046`).** The screen reads the newest vintage and summed its two
negatives (-280.4 and -1.7 = -282.1) into a reported inflow. **SMPL PAID about $280M** for
OWYN on 2024-06-13, financed with $250.0M of incremental term debt, booking **$223.0M of brand
intangible**; the FY2025 -$1.7M is a genuine small inflow, escrow proceeds on a working-capital
true-up, correctly signed. **The project's six recorded perimeter understatements all came
from stock consideration invisible to the tags. This one came from a sign convention changing
underneath a tag that resolved perfectly well.** The flag should compare the SAME year across
the two newest vintages before reporting a direction; that costs one dictionary lookup and
would have caught it.

**3. The brief's own guess about `deal_note` was RIGHT and should be kept.** It said *"most
likely a credit facility or offering; open them only if something else is odd."* The 8-K of
2025-11-20 (`0001104659-25-114309`) is the **2026 Incremental Facility Amendment**: +$150.0M
on the Term Facility, maturity out from March 2027 to **March 2030**. SMPL is live, Nasdaq,
independent. **The liveness check cost four minutes and it has now paid three times this
month** (ROKU, LEG, and here as a negative).

## What the flags found that the screen could not

**`level_shift` 2.16's "normalize down [E4-41]" is REFUSED, with the reason recorded.** The
step is two dated purchases — **Quest, 2019-11-07, on $460.0M of incremental term debt; OWYN,
2024-06-13, on $250.0M** — and **[E4-41] removes favourable EXOGENOUS breaks, which a bought
business is not.** Normalising it away would delete Quest, the only brand still growing.
**But the ratio was pointing at something real from the wrong end: $391.9M of brand and
goodwill written off in twenty-four months against $400.0M of borrowed money.** OWYN cost
about $280M in June 2024 and **$200.0M of its brand was written off by May 2026** — twenty-three
months — while Atkins takeaway fell 22.1% and Atkins marketing spend was cut by plan. That is
**[E3-40]** loss of focus and **[E2-56]** the Pro-Am effect, filed and dated.

**The [E4-25] rebuild lowers the band by a quarter.** The screen's $128-160M was five-year
construction width. Over all eight filed fiscal years the owner-earnings mean is **$98.0M at
c=D&A** (111.2 at depreciation only, 107.8 at total capex) — **23% below the screen's bottom**
— against 127.9 at five years, 151.5 at three and **107.9 TTM to 2026-05-30**. `spread_caveat`
was right that the published band could not see past five years, and the window it could not
see is the one holding the pre-Quest business.

**(c) and the SPGI question, which paid again.** FY2025 D&A of $21.4M is **$6.1M of
depreciation and $15.1M of amortisation of purchased intangibles**. **The amortisation is the
unwinding of the Quest and OWYN purchase prices and is not a renewal cost of anything**, so
**[E3-44]**'s D&A default over-charges this filer and would bill the owner twice for
acquisitions already paid in cash and already sitting in the debt balance. Not the **[E5-20]**
exception either: no plant, capex $1.0M to $20.5M on revenue of $431M to $1,451M. **The
disclosed guess, and it makes every owner-earnings figure in the file an OVERSTATEMENT: the
real (c) for this business is the advertising and trade spend needed to hold the facing, and
the filed evidence is that what is being spent is not enough** — takeaway -3.8%, net sales
guided -6% to -7%, and the marketing line cut 6.7% in FY2025.

## Q3 items, recorded without a verdict because the gate was shut

- **[E4-29] fires at full strength in the EX-99.1 and the CGNX standing rule is what found
  it.** Four of five headline bullets in the 2026-07-09 release are non-GAAP, and **the
  forward outlook is stated in Adjusted EBITDA** (*"$220 and $225 million, or -21% to -19%"*),
  a measure that excludes SBC (**[E5-06]** refuses it outright) and the impairments
  (**[E5-33]** says they belong in the mean). A run reading only the 10-K would have seen the
  measure and not the guidance built on it.
- **[E2-49] metric-switching: CHECKED, NOT FIRED — a sixth failure of that prior**, which now
  stands at six fires and six failures. The Adjusted EBITDA definition is unchanged across the
  FY2024 10-K, the FY2025 10-K and the FY2026 releases, straight through the deterioration.
- **[E4-30] cash-tax tell: CHECKED, NOT FIRED.** Cash taxes as a share of pretax RISE across
  the window: 8.7, 11.7, 5.7, 39.8, 32.7, 15.6, 17.8, **28.9%**.
- **A live capital-allocation flag [E5-08, E2-52, E5-24].** Thirty-nine weeks to 2026-05-30:
  **$213.2M of buybacks** (11,651,767 shares) while **drawing $150.0M of new term debt** on
  2025-11-19, against **$102.2M of operating cash flow** — buybacks at **2.1x** operating cash
  with the gap borrowed. Average prices from the equity statement: **$19.40** in Q2 and
  **$12.26** in Q3, against $10.13 now, with $331.0M written off the brands in the same nine
  months. **[E4-50]** licenses exactly this conduct, but the discount does the licensing and
  not the borrowing; **[E5-24]**, *"what is smart at one price is dumb at another."*
- **[E2-26] mostly PASSES, and it deserves saying.** This company writes *"poor velocities,
  including on newly expanded distribution"* about its own acquisition, discloses that its
  impairment trigger was *"largely the result of ... declines in stock price"*, and carries
  the Atkins impairment as a critical audit matter. **A company hiding this would not write
  that sentence.**
- **[E2-01] with its [E2-43] scoping.** Return on book equity never exceeded **10.5%** in
  eight years (10.5, 5.7, 5.8, 3.4, 7.5, 8.5, 8.1, 5.7) — but the denominator is **73%
  goodwill and purchased intangibles**, so that series is a statement about **the prices paid
  for Quest and OWYN**, not about the operators (**[E2-73]**). Tangible book equity at
  2026-05-30 is **negative $90.8M**.
- **[E4-23] key-person defect, recorded at Q2 and not at Q3**: on 2026-01-19 the founder-era
  CEO **Joseph E. Scalzo, 66, returned**, succeeding Geoff Tanner after two years. **The
  answer to a broken brand portfolio was to bring back the man who built it.**

## The uncomfortable part, written down rather than hedged

**This name did NOT fail on price and did NOT fail on survival.** Q4 is **GOOD** under
**[E4-20]**, and **[E4-43]** says the good class passes. The Q5 computation (headed NOT A
CLEARANCE) puts trailing owner earnings at **$103.8-123.5M on a $896.1M cap, roughly a 12%
yield, ABOVE the ~10% [E4-28] floor**, with net debt at 1.25x guided Adjusted EBITDA and **no
principal due for twelve months, maturity March 2030**. **Quest grew retail takeaway 5.1% and
passed the same impairment test Atkins and OWYN failed.** If Quest is a franchise and the
market is pricing the whole company as Atkins, **this OUT is an [E3-47] omission error and it
will be invisible.** The pre-committed reversal condition is therefore a unit test and not a
price test: **Quest takeaway positive for four consecutive quarters WHILE gross margin
recovers above 36%** — both, because either alone proves nothing. Next artifact: the **FY2026
10-K, expected late October 2026**.

**[E5-35] is why 12% promotes nothing:** *"You can turn any investment into a bad deal by
paying too much. What you can't do is turn any investment into a good deal by paying little."*

## Two work orders left open, neither a gate verdict

1. **The Credit Agreement's financial covenant LEVELS** are not quantified in the 10-Q text.
   Artifact: the Credit Agreement exhibit to the 8-K of 2025-11-20, `0001104659-25-114309`.
2. **The full guidance-versus-outturn table [E3-48]**, which the projections flag asks for.
   Artifact: the EX-99.1 series, `0001702744-26-000004`, `-000010`, `-000021`.

## What no tooling change is proposed for

`tools/run.py` was not used on this name; the arithmetic was built by hand from
`companyfacts` and read back against the filed statements, so no new defect in it is reported
here. **Two screen-layer defects ARE reported** and both are above: the `cap_flag` class
error, and the `acq_note` sign-flip. Neither is fixed in code by this fold, because a fix is a
tooling decision and this run's job was to find it, name it and leave it on the record.

## One pointer correction the acceptance test surfaced, recorded and NOT edited into CLAUDE.md

`python tools/check_framework.py` at the SMPL fold prints **`LEDGER 311 rows, 311 unique ids`**,
and a direct `csv.DictReader` count of `principle_ledger.csv` returns **311 data rows, 311 unique
ids**. **`CLAUDE.md` still says 267** in its KEY FILES table, and the SMPL brief repeated the 267
from it. This is the same class of error the 2026-09-19 USAR run caught when the pointer said 117
and the file held 267, and CLAUDE.md's own note on that line is the remedy: **"Count the file,
never the pointer."** The count is recorded here rather than corrected in place, because CLAUDE.md
is the operator's session instruction and an unattended run does not edit it (operator rule 6 on
history, and the standing rule that a run decides on the record rather than amending the
governing files). **The acceptance test PASSES at 311: 311/311 source files on disk, 310/311
verbatim against the cited source, with E5-07 declared not a quote, and 0 phantom citations across
1,052 run files.** Every ledger id cited in the SMPL run was checked to exist before it was
written.

# SIG (Signet Jewelers) - Q2 OUT on the business. Wave 7, name 4, register entry 136. 2026-09-20

**Q1 IN, Q2 OUT, file closed.** Price **$100.38** (close 2026-09-18, aggregator, FLAGGED),
shares **38,317,243** from the 10-Q cover, accession `0000832988-26-000229`, cap
**$3,846.3M**, sovereign **5.34%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve 30Y, 09/18/2026, cache
deleted and re-struck this session). Run file:
`Test Runs/2026-09-20 Run - SIG Signet Jewelers.md`.

## The finding, and it is a physical one

**North America units fell 7.4%, 6.9%, 6.3% and 8.3% across four consecutive filed periods
while AUR rose 3.3%, 7.6%, 6.3% and 7.8% and the dollar line stayed flat.** Stores went 2,698
to 2,642 to 2,582; North America net selling square feet 3,765 to 3,748 to 3,714 thousand;
US market share **8.5%, "virtually flat"**, in a market the 10-K itself calls *"approximately
$63 billion in calendar year 2025, flat to the prior year."*

This is **[E4-55]** in a company that files the series itself: Precision Steel's pounds fell
69M to 46M while a 40% price rise held dollar volume level, and Munger called it *"a serious
reverse, not likely to disappear in some 'bounce back' effect."* **The physical series is the
honest one and every line of it points down.** Dollar revenue is **-13.1% over three years**
in a flat market.

**The price rise is not the pricing power it resembles.** The MD&A attributes it to *"filling
merchandise assortment gaps at key price points"* and *"strength in the higher-end consumer and
better performance at higher price points"* - **mix**, fewer and richer customers - and credits
gross margin partly to *"accelerating scrap recovery to take advantage of higher gold prices."*
**[E2-44]**'s first characteristic, raising prices *"even when product demand is flat"*, is not
demonstrated by a mix shift bought with 7% of the units a year.

## Criterion (2) fails on the registrant's own words, which is why the verdict is OUT and not UNKNOWABLE

The framework as amended 2026-09-20 sends a name that **passes** [E3-03] and whose durability
cannot be judged to the **[E4-04] perimeter close, UNKNOWABLE at Q2.** Signet never reaches
that door. Its own Fiscal 2026 10-K says jewelry retailing is *"highly fragmented and
competitive"*; that it *"faces significant competition from independent and regional specialty
jewelry retailers that are able to adjust their competitive stance, for example on pricing, to
local market conditions"*; that discounting bites *"particularly … for **easily comparable
pieces of jewelry, of similar quality, sold through stores that are situated near those that
Signet operates**"*; and that with *"increased price transparency"*, *"**If Signet's brands do
not offer the same or a similar item at the lowest price** … consumers may purchase their
jewelry from competitors."* **A company whose annual report says the customer can find the same
item next door and will leave over price has answered criterion (2) itself.**

**[E2-53] dominance applied and FAILS.** Signet **is** the dominant US specialty jeweler - Kay
*"the largest specialty retail jewelry brand in the US based on sales"*, 38% of consolidated
sales, Zales third, Jared fifth - and it is **not prospering**. *"Good or bad, it will prosper"*
is the observable the dominance class is defined by, and this position is not carrying this
business.

**[E3-51] surfing, and the wave is dateable.** The record's peak is **Fiscal 2022: revenue
$5,226.9M to $7,826.0M in one year, +49.7%**, the pandemic goods-spending wave. Revenue has
fallen in **three of the four years since**. The advantage lived in the wave.

## The competitor row, and the number that does the work

Five companies, every figure computed in the run from filed 10-Ks. Same metric, same window,
fiscal-year offsets stated. Return on tangible capital employed is operating income divided by
(total assets - cash - goodwill - intangibles - current liabilities), used instead of return on
book equity because Signet, Tapestry and Movado have all bought back enough stock that book
equity measures the buyback (**[E2-73]**: *"the amount of capital its manager has to work
with"*).

| | gross margin | operating margin | op inc / tangible capital | revenue, 3 years to latest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SIG** | **39.5%** | **5.8%** | **15.9%** | **-13.1%** |
| BRLT | 57.5% | -1.2% | -17.0% | -0.5% |
| MOV | 54.2% | 4.4% | 7.6% | -9.8% |
| FOSL | 56.1% | -1.9% | -6.5% | -40.3% |
| TPR (control) | **77.8%** | **23.9%** | **79.8%** | **+20.2%** |

**Signet's gross margin is the lowest in its own comparator set by fifteen points, and its
operating margin is the best of the four jewelry and accessory names.** Both halves matter.
The low gross margin is partly structural - a retailer of other people's product keeps less -
**and that is the finding**: after fifty years and **$555.0M a year of gross advertising**,
Kay, Zales and Jared are **store signs, not product brands**, and Tapestry shows in the same
consumer wallet, at almost identical revenue, what an owned trademark is worth. The relatively
good operating margin says the **category** is the problem, which is **[E2-58]**'s equation
operating on all five filers at once, with **16,800 US jewelry stores** chasing a flat $63bn.
[E2-58]'s only exception is *"a cost advantage that is both wide and sustainable"*, and none
appears in the row.

Five peers named unavailable with the obstacle rather than dropped: **Pandora A/S** (Nasdaq
Copenhagen, not an SEC registrant), **Tiffany** (no separate filings since LVMH closed in
January 2021), **Richemont** (SIX-listed, no SEC registration), **Costco / Walmart / Amazon**
(jewelry unsegmented in all three 10-Ks), **Helzberg Diamonds** (a Berkshire subsidiary, not
separately reported).

## The [E4-25] rebuild was owed, was performed, and it found what no five-year window can see

The screen's `spread_caveat` named [E4-25] and `years_filed` was **18**. Rebuilt across all
eighteen filed fiscal years:

| window | c = D&A | c = total capex |
|---|---|---|
| 18 years, AS FILED | $484.1M | $486.9M |
| **18 years, the receivable-sale proceeds removed** | **$406.4M** | **$409.2M** |
| **18 years, proceeds and receivable run-off removed** | **$390.4M** | **$393.2M** |
| 10 years, proceeds removed | $575.3M | $590.0M |
| **5 years (the corpus default [E2-42])** | **$581.6M** | **$598.7M** |
| 4 years, pandemic year removed [E4-41] | $465.0M | $477.9M |
| 3 years | $422.9M | $431.5M |
| TTM to 2026-08-01 | $520.3M | $505.8M |

**The screen's arithmetic is right and should be said so first.** Its band was **$423M to
$599M**; this run's **3-year c=D&A figure is $422.9M** and its **5-year c=total-capex figure is
$598.7M**, which is exactly the *"3y/5y x two capex ends"* construction the caveat describes.
**What the rebuild adds sits below that floor**: over eighteen years the figure is **$406.4M to
$409.2M** with the receivable-sale proceeds removed and **$390.4M to $393.2M** with the run-off
removed too, **3% to 8% below the screen's bottom boundary**. The caveat asked for the rebuild;
the rebuild moves the bottom of the band down rather than confirming it.

**THE FINDING: Fiscal 2018's $1,940.5M of "operating cash flow" is not operating cash flow.**
The Fiscal 2019 10-K's cash-flow statement (accession `0000832988-19-000003`) carries, **inside
operating activities**, a line reading **"Proceeds from sale of in-house finance receivables"
of $952.5M in Fiscal 2018 and $445.5M in Fiscal 2019**, beside a $242.1M accounts-receivable
decrease and $27.6M of receivables held for sale. Signet sold its prime customer credit book in
Q3 Fiscal 2018 and the non-prime in June 2018, taking **$167.4M of charges** on the second sale.
Removing the two explicit proceeds lines takes Fiscal 2018 to **$988.0M** and Fiscal 2019 to
**$252.2M**.

**This is a NEW member of the screen-artefact family and it is worth naming as a class.** The
recorded classes so far are the perimeter mismatch, the SBC-of-zero substitution, the cover-date
drawdown detector (SMPL this morning) and the XBRL sign flip between vintages (SMPL, same run).
**This one is different: the tag is correct, the vintage is consistent, the sign is right, and
the number is still not owner earnings**, because a filer routed **an asset disposal through the
operating section** and no undimensioned element distinguishes it. **Only a reader who opens the
cash-flow statement and reads its detail lines can see it** - which is exactly what the
framework's section II demands and what a screen cannot do. **No code fix is proposed**: there
is no tag rule that recovers this, for the same reason the resume state's nine source limits are
limits and not bugs.

## What the run found at Q3 and Q4 without scoring them

- **[E2-49] FIRES. Seventh fire against five failures; the prior stands and is not retired.**
  The Fiscal 2023 and Fiscal 2024 10-Ks carry five numbered non-GAAP measures and EBITDA appears
  **only inside the leverage-ratio definition**. The **Fiscal 2025 10-K promotes "EBITDA,
  adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EBITDAR" to its own numbered headline section** and renames
  "non-GAAP operating income" to "adjusted operating income" - **in the year GAAP operating
  income fell 82%, from $621.5M to $110.7M.** The yardstick was not discarded; a more flattering
  one was **added** when the reported one collapsed. **[E2-49] is written about disposal, and
  this is the same doctrine from the other side** - the demand is for *"pre-set, long-lived and
  small bullseyes"*, and a measure introduced as a headline in the worst year of the decade is
  the opposite of pre-set.
- **[E4-29] FIRES IN BOTH DOCUMENTS, and the CGNX rule paid again.** The 10-K shows EBITDA
  $539.8M, Adjusted EBITDA $687.2M and **Adjusted EBITDAR $1,116.2M against GAAP operating
  income of $393.1M** - and EBITDAR reaches that by **adding back $429.0M of rent, for a company
  whose entire operating structure is 2,582 leased stores.** **[E5-41]**'s reverse-float image
  is exact: depreciation is money already spent, and EBITDAR deletes both it and the rent. The
  EX-99.1 of 2026-09-09 gives **every forward number in non-GAAP** and **no GAAP forecast at
  all**, under *"we cannot provide … without unreasonable efforts"* - while the excluded item,
  impairment, has appeared in **ten of the eighteen filed years**. **[E4-22]'s third flag fires
  with it**: the release is headed *"Raises Fiscal 2027 Guidance."*
- **[E4-30] DOES NOT FIRE, and the reason is worth having.** Reported net income across the
  eighteen years runs -$402.6M, ... -$657.4M, ... +$810.4M, $61.2M, $294.4M - the opposite of
  smooth. Cash taxes as a share of pretax income are **volatile, not declining**: 27.4%, 14.6%,
  23.2%, 4.4%, 13.6%, 16.5%, **2.0%**, **93.0%**, 19.5%. The Fiscal 2024 low has a disclosed
  cause - Bermuda's new 15% tax and a **$263.3M** economic-transition deferred tax asset, whose
  benefit the same note volunteers is limited by OECD Pillar Two to *"approximately $52.7
  million."* **Volunteering the limit on your own tax asset is an [E2-26] candor point.**
- **[E5-15] and [E2-52] DO NOT FIRE**, and the record is the reverse: **$3,679.8M of cumulative
  buybacks since Fiscal 2012 and zero share issuance** since Fiscal 2012, including $1,000.0M
  in Fiscal 2017, $460.0M in Fiscal 2018 and $485.0M in Fiscal 2019 - **the three years
  immediately before the Fiscal 2019 loss of $657.4M.** **[E5-24]**, *"what is smart at one
  price is dumb at another"*, is the row that record is measured against, and it is left
  unscored because scoring it needs a Q5 verdict this run is forbidden to reach.
- **The capital-allocation record, transcribed.** Acquisitions **$913.6M** (Diamonds Direct and
  Rocksbox Fiscal 2022, Blue Nile Fiscal 2023) against **$1,835.1M of goodwill and
  indefinite-lived trade-name impairments across the eighteen filed years** and **$4,664.4M of
  cumulative net income** over the same eighteen. Goodwill and intangibles fell from $1,159.1M
  at Fiscal 2023 to $714.8M at Fiscal 2026 with nothing sold.
- **The half-owner test [E2-26], as an observation and not a finding.** The release quotes the
  CEO on *"high single-digit unit growth at higher price points"*; the same-day 10-Q says
  *"the number of units sold having decreased 8.3% year over year."* **Both can be true at
  once** and no accusation is made. What is recorded is that **the aggregate unit figure, the
  most informative series in the file, appears only in the 10-Q.**

## The uncomfortable part, written down rather than hedged

**SIG did NOT fail on price and did NOT fail on survival.** Q4 items are **GOOD** under
**[E4-20]**, and **[E4-43]** says the good class passes. All three **[E5-11]** strengths pass,
and the third - the one that usually kills - passes outright: **there is no debt.** The Senior
Notes were repaid at maturity in Fiscal 2025, the Series A preferred was retired for $813.8M
the same year, cash is **$526.8M** with a **$1.2bn ABL undrawn to August 2029**, and Fiscal 2026
free cash flow was **$525.3M**. The Q5 computation (headed NOT A CLEARANCE) puts trailing owner
earnings at **$390M-$599M on a $3,846.3M cap - a 10.2% to 15.6% yield, ABOVE the ~10% [E4-28]
floor on every one of the six windows built**, and **4.8 to 10.2 points over the 5.34%
sovereign.**

**So this is the second consecutive wave-7 name to fail at Q2 while clearing the floor**, and
the pattern is worth the operator's attention: the screen ranks by growth-required, which finds
**cheap** names, and cheap names in 2026 are disproportionately **businesses whose unit volumes
are falling**. The gate is doing its job, and the rank order is feeding it exactly the class of
name it is built to refuse. **[E5-35]**: *"You can turn any investment into a bad deal by paying
too much. What you can't do is turn any investment into a good deal by paying little."*

**And the [E3-47] risk is stated, not hedged away.** If the unit decline is the deliberate
shedding of a low-price customer the company no longer wants, and the AUR rise is a permanent
repositioning rather than a mix accident, this OUT is an omission error and it will be
invisible. That is why the pre-committed reversal is a **unit-and-share test, never a price
test**: North America units positive for four consecutive filed periods **with AUR not falling
to buy them**; US share above 8.5% for two consecutive annual reports on the same
MasterCard/Circana basis; and a full year with no brand impairment. **Any two of the three
reopen the file.** Next artifacts: the Q3 Fiscal 2027 release, early December 2026 (which will
also carry the Bread program agreement as a 10-Q exhibit), and the Fiscal 2027 10-K, March 2027.

## Screen items resolved

- **`deal_note` resolved, and its advice would have missed the document.** The single 8-K Item
  1.01 since 2026-03-19 is **not** *"most likely a credit facility or offering"*: it is the
  **Second Amended and Restated Credit Card Program Agreement with Comenity Bank and Comenity

  **through December 31, 2035**, with a **signing bonus** and a **profit share** that the 8-K

  else was odd, and opening it was right.** For a retailer whose card finances **42.0% of

- **`newest_periodic` 2026-05-02 is one quarter stale** (screen cut 2026-09-02, Q2 10-Q filed
  2026-09-09), and **`cap_m` 3198 is eighteen days stale against $3,846.3M**. Neither is a
  defect. Both are recorded because the honest accounting of screen flags includes the ones
  that are merely old, and because the SMPL fold this morning showed how easily "stale" and
  "wrong" get conflated in the other direction.
- **`acq_note` is CORRECT and should be kept.** $913.6M reconciles, and the acquisitions do sit

# CALM (Cal-Maine Foods) - Q2 OUT on the business. Wave 7, name 5, register entry 137. 2026-09-20

**Q1 IN, Q2 OUT, file closed.** Price **$72.89** (close 2026-09-18, aggregator, FLAGGED),
shares **46,917,080** from the **10-K cover**, accession `0001562762-26-000080`, cap
**$3,419.8M**, sovereign **5.34%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve 30Y, 09/18/2026, cache
deleted and re-struck this session). Run file:
`Test Runs/2026-09-20 Run - CALM Cal-Maine Foods.md`.

## The finding: the filer wrote [E2-58] into its own risk factors

The corpus's commodity equation is *"persistent over-capacity without administered prices (or
costs) equals poor profitability"*, with long-term profitability set by *"the ratio of
supply-tight to supply-ample years"* and prosperity breeding the next glut. **Cal-Maine's Item
1A says it in the company's own voice:**

> *"During times when prices are high, the egg industry has typically produced more eggs,
> primarily by increasing the number of layers, which historically has ultimately resulted in an
> oversupply of eggs, leading to periods of lower prices."*

That is *"nothing fails like success"* filed with the Commission. Beside it: *"Our operating
results are materially impacted by market prices for eggs and feed grains (corn and soybean
meal), which are highly volatile, independent of each other, and out of our control"*; the
industry *"remains highly fragmented"* with the ten largest holding **57%** of table-egg layer
hens; and *"Competitive pressures may also restrict our ability to increase prices."*

**Criterion (2) of [E3-03] fails, and the mechanism is in the pricing disclosure rather than in
an impression.** *"Almost all of our conventional shell eggs are priced and sold under
market-based pricing frameworks"* keyed to *"one of the independently quoted regional wholesale
market prices for shell eggs"* - Urner Barry or the USDA. **A product priced off a published
quote for the identical product from anyone else has a close substitute by construction.** And
*"We do not sell eggs directly to consumers or set the prices at which eggs are sold to
consumers."*

## The [E2-58] exception is the whole question on a name like this, and it was tested

*"The one exception is a cost advantage that is both wide and sustainable … By definition such
exceptions are few."* **Cal-Maine has the strongest claim to that exception of any egg producer
in the United States** - the largest flock (50.0 million layers, 14.5 million pullets and
breeders), its own hatcheries, pullet farms and feed mills (2.1 of 2.2 million tons of finished
feed milled in-house), substantially all in-line processing, and 28 acquisitions since 1989. So
the run did not assert the commodity class; it built [E2-01]'s series and let the record answer.

| | |
|---|---|
| sixteen-year mean ROE | **16.6%** |
| **FY2017** | **-8.8%**, net loss $74.3M, **operating cash flow -$45.9M** |
| **FY2021** | **+0.2%**, net income $2.1M |
| the three supply-shock years (FY2016, FY2023, FY2025) | 34.5%, 47.1%, 47.6% |
| **the other thirteen years, mean** | **10.4%** |

**A cost advantage that is wide and sustainable does not produce a -8.8% year.** Ten point four
per cent is about where [E2-42] says *"red lights should start flashing."* The exception was
available, was tested against sixteen filed years, and was refused by the record rather than by
a prior.

## [E4-41] had a clean worked case here, and the flag was right

`level_shift` fired at **3.07** and `level_shift_oe` at **0.343**, both with *"STEP UP -
normalize down [E4-41]"*. Read against the filer's own variance table, the normalisation is owed
and the cause is named: conventional shell egg prices **+99.7% in FY2025** and **-50.9% in
FY2026**, with volumes *"relatively flat"* in both directions, because **40.2 million and 45.2
million commercial layer hens and pullets were depopulated due to HPAI** in 2024 and 2025.
**Those were overwhelmingly rivals' hens.** Cal-Maine lost about **352,000 pullets** to one
Maryland outbreak on 2026-03-14 and *"operations have fully resumed."* Conventional segment
income ran **$213.7M -> $1,290.0M -> $216.6M**.

**This is the cleanest [E4-41] case the project has had:** a favourable exogenous break whose
mechanism is a competitor's inventory being destroyed by a disease, disclosed in the filer's own
numbers on both the way up and the way down. **The flag has been wrong in other runs in this
project. It was checked, not assumed, and here it was right.**

## [E3-62]'s second step is answered by the contracts, not by inference

*"how much is going to stay home and how much is just going to flow through to the customer."*
Cal-Maine has written the answer into its own pricing frameworks: *"The majority of our specialty
shell eggs are priced and sold under frameworks that are based on cost of production"* -
**cost-plus passes every efficiency gain to the buyer by construction**, and specialty was
**36.8% of FY2026 net sales**. On the conventional half the price is a third-party quote. Even
the cost-based contracts leak the other way: *"customers may seek to renegotiate the terms of
their arrangements during periods of sustained low prices."* **Walmart with Sam's Club is 30.0%
of net sales and the top three are 43.1%**, so the counterparty has the weight to ask.

## The competitor row, and what makes it a category finding

Same metric ([E2-01] ROE), same window (eight filed fiscal years), each figure from that
registrant's own 10-K filings.

| | mean ROE, 8 filed years | the shape |
|---|---|---|
| **CALM** | **17.7%** | 0.2% in FY21, 47.6% in FY25 |
| **PPC** (Pilgrim's Pride) | 15.8% | 1.2% in FY21, 26.3% in FY22 |
| **VITL** (Vital Farms, seven filed years) | 12.6% | 0.8% in FY22, 19.8% in FY24 |
| **TSN** (Tyson) | 11.0% | -3.6% in FY23, 23.2% in FY18 |
| **POST** (Post Holdings, owner of Michael Foods) | 9.3% | 0.0% in FY20, 23.3% in FY22 |

**Cal-Maine's mean is the highest and every name has the same signature:** two or three spike
years carrying a mean the median year does not support. **That is the commodity equation showing
up five times in one table.** A higher mean here is a better position *inside* the class, not an
exit from it. The row was still held to [E3-61]'s limit - it shows position, it cannot show
conduct.

**The row's honest limit, stated as the evidence ladder requires:** the industry's *"ten largest
producers owned approximately 57% … of industry table egg layer hens"* and **the rest of that ten
file nothing with the Commission** (Rose Acre, Versova, Daybreak, Hillandale, MPS). The rung is
competitor filings; the obstacle is that the competitors are not registrants. **The moat class is
NONE and not PROVISIONAL, because the verdict rests on the subject's own filed words about its own
product rather than on the completeness of the row.**

## The disconfirming hunt [E4-26] found a rented brand, not a moat

The strongest case against OUT was the specialty segment - 36.8% of sales, carrying *"Eggland's
Best®, Land O'Lakes®, Farmhouse Eggs®, 4Grain®"*. **The two that matter are rented.** They come
*"from our cooperative membership in Eggland's Best, Inc."* against **franchise fees the co-op
sets**, and the co-op reprices them against Cal-Maine's own cycle: cut in FY2025 when conventional
prices were high (*"EB temporarily reduced the related franchise fees"*), restored in FY2026 as
**a $4.7 million increase** into a segment whose income fell **45.6%** on a **2.4% volume
increase** and a **9.5% price decrease**. **Shape #13 THE TENANT by construction** - recorded as
Q2 evidence, and **no shape is named**, because Q4 was never opened and the index takes no new row
from this run.

## The [E4-25] rebuild was owed, and the screen was right about its own blindness

The screen published **$491M to $614M** and said so in `spread_caveat`: *"4-construction width
only (3y/5y x two capex ends): CANNOT see variation older than the 5-year window; rebuild it
[E4-25]."* Rebuilt from the filed cash-flow statements over **seventeen years, FY2010-FY2026**,
eight windows, both (c) ends:

| window | (c)=D&A | (c)=capex |
|---|---|---|
| 3y FY2024-26 | **$614.2M** | $560.6M |
| 5y FY2022-26 | $536.6M | $490.7M |
| 5y with FY2025 removed | $303.9M | $264.4M |
| 9y FY2018-26 | $317.5M | $283.1M |
| 10y FY2017-26 | $275.9M | $243.1M |
| 8y FY2010-17 | $85.8M | $75.8M |
| 13y FY2010-22 | $70.4M | **$57.7M** |
| **17y, whole filed history** | $208.5M | $185.5M |

**$57.7M to $614.2M - a factor of 10.6.** The screen's published bottom is not a bottom; it is the
top of the second-best window, and the true bottom is **one-eighth of it**. **Owner earnings are
negative in three of seventeen filed years** - FY2017 on both ends (-$98.5M / -$116.0M), FY2021 on
both ends (-$37.1M / -$72.7M), FY2020 on the capex end (-$54.2M). **In 18% of the filed record this
business returned nothing to an owner, and in one year it consumed cash.**

`flags_disagree` resolved: the two series disagree because **owner earnings go negative where net
income does not** - FY2021 has net income of **+$2.1M** and owner earnings of **-$37.1M to
-$72.7M**. A ratio across a sign change is not a ratio, which is the same defect the Opus session
fixed in `level_shift` for ARM. `window_disagree` confirmed and understated: the nine-year base
contains both HPAI cycles and misses both troughs; the seventeen-year base contains a full
peak-to-glut round trip (FY2016 +$340.8M -> FY2017 -$98.5M) the nine-year base cannot see.

## Screen items resolved

- **`cap_flag` is a DEFECT IN THE SCREEN, and it is general.** It said *"A cap cannot be smaller
  than a subset of itself"* against a filed float of $3,825,418,582. The float is real and the
  accession is `0001562762-26-000080`, but **it is measured at 2025-11-28 and the cap at
  2026-09-02**, across a 12.5% drawdown. Implied non-affiliate shares 45,912,369 against
  47,654,046 outstanding on the Q2 10-Q cover: **affiliates hold about 3.6%**. On the same date
  float is **96.2%** of the screen's cap and **97.9%** of the re-struck one. **The flag fires on
  any name that has fallen further than its affiliate percentage since its last float measurement
  date**, and it states an arithmetic impossibility where there is only a falling share price.
  Operator rule 8: a tool may not conclude, and this one did.
- **`newest_filing` / `newest_periodic` 2026-05-30 are both CORRECT and neither is stale.**
  Cal-Maine's fourth quarter is not reported on a 10-Q, so the FY2026 10-K filed 2026-07-22 *is*
  the newest periodic filing; the last 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-02-28) is older. **A date, not a
  defect** - and a reminder that the stale-screen test inverts on a filer whose fiscal year ends
  in May.
- **`deal_note` opened.** The one Item 1.01 since 2026-07-22 is the 8-K of 2026-09-02, accession
  `0001562762-26-000102`: a **$250M senior unsecured revolver with BMO**, undrawn, $5.9M of
  letters of credit, maturing 2031. **No merger, no EX-2.1** - the quote is an owner-earnings
  price and not a spread.
- **`acq_note` rebuilt and the screen UNDERSTATED it.** $667.3M over five years, **19.5% of the
  re-struck cap**, across eight dated events (ISE America, MeadowCreek, Crepini, Deal-Rite, Echo
  Lake $289.5M, Clean Egg $23.7M, Creighton $129.3M, Van's $24.8M). The screen's $643M omitted the
  **separately-tagged Van's line**, which sits on its own cash-flow row rather than inside
  `PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired`. **Fifteen of the seventeen years in the series
  are a different company from the one the price buys.**
- **`wc_note` was blank and arguably should not have been.** Trade receivables swung **-$105.0M in
  FY2025 and +$139.8M in FY2026**, and income taxes receivable/payable swung **+$91.6M in FY2024
  and -$94.8M in FY2026**. Against FY2026 operating cash of $479.8M the receivables swing is
  **29.1%**, just under the 30% threshold the Opus session measured; against FY2024's $451.4M the
  tax swing is **20.3%**. **The flag did not fire and the threshold is why.** Recorded as a
  near-miss rather than proposed as a change: the threshold was measured, not chosen, and one name
  is not a reason to move it.

## The SBC check, which cost nothing and closed a question

The BE defect (SBC silently zero) and the ARM/CALX finding (SBC consuming the business) both
demanded a check here, and it is **negative in the useful direction**. `ShareBasedCompensation`
resolves only from FY2019; the earlier years resolve under
`AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense` and the paid-in-capital tag, and **the two agree to the
rounding**, so **no year had zero substituted for it**. Materiality: **$5.757M in FY2026, 1.2% of
operating cash flow**, on 89,867 restricted shares granted. **Neither the charge nor the [E3-70]
grant value can move this series enough to matter**, so the grant-table hand-read that CORT and
ARM required was not needed, and the question is closed rather than deferred.

## What the run found without scoring it, because the gate was shut

Recorded in the run file's **FINDINGS NOT SCORED** section and repeated here only as pointers: the
**antitrust record** (jury decision 2023-12-01 of $17.8M; final judgment 2024-11-06 of **$43.6M
after trebling**, joint and several, for *"agreeing to limit the production of eggs"*; a DOJ and
17-state settlement on or about **2026-06-25** with no fines, $1.5M and 30 million eggs donated,
wrongdoing denied; **Washington State did not join**; a new MDL consolidated 2026-02-10 with no
discovery taken); the **segment-reporting change in Q4 FY2026** from one reportable segment to
three, recast, in the year conventional segment income fell **83.2%** - **[E2-49] flagged and NOT
resolved**, with the case stated both ways so the next brief cannot smuggle in a verdict; and the
**variable dividend** ($8.319 per share FY2025, $2.458 FY2026) on which [E2-52] does **not** fire,
because the share count fell every year of the window and no equity was sold.

**A second-order note for whoever opens Q2 on this industry again.** The nearest thing US shell
eggs ever had to an administered price was the **United Egg Producers animal-welfare guidelines**,
and that is precisely what the Egg Products Plaintiffs attacked and a jury found against.
**[E2-59] is the row:** administered pricing can floor a commodity business, but the moat belongs
to the **regime**, and *"That day is gone"* is how it ends. **Here the regime is being dismantled
in court**, which is why the run recorded the litigation as Q2 class evidence and not as a Q3
conduct finding it had no authority to score.

## The uncomfortable part, written down rather than hedged

**This is not a bad business and the run should not be read as saying so.** Sixteen-year mean ROE
of 16.6% is respectable; there is no debt, the revolver is undrawn, equity is $2,640.5M, and the
company has compounded its flock by buying 28 businesses since 1989 without issuing paper.
**[E4-20]'s three savings accounts would very likely have called it *good*, and possibly better
than good, had Q4 been reached.** The file closed at Q2 for one reason and it is a structural one:
**the price of the product is a published number that anybody else's identical product also trades
at**, so whatever Cal-Maine earns above its cost of capital in a tight year is competed away in an
ample one, and the seventeen-year record is what that looks like. **[E2-38]'s line applies to the
industry rather than to these managers:** good jockeys, and the horse is a commodity.

**And the honest counterweight, because [E4-26] runs both ways.** If the prepared-foods and
owned-brand build actually crosses over - shell eggs were **84.6% to 94.3%** of net sales over
three years, and the announced projects add *"more than 30 percent"* of prepared-foods capacity
from mid-2027 through 2028 - **that is a different company and would need a new run, not a revision
of this one.** The reversal condition is recorded in words in the run file. **No price band is
armed and no `PORTFOLIO.md` row is added**, because the name failed on the business.
